verdict.evidence_span_a: Het besluit wordt onverwijld na het tijdstip van ontvangst van de melding genomen.
verdict.evidence_span_b: een incidentmelding indienen met, indien van toepassing, een update van de in punt a) bedoelde informatie, een initiële beoordeling van het significante incident, met inbegrip van de ernst en de gevolgen ervan en, indien beschikbaar, de indicatoren voor aantasting

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Neither norm imposes the same compliance action: Norm A concerns the opposability of a shareholders-register entry to persons who later become participants in a deposit; Norm B requires preparing the GDPR record of processing activities in written or electronic form.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an effect of registration in a securities/deposit context, whereas Norm B is an organisational record-keeping requirement under data-protection law.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms concern different legal objects, actors, and operative actions: opposability of a shareholders-register entry versus preparation of a written/electronic processing-activities register.

verdict.evidence_span_b: Het in de leden 1 en 2 bedoelde register is in schriftelijke vorm, waaronder in elektronische vorm, opgesteld.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A telecommunicatiepartij must, at the Minister’s request, investigate the identity of a control holder and that holder’s links with third parties; B requires providers of general-purpose AI models to prepare, maintain, and make available technical and other model documentation, including specified information, for AI-system providers and authorities on request.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: The norms concern fundamentally different duties, actors, subject matter, and purposes: a targeted investigation into control ownership versus ongoing AI-model documentation, copyright compliance, and training-content transparency.
verdict.criterion_fired: Different event family, actor role, and core action; the apparent similarity is not a duplicated compliance obligation.
verdict.evidence_span_a: stelt een telecommunicatiepartij op verzoek van Onze Minister een onderzoek in naar de identiteit van een houder van zeggenschap en de banden die deze heeft met derden.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Aanbieders van AI-modellen voor algemene doeleinden moeten: a) de technische documentatie van het model opstellen en up-to-date houden

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms involve making information or documentation available to an institutional recipient, but Norm A requires substantiating an assessment and safeguards in an Article 30 register, whereas Norm B requires an authorised representative to provide AI-related information and documentation to the AI Office upon a reasoned request.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A concerns documenting and substantiating GDPR safeguards for an exceptional international data transfer in a register; Norm B concerns an authorised representative’s on-request production of AI-model compliance information and documentation to the AI Office.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in core action, triggering context, actor role, and substantive content; the fact that both involve supplying information to an institutional recipient is insufficient to establish duplicated compliance work.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De verwerkingsverantwoordelijke of de verwerker staaft de beoordeling en de in lid 1, tweede alinea, van dit artikel bedoelde passende waarborgen in het artikel 30 bedoelde register.
verdict.evidence_span_b: het verstrekken aan het AI-bureau, na een met redenen omkleed verzoek, van alle informatie en documentatie, waaronder die in punt b), die nodig is om aan te tonen dat de verplichtingen van dit hoofdstuk worden nageleefd

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A requires an appointed representative to cooperate with risk-elimination measures when requested by the Minister; B requires high-risk AI providers to retain automatically generated logs under Article 19 when they control them. These are not the same underlying compliance action.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A concerns cooperation with governmental risk-remediation measures, whereas Norm B concerns proactive retention of system-generated logs.
verdict.criterion_fired: Different core action, event family, and actor role; no duplicated compliance work is established.
verdict.evidence_span_a: het op verzoek van Onze Minister verlenen van medewerking aan eventueel genomen maatregelen ter uitschakeling van de risico's van apparaten of radioapparaten waarvoor hij als gemachtigde is aangewezen
verdict.evidence_span_b: bewaren de in artikel 19 bedoelde logs die automatisch door hun AI-systemen met een hoog risico zijn gegenereerd, wanneer zij hierover de controle hebben

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern serious-incident compliance, but Norm A requires financial entities to report serious ICT-related incidents and submit prescribed notifications/reports to a competent authority, whereas Norm B requires an AI provider to investigate a serious incident, including risk assessment and corrective measures, and to cooperate with authorities.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an incident-reporting duty imposed on financial entities; Norm B is an investigation, risk-assessment, and remediation duty imposed on AI providers. The texts do not establish the same actor, action, or compliance output.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in both actor role and core action: Norm A requires reporting an ICT incident to a competent authority, while Norm B requires the AI provider to investigate the incident, assess its risks, and take corrective measures. The shared serious-incident trigger is insufficient to establish duplicated compliance work.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Financiële entiteiten melden overeenkomstig lid 4 van dit artikel ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incidenten aan de relevante bevoegde autoriteit als bedoeld in artikel 46.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Na de melding van een ernstig incident op grond van lid 1 verricht de aanbieder onverwijld het nodige onderzoek in verband met het ernstige incident en het betrokken AI-systeem. Dit omvat een risicobeoordeling van het incident en corrigerende maatregelen.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms involve an entity providing information to a competent authority in connection with an ICT/security incident, but A requires an immediate early warning about a significant incident, whereas B requires an estimate of aggregated annual costs and losses from serious ICT-related incidents upon request.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a time-bound early-warning notification to the CSIRT and competent authority; Norm B is an on-request provision of quantified annual cost-and-loss information to competent authorities.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in their core action, actor scope, and required content: A requires an essential or important entity to issue an early warning within 24 hours of learning of a significant incident, while B requires non-micro financial entities to provide an annual cost-and-loss estimate only when competent authorities request it.
verdict.evidence_span_a: geeft ... een vroegtijdige waarschuwing over het significante incident aan haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit
verdict.evidence_span_b: verstrekken de bevoegde autoriteiten op hun verzoek een raming van de geaggregeerde jaarlijkse kosten en verliezen als gevolg van ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incidenten

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A requires answering a legitimate, duly reasoned access request for specific domain-registration data within 72 hours. B governs and restricts further processing of personal data in an AI regulatory sandbox, including a prohibition on sharing data created in the sandbox outside it, plus retention, logging, safeguards, and publication requirements.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: The norms address fundamentally different duties: responding to an access request for domain-registration data versus controlling further processing and external sharing of personal data in an AI testing environment.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties do not concern the same event or underlying action: A requires timely access-request response, while B imposes conditions and restrictions on AI-sandbox personal-data processing and sharing.
verdict.evidence_span_a: beantwoorden een verzoek om toegang als bedoeld in het eerste lid onverwijld of, indien dat niet mogelijk is, binnen 72 uur na ontvangst van het verzoek
verdict.evidence_span_b: persoonsgegevens die in de testomgeving worden aangemaakt mogen niet buiten de testomgeving worden gedeeld

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Geen gedeelde compliance-actie: norm A verplicht openbaarmaking van niet-persoonsgebonden domeinnaamregistratiegegevens; norm B verplicht het opstellen en actualiseren van technische documentatie voor een hoog-risico-AI-systeem.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A betreft onverwijlde publieke openbaarmaking na domeinnaamregistratie, terwijl norm B betreft technische conformiteitsdocumentatie die vóór marktintroductie of ingebruikneming wordt opgesteld en daarna wordt geactualiseerd.
verdict.criterion_fired: De normen hebben noch dezelfde kernhandeling, noch hetzelfde triggering event of dezelfde actorrol: domeinnaamregisters/dienstverleners moeten gegevens openbaar maken, terwijl aanbieders van hoog-risico-AI technische documentatie moeten opstellen en actualiseren.
verdict.evidence_span_a: de registers voor topleveldomeinnamen en de entiteiten die domeinnaamregistratiediensten verlenen, onverwijld na de registratie van een domeinnaam, de domeinnaamregistratiegegevens die geen persoonsgegevens zijn, openbaar maken
verdict.evidence_span_b: De technische documentatie van een AI-systeem met een hoog risico wordt opgesteld voordat dit systeem in de handel wordt gebracht of in gebruik wordt gesteld, en wordt geactualiseerd.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Geen gedeelde compliance-actie: norm A betreft registratie en rechtswege ingebruikgeving van nummers aan nummergebruikers; norm B legt aanbieders van hoog-risico-AI-systemen een breed pakket product-, documentatie-, conformiteits- en correctieverplichtingen op.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: De normen hebben verschillende gereguleerde objecten, actoren en verplichtingen. Norm A vereist dat nummerhouders nummergebruikers registreren; norm B vereist onder meer dat AI-aanbieders hun systemen conform de toepasselijke eisen maken en diverse aanvullende maatregelen nemen.
verdict.criterion_fired: Verschillende kernactie, actorrol en event-/onderwerpcontext; er is geen dubbele compliance-werkzaamheid.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Nummerhouders registreren binnen zes maanden na de inwerkingtreding van artikel 4.9, derde lid, onderdeel b, de nummergebruikers.
verdict.evidence_span_b: zorgen ervoor dat hun AI-systemen met een hoog risico in overeenstemming zijn met de eisen van afdeling 2;

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern risk-oriented cybersecurity governance, but A requires incorporating supplier/service-provider cybersecurity considerations into supply-chain security measures, whereas B requires conducting a risk assessment after each significant change affecting ICT-supported business functions or ICT assets.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a continuing supply-chain security due-diligence consideration within broader NIS2 risk-management measures; Norm B is an event-triggered risk assessment obligation for financial entities following significant infrastructure, process, or procedure changes.
verdict.criterion_fired: The underlying actions, triggering events, and actor scopes differ: A concerns considering supplier vulnerabilities, product quality, and suppliers’ cybersecurity practices when selecting supply-chain measures; B concerns performing a risk assessment upon a significant change in ICT infrastructure, processes, or procedures. Similar cybersecurity-risk subject matter is insufficient for duplicate burden.
verdict.evidence_span_b: verrichten een risicobeoordeling bij elke belangrijke wijziging in de netwerk- en informatiesysteeminfrastructuur en in de processen of procedures

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms involve organizational compliance duties, but A requires financial entities to establish ICT-incident management procedures and processes, while B requires an authorized representative to provide information and documentation to the AI Office upon a reasoned request.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a standing internal ICT-incident management and recordkeeping obligation for financial entities; Norm B is a request-based disclosure, document-availability, and cooperation obligation for authorized representatives of providers of general-purpose AI models.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in actor, event/context, and operative action: A requires establishing internal procedures and processes for monitoring, handling, and following up ICT-related incidents; B requires an authorized representative to provide specified information and documentation to the AI Office upon request.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Financiële entiteiten stellen passende procedures en processen vast voor een consistente en geïntegreerde monitoring, behandeling en follow-up van ICT-gerelateerde incidenten
verdict.evidence_span_b: het verstrekken aan het AI-bureau, na een met redenen omkleed verzoek, van alle informatie en documentatie, waaronder die in punt b), die nodig is om aan te tonen dat de verplichtingen van dit hoofdstuk worden nageleefd

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern handling or maintaining data, but Norm A requires domain-name registries and registration-service entities to collect and maintain accurate, complete domain-registration data, whereas Norm B requires appropriate technical and organisational protection of personal data processed in an AI regulatory sandbox, together with extensive conditions governing that processing.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a domain-registration database accuracy and maintenance duty; Norm B is a data-protection and controlled-processing regime for personal data used to develop, train, and test certain AI systems.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties do not concern the same underlying action, triggering event, or actor role. Norm A imposes a standing collection and maintenance obligation on TLD registries and domain-registration service entities; Norm B governs protective measures and conditions for processing personal data in an AI regulatory test environment. The apparent similarity is only data-related and does not establish duplicated compliance work.
verdict.evidence_span_a: verzamelen nauwkeurige en volledige domeinnaamregistratiegegevens in een database en houden die gegevens bij
verdict.evidence_span_b: in het kader van de testomgeving verwerkte persoonsgegevens worden beschermd met passende technische en organisatorische maatregelen

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms involve compliance-related action connected to an authority or regulatory oversight, but Norm A requires carrying out orders and providing all cooperation to the military authority, whereas Norm B requires preparing and updating technical documentation demonstrating a high-risk AI system’s conformity and supplying information for conformity assessment.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an event-triggered cooperation and order-execution duty owed to the military authority when Article 31 of the War Act is applied; Norm B is an ongoing, pre-market and updated documentation duty for high-risk AI systems, aimed at conformity assessment by competent authorities and notified bodies.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in actor role, triggering context, core action, recipient relationship, and substantive content; any superficial similarity from regulatory oversight or authority involvement does not establish duplicated compliance work.
verdict.evidence_span_a: verplicht het militair gezag alle medewerking te verlenen, daaronder begrepen het uitvoeren van door dat gezag gegeven opdrachten
verdict.evidence_span_b: De technische documentatie van een AI-systeem met een hoog risico wordt opgesteld voordat dit systeem in de handel wordt gebracht of in gebruik wordt gesteld, en wordt geactualiseerd.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms involve supplying information or cooperation to a public authority in the context of regulated-product conformity oversight, but they do not require the same underlying action: A requires an authorised representative to cooperate with risk-elimination measures when requested, while B requires notified bodies to notify the notifying authority about specified certification, accreditation, and information-request matters.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A concerns an authorised representative's cooperation with measures to eliminate product risks; Norm B concerns a notified body's notifications about conformity-assessment certificates, quality-management approvals, changes affecting notification, and related requests or activities.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in both actor role and operative event/content: A is cooperation with risk-elimination measures for devices or radio equipment, whereas B is notification by notified bodies of specified conformity-assessment and notification-related matters.
verdict.evidence_span_a: het op verzoek van Onze Minister verlenen van medewerking aan eventueel genomen maatregelen ter uitschakeling van de risico's van apparaten of radioapparaten waarvoor hij als gemachtigde is aangewezen
verdict.evidence_span_b: Aangemelde instanties brengen de aanmeldende autoriteit op de hoogte van:

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Beide normen houden verband met het vastleggen/documenteren van incidentgerelateerde informatie, maar norm A vereist een breed ICT-incidenten- en dreigingenregistratie- en beheerproces, terwijl norm B aanbieders verplicht relevante informatie over ernstige incidenten en mogelijke corrigerende maatregelen bij te houden, te documenteren en onverwijld aan bevoegde instanties te rapporteren.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A ziet op financiële entiteiten en een intern, alle ICT-gerelateerde incidenten en significante cyberdreigingen omvattend beheer- en registratieproces. Norm B ziet op aanbieders van AI-modellen met systeemrisico en omvat bovendien rapportage aan het AI-bureau/nationale autoriteiten, met informatie over ernstige incidenten en mogelijke corrigerende maatregelen.
verdict.criterion_fired: Niet dezelfde actorrol en niet dezelfde kernverplichting: norm A betreft interne registratie en incidentbeheer; norm B betreft AI-specifieke beoordeling/beperking en het bijhouden, documenteren en onverwijld rapporteren van ernstige incidenten en corrigerende maatregelen.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Financiële entiteiten registreren alle ICT-gerelateerde incidenten en significante cyberdreigingen.
verdict.evidence_span_b: relevante informatie over ernstige incidenten en mogelijke corrigerende maatregelen bijhouden, documenteren en onverwijld rapporteren aan het AI-bureau en, in voorkomend geval, aan de nationale bevoegde autoriteiten

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern taking appropriate technical and organisational measures, but A concerns measures that can exempt or substitute for communicating a personal-data breach to data subjects, whereas B requires high-risk-AI deployers to ensure use in accordance with the system’s instructions.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a GDPR data-subject communication exception/substitution tied to a personal-data breach and high risk to individuals; Norm B is an ongoing operational-governance duty for high-risk-AI system deployers, with related incident notification duties directed to providers, distributors, and market-surveillance authorities.
verdict.criterion_fired: The apparent verb overlap (taking appropriate technical and organisational measures) does not establish duplicate burden: the duties have different triggering contexts, purposes, actor roles, and substantive measures. A concerns personal-data-breach communications to data subjects; B concerns compliant operation of high-risk AI systems according to instructions.
verdict.evidence_span_a: de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke heeft passende technische en organisatorische beschermingsmaatregelen genomen en deze maatregelen zijn toegepast op de persoonsgegevens waarop de inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens betrekking heeft
verdict.evidence_span_b: Gebruiksverantwoordelijken van AI-systemen met een hoog risico nemen passende technische en organisatorische maatregelen om te waarborgen dat zij dergelijke systemen gebruiken in overeenstemming met de gebruiksaanwijzingen die bij de systemen zijn gevoegd

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both provisions concern an authorised representative making information or documentation available to a public authority on request, but they do not impose the same concrete compliance task. Article 10.4(b) requires supplying all information and documentation needed to demonstrate conformity to the Minister; Article 54 separately requires supplying information and documentation needed to demonstrate compliance with the AI Act to the AI Office, following a reasoned request. Article 54 also contains additional mandate, retention, verification, and cooperation duties.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: The duties concern different regulated products and different substantive compliance regimes, with different requesting authorities and different proof purposes: device/radio-equipment conformity versus compliance with the AI Act obligations for general-purpose AI models.
verdict.criterion_fired: Same request-based provision of information/documentation by an authorised representative to demonstrate regulatory compliance, but the required material and compliance purpose are not shown to be the same; therefore this is related rather than duplicated burden.
verdict.evidence_span_a: b) het op verzoek van Onze Minister verstrekken van alle benodigde informatie en documentatie om de conformiteit van de apparaten of radioapparaten aan te tonen;
verdict.evidence_span_b: c) het verstrekken aan het AI-bureau, na een met redenen omkleed verzoek, van alle informatie en documentatie, waaronder die in punt b), die nodig is om aan te tonen dat de verplichtingen van dit hoofdstuk worden nageleefd;

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both provisions concern an authority obtaining or directing information/cooperation from an entity, but A requires the designated person to issue narrowly purpose-bound orders to secure cooperation with a suspension or prevent network/service abuse or outage, whereas B empowers the lead overseer to request reports from critical ICT third-party providers about actions or corrective measures concerning oversight recommendations, among broader oversight powers.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an operational order/cooperation power tied to an intervention involving suspension or prevention of network/service abuse or outage; Norm B is a supervisory reporting and information-gathering power concerning critical ICT third-party providers and corrective measures following oversight recommendations.
verdict.criterion_fired: The provisions do not impose the same underlying duty: A concerns compliance with targeted orders issued to a party involved in a suspension or network/service disruption context, while B concerns a critical ICT third-party provider's supervisory reporting and information/documentation obligations to a lead overseer. The actors, regulatory purposes, and required content differ materially.
verdict.evidence_span_a: de aangewezen persoon verstrekt uitsluitend opdrachten die tot doel hebben om: a. de medewerking van de betrokken partij aan de schorsing, bedoeld in artikel 14a.7, eerste lid, te verzekeren, of b. misbruik of uitval van het netwerk of de dienst van de betrokken partij te voorkomen.
verdict.evidence_span_b: na afloop van de oversightactiviteiten te verzoeken om verslagen met vermelding van de ondernomen acties of de corrigerende maatregelen die door de kritieke derde aanbieders van ICT-diensten zijn genomen met betrekking tot de in punt d) bedoelde aanbevelingen

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Beide normen betreffen het opstellen en bijhouden van schriftelijke/documentaire informatie, maar niet dezelfde concrete compliance-actie: norm A vereist een register van verwerkingsactiviteiten; norm B vereist uitgebreide technische, gebruikersgerichte, auteursrechtelijke en openbaar te maken documentatie over een AI-model voor algemene doeleinden.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A ziet op het register van verwerkingsactiviteiten van een verwerkingsverantwoordelijke of verwerker; norm B ziet op documentatie-, informatie-, auteursrechtbeleid- en openbaarmakingsverplichtingen van aanbieders van AI-modellen voor algemene doeleinden.
verdict.criterion_fired: De normen leggen geen dezelfde of inhoudelijk gelijkwaardige duty op: zij hebben verschillende actoren, verschillende onderwerpen en verschillende compliance-doeleinden. De oppervlakkige overeenkomst dat schriftelijke documentatie moet worden opgesteld is onvoldoende voor duplicate burden.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Het in de leden 1 en 2 bedoelde register is in schriftelijke vorm, waaronder in elektronische vorm, opgesteld.
verdict.evidence_span_b: de technische documentatie van het model opstellen en up-to-date houden, inclusief het trainings- en testproces en de resultaten van de evaluatie ervan

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both concern regulatory compliance relating to digital/AI governance, but A requires publication of policies and procedures, whereas B requires an affected provider to remedy specified formal non-conformities within a market-surveillance deadline.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a standing transparency/publication duty imposed on domain-name registries and registration-service entities; Norm B is an enforcement order imposed on a provider after a market-surveillance authority finds a formal non-conformity.
verdict.criterion_fired: Different underlying action, triggering event, and duty-bearing actor; the apparent similarity is only a broad digital-regulatory context, not duplicated compliance work.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Zij maken dat beleid en die procedures openbaar.
verdict.evidence_span_b: schrijft zij de betrokken aanbieder voor dat deze binnen een door haar vast te stellen termijn een einde maakt aan deze non-conformiteit

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require the relevant regulated entity to establish procedures/processes, but they address different compliance systems: domain-name registration-data accuracy and publication versus ICT-incident monitoring, handling, follow-up, and root-cause remediation.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A concerns procedures ensuring accurate and complete domain-name registration data and requires those policies and procedures to be made public; Norm B concerns recording ICT incidents and significant cyber threats and establishing integrated processes for monitoring, handling, follow-up, and prevention through root-cause remediation.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties concern different subject matters and actor categories: domain-name registries/registration-service entities must establish and publish data-verification policies, while financial entities must establish ICT-incident-management processes. Similar wording ('establish procedures/processes') is insufficient for duplicate burden.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De registers voor topleveldomeinnamen en de entiteiten die domeinnaamregistratiediensten verlenen stellen het beleid en de procedures vast, waaronder verificatieprocedures, om ervoor te zorgen dat de database, bedoeld in het eerste lid, juiste en volledige informatie bevat.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Financiële entiteiten stellen passende procedures en processen vast voor een consistente en geïntegreerde monitoring, behandeling en follow-up van ICT-gerelateerde incidenten

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms involve maintaining or making compliance-related records/information available, but they impose different duties: A requires financial entities to provide an ICT-services information register to a competent authority on request; B requires high-risk AI providers to retain documentation under Article 18.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an on-request disclosure duty to a competent authority concerning ICT-service contracts; Norm B is a record-retention duty concerning high-risk AI-system documentation, with no recipient or request specified.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in actor role, subject matter, and operative action: disclosure of an ICT-contract register to a competent authority versus retention of AI-system documentation.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Financiële entiteiten stellen de bevoegde autoriteit op verzoek het volledige informatieregister of desgevraagd specifieke onderdelen daarvan ter beschikking
verdict.evidence_span_b: bewaren de in artikel 18 bedoelde documentatie

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Geen gedeelde concrete compliance-actie: norm A verplicht het verstrekken en actualiseren van identificatie- en contactinformatie aan bevoegde autoriteiten; norm B verplicht het bijhouden van toegankelijke registers van activiteiten rond geactiveerde ICT-continuïteits- en respons-/herstelplannen.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A betreft een meld-/informatieverstrekkingsplicht over de entiteit en wijzigingen daarin, met een termijn van uiterlijk twee weken na wijziging. Norm B betreft interne registratie en bewaring/toegankelijkheid van activiteiten vóór en tijdens storingen; zij noemt in de aangehaalde tekst geen autoriteit, melding of termijn.
verdict.criterion_fired: De kernactie, het relevante gebeurtenistype en de aard van de informatie verschillen: externe verstrekking van entiteitsgegevens aan bevoegde autoriteiten versus interne registratie van activiteiten bij geactiveerde ICT-continuïteits- en herstelplannen.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De in lid 3 bedoelde entiteiten melden onmiddellijk elke wijziging in de bijzonderheden die zij op grond van de eerste alinea van dit lid hebben ingediend, en in elk geval binnen twee weken na de datum van de wijziging.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Financiële entiteiten houden gemakkelijk toegankelijke registers bij van hun activiteiten vóór en tijdens storingen wanneer hun ICT-bedrijfscontinuïteitsplannen en ICT-respons- en herstelplannen worden geactiveerd.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms impose affirmative compliance-system or process obligations on regulated providers, but they require different measures: Norm A requires establishing and publishing policies and procedures to ensure accurate and complete domain-registration data, while Norm B requires high-risk AI providers to ensure conformity with specified AI Act requirements before placing the system on the market or putting it into service, among other duties.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A concerns domain-name registration databases and policies/procedures for data accuracy and completeness; Norm B concerns conformity of high-risk AI systems with the AI Act before market placement or use, including a broad set of documentation, assessment, marking, registration, corrective-action, and accessibility obligations.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms do not impose the same underlying action on the same kind of actor in response to the same event. Norm B is a simplified but comprehensive ICT-risk-management framework duty for specified financial entities, including establishment, maintenance, monitoring, testing, evaluation, and possible reporting to the competent authority.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms do not impose the same core compliance action: Norm A concerns considering supplier-specific and supply-chain risk information when determining measures, whereas Norm B requires specified financial entities to establish and maintain a documented ICT-risk-management framework and related controls. Their actor populations and regulatory contexts also differ, and there is no same reporting recipient or duplicated reporting channel.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms involve promptly reporting information about a serious/significant incident to a public authority, but A requires a structured NIS2 incident-reporting sequence, while B requires providers of general-purpose AI models with systemic risk to keep and document information about serious incidents and possible corrective measures and report it to the AI Office and, where applicable, national competent authorities.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A requires an entity to take proportionate security measures and account for risks, technology, costs, standards, exposure, size, incident likelihood and severity. B empowers a lead overseer to request reports from critical ICT third-party providers concerning actions or corrective measures taken in response to recommendations. These are not the same compliance action.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a substantive risk-based security-measures and proportionality duty imposed on an essential or important entity; Norm B is an oversight power enabling a lead overseer to request post-oversight reports from critical ICT third-party providers.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms differ in actor, operative action, and legal purpose: A concerns implementing and calibrating security measures to manage incident risks, whereas B concerns an overseer’s power to request reports on actions or corrective measures following oversight recommendations.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Bij het nemen van de maatregelen houdt de entiteit in ieder geval rekening met de stand van de techniek, de uitvoeringskosten en, indien van toepassing, de desbetreffende Europese en internationale normen.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern incident-related compliance, but A requires an early-warning notification of a significant incident to the entity’s CSIRT and competent authority; B requires financial entities to establish and implement an ICT-incident management process capable of detecting, managing, and reporting ICT-related incidents.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A imposes a concrete, time-bound external early-warning duty for a significant incident. Norm B imposes an organisational/process duty to design, adopt, and implement ICT-incident management procedures; its reference to reporting incidents does not itself specify the same notification, recipients, content, or deadline.
verdict.criterion_fired: The actor role and core compliance action differ: A is an essential or important entity’s immediate incident warning to specified authorities/CSIRT, while B is a financial entity’s internal governance and implementation of an ICT-incident management process. The shared incident theme is insufficient to establish duplicated reporting work.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit geeft ten behoeve van de melding, bedoeld in artikel 27, eerste lid, een vroegtijdige waarschuwing over het significante incident aan haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Financiële entiteiten omschrijven een beheerproces voor ICT-gerelateerde incidenten, stellen dit vast en leggen dit ten uitvoer, om ICT-gerelateerde incidenten te detecteren, te beheren en te melden.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern cooperation with or provision of material to an EU supervisory authority, but they do not impose the same underlying compliance action: Article 38 concerns investigators' written authorization and possible coercive fines for failure to provide requested records, data, procedures, other material, or answers; Article 54 imposes an authorized representative's duties to maintain specified technical documentation and provide information/documentation to the AI Office upon a reasoned request.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A regulates the lead overseer's investigation authorization and the possible coercive fines tied to non-provision of investigative material or answers by representatives of third-party ICT-service providers. Norm B requires representatives of providers of general-purpose AI models to maintain technical documentation and, upon a reasoned request, provide information and documentation to the AI Office, and to cooperate with authorities.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms do not impose the same core duty on the same actor in response to the same event. Norm A concerns investigative powers and coercive fines in the DORA oversight context; Norm B concerns the standing documentation, information-provision, and cooperation duties of an authorized representative for a general-purpose AI model provider.

verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an internal ICT-incident management and remediation duty for financial entities; Norm B is an authorised representative’s AI Act mandate involving technical-documentation verification, ten-year availability, information production on reasoned request, and cooperation with authorities.
verdict.criterion_fired: The underlying actions, triggering event families, and duty-bearing actor roles differ materially; the apparent similarity does not establish repeated compliance work.

verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is een externe meldplicht voor essentiële of belangrijke entiteiten; Norm B is een interne classificatie- en effectbeoordelingsplicht voor financiële entiteiten, zonder meldingshandeling of ontvanger in de aangehaalde bepaling.
verdict.criterion_fired: De kernactie en actorrol verschillen: melden aan een bevoegde instantie tegenover intern classificeren en effecten bepalen; een gedeelde incidentcontext maakt dit niet dezelfde compliance-verplichting.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms include obligations to maintain or retain compliance documentation: A requires the authorised representative to keep the EU declaration of conformity and technical documentation available to the Minister for ten years; B requires providers of high-risk AI systems to retain the documentation referred to in Article 18. The overlap is limited to documentation retention, not the full set of duties in either provision.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A concerns an authorised representative for devices/radio equipment and requires documentation to be kept available to the Minister for ten years, while Norm B concerns providers of high-risk AI systems and requires retention of Article 18 documentation as part of a broader AI-compliance regime.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms do not impose the same duty on the same actor concerning the same regulated product or event. Their limited shared verb-level action—retaining compliance documentation—is insufficient because the actor roles, regulated subject matter, and documentation categories differ; A also includes availability to a Minister and a ten-year period, whereas B concerns Article 18 documentation retained by an AI provider.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require the regulated actor to establish or maintain an information-related compliance system: Norm A requires policies and procedures ensuring accurate and complete domain-registration data, while Norm B requires financial entities to maintain and update a register of ICT-service contracts and provide related reporting or access to the competent authority.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A concerns policies and procedures for the accuracy and completeness of a domain-name-registration database; Norm B concerns maintaining, documenting, reporting on, and providing access to a financial entity’s ICT third-party-contract register.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties concern different actors, subject matter, and compliance purposes: domain-name registries/registration-service entities must establish and publish data-quality policies and procedures, whereas financial entities must maintain an ICT-contract register and report or provide it to competent authorities.

verdict.criterion_fired: De normen hebben verschillende kernacties, verschillende gereguleerde situaties en verschillende soorten verplichtingsdragers: betaling van auditkosten versus het niet verrichten van verboden AI-handelingen.

verdict.criterion_fired: The norms impose different kinds of duties on different regulatory objects: maintaining a processing-activities register versus restricting the effects of processing and satisfying conditions for AI testing. verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern monitoring and responding to adverse technology-related events, but Norm A requires registration and internal incident-management/root-cause remediation, whereas Norm B requires high-risk-AI users to notify specified parties and authorities of risks or serious incidents, and in some cases suspend use.

verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in both the core action and actor role: Norm A requires financial entities to register ICT incidents and establish internal processes to identify, document, and remove root causes; Norm B requires high-risk-AI users to notify providers, importers/distributors, and market-surveillance authorities, and to interrupt use in specified circumstances. verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms involve providing information or documentation to a public authority, but they do not require the same underlying compliance work. Norm A requires a telecommunications party, upon ministerial request, to provide an extract from a corporate register concerning a share right and/or investigate the identity and third-party links of a control holder. Norm B requires financial entities to maintain and document an ICT-services contract register, report specified aggregate information at least annually, provide the full register or specified parts on request, and notify the competent authority of certain planned contracts or changes in criticality.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A concerns ministerial scrutiny of potentially dominant control over a telecommunications party and a specific share-right/register extract or control-identity investigation. Norm B concerns ICT third-party-service contract-register governance, recurring reporting, on-request supervisory access, and advance notification of contracts supporting critical or important functions.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in actor, triggering subject matter, and substantive content: Norm A is an ad hoc ministerial request concerning control/share ownership, whereas Norm B is an ICT-risk-management register, annual reporting, on-request disclosure, and advance-notification regime for financial entities.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern making information available in connection with a triggering circumstance, but A requires a telecommunications party to provide a register extract to the Minister on request, whereas B requires domain-name registries/registration-service entities to publicly disclose non-personal domain-registration data immediately after registration.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A requires essential and important entities to implement proportionate technical, operational, and organisational cybersecurity-risk-management measures to prevent incidents or limit their effects; B requires non-micro financial entities to provide competent authorities, on request, with an estimate of aggregated annual costs and losses from serious ICT-related incidents.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an ex ante risk-management and incident-prevention/impact-limitation measure duty, whereas Norm B is an on-request information-provision duty concerning aggregated annual incident costs and losses.

The shared ICT-incident context is insufficient to make the duties the same or a duplicated burden.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms address mitigating the consequences or risks of security-related incidents/risks, but Norm A requires preventive technical, operational, and organisational measures, whereas Norm B requires AI-model risk assessment and mitigation plus keeping, documenting, and promptly reporting information about serious incidents and possible corrective measures.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A imposes a general security-risk mitigation duty on providers of public electronic communications networks or services; Norm B imposes AI-model-specific duties on providers of general-purpose AI models with systemic risk, including an express incident-information reporting obligation.
verdict.criterion_fired: The actor roles and operative duties differ: Norm A requires communications providers to implement security measures to limit incident consequences, while Norm B requires systemic-risk AI providers to assess and mitigate AI risks and to keep, document, and report serious-incident information. The shared security-incident/risk theme is insufficient to establish duplicated compliance work.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern submitting incident-related information to a CSIRT, but Norm A requires an early warning about a significant incident, while Norm B requires the DORA Article 19 incident report or voluntary notification to be made additionally to the designated financial-sector CSIRT.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an immediate/within-24-hours early-warning duty to both the CSIRT and competent authority; Norm B extends specified DORA mandatory or voluntary ICT-incident notifications to a sectoral CSIRT and does not specify a deadline in the provision.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties do not have the same actor scope: Norm A applies to essential or important entities generally, whereas Norm B applies specifically to banks, trading venues, central securities depositories and central counterparties. Their reporting content and legal purposes also differ: an early warning of a significant incident versus a DORA Article 19 mandatory or voluntary ICT-incident notification.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit geeft ten behoeve van de melding, bedoeld in artikel 27, eerste lid, een vroegtijdige waarschuwing over het significante incident aan haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Banken, handelsplatformen, centrale effectenbewaarinstellingen en centrale tegenpartijen doen de melding, bedoeld in artikel 19, eerste lid, eerste paragraaf, van de verordening, en de vrijwillige melding, bedoeld in artikel 19, tweede lid, eerste paragraaf, van de verordening, tevens bij het bij of krachtens artikel 16, eerste lid, van de Cyberbeveiligingswet aangewezen CSIRT voor de sectoren bankwezen en infrastructuur voor de financiële markt.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Beide normen leggen een administratieve/documentatiebewaarplicht op: norm A vereist een register van verwerkingsactiviteiten; norm B vereist het bewaren van automatisch gegenereerde AI-systeemlogs.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Beide normen bevatten een openbaarmakings/publicatie-element, maar niet dezelfde compliance-actie in inhoud of doel: norm A vereist openbaarmaking van beleid en procedures voor bekendmaking van domeinnaamregistratiegegevens; norm B vereist publicatie van een korte samenvatting van een AI-project, de doelstellingen en verwachte resultaten op de website van bevoegde autoriteiten.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A betreft transparantie over beleid en procedures voor toegang tot domeinnaamregistratiegegevens; norm B betreft transparantie over een AI-testproject en de verwachte resultaten daarvan, binnen een regime voor verdere verwerking van persoonsgegevens.
verdict.criterion_fired: De normen hebben geen dezelfde event family of actor role en vereisen inhoudelijk verschillende publicaties; een oppervlakkige overeenkomst in het werkwoord ‘openbaar maken/publiceren’ is onvoldoende voor duplicatie.

verdict.evidence_span_b: een korte samenvatting van het in de testomgeving ontwikkelde AI-project en de doelstellingen en verwachte resultaten ervan worden op de website van de bevoegde autoriteiten gepubliceerd

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Beide normen vereisen het vastleggen/registreren van informatie, maar niet dezelfde informatie of voor hetzelfde compliance-doel: norm A vereist een register van verwerkingsactiviteiten met specifieke gegevens over verwerkingen, partijen, doorgiften en beveiligingsmaatregelen; norm B vereist registratie van ICT-gerelateerde incidenten en significante cyberdreigingen als onderdeel van incidentbeheer.

verdict.criterion_fired: De normen hebben niet dezelfde gebeurtenisfamilie en niet dezelfde actorrol; bovendien verschilt de inhoud van de registratie wezenlijk.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De verwerker, en, in voorkomend geval, de vertegenwoordiger van de verwerker houdt een register van alle categorieën van verwerkingsactiviteiten
verdict.evidence_span_b: Financiële entiteiten registreren alle ICT-gerelateerde incidenten en significante cyberdreigingen.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A requires investigators’ written authorisations to mention possible coercive fines; B requires personal data processed in the AI regulatory sandbox to be protected with appropriate technical and organisational measures, alongside other sandbox-processing conditions.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: A concerns the content of an investigative authorisation and possible enforcement consequences for third-party ICT-service providers; B concerns safeguards governing personal-data processing in an AI regulatory sandbox.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms impose different kinds of duties on different actors in different contexts: A concerns stating coercive fines in an investigative authorisation, while B concerns protecting personal data during AI-system development, training and testing.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require an entity/provider to disclose identifying information, including its name and contact details, but they do so for different regulatory purposes and within different broader duties.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires covered entities to provide information to competent authorities for inclusion in the Member State list and to report changes within two weeks. Norm B requires high-risk AI providers to display their name or registered trade name/mark and contact address on the AI system, packaging, or accompanying documentation, as part of product-compliance obligations.
verdict.criterion_fired: The identifying-information elements overlap superficially, but the duties concern different actor roles, regulatory contexts, purposes, and channels: authority-facing entity registration/list information versus product labelling for high-risk AI systems.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require the regulated entity to take or maintain cybersecurity risk-management measures, but A specifically requires consideration of suppliers’ vulnerabilities and security practices when selecting supply-chain measures, whereas B requires financial entities to implement a broad ICT-security and infrastructure-management framework.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a supplier-specific decision-making consideration within supply-chain security; Norm B is a comprehensive, documented ICT-risk-management and protection framework, including network/infrastructure management and multiple controls.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms do not impose the same verb-level duty or require the same compliance work: A concerns taking supplier vulnerabilities and practices into account when determining supply-chain measures; B concerns implementing and documenting a broad set of ICT-security controls for financial entities.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both provisions concern incidents reported by regulated entities, but Norm A imposes a duty to report every significant incident, whereas Norm B concerns supervisory authorities' feedback and preserves the financial entity's responsibility for handling and consequences after an ICT-related incident has been reported.

verdict.criterion_fired: Different core action and actor role: Norm A requires an entity to report significant incidents; Norm B addresses the competent authority's feedback and the financial entity's continuing responsibility for already-reported ICT incidents.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Geen gedeelde verb-level compliance-actie: norm A vereist governance-maatregelen (goedkeuren, toezicht houden en aansprakelijkheid aanvaarden), terwijl norm B het opstellen en indienen van incidentmeldingen en verslagen vereist.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A betreft intern bestuur en toezicht op cyberbeveiligingsrisicobeheersmaatregelen; norm B betreft rapportage van ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incidenten aan bevoegde autoriteiten, met voorgeschreven modellen en inhoud.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require the regulated actor to take a compliance measure concerning ICT/AI systems, but the measures are fundamentally different: Norm A requires implementing and maintaining resilient, up-to-date ICT systems, protocols and tools to mitigate ICT risk; Norm B prohibits placing on the market, putting into service, or using specified biometric categorisation AI systems.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an ongoing ICT-risk-management and resilience obligation for certain financial entities, whereas Norm B is a prohibition on specified AI-system activities, including biometric categorisation to infer highly sensitive characteristics.
verdict.criterion_fired: The underlying actions, triggering circumstances, actor roles and compliance purposes are materially different; any superficial overlap in regulated technology does not amount to repeated compliance work.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern actions taken in response to an ICT/security-related incident: A requires an essential or important entity to submit a progress report (and later a final report), while B requires a financial entity to perform checks and reconciliations during ICT-incident recovery to preserve data integrity and consistency.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A imposes an incident-reporting duty, including a progress report when the incident continues and a final report within one month after handling; Norm B imposes operational data-integrity controls during recovery and reconstruction, with no reporting or recipient duty.
verdict.criterion_fired: The underlying actions and actor roles differ: A is an essential/important entity's reporting obligation, whereas B is a financial entity's recovery and data-integrity control obligation. The shared incident context is insufficient to make the compliance work duplicative.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A requires prompt notification of a qualifying personal-data security breach to the Dutch Data Protection Authority. B requires financial entities to conduct post-incident ICT evaluations after serious ICT incidents, analyze causes and improvements, assess procedures and measures, and—on request for non-micro entities—communicate resulting changes to competent authorities.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: A is an immediate breach-notification duty focused on personal-data protection and addressed to the data-protection authority; B is an internal post-incident review and improvement duty, with possible later disclosure of implemented changes to competent authorities.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms concern different core actions and different actor categories: A requires immediate regulatory notification of a qualifying security breach, while B requires post-incident evaluation and improvement analysis by financial entities. The shared broad incident context and regulatory-authority involvement do not make the compliance work the same.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both provisions concern handling or obtaining information/data, but they impose fundamentally different actions: Norm A empowers a supervisory authority to inspect and obtain certified copies or extracts; Norm B permits providers to process personal data for developing, training, and testing AI systems subject to cumulative safeguards.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an investigative power of the lead overseer directed at obtaining records and other materials from critical ICT third-party providers. Norm B is a conditional authorization and set of safeguards governing providers’ further processing of personal data in an AI regulatory sandbox; it is not an information-production or reporting duty.
verdict.criterion_fired: The underlying actions, triggering contexts, and duty-bearing roles differ. Norm A concerns supervisory investigation and certified copying/extraction of records; Norm B concerns lawful further processing of personal data for AI development, training, and testing under specified public-interest and data-protection conditions. Similarity in the broad subject of information/data is insufficient.

verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A concerns immediate public disclosure of non-personal domain-registration data after domain registration, whereas Norm B concerns establishing an internal ICT-incident management process, including monitoring, treatment, follow-up, and root-cause remediation.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern responding to or managing circumstances involving potentially disruptive or harmful events, but they require fundamentally different actions: A requires telecommunications providers and spectrum users to cooperate with military authorities and execute their orders; B requires financial entities to establish internal ICT-incident procedures and processes and to register ICT-related incidents and significant cyber threats.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern making information or documentation available in response to an information-access or information-request context, but Norm A requires establishing and publishing policies and procedures for disclosure of domain-registration data, whereas Norm B requires importers to provide all necessary high-risk-AI conformity information and documentation to competent authorities upon a reasoned request and ensure technical documentation is available.

verdict.evidence_span_a: De registers voor topleveldomeinnamen en de entiteiten die domeinnaamregistratiediensten verlenen stellen het beleid en de procedures met betrekking tot de bekendmaking van de gegevens, bedoeld in het eerste lid, vast en maken dat beleid en die procedures openbaar.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern ICT/security incidents and refer to incident-related information or handling, but they do not impose the same operative compliance action: Norm A requires an entity to promptly inform its service recipients of significant incidents; Norm B states that financial entities remain responsible for handling and consequences of ICT-related incidents reported under Article 19(1), while describing supervisory feedback and possible discussion of corrective measures.

Norm B is primarily a responsibility rule and supervisory-feedback provision concerning incidents reported to the competent authority; it does not require the financial entity to repeat the same notification to the same or an equivalent recipient.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms do not impose the same core action on the same actor role: A requires prompt customer/service-recipient notification, whereas B concerns a financial entity’s continuing responsibility for reported ICT incidents and supervisory authority feedback.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit stelt in voorkomend geval onverwijld de ontvangers van haar diensten in kennis van significante incidenten

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A requires the controller to report a personal-data breach to the competent supervisory authority within 72 hours where applicable. verdict.criterion_fired: The underlying action and responsible actor role differ: A is a controller's regulatory notification of a personal-data breach, while B is a financial entity's post-incident evaluation and improvement process. verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both concern handling or communicating information related to adverse cyber/AI events, but Norm A establishes a voluntary information-sharing framework, whereas Norm B requires providers (and potentially deployers) to report serious incidents to market-surveillance authorities within a deadline.

verdict.criterion_fired: The duties are not the same core action or actor role: Norm A requires Member States to enable voluntary cybersecurity information exchange among entities, while Norm B requires high-risk AI providers (and potentially deployers) to make a mandatory serious-incident report to market-surveillance authorities. The shared incident/cybersecurity context and broad information element do not make the compliance work duplicative.

verdict.criterion_fired: The norms differ in actor role, triggering event, and operative action: internal management of ICT-related incidents versus verification and market-placement controls for high-risk AI systems.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Financiële entiteiten stellen passende procedures en processen vast voor een consistente en geïntegreerde monitoring, behandeling en follow-up van ICT-gerelateerde incidenten

verdict.criterion_fired: The norms do not impose the same underlying action on the same actor in response to the same event: A requires providing a processing-activities register on request, whereas B concerns an investigation authorisation and possible coercive fines for failure to provide specified investigative materials or answers.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms impose transparency/information-related obligations concerning regulated subject matter, but they do not require the same compliance action: Norm A requires prompt public disclosure of non-personal domain-registration data, whereas Norm B requires an authorised representative to retain conformity materials, provide information/documentation to the Minister on request, and cooperate with risk-reduction measures.

verdict.criterion_fired: The norms differ in actor role, triggering event, core action, recipient, and substantive content; the superficial similarity of making information available does not establish duplicated compliance work.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms involve making compliance-related information or documentation available, but Norm A requires producing an existing processing-activities register to a supervisory authority on request, whereas Norm B imposes broader ex ante documentation, maintenance, disclosure to downstream AI-system providers, and public-summary obligations.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an on-request disclosure of a GDPR processing register by a controller or processor; Norm B concerns providers of general-purpose AI models creating and maintaining technical and other documentation, supplying it to AI-system providers or authorities on request, and publicly summarising training content.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in actor role, subject matter, and operative obligation: Norm A concerns disclosure of a processing-activities register to a supervisory authority, while Norm B concerns general-purpose AI-model providers' documentation, downstream information, copyright policy, and public training-content summary obligations.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both require organizational measures concerning communication or mitigation of ICT/security incidents, but A requires risk-based technical, operational, and organizational measures to prevent incidents or limit their effects, whereas B requires financial entities to maintain crisis-communication plans enabling responsible disclosure of serious ICT incidents or vulnerabilities.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a broad preventive and impact-mitigation duty; Norm B is a specific crisis-communication planning and disclosure duty directed to clients, counterparties, and potentially the public.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties concern the same broad ICT/security-incident family but impose different core actions and different actor roles: A applies to essential or important entities and requires risk-control measures to prevent or mitigate incidents; B applies to financial entities and requires crisis-communication plans enabling disclosure. They are therefore not the same compliance work repeated.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A requires establishing and implementing an ICT-incident management process for detecting, managing, and reporting ICT-related incidents. verdict.criterion_fired: The norms concern the same broad incident-related context but impose different core actions on different regulated actor roles: process establishment and implementation versus post-incident investigation and related safeguards.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern making compliance-related information or procedures available, but they impose different substantive duties: Norm A requires publication of domain-registration database policies and procedures; Norm B requires preparation and updating of technical documentation for high-risk AI systems, including information sufficient for conformity assessment.

Norm B is a technical-documentation and conformity-assessment duty concerning high-risk AI systems; its final sentence additionally requires notified bodies to accept a prescribed simplified form.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties concern different regulated objects, different substantive actions, different actor roles, and different compliance purposes; any superficial similarity in making information or procedures available does not create duplicated compliance work.

verdict.criterion_fired: The duties concern different actors, different triggering situations, different actions, and different subject matter: an optional ACM adjudication request after failed negotiations versus ongoing ICT-risk management and incident handling.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A requires the controller to consult the supervisory authority before processing where a DPIA indicates an unmitigated high risk, including provision of specified processing, safeguards, DPIA and other information. verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern incident-related compliance, but A requires adding specific information to an early warning, whereas B requires making a substantive report of a serious incident to market-surveillance authorities within a specified deadline.

Norm B requires high-risk AI providers (and, where applicable, deployers) to report serious incidents to market-surveillance authorities, with a deadline of immediately after establishing causation or reasonable likelihood and no later than 15 days after awareness.
verdict.criterion_fired: The event family is broadly similar (a significant/serious incident), but the underlying duties and actor roles differ: A concerns information supplied as part of an early warning by an entity, while B concerns reporting serious incidents by high-risk AI providers or, where applicable, deployers to market-surveillance authorities.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern action in response to a significant/serious incident, but A requires a structured incident-reporting sequence to the CSIRT or competent authority, whereas B requires the AI provider to investigate the incident and AI system, assess risks, take corrective measures, cooperate with authorities, and avoid unnotified system-altering investigation.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern establishing or enabling procedures for providing information to a public or regulatory body, but they do not require the same concrete compliance work: Norm A requires domain-name registries/registrars to establish and publish policies and procedures for disclosure of domain-registration data, while Norm B concerns an authorised representative’s mandate and ongoing duties, including retaining AI documentation, supplying information and documentation to the AI Office on a reasoned request, and cooperating with authorities.

verdict.criterion_fired: The duties do not impose the same core action or the same actor role: Norm A concerns ICT-system resilience and risk-management measures, while Norm B concerns investigation of a serious incident and cooperation with authorities.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Beide normen leggen een preventieve ICT/cybersecurity-risicobeheeractie op, maar niet dezelfde concrete actie: norm A vereist dat bij de keuze van maatregelen rekening wordt gehouden met leverancierskwaliteit en cyberbeveiligingspraktijken; norm B vereist onder meer het opzetten en onderhouden van een ICT-risicobeheerkader, voortdurende monitoring, incidentdetectie/-afhandeling, continuïteit en periodieke tests.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both require the regulated actor to create and maintain documentation or records, but the underlying duties are not the same: Norm A requires a processor to keep a register of processing activities, while Norm B requires a high-risk AI provider to prepare and update technical documentation demonstrating regulatory conformity.

verdict.criterion_fired: The duties concern different regulated actors, different subject matter, and different compliance purposes: processing-activity recordkeeping under GDPR versus conformity documentation for a high-risk AI system under the AI Act. verdict.evidence_span_a: De verwerker, en, in voorkomend geval, de vertegenwoordiger van de verwerker houdt een register van alle categorieën van verwerkingsactiviteiten

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A requires essential and important entities to promptly inform service recipients about measures they can take in response to a significant cyber threat and, where necessary, to inform them of the threat itself. B requires financial entities to conduct post-incident ICT evaluations and, on request, for non-micro financial entities to communicate to competent authorities the changes implemented after those evaluations.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: A is an outward-facing warning/information duty to potentially affected service recipients concerning a significant cyber threat; B is an internal post-incident evaluation and a possible authority-facing disclosure of resulting changes.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties do not impose the same core action, actor role, or substantive content: A requires communicating threat information and protective measures to service recipients, whereas B requires post-incident analysis and, if requested, reporting implemented improvements to competent authorities.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Indien nodig stellen de entiteiten die ontvangers ook in kennis van de significante cyberdreiging zelf.
