verdict.shared_compliance_action: Norm A concerns the legal effect of an entry in a shareholders’ register; Norm B imposes multiple product-compliance, documentation, marking, registration, corrective-action, and information duties on providers of high-risk AI systems. They do not require the same compliance action.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an opposability rule concerning a shareholders’ register entry after a request for delivery from a depot; Norm B is a set of regulatory obligations for providers of high-risk AI systems.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms concern different legal functions, actors, subject matter, and duties: Norm A establishes opposability of a register entry to later depot participants, while Norm B regulates providers’ compliance obligations for high-risk AI systems.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De inschrijving in het aandeelhoudersregister kan worden tegengeworpen aan een ieder
verdict.evidence_span_b: zorgen ervoor dat hun AI-systemen met een hoog risico in overeenstemming zijn met de eisen van afdeling 2

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms impose substantive operational requirements concerning ICT/AI systems, but they do not require the same compliance work: Norm A requires covered financial entities to map key dependencies on ICT third-party providers as part of ICT-risk management, while Norm B prohibits placing on the market, putting into service, or using specified AI systems and practices.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an ICT-risk-management and third-party-dependency mapping obligation for specified financial entities; Norm B is a prohibition on specified AI practices applicable to actors placing on the market, putting into service, or using prohibited AI systems.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms differ in core action, triggering/event structure, and actor role. Norm A requires mapping dependencies on ICT service providers; Norm B prohibits specified AI-system activities. No duplicated reporting, notification, retention, information-provision, or remedial work is imposed.
verdict.evidence_span_a: e) de belangrijkste afhankelijkheden ten aanzien van derde aanbieders van ICT-diensten in kaart brengen;
verdict.evidence_span_b: a) het in de handel brengen, het in gebruik stellen of het gebruiken van een AI-systeem dat subliminale technieken waarvan personen zich niet bewust zijn of doelbewust manipulatieve of misleidende technieken gebruikt

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern making information or documentation available to public-facing recipients, but A requires immediate public disclosure of non-personal domain-registration data, whereas B requires an authorised representative to retain technical documentation and make it available to the AI Office and national authorities for ten years, and provide it on reasoned request.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: The duties differ fundamentally in subject matter, purpose, timing, and operational form: A is immediate public disclosure after domain registration; B is regulatory record-keeping and cooperation concerning AI-model compliance, including retention and request-based provision to authorities.
verdict.criterion_fired: Different event family, actor role, recipient relationship, and substantive content; the apparent similarity is limited to making information available.
verdict.evidence_span_a: maken de domeinnaamregistratiegegevens, die geen persoonsgegevens zijn, onverwijld na de registratie van een domeinnaam openbaar
verdict.evidence_span_b: een kopie van de in bijlage XI gespecificeerde technische documentatie beschikbaar houden voor het AI-bureau en de nationale autoriteiten gedurende een periode van tien jaar

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both require prompt communication concerning an incident: Norm A requires an entity’s early warning to state specified facts about a significant incident, while Norm B requires a processor to inform the controller of a personal-data breach without undue delay.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an early-warning content requirement for a significant incident, including whether it was likely caused by an unlawful or malicious act, whether it may have cross-border effects, and the responsible reporting officer’s contact details. Norm B is a processor-to-controller notification duty upon becoming aware of a personal-data breach.
verdict.criterion_fired: The actor roles and operative duties differ: Norm A concerns an entity’s early warning with prescribed incident information, whereas Norm B concerns a processor informing the controller of a personal-data breach. The shared incident-related context is insufficient to establish duplicated compliance work.
verdict.evidence_span_a: geeft de entiteit aan of het significante incident vermoedelijk door een onrechtmatige of kwaadwillige handeling is veroorzaakt
verdict.evidence_span_b: De verwerker informeert de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke zonder onredelijke vertraging zodra hij kennis heeft genomen van een inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Beide normen vereisen het bijhouden/opstellen en onderhouden van documentatie of registers, maar niet dezelfde concrete compliance-actie: norm A betreft operationele registers tijdens geactiveerde ICT-continuïteits- en herstelplannen; norm B betreft technische AI-documentatie voor conformiteitsbeoordeling.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A ziet op operationele registratie van activiteiten vóór en tijdens ICT-storingen; norm B op technische documentatie van hoog-risico-AI-systemen, opgesteld vóór marktintroductie of ingebruikname en bijgewerkt voor conformiteitsbeoordeling.
verdict.criterion_fired: De normen betreffen verschillende actoren, verschillende triggering contexts en wezenlijk verschillende documentatie-inhoud en doeleinden; een oppervlakkige overeenkomst in het bijhouden of actualiseren van documentatie creëert geen dubbele compliance-last.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Financiële entiteiten houden gemakkelijk toegankelijke registers bij van hun activiteiten vóór en tijdens storingen wanneer hun ICT-bedrijfscontinuïteitsplannen en ICT-respons- en herstelplannen worden geactiveerd.
verdict.evidence_span_b: De technische documentatie van een AI-systeem met een hoog risico wordt opgesteld voordat dit systeem in de handel wordt gebracht of in gebruik wordt gesteld, en wordt geactualiseerd.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms involve making a notification connected with a network/service security-related event or measure, but they require different notifications serving different purposes: A requires supplying the contact details of the person responsible for reporting as part of an early warning about a significant incident; B requires the provider to notify the affected subscriber before, or urgently after, taking a protective suspension or termination measure and to give the subscriber an opportunity to remedy the threat.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A concerns the content of an early-warning incident report, including the responsible reporting officer's contact details; Norm B concerns notice to the affected subscriber of an impending or urgent protective service measure and an opportunity to remove the threat.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties are not meaningfully the same because they are borne by different actor roles and require different communications: an incident early-warning disclosure versus customer notice of a protective service suspension or termination.
verdict.evidence_span_a: verstrekt de entiteit de contactgegevens van de functionaris die verantwoordelijk is voor de melding
verdict.evidence_span_b: doet de aanbieder melding aan de betrokken abonnee, en geeft de abonnee daarbij de gelegenheid de in dit onderdeel bedoelde bedreiging van de integriteit en veiligheid van netwerk, dienst of randapparaat weg te nemen

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern ICT/cyber-risk management in regulated entities, but Norm A requires incident reporting to a CSIRT or competent authority, whereas Norm B requires establishing, maintaining, monitoring, and documenting an internal ICT-risk-management framework and related controls.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an external, time-bound reporting duty triggered by a significant incident; Norm B is an ongoing internal risk-management and control duty, with documentation/evaluation and submission of an evaluation report only on request.
verdict.criterion_fired: Same broad ICT/security-risk context and generally the same regulated-entity role, but the operative actions, purpose, timing, and required content differ substantially: incident notification versus internal ICT-risk governance and controls.
verdict.evidence_span_a: onverwijld en in elk geval binnen 72 uur nadat zij kennis hebben gekregen van het significante incident, een incidentmelding indienen
verdict.evidence_span_b: een degelijk en gedocumenteerd kader voor ICT-risicobeheer tot stand brengen en handhaven

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A requires domain-name registries and registration-service entities to grant legitimate, duly justified access to specific domain-registration data, and to answer access requests within 72 hours. B requires providers of high-risk AI systems, among other things, to retain documentation referred to in Article 18 and logs referred to in Article 19.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: The norms concern different regulated actors, different subject matter, and different actions: disclosure/access to domain-registration data on request versus retention of AI-system documentation and logs.
verdict.criterion_fired: Different actor roles, different event families, and different core actions; A concerns responding to access requests for domain-registration data, while B concerns retaining AI-system documentation/logs.
verdict.evidence_span_a: toegang verlenen tot specifieke met gegevens over de registratie van domeinnamen
verdict.evidence_span_b: bewaren de in artikel 18 bedoelde documentatie

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A requires covered entities to provide registration information to the Dutch Minister for the national register; B requires high-risk AI providers to perform a broad set of product-compliance duties, including corrective measures and provision of information under Article 20, but not the registration-information submission required by A.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a targeted administrative information-submission duty for national-register registration and subsequent updates. Norm B is a comprehensive set of high-risk-AI provider obligations, principally concerning product conformity, documentation, logging, assessment, marking, registration, corrective measures, and demonstrating compliance; it does not impose the same national-register information submission.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms do not impose the same verb-level duty, concern different compliance subject matters and triggering contexts, and do not identify the same actor role or recipient. Any superficial overlap in the word 'registration' or in information provision is insufficient because A concerns information for a national register, whereas B concerns obligations of providers of high-risk AI systems.
verdict.evidence_span_a: verstrekt ten behoeve van de registratie in het nationale register, bedoeld in artikel 43, aan Onze Minister de volgende informatie
verdict.evidence_span_b: zorgen ervoor dat hun AI-systemen met een hoog risico in overeenstemming zijn met de eisen van afdeling 2

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Norm A requires domain-name registries and registration-service entities to establish and publicly disclose policies and procedures for disclosure of domain-registration data. Norm B requires public telecommunications network/service providers and frequency-space users, when the War Act is applied, to provide all cooperation to the military authority, including carrying out its orders.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a standing transparency and policy-publication duty concerning procedures for disclosing domain-name registration data; Norm B is a contingent operational cooperation duty to the military authority, including executing orders during application of the War Act.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in actor role, triggering context, and core action: public disclosure of policies and procedures versus operational cooperation with military authorities and execution of their orders.
verdict.evidence_span_a: stellen het beleid en de procedures met betrekking tot de bekendmaking van de gegevens, bedoeld in het eerste lid, vast en maken dat beleid en die procedures openbaar

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both provisions concern maintaining or communicating compliance-related information, but they do not impose the same underlying compliance action: Norm A requires a controller to keep a record of processing activities, while Norm B requires a notified body to inform other notified bodies about specified decisions and certificates.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an internal record-keeping duty concerning processing activities and personal-data governance; Norm B is an inter-body notification duty concerning refused, suspended, withdrawn, or otherwise limited quality-system approvals and technical-documentation certificates.
verdict.criterion_fired: Different underlying action, event/subject matter, and actor role; the apparent similarity is only that both provisions concern compliance information.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms involve making information or documentation available to a public authority on request, but they do not impose the same underlying compliance action: Norm A requires financial entities to maintain and periodically report an ICT-contract register and provide it for supervision; Norm B requires an authorised representative to retain specified AI technical documentation and provide information/documentation to the AI Office on a reasoned request, while also cooperating with authorities.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A concerns an ICT-service contractual-register and supervisory reporting duty of financial entities; Norm B concerns an authorised representative’s AI-model documentation-retention, information-production, and cooperation duties for general-purpose AI models.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in actor, subject matter, and operative action: Norm A concerns financial entities’ ICT-contract registers and reporting, whereas Norm B concerns authorised representatives of providers of general-purpose AI models, including retention and production of AI technical documentation.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern organizational handling of information related to regulated entities or ICT events, but A requires supplying registry information to the Minister, whereas B requires internal ICT-incident registration and incident-management procedures.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an external information-provision duty for national-register data, including updates within two weeks; Norm B is an internal ICT-incident and cyber-threat recording and management-process duty, with no reporting recipient specified.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in core action, triggering subject matter, and compliance purpose: A concerns providing entity-registration information to a Minister, while B concerns internally registering ICT incidents and establishing procedures for monitoring, treatment, follow-up, and remediation.

Norm A ziet op het meewegen van cyberbeveiligingsrisicobeoordelingen bij het kiezen van maatregelen; norm B ziet op een verbod op het op de markt brengen, in gebruik stellen of gebruiken van bepaalde AI-systemen.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both require an entity to submit incident-related reporting to a public authority, including interim/progress reporting while the incident remains ongoing and a final report after handling or analysis is complete.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a continuation/final-report fallback duty for an incident already subject to reporting by an essential or important entity, whereas Norm B is the DORA duty for financial entities to report serious ICT-related incidents to the relevant competent authority using prescribed notices and reports, with specified substantive information and possible onward reporting.
verdict.criterion_fired: The actor roles are materially different: Norm A applies to essential or important entities under the Dutch NIS2 implementation framework, while Norm B applies to financial entities under DORA. The provisions also concern different reporting regimes and content, so the apparent overlap in incident reporting does not establish the same compliance duty.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern assessing risks or impacts associated with technology, but Norm A requires the entity to perform a specific ICT-risk assessment, whereas Norm B requires high-risk-AI deployers, where applicable, to use supplied information in carrying out a separate data-protection impact assessment.

verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in core action, triggering context, actor role, and assessment subject: an annual/connection-related ICT-risk assessment of legacy systems versus use of AI-provided information for a legally distinct data-protection impact assessment.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Norm A concerns the legal effect/opposability of an entry in a shareholders' register after a request for delivery of a deposited share interest; Norm B requires high-risk AI providers to retain automatically generated logs for at least six months.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an opposability rule concerning a shareholders-register entry in a securities/depositary enforcement context, whereas Norm B is a record-retention obligation imposed on providers of high-risk AI systems.

Norm A makes a register entry opposable to persons who later become participants in a deposit; Norm B requires AI providers to retain automatically generated logs for a specified minimum period.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both concern handling ICT/cyber incidents, but A requires affected entities to report significant incidents externally through warnings, incident reports, updates and final reports, whereas B requires financial entities to maintain internal incident registration and procedures for monitoring, follow-up, root-cause remediation and prevention.

verdict.criterion_fired: The event family overlaps, but the core actions and actor roles differ: A concerns external regulatory reporting by affected entities, while B concerns internal incident-management processes by financial entities.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Beide normen vereisen onverwijlde kennisgeving in verband met een ICT-/beveiligingsincident, maar A vereist melding aan de Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens, terwijl B kennisgeving aan cliënten vereist over het incident en genomen beperkende maatregelen (en bij een cyberdreiging over beschermingsmaatregelen).
verdict.distinguishing_factor: De ontvanger en het doel van de kennisgeving verschillen wezenlijk: toezichthoudende datalekmelding onder A tegenover cliëntgerichte incident- of beschermingsinformatie onder B.
verdict.criterion_fired: Niet dezelfde actorrol: A betreft de aanbieder van een openbare elektronische communicatiedienst en een beveiligingsinbreuk met nadelige gevolgen voor persoonsgegevens; B betreft financiële entiteiten en ernstige ICT-incidenten die financiële belangen van cliënten raken, of significante cyberdreigingen. Bovendien verschillen ontvanger en inhoud/purpose wezenlijk. De overeenkomst in onverwijlde kennisgeving en een brede incidentcontext maakt dit niet tot dezelfde compliance-last.
verdict.evidence_span_a: stelt de Autoriteit persoonsgegevens onverwijld in kennis van een inbreuk op de beveiliging
verdict.evidence_span_b: stellen financiële entiteiten, zodra zij het incident hebben opgemerkt, hun cliënten onverwijld in kennis van het ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incident en van de maatregelen die zijn genomen om de negatieve gevolgen van een dergelijk incident te beperken

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require communicating information about a cyber/data-related threat or incident promptly to affected external recipients. However, Norm A requires a controller to notify the data subject of a personal-data breach, while Norm B requires essential/important entities to inform service recipients about a significant cyber threat and, where necessary, the threat-response measures they can take.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a GDPR personal-data-breach notification to the data subject, triggered by a likely high risk to individuals' rights and freedoms. Norm B is an NIS2 communication to service recipients concerning a significant cyber threat, including potentially recommended protective measures.
verdict.criterion_fired: The actor role and legal purpose differ: Norm A is imposed on a personal-data controller for a high-risk personal-data breach, whereas Norm B is imposed on essential or important entities for significant cyber-threat communications to service recipients. The shared communication form and incident-related context do not make the underlying compliance duty the same.

verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an ongoing documentation/record-keeping duty for controllers or their representatives, whereas Norm B is a pre-market conformity-verification and, in specified cases, notification/non-placement duty for importers of high-risk AI systems.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in actor, event family, and core action: A concerns maintaining a register of processing activities, while B concerns importer checks before placing a high-risk AI system on the market, with additional action if non-compliance or risk is suspected.

verdict.criterion_fired: De normen hebben geen dezelfde actorrol of hetzelfde soort triggering event; de beperkte overlap in het bewaren of beschikbaar houden van technische documentatie is onvoldoende om dezelfde compliance duty of dubbele compliance-burden vast te stellen.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require an entity to provide information to a public authority, but they concern different information and compliance purposes.

verdict.criterion_fired: The norms differ in actor role, event family, and core action: an investigative authority's power to obtain certified copies or extracts versus a notified body's duty to notify peer notified bodies about specified approvals and certificates.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A requires registers and domain-name registration service entities to make non-personal domain-registration data public immediately after registration. B restricts further sharing of personal data created in an AI regulatory sandbox to sharing only in accordance with EU data-protection law and prohibits sharing it outside the sandbox; it also imposes related processing, security, logging, retention, documentation, and publication conditions.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: The norms concern fundamentally different regulated activities and data: public disclosure of non-personal domain-registration data versus controlled processing and non-disclosure of personal data in an AI testing environment.
verdict.criterion_fired: Different core action, event family, and actor role; A is an immediate public-disclosure duty triggered by domain registration, while B is a data-processing and sharing restriction in an AI regulatory sandbox.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern making information available to another party, but they do not impose the same underlying compliance action: Norm A requires the controller or processor to substantiate an assessment and safeguards in the Article 30 record, whereas Norm B requires domain-name registries and registration-service entities to grant access to specified domain-registration data, respond within 72 hours, and publish access policies and procedures.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a documentation/record-keeping duty concerning safeguards for a specific international data transfer; Norm B is an access-and-response duty concerning domain-name registration data, plus publication of related policies and procedures.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in actor, triggering context, and substantive action: Norm A concerns documenting an assessment and safeguards for a GDPR Article 49 transfer, while Norm B concerns granting access to domain-registration data in response to a legitimate request and responding within 72 hours.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A requires the controller to notify the competent supervisory authority of a personal-data breach within (if possible) 72 hours of becoming aware of it. verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both concern communicating cybersecurity-related information in a broad sense, but Norm A imposes a provider's duty to notify the affected subscriber about a specific measure or, where urgent, to notify the measure as soon as possible. Norm B requires Member States to enable covered entities and, where applicable, other entities to exchange relevant cybersecurity information voluntarily for cybersecurity purposes. The underlying compliance work and legal purpose are materially different.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a mandatory, event-specific notification by a provider to the affected subscriber concerning a measure addressing a threat to network, service, or terminal-device integrity and security. Norm B is a Member-State-facilitated voluntary information-sharing framework among entities, covering broad categories of cybersecurity information and purposes.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms do not impose the same actor-level duty: Norm A requires a provider to notify an affected subscriber about a specific measure, whereas Norm B requires Member States to ensure that entities can voluntarily exchange broad cybersecurity information. The different actor role, voluntary framework, recipient relationship, and low content overlap mean this is not duplicated compliance work.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Norm A requires an entity to promptly inform potentially affected service recipients about measures they can take in response to a significant cyber threat and, where necessary, inform them of the threat itself. verdict.criterion_fired: The core action and compliance purpose differ: informing potentially affected service recipients about a cyber threat and protective measures is not the same work as conducting a post-incident evaluation and identifying or reporting implemented improvements to competent authorities.

verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A betreft documentatie van een specifieke internationale doorgifte van persoonsgegevens en de daarvoor gemaakte beoordeling/waarborgen; norm B betreft voorafgaande en doorlopende technische conformiteitsdocumentatie voor een hoog-risico-AI-systeem.
verdict.criterion_fired: De normen hebben niet dezelfde actorrol of gebeurtenisfamilie en vereisen inhoudelijk verschillende documentatie voor verschillende compliance-doeleinden; een oppervlakkige overeenkomst in het vastleggen/staven van informatie is onvoldoende voor duplicate burden.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De verwerkingsverantwoordelijke of de verwerker staaft de beoordeling en de in lid 1, tweede alinea, van dit artikel bedoelde passende waarborgen in het artikel 30 bedoelde register.
verdict.evidence_span_b: De technische documentatie van een AI-systeem met een hoog risico wordt opgesteld voordat dit systeem in de handel wordt gebracht of in gebruik wordt gesteld, en wordt geactualiseerd.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Geen gedeelde compliance-actie: norm A verplicht de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke de toezichthoudende autoriteit over een specifieke internationale doorgifte van persoonsgegevens te informeren; norm B verplicht de importeur vóór het in de handel brengen van een hoog-risico-AI-systeem conformiteitsaspecten te controleren. De latere kennisgevingsplicht in art. 23, lid 2, betreft bovendien een andere, voorwaardelijke situatie.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A betreft een kennisgeving aan een toezichthoudende autoriteit over een niet-anderszins gerechtvaardigde doorgifte van persoonsgegevens; norm B betreft voorafgaande conformiteitscontrole door een importeur, met slechts bij een afzonderlijk risico een kennisgeving aan markttoezichtautoriteiten.
verdict.criterion_fired: Verschillende kernactie, actorrol en gebeurtenisfamilie; A ziet op een uitzonderlijke internationale gegevensdoorgifte en melding aan een privacytoezichthouder, B op importeurscontrole van een hoog-risico-AI-systeem vóór marktintroductie.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De verwerkingsverantwoordelijke informeert de toezichthoudende autoriteit over de doorgifte.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Alvorens een AI-systeem met een hoog risico in de handel wordt gebracht, zorgen de importeurs ervoor dat het systeem in overeenstemming is met deze verordening door na te gaan of:

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A requires an aanbieder to notify the affected subscriber about a measure (or, if prior notice is impossible due to urgency, notify the subscriber as soon as possible afterward). B requires financial entities to conduct post-incident ICT evaluations and, on request, communicate implemented changes to competent authorities. These are not the same underlying compliance action.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: A is a subscriber-facing notice concerning a network, service, or terminal-device integrity/security measure; B is an internal post-incident evaluation and, for non-micro financial entities, an authority-facing disclosure of resulting changes.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in actor role, triggering event, core action, recipient, and substantive content; the superficial similarity of a security-related context and notification/information language does not establish duplicated compliance work.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Voorafgaand aan het nemen van een maatregel, bedoeld in het eerste lid, onderdeel g, doet de aanbieder melding aan de betrokken abonnee
verdict.evidence_span_b: Financiële entiteiten verrichten ICT-gerelateerde post-incidentevaluaties na verstoringen van hun kernactiviteiten ten gevolge van een ernstig ICT-gerelateerd incident

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern maintaining or supplying compliance-related information/documentation, but they impose different duties: Norm A requires an importer-like processor to maintain an internal register of processing activities, while Norm B requires AI-system importers to provide necessary conformity information and documentation to competent authorities on a reasoned request and to make technical documentation available.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an ongoing record-keeping duty concerning processing activities carried out for controllers; Norm B is a request-triggered disclosure and availability duty concerning conformity of a high-risk AI system, supplemented by a ten-year retention obligation for specified documents.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in actor role, triggering context, and substantive content: a processor's register of processing activities versus an AI importer’s provision of conformity information/documentation to competent authorities.
verdict.evidence_span_a: houdt een register van alle categorieën van verwerkingsactiviteiten die zij ten behoeve van een verwerkingsverantwoordelijke hebben verricht
verdict.evidence_span_b: verstrekken ter staving van de conformiteit van een AI-systeem met een hoog risico met de eisen van afdeling 2, de relevante bevoegde autoriteiten op met redenen omkleed verzoek alle nodige informatie en documentatie

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A requires registers and domain-name registration service providers to answer access requests for domain-registration data within 72 hours. B requires providers of high-risk AI systems to prepare and update technical documentation demonstrating conformity and enabling assessment by authorities and notified bodies.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: The norms concern different underlying duties and event families: A is a responsive disclosure/access-request obligation concerning domain-registration data, while B is an ongoing ex ante and update obligation to maintain AI-system technical documentation.
verdict.criterion_fired: Different core action, triggering context, and regulated actor: responding to a domain-registration data access request is not the same compliance work as preparing or updating high-risk AI technical documentation.
verdict.evidence_span_a: verzoeken om toegang onverwijld en in elk geval binnen 72 uur na ontvangst van het verzoek beantwoorden
verdict.evidence_span_b: De technische documentatie van een AI-systeem met een hoog risico wordt opgesteld voordat dit systeem in de handel wordt gebracht of in gebruik wordt gesteld, en wordt geactualiseerd.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: There is no shared compliance action: Norm A requires domain-name registration entities/registers to publish non-personal registration data promptly after registration, whereas Norm B empowers the lead overseer to request telephone and data-traffic records during a general investigation.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a proactive publication duty triggered by domain-name registration; Norm B is an investigative information-gathering power exercised by a supervisory authority, including requests for traffic records.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms differ in actor, operative action, purpose, and triggering event: publication after domain registration versus an overseer's investigative request for telephone/data-traffic overviews.
verdict.evidence_span_a: onverwijld na de registratie van een domeinnaam, de domeinnaamregistratiegegevens die geen persoonsgegevens zijn, openbaar maken
verdict.evidence_span_b: overzichten van telefoon- en dataverkeer op te vragen

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern compliance-related handling of information or data, but they do not impose the same underlying action: A requires an authorised representative to provide conformity information and documentation to the Minister on request, while B permits and regulates exceptional processing of special-category personal data by providers of high-risk AI systems to detect and correct bias.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an on-request information/documentation disclosure duty to a minister concerning product conformity; Norm B is a substantive data-processing permission subject to necessity, security, access-control, non-disclosure, deletion, and record-keeping conditions for bias detection and correction.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms differ in the core action, triggering/compliance context, and actor role; A requires supplying conformity evidence to a minister, whereas B governs exceptional processing of sensitive personal data for AI-bias correction.
verdict.evidence_span_a: b) het op verzoek van Onze Minister verstrekken van alle benodigde informatie en documentatie om de conformiteit van de apparaten of radioapparaten aan te tonen;
verdict.evidence_span_b: mogen de aanbieders van dergelijke systemen uitzonderlijk bijzondere categorieën persoonsgegevens verwerken, mits passende waarborgen worden geboden voor de grondrechten en fundamentele vrijheden van natuurlijke personen.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: NORM A requires registers and domain-registration service entities to collect and maintain accurate, complete domain-registration data in a database. NORM B requires importers, before placing a high-risk AI system on the market, to verify specified conformity conditions and, where applicable, withhold placement and notify relevant parties and market-surveillance authorities.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: The norms concern different regulated activities and event families: maintaining domain-registration data for DNS security versus importer conformity checks for high-risk AI systems before market placement.
verdict.criterion_fired: Different underlying action, triggering context, and actor role; the apparent similarity does not establish overlapping compliance work.
verdict.evidence_span_a: de registers voor topleveldomeinnamen en de entiteiten die domeinnaamregistratiediensten verlenen, met de nodige zorgvuldigheid nauwkeurige en volledige domeinnaamregistratiegegevens verzamelen en bijhouden in een speciale database
verdict.evidence_span_b: Alvorens een AI-systeem met een hoog risico in de handel wordt gebracht, zorgen de importeurs ervoor dat het systeem in overeenstemming is met deze verordening door na te gaan of:

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern making information or documentation available to authorities in the context of regulatory oversight, but Norm A primarily specifies that an investigation authorisation must mention possible coercive fines if requested records, data, procedures, materials, or answers are not fully provided; Norm B requires importers to provide requested information and documentation substantiating conformity and ensure technical documentation is available to competent authorities.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A concerns the contents of an investigation authorisation and the consequences of non-cooperation by third-party ICT-service providers, whereas Norm B imposes a substantive information/documentation-access duty on importers of high-risk AI systems.
verdict.criterion_fired: The actor role and operative duty differ: Norm A concerns investigators' authorisation and possible coercive fines relating to third-party ICT-service providers' responses, while Norm B directly obliges importers to provide conformity information and documentation to competent authorities.
verdict.evidence_span_a: In deze machtiging worden eveneens de in artikel 35, lid 6, bedoelde dwangsommen genoemd
verdict.evidence_span_b: Importeurs verstrekken ter staving van de conformiteit van een AI-systeem met een hoog risico met de eisen van afdeling 2, de relevante bevoegde autoriteiten op met redenen omkleed verzoek alle nodige informatie en documentatie

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both provisions concern cooperation with an authority in connection with official powers, but A requires regulated telecommunications actors and frequency users to comply with military-authority orders, whereas B empowers the lead overseer to conduct investigations and request or obtain records, explanations, testimony, and traffic overviews.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A imposes a broad mandatory cooperation-and-order-compliance duty in the context of Article 31 of the Dutch War Act; Norm B grants an investigative authority powers over critical third-party ICT-service providers and other persons, including requesting traffic overviews. They do not require the same compliance work.
verdict.criterion_fired: Different actor roles and different operative duties: A is a mandatory military-authority cooperation/order-execution obligation triggered by application of the War Act; B is an investigative power of the lead overseer to inspect, copy, summon, hear, and request traffic data.
verdict.evidence_span_a: verplicht het militair gezag alle medewerking te verlenen, daaronder begrepen het uitvoeren van door dat gezag gegeven opdrachten
verdict.evidence_span_b: e) overzichten van telefoon- en dataverkeer op te vragen

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Beide normen vereisen het opstellen en openbaar maken/beschikbaar stellen van informatie of procedures, maar zij leggen niet dezelfde concrete compliance-actie op: norm A vereist openbaarmaking van beleid en procedures voor toegang tot domeinnaamregistratiegegevens; norm B vereist AI-modeldocumentatie en informatie voor integrerende AI-systeemaanbieders, plus andere AI-verplichtingen.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: De normen betreffen verschillende gereguleerde onderwerpen en verschillende informatieplichten: domeinnaamregistratiegegevens versus technische en gebruiksdocumentatie voor algemene AI-modellen.
verdict.criterion_fired: De verplichtingen zien op verschillende onderwerpen, actoren en ontvangers; een oppervlakkige overeenkomst in openbaarmaking/beschikbaarstelling maakt de compliance-werkzaamheden niet hetzelfde.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De registers voor topleveldomeinnamen en de entiteiten die domeinnaamregistratiediensten verlenen stellen het beleid en de procedures met betrekking tot de bekendmaking van de gegevens, bedoeld in het eerste lid, vast en maken dat beleid en die procedures openbaar.
verdict.evidence_span_b: informatie en documentatie opstellen, up-to-date houden en beschikbaar stellen voor aanbieders van AI-systemen die het AI-model voor algemene doeleinden in hun AI-systemen willen integreren

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms involve responding to or deciding on a request within a specified period, but they impose different underlying actions: Norm A requires domain-name registries and registration-service entities to answer access requests; Norm B concerns a decision by the Joint Committee on whether to designate an ICT third-party provider as critical after that provider submits a reasoned request.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an access-request response duty imposed on domain-name registries and registration-service entities, with access to specific domain-registration data; Norm B is a designation decision concerning critical ICT third-party providers, made by the Joint Committee following an application.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties involve different actors, different triggering events, different purposes, and different substantive actions: answering a data-access request versus deciding whether to designate an ICT provider as critical.
verdict.evidence_span_a: verzoeken om toegang onverwijld en in elk geval binnen 72 uur na ontvangst van het verzoek beantwoorden
verdict.evidence_span_b: Het in de tweede alinea bedoelde besluit wordt binnen zes maanden na ontvangst van het verzoek vastgesteld en ter kennis gebracht van de derde aanbieder van ICT-diensten.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern regulated digital-sector compliance, but Norm A requires domain-registration entities to collect and maintain accurate, complete registration data, whereas Norm B concerns investigative powers exercised by the lead overseer and the possible provision of records, data, procedures, materials, or answers during an investigation.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A imposes an ongoing data-collection and database-maintenance duty on domain-name registries and registration-service providers; Norm B governs supervisory investigations and the exercise of investigative powers concerning third-party ICT-service providers, including possible requests for information or materials.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in core action, triggering context, and actor role: Norm A is an ongoing domain-registration-data collection and maintenance obligation, while Norm B concerns supervisory investigation powers and potential investigative requests to third-party ICT-service providers.
verdict.evidence_span_a: de registers voor topleveldomeinnamen en de entiteiten die domeinnaamregistratiediensten verlenen, met de nodige zorgvuldigheid nauwkeurige en volledige domeinnaamregistratiegegevens verzamelen en bijhouden in een speciale database
verdict.evidence_span_b: De functionarissen van de lead overseer en andere door hem voor de uitvoering van de in lid 1 bedoelde onderzoeken gemachtigde personen oefenen hun bevoegdheden uit na overlegging van een schriftelijke machtiging

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require an entity to provide information to a public authority, but the information, purpose, and triggering conditions differ: A requires a telecommunications party, on ministerial request, to provide a register extract concerning a share right or investigate a controller's identity and third-party ties; B requires covered entities to provide identification, contact, sector/subsector, and service-territory information for an official cybersecurity-entity list, and to report changes immediately and within two weeks.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an on-request disclosure or investigation concerning suspected or potential overriding control threatening the public interest; Norm B is a standing cybersecurity-register information and change-notification duty concerning the entity's identity, contacts, sectors, and Member States of service.
verdict.criterion_fired: The apparent similarity is limited to providing information to an authority. The triggering event, regulated actor scope, information requested, and regulatory purpose are materially different; therefore the duties are not the same compliance work repeated.
verdict.evidence_span_a: verstrekt een telecommunicatiepartij aan Onze Minister op verzoek om niet een uittreksel uit het door de rechtspersoon gehouden register met betrekking tot een recht op een aandeel
verdict.evidence_span_b: De in lid 3 bedoelde entiteiten melden onmiddellijk elke wijziging in de bijzonderheden die zij op grond van de eerste alinea van dit lid hebben ingediend, en in elk geval binnen twee weken na de datum van de wijziging.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A: submit a final incident report to the entity’s CSIRT and competent authority, containing specified incident details, causes/threats, mitigation measures, and possible cross-border effects, within one month after the initial notification. B: continuously identify ICT-risk sources and regularly assess cyber threats, ICT vulnerabilities, and risk scenarios, at least annually.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a post-incident reporting duty for essential or important entities; Norm B is an ongoing ICT-risk identification and assessment duty for financial entities, not a reporting obligation.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms impose different underlying actions and concern different compliance contexts: incident reporting to authorities/CSIRT versus ongoing internal ICT-risk identification and assessment.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit dient uiterlijk één maand na de melding, bedoeld in artikel 27, eerste lid, een eindverslag in bij haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit waarin het volgende is opgenomen:
verdict.evidence_span_b: Financiële entiteiten identificeren permanent alle bronnen van ICT-risico, met name de wederzijdse risicoblootstelling ten aanzien van andere financiële entiteiten, en beoordelen de cyberdreigingen en ICT-kwetsbaarheden

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Beide normen leggen een informatie-/documentatiegerelateerde verplichting op, maar Norm A vereist het openbaar maken van beleid en procedures voor domeinnaamregistratiedatabases, terwijl Norm B aanbieders van algemene AI-modellen verplicht technische documentatie, informatie voor AI-systeemaanbieders, auteursrechtenbeleid en een trainingscontentsamenvatting op te stellen, bij te houden, beschikbaar te stellen of openbaar te maken.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: De normen betreffen verschillende gereguleerde objecten en inhoud: domeinnaamregistratiegegevens en verificatieprocedures versus documentatie en informatie over algemene AI-modellen, inclusief trainings- en testprocessen, auteursrechten en trainingscontent.
verdict.criterion_fired: De onderliggende plicht, het gereguleerde object, de actorrol en de vereiste inhoud verschillen wezenlijk; er is geen identieke rapportage- of openbaarmakingswerkzaamheid die tweemaal moet worden verricht.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Zij maken dat beleid en die procedures openbaar.
verdict.evidence_span_b: informatie en documentatie opstellen, up-to-date houden en beschikbaar stellen voor aanbieders van AI-systemen die het AI-model voor algemene doeleinden in hun AI-systemen willen integreren.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A requires significant-incident notification/reporting (including, where applicable, notifying service recipients); B requires financial entities to monitor user activity and detect ICT anomalies and ICT-related incidents. They do not require the same operational action.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an urgent external incident-notification/reporting duty triggered by a significant incident; Norm B is an ongoing internal detection and monitoring measure, with no recipient or reporting deadline specified.
verdict.criterion_fired: Different core action and different actor role: A concerns essential/important entities reporting significant incidents, while B concerns financial entities deploying resources and capabilities for ongoing monitoring and detection.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Elke lidstaat zorgt ervoor dat essentiële en belangrijke entiteiten elk incident dat aanzienlijke gevolgen heeft voor de verlening van hun diensten als bedoeld in lid 3 (significant incident) onverwijld meldt bij zijn CSIRT of, indien van toepassing, zijn bevoegde autoriteit overeenkomstig lid 4.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Financiële entiteiten zetten voldoende middelen en capaciteiten in om toezicht te houden op activiteiten van gebruikers en het optreden van ICT-anomalieën en ICT-gerelateerde incidenten, met name cyberaanvallen.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern supplying information or reporting-related material to support regulatory oversight or incident handling, but they do not impose the same concrete compliance action.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires an essential or important entity to proactively send an early warning about a significant incident to its CSIRT and competent authority within 24 hours. Norm B concerns the lead overseer’s power to request reports from critical ICT third-party providers about actions or corrective measures taken in response to recommendations; it is an oversight request, not an incident-warning duty, and no deadline is specified for the requested report itself.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in actor, triggering context, and substantive purpose: A is a mandatory early-warning notification of a significant incident, while B is an oversight authority’s power to request post-oversight corrective-action reports from critical ICT third-party providers.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit geeft ten behoeve van de melding, bedoeld in artikel 27, eerste lid, een vroegtijdige waarschuwing over het significante incident aan haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit.
verdict.evidence_span_b: na afloop van de oversightactiviteiten te verzoeken om verslagen met vermelding van de ondernomen acties of de corrigerende maatregelen die door de kritieke derde aanbieders van ICT-diensten zijn genomen

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A requires registers and domain-name registration service entities to make non-personal domain-name registration data public immediately after domain registration. B requires providers of high-risk AI systems to prepare and update technical documentation demonstrating conformity and enabling assessment by competent authorities and notified bodies.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: The norms concern fundamentally different compliance actions and event families: publication of domain-registration data after a domain is registered versus preparation and updating of high-risk AI technical documentation before market placement or use.
verdict.criterion_fired: Different core action, triggering event, and regulated actor; the apparent similarity is not a duplicated or merely related reporting/documentation burden.
verdict.evidence_span_a: maken de domeinnaamregistratiegegevens, die geen persoonsgegevens zijn, onverwijld na de registratie van een domeinnaam openbaar
verdict.evidence_span_b: De technische documentatie van een AI-systeem met een hoog risico wordt opgesteld voordat dit systeem in de handel wordt gebracht of in gebruik wordt gesteld, en wordt geactualiseerd.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A: de lead overseer mag personen horen om informatie over een onderzoek te verzamelen. B: aanbieders van AI-modellen voor algemene doeleinden moeten technische documentatie opstellen, bijhouden en op verzoek verstrekken aan het AI-bureau en nationale bevoegde autoriteiten.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A betreft een toezichthoudende onderzoeksbevoegdheid om personen mondeling of schriftelijk te horen; norm B betreft een doorlopende documentatie- en beschikbaarstellingsplicht van AI-modelaanbieders, met specifieke technische modelinformatie.
verdict.criterion_fired: De normen verschillen zowel in actor/rol als in kernhandeling en event/context: een toezichthouder die personen hoort in een onderzoek versus een AI-modelaanbieder die technische documentatie opstelt en aan autoriteiten beschikbaar stelt.
verdict.evidence_span_a: alle andere dan onder punt c) genoemde natuurlijke personen of rechtspersonen te horen, voor zover die daarin toestemmen, om informatie over het onderwerp van een onderzoek te verzamelen
verdict.evidence_span_b: de technische documentatie van het model opstellen en up-to-date houden, inclusief het trainings- en testproces en de resultaten van de evaluatie ervan, die ten minste de in bijlage XI vermelde informatie moet bevatten, zodat deze op verzoek aan het AI-bureau en de nationale bevoegde autoriteiten kunnen worden verstrekt

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern responding to cyber/ICT-related incidents or threats, but A requires urgent communication to service recipients about protective measures, whereas B requires financial entities to establish and implement an internal ICT-incident management process for detection, management, and reporting.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an external, recipient-facing information duty triggered by a significant cyber threat; Norm B is an internal governance and process-implementation duty covering detection, management, and reporting of ICT-related incidents.
verdict.criterion_fired: The underlying actions and actor roles differ: A requires an essential or important entity to promptly inform its service recipients about measures in response to a significant cyber threat, while B requires financial entities to create, adopt, and implement an internal process for detecting, managing, and reporting ICT-related incidents. The shared incident/cyber-threat context is insufficient to establish duplicated compliance work.
verdict.evidence_span_a: deelt de ontvangers van haar diensten, die mogelijkerwijs door een significante cyberdreiging in relatie tot het ontvangen van die diensten worden getroffen, onverwijld mee welke maatregelen die ontvangers kunnen nemen in reactie op die dreiging
verdict.evidence_span_b: om ICT-gerelateerde incidenten te detecteren, te beheren en te melden

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A requires municipal authorities to decide on consent for planned cable works after a written notification; B requires financial entities to establish and implement an ICT-incident management process for detecting, managing, and reporting incidents.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: The norms concern different actors, different event families, and different underlying actions: an administrative consent decision versus an internal ICT-incident management process.
verdict.criterion_fired: Different actor roles and different event families; the apparent similarity does not establish the same compliance obligation.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Burgemeester en wethouders nemen het instemmingsbesluit binnen acht weken na ontvangst van de schriftelijke melding
verdict.evidence_span_b: Financiële entiteiten omschrijven een beheerproces voor ICT-gerelateerde incidenten, stellen dit vast en leggen dit ten uitvoer, om ICT-gerelateerde incidenten te detecteren, te beheren en te melden.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Beide normen vereisen het opstellen en actueel houden van gedocumenteerde informatie, maar norm A betreft een register van contractuele ICT-dienstverlening en norm B technische/model- en trainingsdocumentatie voor AI-modellen, met verschillende verdere doeleinden en ontvangers.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: De inhoud en het doel van de documentatie verschillen wezenlijk: norm A ziet op een informatieregister over contracten met ICT-dienstverleners en toezicht door bevoegde autoriteiten; norm B ziet op technische documentatie, modelcapaciteiten, auteursrechtenbeleid en een openbare trainingscontentsamenvatting, ten behoeve van AI-systeemaanbieders en autoriteiten.
verdict.criterion_fired: Niet dezelfde wezenlijke complianceplicht: de actorcategorieën, het onderwerp van de documentatie, de doeleinden en de primaire ontvangers verschillen; een gedeelde documentatiehandeling is daarvoor onvoldoende.
verdict.evidence_span_a: handhaven en actualiseren financiële entiteiten op het niveau van de entiteit en op gesubconsolideerd en geconsolideerd niveau een informatieregister
verdict.evidence_span_b: informatie en documentatie opstellen, up-to-date houden en beschikbaar stellen voor aanbieders van AI-systemen die het AI-model voor algemene doeleinden in hun AI-systemen willen integreren

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require the addressee to provide information in response to an information-related trigger, but they do not require the same underlying compliance work: Norm A requires answering a lawful, duly justified access request for specific domain-registration data, whereas Norm B requires notifying the notifying authority about specified conformity-assessment and accreditation-related matters.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A concerns granting access to specific domain-registration data to a legitimate requesting party; Norm B concerns notifying the notifying authority about the notified body's certification, accreditation, and conformity-assessment circumstances and activities.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in actor role, triggering event, recipient, and substantive content. Norm A is an access-request response duty for domain-registration data; Norm B is an ongoing notification duty of notified bodies to the notifying authority concerning conformity-assessment matters.
