verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms involve providing information to a competent/designating authority, but they require different information for different regulatory purposes: financial entities provide an estimate of aggregated annual costs and losses from serious ICT-related incidents, while notified bodies inform the notifying authority about certification, designation-scope, and conformity-assessment matters.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A concerns quantified annual costs and losses caused by serious ICT incidents and is supplied on request by certain financial entities; Norm B concerns the status and scope of a notified body's designation and its conformity-assessment activities.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in actor role, subject matter, and regulatory event: financial-entity ICT-incident loss estimation versus notified-body designation and conformity-assessment information.
verdict.evidence_span_a: verstrekken de bevoegde autoriteiten op hun verzoek een raming van de geaggregeerde jaarlijkse kosten en verliezen als gevolg van ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incidenten
verdict.evidence_span_b: omstandigheden die van invloed zijn op het toepassingsgebied van of de voorwaarden voor de aanmelding

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require the regulated entity to establish or apply internal controls/processes, but they concern materially different compliance duties: ICT-incident management versus safeguards for processing personal data in an AI regulatory sandbox.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A concerns registering and managing ICT-related incidents and cyber threats; Norm B concerns lawful, secure, monitored, documented, and time-limited processing of personal data for AI-system development, including deletion after participation or the retention period ends.
verdict.criterion_fired: Different underlying duty, event/purpose, and compliance content; the apparent similarity does not establish duplicated reporting or other repeated compliance work.
verdict.evidence_span_a: stellen passende procedures en processen vast
verdict.evidence_span_b: worden gewist nadat de deelname aan de testomgeving is beëindigd of de periode van bewaring van de persoonsgegevens ten einde is gekomen

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Norm A requires an essential or important entity to submit an interim progress report when an incident is still ongoing at the final-report deadline, followed by a final report within one month after resolution. Norm B requires a cable provider to give advance notice of maintenance work on public land to the municipal mayor (or authorized official); if notice is given to the authorized official, that official must promptly inform the mayor.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: The norms concern different triggering events, actors, actions, recipients, and compliance purposes: an incident-progress/final reporting duty versus advance notification of cable-maintenance works on public land.
verdict.criterion_fired: Different event family and different actor role; the duties are not the same compliance work, and the recipient/channel distinction is not the decisive reason.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Indien het incident nog voortduurt op het moment dat het eindverslag had moeten worden ingediend, dient de essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit op dat moment in plaats van een eindverslag een voortgangsverslag in
verdict.evidence_span_b: Ingeval de werkzaamheden in verband met de instandhouding van kabels worden verricht in of op openbare gronden, wordt hiervan door de aanbieder tevens voorafgaand aan de uit te voeren werkzaamheden melding gedaan bij de burgemeester

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Beide normen raken aan incidentrapportage, maar norm A legt een meldplicht op voor significante incidenten, terwijl norm B in het aangehaalde fragment alleen bepaalt dat de financiële entiteit verantwoordelijk blijft voor naleving wanneer rapportage wordt uitbesteed.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm B bevat geen zelfstandige meldplicht of concrete rapportage-inhoud; zij regelt verantwoordelijkheid bij uitbesteding. Norm A bevat de daadwerkelijke verplichting om significante incidenten onverwijld te melden en informatie over mogelijke grensoverschrijdende gevolgen te rapporteren.
verdict.criterion_fired: De normen hebben wel een verwante incidentrapportagecontext, maar norm B is een verantwoordelijkheid-/uitbestedingsregel en geen parallelle meldplicht. Bovendien verschillen de actorrollen: essentiële en belangrijke entiteiten onder norm A tegenover financiële entiteiten onder norm B.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Elke lidstaat zorgt ervoor dat essentiële en belangrijke entiteiten elk incident dat aanzienlijke gevolgen heeft voor de verlening van hun diensten als bedoeld in lid 3 (significant incident) onverwijld meldt bij zijn CSIRT of, indien van toepassing, zijn bevoegde autoriteit overeenkomstig lid 4.
verdict.evidence_span_b: In het geval van een dergelijke uitbesteding blijft de financiële entiteit volledig verantwoordelijk voor het naleven van de vereisten inzake incidentrapportage.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Geen gedeelde concrete compliance-actie: norm A vereist dat entiteiten ontvangers onverwijld informeren over een significante cyberdreiging en zo nodig over maatregelen; norm B vereist permanente identificatie en periodieke beoordeling van ICT-risico’s, cyberdreigingen en kwetsbaarheden.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is een externe mededelingsplicht aan mogelijk getroffen dienstontvangers naar aanleiding van een significante cyberdreiging. Norm B is een interne, doorlopende risicobeheer- en beoordelingsplicht voor financiële entiteiten, zonder aangewezen ontvanger.
verdict.criterion_fired: De normen verschillen zowel in actorrol als in kernactie: A betreft waarschuwing/informatie aan dienstontvangers; B betreft interne identificatie en beoordeling van ICT-risico’s en dreigingen. De gedeelde verwijzing naar cyberdreigingen maakt ze slechts thematisch verwant en creëert geen dubbele compliance-last.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Indien nodig stellen de entiteiten die ontvangers ook in kennis van de significante cyberdreiging zelf.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Financiële entiteiten identificeren permanent alle bronnen van ICT-risico, met name de wederzijdse risicoblootstelling ten aanzien van andere financiële entiteiten, en beoordelen de cyberdreigingen en ICT-kwetsbaarheden

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A requires affected entities to submit a sequence of reports about a significant incident, including a final report after handling the incident. B requires financial entities to establish and implement an ICT-incident management process for detecting, managing, and reporting ICT-related incidents.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: A is an incident-specific reporting duty to the CSIRT or competent authority, with prescribed report contents and deadlines. B is an organisational/process-management duty covering detection, management, and reporting generally, without requiring submission of a particular report to an authority.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties do not impose the same core action: A requires submission of specified incident reports to an authority, whereas B requires financial entities to establish and implement an internal ICT-incident management process. The shared incident subject matter is insufficient because the actor scope and operative obligations differ.

verdict.evidence_span_b: om ICT-gerelateerde incidenten te detecteren, te beheren en te melden

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Geen gedeelde compliance-actie: norm A verplicht registers en domeinnaamregistratiedienstverleners om niet-persoonsgebonden domeinnaamregistratiegegevens openbaar te maken; norm B stelt cumulatieve voorwaarden aan de verdere verwerking van persoonsgegevens voor het ontwikkelen, trainen en testen van bepaalde AI-systemen in een AI-testomgeving.

verdict.evidence_span_b: rechtmatig voor andere doeleinden verzamelde persoonsgegevens uitsluitend worden verwerkt ten behoeve van het ontwikkelen, trainen en testen van bepaalde AI-systemen in de testomgeving indien aan alle volgende voorwaarden is voldaan

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Geen gedeelde compliance-actie: norm A bepaalt uitsluitend welke lidstaat jurisdictie heeft over bepaalde entiteiten; norm B verplicht financiële entiteiten tot registratie van ICT-incidenten en significante cyberdreigingen en tot procedures voor monitoring, behandeling, follow-up en oorzaakanalyse/-herstel.

verdict.evidence_span_b: Financiële entiteiten registreren alle ICT-gerelateerde incidenten en significante cyberdreigingen.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Beide normen verplichten een entiteit informatie aan een bevoegde/aanmeldende autoriteit te verstrekken, maar de informatie en het doel van de melding verschillen wezenlijk.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A betreft registratie- en identificatiegegevens van essentiële en belangrijke entiteiten, inclusief wijzigingen daarin. Norm B betreft informatie over door aangemelde instanties verrichte conformiteitsbeoordelings- en andere activiteiten, alsmede specifieke certificerings- en toezichtgebeurtenissen.
verdict.criterion_fired: De actorrol en het voorwerp van de informatieplicht verschillen: Norm A ziet op entiteiten die onder de NIS2-richtlijn vallen en hun identificatie-/registratiegegevens; Norm B ziet op aangemelde instanties en hun conformiteitsbeoordelingsactiviteiten. De gedeelde handeling van informatie verstrekken aan een autoriteit is te algemeen om een dubbele compliance-last te vormen.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De in lid 3 bedoelde entiteiten melden onmiddellijk elke wijziging in de bijzonderheden die zij op grond van de eerste alinea van dit lid hebben ingediend, en in elk geval binnen twee weken na de datum van de wijziging.
verdict.evidence_span_b: op verzoek, de binnen het toepassingsgebied van hun aanmelding verrichte conformiteitsbeoordelingsactiviteiten en andere activiteiten, waaronder grensoverschrijdende activiteiten en onderaanneming.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Geen gedeelde concrete compliance-actie: norm A verleent de lead overseer onderzoeksbevoegdheden, terwijl norm B aanbieders van hoog-risico-AI meerdere product-, documentatie-, kwaliteits- en conformiteitsverplichtingen oplegt.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is een bevoegdheidsgrondslag voor toezichtsonderzoek door de lead overseer; norm B is een set doorlopende verplichtingen voor aanbieders van hoog-risico-AI, waaronder kwaliteitsbeheer, documentatie, logs en conformiteitsbeoordeling.
verdict.criterion_fired: De normen hebben niet dezelfde actorrol of kernhandeling: A betreft onderzoeksbevoegdheden van een toezichthouder, B verplicht aanbieders tot kwaliteitsbeheer en andere AI-conformiteitsmaatregelen.
verdict.evidence_span_a: registers, data, procedures en alle overig voor de uitvoering van zijn taken relevant materiaal te onderzoeken
verdict.evidence_span_b: beschikken over een systeem voor kwaliteitsbeheer dat in overeenstemming is met artikel 17

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms impose an information-recordkeeping obligation: A requires financial entities to maintain and update a register of ICT-service contracts, while B requires high-risk AI providers to retain automatically generated logs.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: The records, regulated activities, and compliance purposes differ: A concerns contractual ICT-service documentation and supervisory reporting/access; B concerns system-generated AI logs retained for at least six months.
verdict.criterion_fired: The underlying duties concern different record types and different regulated activities, are imposed on different actor roles, and are not triggered by the same event; superficial similarity in retaining information does not establish duplicate compliance work.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both impose ongoing/pre-market compliance-control obligations, but not the same verb-level action: A requires maintaining a processing-activity register, while B requires an importer to verify and ensure conformity of a high-risk AI system before placing it on the market, with notification only in a specified risk/non-compliance situation.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a GDPR processor record-keeping duty concerning categories of personal-data processing; Norm B is an AI Act importer conformity-check and market-placement duty, potentially including notification to specified parties and market-surveillance authorities.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties concern different actors, different operational actions, and different subject matter: maintaining a processing register versus verifying conformity and controlling the placing of a high-risk AI system on the market. The related paragraph does not make B a reporting duty generally; its notification requirement is conditional and distinct.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De verwerker, en, in voorkomend geval, de vertegenwoordiger van de verwerker houdt een register van alle categorieën van verwerkingsactiviteiten die zij ten behoeve van een verwerkingsverantwoordelijke hebben verricht.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms involve making information available in response to a legal or regulatory need, but they require different underlying work: Norm A requires answering a justified access request for specific domain-registration data, whereas Norm B requires preparing and maintaining technical documentation for a high-risk AI system.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an on-demand access response concerning specific domain-registration data, with a 72-hour deadline; Norm B is proactive technical-documentation preparation and updating concerning AI-system conformity, including Annex IV elements, for assessment by authorities and notified bodies.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties concern different actors, different subject matter and event contexts, and different core actions: responding to a domain-registration data-access request versus preparing/updating high-risk-AI technical documentation.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De registers voor topleveldomeinnamen en de entiteiten die domeinnaamregistratiediensten verlenen beantwoorden een verzoek om toegang als bedoeld in het eerste lid onverwijld of, indien dat niet mogelijk is, binnen 72 uur na ontvangst van het verzoek.
verdict.evidence_span_b: De technische documentatie van een AI-systeem met een hoog risico wordt opgesteld voordat dit systeem in de handel wordt gebracht of in gebruik wordt gesteld, en wordt geactualiseerd.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A requires essential and important entities to promptly inform their service recipients about a significant cyber threat and, where necessary, the threat itself; B requires financial entities to establish and implement an ICT-incident management process that includes detecting, managing, and reporting ICT-related incidents.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: A is an outward communication duty to potentially affected service recipients concerning a significant cyber threat and protective measures. B is an internal governance/process duty whose reporting component concerns ICT-related incidents, without specifying a recipient or the content of any report.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties do not impose the same core action on the same actor role: A requires threat communication to service recipients, whereas B requires financial entities to implement an ICT-incident management process, including incident reporting. The shared cyber/ICT-event context is insufficient, and the reporting content and recipient under B are unspecified.
verdict.evidence_span_a: de significante cyberdreiging zelf
verdict.evidence_span_b: om ICT-gerelateerde incidenten te detecteren, te beheren en te melden

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Norm A requires telecommunications providers and frequency users to give the military authority all cooperation, including carrying out its orders. Norm B permits and conditions the processing of previously collected personal data for developing, training, and testing specified AI systems in a regulatory sandbox, subject to extensive safeguards, documentation, logging, deletion, and publication requirements.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a broad cooperation-and-compliance duty owed to military authorities in the context of applying the Dutch War Act; Norm B is a conditional data-processing and AI-test-environment regime, with safeguards and documentation/publication obligations, and no identified duty to cooperate with or report to the military authority.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms impose materially different actions on different actor categories in different regulatory contexts: military-authority cooperation under the War Act versus controlled further processing of personal data for AI development and testing.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern managing ICT/security risks associated with incidents, but A requires implementing proportionate technical, operational, and organisational measures to prevent incidents or limit their consequences, whereas B requires deploying resources and capabilities to monitor user activity and detect ICT anomalies and ICT-related incidents.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a preventive/mitigating security-measures duty; Norm B is a monitoring and detection-capability duty. They do not require the same compliance work to be performed twice.
verdict.criterion_fired: The underlying actions and actor roles differ: A imposes a security-risk mitigation and incident-consequence-limitation duty on essential or important entities, while B imposes an ICT monitoring and anomaly/incident detection duty on financial entities.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A requires investigators’ written authorisation to state applicable coercive fines in the context of an investigation; B requires importers to verify high-risk AI-system conformity before placing it on the market, and, where a risk exists, notify specified parties and market-surveillance authorities.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: The norms concern fundamentally different duties: an investigative-authorisation content requirement for a lead overseer, versus an importer’s pre-market conformity checks and possible notification duty.
verdict.criterion_fired: Different actor roles and different event families/core actions; A concerns an overseer’s investigation authorisation and coercive fines, while B concerns an importer’s conformity verification and possible risk notification.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Norm A requires registers and domain-name registration service entities to establish and publicly disclose policies and procedures for disclosure of domain-registration data. Norm B requires importers of high-risk AI systems to verify specified compliance conditions before placing the system on the market, including conformity assessment, technical documentation, CE marking, EU declaration, instructions, and an authorised representative; where a risk exists, the importer must notify the provider, authorised representatives, and market-surveillance authorities.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: The norms concern fundamentally different duties: public disclosure of domain-name data-access policies and procedures versus pre-market compliance verification and, in specified circumstances, notification and withholding of a high-risk AI system.
verdict.criterion_fired: Different event family and different actor role; the apparent similarity does not establish the same compliance obligation.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms involve communicating information to an authority, but Norm A primarily requires financial entities to conduct post-incident ICT evaluations and analyze disruption causes; its authority communication concerns implemented changes only on request. Norm B requires notified bodies to inform the notifying authority about specified certification, notification-scope, market-surveillance, and conformity-assessment matters.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A concerns post-incident ICT resilience evaluation and resulting changes by financial entities; Norm B concerns notified bodies' conformity-assessment and notification-status information duties.
verdict.criterion_fired: Different actor roles and different event families; the apparent similarity is limited to authority-directed information communication and does not establish duplicated compliance work.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require the regulated actor to maintain or update information-related records: domain-name registration data in a database under Norm A, and technical documentation for a high-risk AI system under Norm B.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A concerns collecting and maintaining accurate, complete domain-name registration data, with related verification procedures. Norm B concerns preparing and updating technical documentation demonstrating conformity of a high-risk AI system and enabling conformity assessment by authorities and notified bodies.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties concern different regulated actors, different subject matter, and different compliance purposes: domain-name registration databases and verification procedures versus high-risk-AI technical conformity documentation. Any superficial similarity is limited to maintaining information.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De registers voor topleveldomeinnamen en de entiteiten die domeinnaamregistratiediensten verlenen verzamelen nauwkeurige en volledige domeinnaamregistratiegegevens in een database en houden die gegevens bij.
verdict.evidence_span_b: De technische documentatie van een AI-systeem met een hoog risico wordt opgesteld voordat dit systeem in de handel wordt gebracht of in gebruik wordt gesteld, en wordt geactualiseerd.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require notifying/reporting a competent public authority about a triggering event connected with regulated activities, but the duties concern different events and substantially different information.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A concerns advance notice of planned cable-maintenance works on public land to the municipal mayor or delegate; Norm B concerns reporting serious ICT-related incidents by financial entities to the relevant authority, using prescribed incident-reporting models and follow-up reports.
verdict.criterion_fired: The underlying verb-level action is broadly notification/reporting, but the triggering event, regulated actor, recipient context, timing, and required content are materially different; therefore this is not the same compliance work repeated.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both concern cybersecurity-related compliance, but Norm A requires an essential entity to bear the cost of a targeted independent security audit, whereas Norm B requires financial entities to implement documented access-control policies, procedures, and controls.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a supervisory cost-allocation obligation triggered by a targeted security audit; Norm B is a preventive ICT-risk-management implementation obligation concerning access controls.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms impose different verb-level duties on different actor roles and concern different compliance objects: paying audit costs versus implementing access-control measures.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require the relevant operator to maintain stored information: Norm A requires collecting and keeping accurate, complete domain-registration data in a database, while Norm B requires retaining automatically generated high-risk-AI logs under the provider’s control.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: The duties concern different information assets and serve different regulatory purposes: domain-registration identity/contact data for DNS security and resilience versus AI-system logs for oversight and the system’s intended purpose.
verdict.criterion_fired: The underlying retention subject, regulated activity, actor category, and regulatory purpose differ; the apparent similarity is limited to a broad information-retention pattern.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern action connected with a legally significant situation involving information or data, but Norm A requires a telecommunications party, on request, to provide a corporate-register extract or investigate a controlling-interest holder to the Minister. Norm B permits an exceptional international transfer only under specified conditions and, in the residual case, requires the controller to inform the supervisory authority and the data subject about the transfer and legitimate interests, while documenting the assessment and safeguards.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a request-based disclosure/investigation duty concerning ownership or control information owed by a telecommunications party to the Minister. Norm B is a GDPR derogation and residual-case notification/documentation regime concerning transfers of personal data to a third country or international organisation, involving a controller or processor and supervisory authority/data-subject information.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in core action, triggering event, actor role, recipient relationship, and substantive content; the apparent similarity from a broad information/reporting theme does not establish duplicated compliance work.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Norm A empowers the lead overseer to hear other natural or legal persons to collect investigation information; Norm B requires importers, before placing a high-risk AI system on the market, to verify the provider’s conformity-assessment, technical documentation, CE marking, EU declaration/instructions, and authorised representative, and in specified risk or non-compliance situations to withhold placement and notify specified parties/authorities.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an investigative power exercised by a supervisory authority; Norm B is a substantive pre-market compliance-verification duty imposed on importers. They do not require the same compliance work.
verdict.criterion_fired: Different actor role and different event/duty family: an authority’s power to hear persons during an investigation versus an importer’s pre-market conformity checks and possible notification/market-withholding duties.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both provisions concern records or information relevant to regulatory compliance, but Norm A imposes a record-keeping duty on a processor, whereas Norm B grants the lead overseer investigative powers to inspect or obtain copies and explanations from ICT-service providers.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires the processor to maintain a register containing specified processing-activity information. Norm B authorizes the lead overseer, during an investigation, to examine or obtain certified copies or extracts of records and other relevant material; it does not impose the same record-maintenance duty.
verdict.criterion_fired: Different underlying duty, actor role, and event family: a processor's ongoing GDPR record-keeping obligation versus a lead overseer's investigative authority.

verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A imposes an incident-triggered, time-bound warning duty to the entity’s CSIRT and competent authority; Norm B imposes an ongoing analytical and governance duty with no reporting recipient or deadline.
verdict.criterion_fired: Same incident-related event family and broadly comparable regulated-entity role, but different core actions, purposes, recipients, and content: external early-warning notification versus internal trend analysis and resilience management.
verdict.evidence_span_a: geeft ten behoeve van de melding, bedoeld in artikel 27, eerste lid, een vroegtijdige waarschuwing over het significante incident aan haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Beide normen leggen een informatieverstrekking aan een andere partij op, maar A betreft het informeren van een toezichthoudende autoriteit over een specifieke doorgifte van persoonsgegevens, terwijl B aangemelde instanties verplicht elkaar bepaalde geweigerde, opgeschorte, ingetrokken of beperkte goedkeuringen/certificaten te melden.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: De meldingsinhoud, het doel en de betrokken actoren verschillen wezenlijk: A is een uitzonderlijke AVG-doorgifte waarbij de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke de toezichthouder informeert; B is structurele informatie-uitwisseling tussen aangemelde instanties over kwaliteitsmanagementgoedkeuringen en technische-documentatiecertificaten.
verdict.criterion_fired: Niet dezelfde complianceplicht: hoewel beide een informatie-/meldingshandeling bevatten, verschillen de gebeurtenis, actorrol, ontvangerfunctie en inhoud van de informatie wezenlijk.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern handling/reporting an incident, but Norm A requires investigation, risk assessment, and corrective measures after a serious AI incident, whereas Norm B requires banks and specified financial-market entities to submit mandatory or voluntary ICT-incident reports to a sectoral CSIRT.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A imposes post-incident investigation and remediation duties on an AI-system provider; Norm B imposes an additional ICT-incident reporting duty/channel on specified financial-sector entities.
verdict.criterion_fired: The underlying action and actor role differ: Norm A requires investigation, risk assessment, and corrective measures by an AI provider, while Norm B requires incident reporting by specified financial-sector entities to a CSIRT. The shared incident context is insufficient to establish the same compliance work.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require the operator/entity to communicate information about a security incident to an external authority or competent recipient. Norm A requires a progress report when the incident is still ongoing at the final-report deadline, followed by a final report after resolution; Norm B requires immediate notification to the Dutch Data Protection Authority of a security breach affecting personal-data protection.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a NIS2-style incident progress/final reporting duty for essential or important entities, triggered by an ongoing incident and focused on the aspects required for the final report. Norm B is a telecommunications privacy-breach notification duty, triggered specifically by a security breach with adverse effects on personal-data protection, and directed to the Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens without delay.
verdict.criterion_fired: Same actor role and broad security-incident family, but different legal purposes, recipients, timing, and required information: an ongoing-incident progress/final report versus an immediate personal-data-breach notification. The texts do not establish that the same report or substantially identical content can satisfy both duties.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A vereist dat registers en domeinnaamregistratiedienstverleners rechtmatige toegangsverzoeken om specifieke domeinnaamregistratiegegevens beantwoorden binnen 72 uur. verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern action following or involving a reported ICT-related matter, but Norm A requires taking a decision promptly after receipt of a report, whereas Norm B requires financial entities to maintain crisis-communication plans enabling responsible disclosure of serious ICT incidents or vulnerabilities to clients, counterparties, and possibly the public.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a prompt decision-making duty triggered by receipt of a report; Norm B is a crisis-communication planning and disclosure-enablement duty directed toward clients, counterparties, and possibly the public.
verdict.criterion_fired: The underlying action and actor role differ: Norm A concerns taking a decision after receiving a report, while Norm B concerns financial entities maintaining communication plans for disclosure of serious ICT incidents or vulnerabilities. verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require maintaining or making available compliance-related information/documentation, but they do not require the same underlying act: Norm A requires an importer-like processor to maintain a processing-activities register, while Norm B requires importers to provide requested conformity information and documentation to competent authorities and ensure technical documentation is available.

verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in actor, subject matter, and operative action: maintaining a GDPR processing register versus supplying AI Act conformity information and technical documentation to competent authorities.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A requires financial entities to maintain/update an ICT-service contractual-information register, report specified aggregate information annually, provide the register or parts of it on request, and notify the competent authority of planned contracts supporting critical or important functions. B requires importers, before placing a high-risk AI system on the market, to verify specified conformity matters and, where non-compliance or risk is identified, withhold placement and notify the provider, authorised representatives, and market-surveillance authorities.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: The norms concern different regulated actors, different subject matter, and different compliance actions: ICT-outsourcing register/reporting and supervisory disclosure versus pre-market AI conformity verification and, conditionally, non-placement and incident/risk notification.
verdict.criterion_fired: Different actor role and different event family/core duty; the superficial similarity of possible reporting to authorities does not make the obligations duplicative.

verdict.criterion_fired: Different underlying action, triggering context, and obligated actor; the apparent similarity does not establish a shared compliance obligation.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms respond to a significant/serious incident-related situation, but A requires informing potentially affected service recipients about protective measures and, if necessary, the cyber threat; B requires the provider to promptly investigate the serious incident and AI system, including risk assessment and corrective measures, while cooperating with authorities and sometimes a notified body.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an outward-facing warning/information duty to potentially affected service recipients. Norm B is an incident-investigation, risk-assessment, remediation, and authority-cooperation duty for an AI-system provider, following a serious-incident report.
verdict.criterion_fired: The core actions and actor roles differ: A requires notifying service recipients of a cyber threat and possible response measures, whereas B requires the AI provider to investigate, assess risk, take corrective measures, and cooperate with competent authorities. The shared incident-related context is insufficient to establish duplicated compliance work.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A requires processors to maintain a processing-activities register containing specified information; B requires providers processing special-category data for bias detection/correction to ensure that the GDPR/related processing-activities register records the reasons for that processing and its strict necessity.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is the general processor register duty, while Norm B is a conditional AI-specific safeguard requiring additional justification to be recorded in an existing register; B does not impose the same complete register-maintenance duty as A.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms do not impose the same underlying action: A requires maintaining a comprehensive register, whereas B requires documenting necessity and reasons for processing special-category data in a register as part of bias-detection safeguards. verdict.shared_compliance_action: A requires submitting a final incident report to the entity’s CSIRT and competent authority, containing specified incident details, within one month after the initial notification. B requires maintaining ICT-risk-management capabilities, including promptly identifying and detecting ICT risks and anomalies and handling ICT-related incidents quickly; the related paragraph adds periodic documentation/evaluation and submission of an evaluation report on request to the competent authority.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: A is a time-bound post-incident reporting duty with prescribed report contents; B is an ongoing ICT-risk-management and incident-handling duty, with possible evaluation-report submission on request, not a duty to submit the same final incident report.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in both actor scope and core action: A applies to essential or important entities and requires a prescribed final incident report, whereas B applies to specified small or exempt financial entities and requires ongoing ICT-risk-management measures. The shared ICT-incident/security context and possible competent-authority involvement do not make the compliance work the same.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both require entities to manage ICT/cybersecurity risk through organisational and technical measures, including attention to supply-chain or third-party risks. Norm B requires a documented ICT-risk-management framework, continuous monitoring, incident detection and handling, continuity measures, testing, and identification of key dependencies on ICT third-party providers, with periodic and incident-triggered evaluation and submission of an evaluation report on request.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a targeted supply-chain-security risk-assessment requirement concerning direct suppliers and service providers, whereas Norm B is a broader simplified ICT-risk-management framework and operational-resilience obligation for specified financial entities. verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in actor scope and core action: Norm A concerns entities’ consideration of supplier vulnerabilities and cybersecurity practices when determining supply-chain measures; Norm B concerns specified financial entities establishing, maintaining, monitoring, testing and evaluating a comprehensive ICT-risk-management and continuity framework. The shared cybersecurity-risk subject matter is too general to establish the same event or duplicated compliance work.

B requires the provider to remedy specified formal non-conformities within a market-surveillance authority’s deadline, potentially followed by market restriction, prohibition, recall, or withdrawal.

The norms do not impose the same underlying compliance work.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in actor, operative action, and purpose: A concerns an authorised representative’s standing support obligations, while B concerns a provider’s remediation of formal non-conformity following a market-surveillance finding.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require an organisation or representative to provide or maintain compliance-related information/documentation for regulatory authorities, but they do not require the same underlying work: A is an initial and updated national-register information submission, while B concerns retaining AI technical documentation and supplying it to AI authorities on request.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires specified entity-identification and registration information to be supplied to the Dutch Minister, including updates within two weeks. Norm B requires an authorised representative for a general-purpose AI model to keep technical documentation for ten years and provide information or documentation to the AI Office or national authorities upon a reasoned request.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms impose affirmative compliance duties on regulated providers, but the underlying duties differ: Norm A requires cooperation with and execution of orders from military authority during application of the War Act; Norm B requires general-purpose AI-model providers to create, maintain, provide, and publish specified documentation and policies.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms impose an ongoing information/documentation-related compliance duty on covered entities, but Norm A requires supplying entity-registration information to the Minister, whereas Norm B requires retaining automatically generated high-risk-AI logs.

verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in core action, triggering context, actor scope, recipient structure, and substantive content; they do not require the same compliance work to be repeated.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both concern communicating information about a significant personal-data/security incident, but A requires a communication to affected individuals describing the personal-data breach and specified information/measures, whereas B requires incident reporting and related updates to a CSIRT or competent authority on specified deadlines.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: The duties differ materially in recipient, legal purpose, and required content: A is an affected-data-subject notification under GDPR Article 34; B is a staged incident-reporting regime to a CSIRT or competent authority under NIS2 Article 23.
verdict.criterion_fired: Different actor role and recipient/purpose, with low content overlap; the shared incident-related trigger does not make the underlying compliance work the same.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require post-incident investigative or evaluative work concerning a serious ICT/AI-related incident, including assessing causes or risks and identifying or taking remedial improvements. However, Norm A requires a financial entity’s post-incident evaluation and identification of ICT/business-continuity improvements, while Norm B requires an AI provider’s immediate investigation, incident risk assessment, and corrective measures, with cooperation and safeguards concerning alteration of the AI system.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A concerns financial entities evaluating disruptions to core activities caused by serious ICT incidents and identifying improvements; Norm B concerns providers investigating serious incidents involving an AI system, including risk assessment and corrective measures, after a prior report. The actor roles, regulatory regimes, and required investigative outputs therefore differ materially.
verdict.criterion_fired: The underlying investigative/evaluative action and broad incident family overlap, but the duties are imposed on different actor roles and serve different regulatory objects: financial-entity ICT operational resilience under Norm A versus AI-system incident investigation and correction under Norm B. This is not the same compliance work repeated for an additional recipient.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Financiële entiteiten verrichten ICT-gerelateerde post-incidentevaluaties na verstoringen van hun kernactiviteiten ten gevolge van een ernstig ICT-gerelateerd incident, analyseren daarbij de oorzaken van de verstoring en identificeren de verbeteringen die moeten worden aangebracht in de ICT-activiteiten of in het kader van het ICT-bedrijfscontinuïteitsbeleid
verdict.evidence_span_b: Na de melding van een ernstig incident op grond van lid 1 verricht de aanbieder onverwijld het nodige onderzoek in verband met het ernstige incident en het betrokken AI-systeem. Dit omvat een risicobeoordeling van het incident en corrigerende maatregelen.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A requires governing bodies of essential and important entities to approve and oversee implementation of cybersecurity-risk-management measures; B requires certain small financial entities to maintain and periodically evaluate an ICT-risk-management framework and incorporate operational conclusions from tests and incident analysis.

verdict.criterion_fired: The norms differ in actor role and core action: A concerns approval, oversight, and possible liability of governing bodies for cybersecurity measures, while B concerns maintaining, evaluating, and improving an ICT-risk-management framework and incorporating operational conclusions. They also do not share the same triggering event; B refers to periodic evaluation and, where relevant, serious ICT-related incidents, whereas A is not incident-triggered.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern follow-up handling of an ICT/security incident, but A requires supplying the contact details of the person responsible for the notification, whereas B requires post-incident evaluation, causal analysis, identification of improvements, and—on request for certain entities—communication of implemented changes.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A requires the entity to implement appropriate and proportionate technical, operational, and organisational security measures and to account for incident risks and consequences; B requires financial entities to promptly inform clients about serious ICT incidents and mitigation measures, or about protective measures for significant cyberthreats.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: A is an ongoing preventive risk-management and security-measures duty, whereas B is a client-notification duty triggered by a serious ICT incident or significant cyberthreat.
verdict.criterion_fired: The underlying actions and actor roles differ: A requires implementation and risk-based calibration of security measures by essential or important entities generally, while B requires financial entities to notify potentially affected clients after an incident or threat.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Bij het nemen van de maatregelen houdt de entiteit in ieder geval rekening met de stand van de techniek, de uitvoeringskosten en, indien van toepassing, de desbetreffende Europese en internationale normen.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Wanneer een ernstig ICT-gerelateerd incident optreedt en gevolgen heeft voor de financiële belangen van cliënten, stellen financiële entiteiten, zodra zij het incident hebben opgemerkt, hun cliënten onverwijld in kennis van het ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incident en van de maatregelen die zijn genomen om de negatieve gevolgen van een dergelijk incident te beperken.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Norm A requires an internet-access provider to notify the affected subscriber before, or as soon as possible after, taking a protective suspension or termination measure. Norm B requires financial entities to conduct post-incident ICT evaluations and, on request, communicate implemented changes to competent authorities.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a subscriber-facing notice tied to a provider’s protective service measure; Norm B is an internal post-incident review and, for non-micro financial entities, an authority-facing disclosure of resulting changes.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in actor role, triggering event, core action, purpose, and required content; the apparent similarity of an ICT/security-related context does not establish duplicated compliance work.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Voorafgaand aan het nemen van een maatregel, bedoeld in het eerste lid, onderdeel g, doet de aanbieder melding aan de betrokken abonnee
verdict.evidence_span_b: Financiële entiteiten verrichten ICT-gerelateerde post-incidentevaluaties na verstoringen van hun kernactiviteiten ten gevolge van een ernstig ICT-gerelateerd incident

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Geen gedeelde concrete compliance-actie: norm A verplicht financiële entiteiten een ICT-contractenregister bij te houden, jaarlijks bepaalde informatie te rapporteren en het register of onderdelen daarvan aan de bevoegde autoriteit beschikbaar te stellen; norm B stelt cumulatieve voorwaarden aan de verwerking van persoonsgegevens in een AI-testomgeving, waaronder beveiliging, monitoring, verwijdering, logging, documentatie en publicatie.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A betreft registerbeheer en toezichtsinformatie over contracten voor ICT-diensten; norm B betreft rechtmatige verdere verwerking en waarborgen voor persoonsgegevens bij de ontwikkeling, training en test van AI-systemen.
verdict.criterion_fired: De normen hebben geen dezelfde kernactie, gebeurtenisfamilie of actorrol. Norm A ziet op financiële entiteiten en ICT-contractuele regelingen; norm B op verwerking van persoonsgegevens in een AI-testomgeving door aanbieders of andere betrokken ontwikkelaars. Een eventuele gedeelde verwijzing naar bevoegde autoriteiten of toezicht maakt de verplichtingen niet dezelfde.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A requires implementing proportionate technical, operational, and organisational measures to control network and information-system security risks and prevent or limit incident consequences. B requires conducting post-incident ICT evaluations after serious ICT-related disruptions, analysing causes and identifying improvements; certain financial entities must communicate implemented changes to competent authorities on request.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: A is a prospective risk-management and incident-impact-limitation duty, whereas B is a retrospective post-incident evaluation and improvement/documentation duty, with possible disclosure to authorities.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require the regulated entity to implement or maintain cybersecurity risk-management measures, but A specifically requires consideration of supplier/service-provider vulnerabilities, security quality, practices, and coordinated supply-chain risk assessments when selecting supply-chain measures; B requires financial entities to develop and document a broad information-security policy and related ICT-security controls.

verdict.criterion_fired: The norms do not impose the same verb-level duty or require the same compliance work: A requires taking specified supplier-risk factors into account when determining measures, whereas B requires developing and documenting an information-security policy and implementing a broad set of ICT-security controls. They also address different regulated-entity categories and no incident-triggered reporting event.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A requires a processor to inform the controller of a personal-data breach without undue delay. verdict.criterion_fired: The duties do not impose the same core action or substantive compliance work: A is breach notification by a processor to the controller; B is post-incident evaluation by a financial entity, with possible authority disclosure of implemented changes.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De verwerker informeert de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke zonder onredelijke vertraging zodra hij kennis heeft genomen van een inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both provisions concern monetary sanctions, but Norm A imposes a coercive daily penalty on a critical ICT third-party provider to compel compliance with oversight measures, whereas Norm B sets the calculation of fines for SMEs/start-ups under the AI Act.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a lead overseer’s enforcement measure tied to non-compliance with specific oversight measures; Norm B is a general rule limiting or determining the amount of Article 99 fines for SMEs and start-ups.
verdict.criterion_fired: The provisions do not impose the same underlying duty: Norm A authorizes the lead overseer to impose a coercive penalty on a critical ICT third-party provider after non-compliance, while Norm B governs the amount of fines applicable to SMEs/start-ups. They concern different regulatory mechanisms, actors, and purposes, not repeated performance of the same compliance work.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both involve maintaining or making information available in connection with regulated data-processing activities, but they do not require the same underlying compliance action: Norm A requires a controller or representative to maintain a processing-activities register, whereas Norm B requires publication of a short AI-project summary and objectives/expected results on competent authorities’ websites, alongside safeguards for processing personal data in an AI regulatory sandbox.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an ongoing internal record-keeping duty covering specified processing-activity information. Norm B is a public-disclosure obligation tied to development, training, and testing of certain AI systems in a regulatory sandbox, with the published content limited to a project summary, objectives, and expected results.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Beide normen vereisen dat een aanbieder/financiële entiteit cliënten of abonnees informeert over een ICT-, netwerk- of veiligheidsgerelateerde gebeurtenis en de genomen of passende maatregelen; de concrete meldingsinhoud en wettelijke context verschillen echter.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A betreft een voorafgaande of, bij spoed, zo spoedig mogelijke melding aan de betrokken abonnee van een voorgenomen maatregel om een bedreiging voor de integriteit en veiligheid weg te nemen. Norm B betreft onverwijlde kennisgeving aan cliënten van een ernstig ICT-incident met gevolgen voor financiële belangen, inclusief genomen beperkende maatregelen, en eventueel van beschermingsmaatregelen bij een significante cyberdreiging.
verdict.criterion_fired: Zelfde meldings-/informatieverstrekking aan de eigen abonnee of cliënt over een ICT- of veiligheidsgebeurtenis, maar niet dezelfde concrete wettelijke melding: Norm A ziet op een voorgenomen maatregel en het wegnemen van een bedreiging, terwijl Norm B ziet op een ernstig incident of significante cyberdreiging en de gevolgen/beperkende of beschermende maatregelen.

verdict.evidence_span_b: stellen financiële entiteiten, zodra zij het incident hebben opgemerkt, hun cliënten onverwijld in kennis van het ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incident en van de maatregelen die zijn genomen om de negatieve gevolgen van een dergelijk incident te beperken

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern conformity-related compliance documentation, but A requires an authorised representative to provide information/documentation or cooperate with risk-reduction measures on request, whereas B requires high-risk AI providers to prepare and update technical documentation before market placement or putting into service, including specified Annex IV content and, for eligible SMEs, use a simplified form.

Norm B is a proactive technical-documentation preparation, updating, and content/form duty for high-risk AI systems, intended to enable conformity assessment by competent authorities and notified bodies.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in actor, triggering context, and operative action: A concerns responding to a Minister's request and cooperating with risk-reduction measures for devices/radio equipment; B concerns preparing and updating high-risk-AI technical documentation before market placement or use, with specified Annex IV elements and a possible simplified form.
verdict.evidence_span_a: b) het op verzoek van Onze Minister verstrekken van alle benodigde informatie en documentatie om de conformiteit van de apparaten of radioapparaten aan te tonen; c) het op verzoek van Onze Minister verlenen van medewerking aan eventueel genomen maatregelen ter uitschakeling van de risico's van apparaten of radioapparaten waarvoor hij als gemachtigde is aangewezen.
verdict.evidence_span_b: De technische documentatie van een AI-systeem met een hoog risico wordt opgesteld voordat dit systeem in de handel wordt gebracht of in gebruik wordt gesteld, en wordt geactualiseerd.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Beide normen leggen geen identieke rapportageplicht op. Norm A vereist dat de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke de toezichthoudende autoriteit informeert over een uitzonderlijke doorgifte van persoonsgegevens naar een derde land of internationale organisatie. Norm B vereist onder meer dat logbestanden van de verwerking in een AI-testomgeving worden bijgehouden gedurende de deelname aan die testomgeving; daarnaast bevat zij afzonderlijke documentatie- en publicatieverplichtingen.
