verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern internal measures connected with ICT/security incidents: A requires the entity to take proportionate technical, operational and organisational risk-control measures, while B requires financial entities to perform checks and reconciliations during ICT-incident recovery or data reconstruction to preserve data integrity.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a general, risk-based cybersecurity duty applying to an essential or important entity and covering prevention and mitigation measures; Norm B is a specific recovery-stage control duty for financial entities, focused on data integrity and consistency during restoration or reconstruction.
verdict.criterion_fired: The underlying actions and actor roles differ: A requires implementing proportionate risk-management/security measures, whereas B requires performing recovery-time data-integrity checks and reconciliations. The shared ICT-incident context is insufficient to establish the same compliance work.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Bij het nemen van de maatregelen houdt de entiteit in ieder geval rekening met de stand van de techniek, de uitvoeringskosten en, indien van toepassing, de desbetreffende Europese en internationale normen.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Bij herstel van een ICT-gerelateerd incident verrichten financiële entiteiten de benodigde controles, ook meerdere controles, waaronder afstemmingen, om ervoor te zorgen dat het hoogste niveau van gegevensintegriteit wordt gehandhaafd.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both provisions concern obtaining or communicating information relevant to regulatory oversight, but they do not impose the same compliance action: Article 38 empowers the lead overseer to investigate and obtain material, whereas Article 45 requires notified bodies to inform the notifying authority about specified certification, accreditation, and activity matters.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A grants investigative powers to a supervisory authority; Norm B imposes mandatory reporting duties on notified bodies concerning conformity-assessment and notification matters.
verdict.criterion_fired: Different actor roles and different underlying duties: investigative powers to inspect, copy, summon, hear, and obtain traffic data versus a notified body's duty to notify the notifying authority of specified matters.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both require responding to a request from an authority or access-seeking party by providing access to information or records, but they concern different information regimes and purposes.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A concerns domain-name registration data held by registries/registration-service entities and also includes publication of disclosure policies; Norm B concerns automatically generated logs of a high-risk AI system held by the provider, supplied to the requesting competent authority.
verdict.criterion_fired: The actor roles and regulated subject matter differ: domain-name registries/registration-service entities must provide access to specific domain-registration data, whereas high-risk AI providers must provide access to AI-system logs on request. The shared request-for-access pattern is insufficient to establish the same compliance duty.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms involve communicating information to an authority, but Norm A primarily requires post-incident evaluation and analysis, while Norm B requires notified bodies to inform the notifying authority about conformity-assessment activities and related matters.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A concerns internal analysis and, on request, communicating changes made after serious ICT incidents; Norm B concerns notified bodies’ regulatory information duties about conformity-assessment activities, including cross-border work and subcontracting.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in actor, triggering subject matter, and substantive content: Norm A concerns serious ICT-related incidents and post-incident improvements by financial entities, whereas Norm B concerns conformity-assessment activities reported by notified bodies.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Financiële entiteiten verrichten ICT-gerelateerde post-incidentevaluaties na verstoringen van hun kernactiviteiten ten gevolge van een ernstig ICT-gerelateerd incident
verdict.evidence_span_b: op verzoek, de binnen het toepassingsgebied van hun aanmelding verrichte conformiteitsbeoordelingsactiviteiten en andere activiteiten, waaronder grensoverschrijdende activiteiten en onderaanneming

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A requires the lead overseer's written investigation authorisation to specify possible coercive fines where requested records, data, procedures, materials, or answers are not fully provided; B requires importers, before placing a high-risk AI system on the market, to verify specified conformity conditions, including that the provider prepared technical documentation, and in the related procedure to notify specified parties and market-surveillance authorities if the system presents a risk.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: A concerns the content of an investigative authorisation and potential enforcement consequences for non-cooperation with an ICT-service-provider investigation; B concerns an importer's pre-market conformity checks and, where applicable, risk notification. They do not impose the same underlying compliance work.
verdict.criterion_fired: Different underlying actions, event families, and duty-bearing actor roles; the apparent similarity is not a duplicated reporting or verification obligation.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require an organisation to make compliance-related material available to public authorities: A requires the controller to inform the supervisory authority about a qualifying personal-data transfer, while B requires the provider to keep specified high-risk-AI documentation available to national competent authorities for ten years.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an event-triggered notification concerning an exceptional international personal-data transfer; Norm B is a long-term document-retention/availability duty concerning a high-risk AI system.
verdict.criterion_fired: The underlying actions, triggering events, actor roles, and required content differ materially: notification of a specific data transfer to a supervisory authority versus retention and availability of AI-system documentation to national competent authorities.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms impose internal compliance measures concerning ICT/data governance: A requires financial entities to register ICT-related incidents and significant cyber threats and establish incident-management processes; B requires providers of high-risk AI systems to satisfy safeguards and conditions when exceptionally processing special categories of personal data to detect and correct bias.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A concerns incident registration and integrated ICT-incident monitoring, handling, follow-up, and root-cause remediation. Norm B concerns exceptional processing of special-category personal data for bias detection and correction, subject to necessity, security, access-control, non-disclosure, deletion, and record-keeping conditions.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms concern different actors, different triggering circumstances, and different substantive duties: ICT-incident registration/process management versus safeguards for exceptional sensitive-data processing in high-risk AI bias correction.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Norm A requires domain-name registries and domain-name registration service entities to establish and publish policies and procedures, including verification procedures, ensuring that registration-data databases contain accurate and complete information. Norm B empowers the lead overseer, during investigations, to inspect or obtain certified copies or extracts of registers, data, documented procedures, and other relevant material.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A imposes a substantive governance and data-quality duty on registries and registration-service entities; Norm B grants an investigative authority power to the lead overseer to obtain or copy materials. The norms do not require the same compliance work by the same obligated actor.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in actor role, operative action, and event family: Norm A concerns establishing and publishing verification/data-quality procedures for a domain-registration database, while Norm B concerns an overseer's investigative power to inspect or obtain copies of materials.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Norm A requires an essential or important entity to report a significant incident, with specified incident information and an initial assessment, to its CSIRT and competent authority. Norm B requires financial entities to monitor and analyse ICT-related incidents and cyberattack patterns as part of implementing digital operational resilience; it does not require reporting the incident to a recipient.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an incident-notification duty triggered by knowledge of a significant incident and directed to supervisory/incident-response bodies. Norm B is an internal, ongoing risk-monitoring and analysis duty concerning the frequency, types, scale, evolution, and patterns of ICT-related incidents.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in both the actor role and the core action: Norm A imposes external incident reporting, while Norm B imposes internal analysis of ICT-incident trends for resilience and risk-exposure purposes. The shared ICT-incident subject matter is insufficient to create duplicate or merely related reporting burden.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit dient onverwijld of, indien dat niet mogelijk is, binnen 72 uur nadat zij kennis heeft gekregen van het significante incident een melding in bij haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit
verdict.evidence_span_b: Zij inventariseren de ontwikkeling van ICT-risico’s in de tijd, analyseren de frequentie, de types, de omvang en de evolutie van ICT-gerelateerde incidenten, met name cyberaanvallen en de patronen daarvan

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Norm A authorizes the lead overseer to hear persons and collect information during an investigation; Norm B requires importers, before placing a high-risk AI system on the market, to verify conformity conditions and, where applicable, notify the provider, authorized representatives, and market-surveillance authorities of a risk.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A concerns an investigative information-gathering power exercised by a supervisory authority; Norm B concerns an importer’s pre-market conformity-checking, market-withholding, and possible risk-notification duties.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms impose materially different duties on different actor roles in different contexts: investigative hearings and information collection versus importer conformity verification and conditional risk notification.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require the responsible actor to take compliance-related measures concerning a regulated digital/ICT system or incident, but the underlying actions differ: Norm A requires incident registration and processes to identify, document, and remove root causes; Norm B requires an importer to verify and ensure conformity before placing a high-risk AI system on the market, with possible non-placement and notification if risks or non-compliance are found.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an ICT-incident management and root-cause-remediation duty for financial entities; Norm B is a pre-market conformity-verification duty for importers of high-risk AI systems, supplemented by a conditional notification duty to specified parties and authorities.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms concern different actors, different triggering situations, and different substantive actions: financial-entity ICT-incident management versus importer pre-market AI conformity checks. Any notification in Norm B is conditional on discovering a non-compliant, falsified, or risky system and does not turn Norm A's incident-management duty into the same obligation.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both provisions concern an authority or designated official compelling an entity to take action or provide information, but they do not impose the same underlying compliance action. Norm A concerns following operational orders and cooperating with a suspension/preventing network or service misuse or outage; Norm B concerns an information-demand decision whose required contents include identifying the requested information, deadline, penalty, and appeal rights.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an operational direction/cooperation duty tied to suspension, misuse, or outage prevention. Norm B is a formal lead-overseer information-request decision with specified procedural particulars and sanctions.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms do not impose the same core action, do not concern the same triggering event family, and do not clearly bind the same actor role. Any superficial similarity from an authority requiring action or information is insufficient for duplicate burden.

B requires financial entities to implement and maintain ICT-security governance and controls, including a documented patch and update policy.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both provisions concern access to or handling of information relevant to regulatory oversight, but they do not impose the same compliance action: Norm A requires a processor to maintain a processing-activity register, while Norm B empowers the lead overseer to request telephone and data-traffic records during an investigation.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an ongoing record-keeping duty imposed on the processor; Norm B is an investigative power of the lead overseer to request traffic records from others.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Norm A requires a controller to report a personal-data breach to the competent supervisory authority within 72 hours where applicable. verdict.criterion_fired: The norms differ in the operative action, actor role, and event/purpose: breach notification to an authority versus approval and oversight of cybersecurity-risk-management measures.

verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in both actor role and core action: Norm A concerns a financial entity remaining responsible for incident reporting after outsourcing, whereas Norm B imposes investigation and remediation duties on an AI provider after a serious incident.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms involve responding to or facilitating access to information or documentation for public authorities, but they do not require the same underlying compliance action.

Norm B vereist dat aanbieders van algemene AI-modellen technische documentatie, informatie/documentatie, auteursrechtbeleid en een trainingscontentsamenvatting opstellen, bijhouden, beschikbaar stellen of openbaar maken.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern compliance-related action in response to a regulatory situation, but Norm A provides procedural hearing/access rights in an enforcement proceeding, whereas Norm B requires a distributor to take corrective measures and immediately notify the provider/importer and competent authorities with detailed information about non-conformity and corrective measures.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a procedural due-process obligation imposed on the lead overseer toward a regulated critical ICT service provider; Norm B is a substantive corrective-action and incident/non-conformity notification duty imposed on a distributor toward suppliers and competent authorities.
verdict.criterion_fired: Different actor roles and different core duties: a lead overseer must afford a hearing and dossier access during an enforcement procedure, while a distributor must remedy, withdraw, or recall a non-compliant high-risk AI system and immediately provide detailed notice.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require an entity to carry out or apply a risk-oriented assessment/consideration in relation to ICT or cybersecurity, but Norm A concerns selecting supply-chain security measures by considering supplier vulnerabilities and practices, whereas Norm B requires recurring, specific assessments of legacy ICT systems and systems before and after technology connections.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a supply-chain security decision criterion embedded in the duty to adopt appropriate measures; Norm B is a standalone periodic ICT-risk-assessment obligation focused on legacy systems and technology integrations.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in core action, subject matter, and operational target: Norm A requires taking supplier vulnerabilities and cybersecurity practices into account when choosing supply-chain measures, while Norm B requires performing a specific ICT-risk assessment at least annually and around system/technology connections.

verdict.evidence_span_b: Andere financiële entiteiten dan micro-ondernemingen verrichten regelmatig en ten minste eenmaal per jaar een specifieke ICT-risicobeoordeling op alle legacy-ICT-systemen en in ieder geval voor en na de aansluiting van technologieën, toepassingen of systemen.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both concern communicating information about a significant/security-related incident, but A requires notifying affected individuals about a personal-data breach, whereas B requires structured incident reporting to a CSIRT or competent authority, including early warning, incident, interim, and final reports.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: The duties differ materially in recipient, legal purpose, and required content: A is a data-subject communication under GDPR Article 34; B is regulatory incident reporting under NIS2 Article 23.
verdict.criterion_fired: The event family is broadly related, but the actor role and core compliance action differ: A concerns a controller communicating a personal-data breach to data subjects; B concerns covered entities submitting prescribed incident reports to a CSIRT or competent authority.

verdict.criterion_fired: The provisions do not impose the same verb-level action, concern different regulated activities and event families, and apply to different actor roles. Any superficial similarity involving data handling or publication does not amount to repeated compliance work.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern maintaining or making information available in connection with regulated digital-service information systems, but they do not impose the same underlying compliance action: Norm A requires registers and domain-name registration service entities to establish and publish policies and procedures, including verification procedures, ensuring accurate and complete registration databases; Norm B requires an authorised representative to provide information and documentation to the AI Office upon a reasoned request.

verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in actor, subject matter, and operative action: Norm A requires maintaining and publishing policies/procedures for accurate domain-registration data; Norm B requires an authorised representative to furnish AI-related information and documentation to the AI Office on a reasoned request. verdict.shared_compliance_action: Norm A requires a critical ICT third-party provider to submit to an on-site inspection ordered by the lead overseer, with the decision specifying inspection details and related procedural information. Norm B requires an AI-system provider to take adequate corrective measures within the market-surveillance authority’s prescribed deadline when the system is found to pose high risk.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both require an incident-related report or communication by the regulated entity to a cybersecurity authority/CSIRT, but Norm B requires a staged incident-reporting process with substantially more information and follow-up reports, whereas Norm A requires a GDPR personal-data-breach notification.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A concerns a personal-data breach and a risk threshold, with notification to the GDPR supervisory authority within 72 hours; Norm B concerns a significant cybersecurity incident and requires an early warning within 24 hours plus a detailed incident report and subsequent updates/final reports to a CSIRT or competent authority.
verdict.criterion_fired: Same general incident-reporting family and broadly comparable regulated-entity role, but the legal triggers, reporting purposes, recipients, deadlines, and required content differ materially; the duties are related rather than the same compliance work repeated.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Indien een inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens heeft plaatsgevonden, meldt de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke deze zonder onredelijke vertraging en, indien mogelijk, uiterlijk 72 uur nadat hij er kennis van heeft genomen, aan de overeenkomstig artikel 55 bevoegde toezichthoudende autoriteit

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Beide normen houden verband met onderzoek/evaluatie na een ernstig ICT-incident, maar norm A vereist een post-incidentevaluatie met analyse van oorzaken en verbeteringen; norm B vereist dat de AI-aanbieder onverwijld onderzoek doet, inclusief risicobeoordeling en corrigerende maatregelen, met beperkingen op wijziging van het AI-systeem en samenwerking met autoriteiten.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A betreft financiële entiteiten en een interne post-incidentevaluatie van verstoringen van kernactiviteiten, met eventuele mededeling van doorgevoerde wijzigingen op verzoek. Norm B betreft aanbieders van AI-systemen en een onmiddellijk onderzoek na een gemeld ernstig incident, inclusief risicobeoordeling, corrigerende maatregelen en procedurele waarborgen tegenover bevoegde autoriteiten.

Bovendien verschillen de concrete onderzoeksdoelen en verplichtingen: A ziet op evaluatie van verstoring, oorzaken, gevolgde procedures en verbeteringen; B op onverwijld onderzoek, risicobeoordeling, corrigerende maatregelen en het niet wijzigen van het systeem zonder voorafgaande kennisgeving.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Financiële entiteiten verrichten ICT-gerelateerde post-incidentevaluaties na verstoringen van hun kernactiviteiten ten gevolge van een ernstig ICT-gerelateerd incident, analyseren daarbij de oorzaken van de verstoring en identificeren de verbeteringen die moeten worden aangebracht
verdict.evidence_span_b: Na de melding van een ernstig incident op grond van lid 1 verricht de aanbieder onverwijld het nodige onderzoek in verband met het ernstige incident en het betrokken AI-systeem. Dit omvat een risicobeoordeling van het incident en corrigerende maatregelen.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A requires a telecommunications party, on request, to provide a register extract or investigate the identity and third-party links of a control holder. B requires the controller or processor to maintain a written/electronic record of processing activities.

verdict.criterion_fired: Different underlying action, triggering context, and actor role; no duplicated compliance work is apparent.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both provisions concern the allocation or exercise of regulatory oversight, but they do not impose the same underlying compliance action: Article 26 assigns jurisdiction, whereas Article 54 requires an authorised representative to perform verification, retain documentation, provide information on request, and cooperate with authorities.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a jurisdiction/territoriality rule determining which Member State has authority; Norm B imposes substantive representative duties concerning AI-model documentation, information production, and cooperation with authorities.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms differ in both the core action and the actor role: A determines the competent Member State for an entity, while B obliges an authorised representative to verify and maintain/provide AI compliance documentation. The apparent similarity in regulatory authority does not create repeated compliance work.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms impose substantive controls on the use or operation of technology, but they require fundamentally different actions: Norm A requires financial entities to implement documented ICT-security policies, procedures and controls; Norm B prohibits specified AI practices, including placing on the market, putting into service, or using certain AI systems.

verdict.evidence_span_b: Aanbieders van AI-systemen met een hoog risico bewaren de in artikel 12, lid 1, bedoelde logs die automatisch worden gegenereerd door hun AI-systemen met een hoog risico voor zover dergelijke logs onder hun controle vallen.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern information-related compliance, but Norm A requires establishing and publishing policies and procedures for disclosing domain-registration data, whereas Norm B requires notified bodies to inform the notifying authority about specified conformity-assessment matters and activities.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a policy/procedure-setting and publication duty concerning access to domain-registration data; Norm B is an authority-notification duty concerning conformity-assessment certificates, status changes, accreditation circumstances, requests, and activities.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in actor, triggering context, operative action, recipient/purpose, and substantive content; the superficial information-related similarity does not establish duplicated compliance work.
verdict.evidence_span_a: stellen het beleid en de procedures met betrekking tot de bekendmaking van de gegevens, bedoeld in het eerste lid, vast en maken dat beleid en die procedures openbaar

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both concern communicating information about an incident or breach, but A requires an incident report to cybersecurity authorities, while B specifies the content of a communication to affected data subjects.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an immediate regulatory incident-reporting duty for a significant incident affecting a trust service; Norm B concerns the substantive content of a GDPR communication to the affected data subject regarding a personal-data breach.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in actor role and recipient purpose: A is a trust-service entity's report to its CSIRT and competent authority, whereas B is a controller's communication to the affected data subject. The shared incident theme and some possible factual overlap do not make the underlying compliance work the same.
verdict.evidence_span_a: een essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit die een vertrouwensdienst aanbiedt onverwijld of, indien dat niet mogelijk is, binnen 24 uur nadat zij kennis heeft gekregen van het significante incident een melding van het significante incident in bij haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit
verdict.evidence_span_b: De in lid 1 van dit artikel bedoelde mededeling aan de betrokkene bevat een omschrijving, in duidelijke en eenvoudige taal, van de aard van de inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens en ten minste de in artikel 33, lid 3, onder b), c) en d), bedoelde gegevens en maatregelen.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Norm A requires a telecommunications party, on request, to provide the Minister free of charge with an extract from a corporate register concerning a share right (and, under the same provision, to investigate a controller’s identity and third-party ties). Norm B governs the lawful further processing, protection, retention/logging, non-sharing, documentation, and publication conditions for personal data used to develop, train, and test certain AI systems in a regulatory sandbox.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: The norms concern fundamentally different duties: a telecommunications party must provide corporate-control information or conduct an identity investigation for the Minister, whereas AI sandbox participants must comply with conditions governing personal-data processing and AI testing, including a prohibition on sharing generated personal data outside the sandbox.
verdict.criterion_fired: The underlying action, triggering situation, actor role, and compliance content do not materially coincide. Norm A is an on-request information/investigation duty concerning suspected or anticipated dominant control threatening the public interest; Norm B is a set of conditions on further processing of personal data in an AI regulatory test environment. The shared candidate similarity is therefore not a duplicated compliance burden.
verdict.evidence_span_a: verstrekt een telecommunicatiepartij aan Onze Minister op verzoek om niet een uittreksel uit het door de rechtspersoon gehouden register met betrekking tot een recht op een aandeel
verdict.evidence_span_b: persoonsgegevens die in de testomgeving worden aangemaakt mogen niet buiten de testomgeving worden gedeeld

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern ICT/cybersecurity incident-related compliance, but A requires incident reporting and B requires establishing, maintaining, monitoring, and improving an ICT-risk-management framework, including incorporating operational lessons after incidents.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an incident-reporting duty to a CSIRT or competent authority, including a progress report while the incident remains ongoing. Norm B is an internal ICT-risk-management and resilience duty; its incident-related element is to incorporate operational conclusions from testing and post-incident analysis into the risk-assessment process, with a framework report supplied only on request.
verdict.criterion_fired: The underlying actions and responsible actor categories differ: A imposes external reporting by entities affected by a significant incident, whereas B imposes internal ICT-risk-management measures on specified financial entities. The shared ICT-incident context and possible authority interaction do not make the compliance work the same.
verdict.evidence_span_a: op dat moment een voortgangsverslag indienen
verdict.evidence_span_b: in voorkomend geval de relevante operationele conclusies die voortvloeien uit de in punt g) bedoelde tests en uit de analyse na een incident opnemen in het ICT-risicobeoordelingsproces

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A betreft het uitoefenen van onderzoeksbevoegdheden door functionarissen van de lead overseer en gemachtigde personen, met een schriftelijke machtiging en mogelijke dwangsommen bij het niet verstrekken van gevraagde registers, data, procedures, materiaal of antwoorden. B betreft het melden door aangemelde instanties aan de aanmeldende autoriteit van certificaten, goedkeuringen, wijzigingen, verzoeken en activiteiten.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: De normen regelen fundamenteel verschillende handelingen: A ziet op toezicht/onderzoek en het afdwingen van medewerking daaraan; B ziet op periodieke of gebeurtenisgebonden informatieverstrekking door aangemelde instanties aan een aanmeldende autoriteit.
verdict.criterion_fired: Verschillende kernactie, actorrol en inhoud; A is een onderzoeksbevoegdheid van de toezichthouder, terwijl B een meldplicht van aangemelde instanties aan de aanmeldende autoriteit is.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De functionarissen van de lead overseer en andere door hem voor de uitvoering van de in lid 1 bedoelde onderzoeken gemachtigde personen oefenen hun bevoegdheden uit na overlegging van een schriftelijke machtiging
verdict.evidence_span_b: Aangemelde instanties brengen de aanmeldende autoriteit op de hoogte van:

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern making information or documentation about digital/ICT arrangements available or public, but Norm A requires publication of domain-name registration database policies and procedures, whereas Norm B requires maintaining, reporting on, and providing an ICT third-party-contract register to competent authorities.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a proactive public-transparency duty concerning policies and procedures for accurate domain-name registration data; Norm B is a financial-entity ICT-risk-management and supervisory-information duty concerning contractual ICT-service arrangements, including annual reporting and provision on request.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in actor, subject matter, purpose, and operative action: Norm A requires domain-name registries and registration-service entities to make policies and procedures public, while Norm B requires financial entities to maintain, report, and provide an ICT-contract information register to competent authorities.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Zij maken dat beleid en die procedures openbaar.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Financiële entiteiten stellen de bevoegde autoriteit op verzoek het volledige informatieregister of desgevraagd specifieke onderdelen daarvan ter beschikking

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Geen gedeelde compliance-actie: norm A verplicht registers en domeinnaamregistratiedienstverleners om nauwkeurige en volledige domeinnaamregistratiegegevens in een speciale database te verzamelen en bij te houden; norm B staat onder cumulatieve voorwaarden verdere verwerking van persoonsgegevens toe en verplicht onder meer publicatie van een korte samenvatting van een AI-project op de website van bevoegde autoriteiten.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A betreft doorlopende registratie en bewaring van domeinnaamregistratiegegevens door registers/dienstverleners; norm B betreft voorwaarden en waarborgen voor verwerking van persoonsgegevens in een AI-testomgeving, met een afzonderlijke publicatieplicht voor een AI-projectsamenvatting.
verdict.criterion_fired: De kernactie, het gereguleerde onderwerp, de actorrol en het doel verschillen wezenlijk; een eventuele algemene overeenkomst rond gegevensbeheer of openbaarmaking maakt de verplichtingen niet dezelfde.
verdict.evidence_span_a: de registers voor topleveldomeinnamen en de entiteiten die domeinnaamregistratiediensten verlenen, met de nodige zorgvuldigheid nauwkeurige en volledige domeinnaamregistratiegegevens verzamelen en bijhouden in een speciale database
verdict.evidence_span_b: een korte samenvatting van het in de testomgeving ontwikkelde AI-project en de doelstellingen en verwachte resultaten ervan worden op de website van de bevoegde autoriteiten gepubliceerd

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms involve communicating information to a public authority, but they do not require the same underlying compliance action: Norm A requires a personal-data-breach notification containing specified incident details and remedial measures, while Norm B requires a notified body to inform the notifying authority about certification, accreditation, requests, and conformity-assessment activities.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A concerns notification of a personal-data breach by the controller; Norm B concerns ongoing or requested information reporting by notified bodies about conformity-assessment and related activities.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in actor role, triggering subject matter, and required information: a personal-data breach notification versus information obligations concerning conformity-assessment activities and certification matters.
verdict.evidence_span_a: de aard van de inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens
verdict.evidence_span_b: de binnen het toepassingsgebied van hun aanmelding verrichte conformiteitsbeoordelingsactiviteiten en andere activiteiten, waaronder grensoverschrijdende activiteiten en onderaanneming

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Norm A requires a controller to inform the supervisory authority about an exceptional international transfer of personal data; Norm B requires financial entities to maintain accessible records of activities before and during ICT disruptions when continuity or response/recovery plans are activated.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an authority-notification duty concerning an exceptional cross-border personal-data transfer, whereas Norm B is an internal record-retention/documentation duty concerning ICT disruption response and recovery.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in both the operative action and the triggering event: informing a supervisory authority about a specific international data transfer versus maintaining internal records during ICT-plan activation.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De verwerkingsverantwoordelijke informeert de toezichthoudende autoriteit over de doorgifte.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Financiële entiteiten houden gemakkelijk toegankelijke registers bij van hun activiteiten vóór en tijdens storingen

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Geen gedeelde compliance-actie: norm A legt civielrechtelijke aansprakelijkheid voor schade door onrechtmatige verwerking op, terwijl norm B een meld- en rapportageplicht voor ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incidenten oplegt.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A betreft aansprakelijkheid en schadevergoeding na verwerking die inbreuk maakt op de AVG; norm B betreft het melden van ernstige ICT-incidenten aan een bevoegde autoriteit, met voorgeschreven kennisgevingen en rapporten.
verdict.criterion_fired: De normen hebben niet dezelfde kernhandeling, gebeurtenisfamilie of actorrol: aansprakelijkheid voor verwerkingsschade versus rapportage van ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incidenten door financiële entiteiten.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Een verwerker is slechts aansprakelijk voor de schade die door verwerking is veroorzaakt wanneer bij de verwerking niet is voldaan aan de specifiek tot verwerkers gerichte verplichtingen van deze verordening
verdict.evidence_span_b: Financiële entiteiten melden overeenkomstig lid 4 van dit artikel ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incidenten aan de relevante bevoegde autoriteit als bedoeld in artikel 46.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern obligations imposed on regulated entities, but A requires a telecommunications party, on request, to provide a register extract or investigate a controller's identity and third-party links; B requires high-risk AI providers to maintain specified documentation and logs, among many other duties. They do not impose the same compliance action.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a request-triggered cooperation/investigation duty concerning control over a telecommunications entity; Norm B is an ongoing recordkeeping and compliance duty for high-risk AI providers.
verdict.criterion_fired: Different core action, event context, and regulated actor role; no duplicated compliance work is apparent.
verdict.evidence_span_a: stelt een telecommunicatiepartij op verzoek van Onze Minister een onderzoek in naar de identiteit van een houder van zeggenschap en de banden die deze heeft met derden.
verdict.evidence_span_b: bewaren de in artikel 18 bedoelde documentatie

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms impose obligations on regulated digital-sector actors, but A requires prompt public disclosure of non-personal domain-registration data, whereas B imposes a broad set of high-risk-AI provider obligations, including conformity, documentation, corrective measures, and information duties.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: The triggering contexts and substantive duties differ: domain-name registration data disclosure versus lifecycle compliance obligations for high-risk AI systems.
verdict.criterion_fired: Different event family, actor role, and core action; the apparent similarity is only a broad digital-regulation/addressee resemblance, not duplicated compliance work.
verdict.evidence_span_a: onverwijld na de registratie van een domeinnaam, de domeinnaamregistratiegegevens die geen persoonsgegevens zijn, openbaar maken
verdict.evidence_span_b: zorgen ervoor dat hun AI-systemen met een hoog risico in overeenstemming zijn met de eisen van afdeling 2

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Beide normen bevatten een informatie-/documentatieverplichting jegens bevoegde publieke instanties, maar niet dezelfde concrete compliance-actie: norm A vereist registratie en het onmiddellijk melden van wijzigingen in entiteitsgegevens; norm B betreft de gemachtigde van een aanbieder van een AI-model voor algemene doeleinden, die op gemotiveerd verzoek documentatie en informatie aan het AI-bureau verstrekt en met autoriteiten samenwerkt.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A ziet op voorafgaande identificatie/registratie van essentiële of belangrijke entiteiten en wijzigingsmeldingen binnen uiterlijk twee weken. Norm B ziet op controle, langdurige beschikbaarheid en verzoekgestuurde verstrekking van technische documentatie en samenwerking rond de naleving van AI-verplichtingen door een gemachtigde.
verdict.criterion_fired: De normen betreffen verschillende actoren, verschillende regelgevingsdoelen en verschillende soorten informatie-/documentatiewerkzaamheden; een vergelijkbare publieke ontvanger en het algemene element van informatieverstrekking maken de verplichtingen niet dezelfde.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De in lid 3 bedoelde entiteiten melden onmiddellijk elke wijziging in de bijzonderheden die zij op grond van de eerste alinea van dit lid hebben ingediend, en in elk geval binnen twee weken na de datum van de wijziging.
verdict.evidence_span_b: het verstrekken aan het AI-bureau, na een met redenen omkleed verzoek, van alle informatie en documentatie, waaronder die in punt b), die nodig is om aan te tonen dat de verplichtingen van dit hoofdstuk worden nageleefd

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Beide normen houden verband met het beheersen van ICT-/gegevensincidentrisico’s, maar norm A verplicht onverwijlde mededeling van een concrete persoonsgegevensinbreuk aan de betrokkene, terwijl norm B een doorlopend ICT-risicobeheer- en evaluatiekader verplicht, met onder meer het opnemen van operationele lessen uit tests en incidentanalyses en eventueel indiening van een evaluatieverslag bij de bevoegde autoriteit op verzoek.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is een incidentgebonden meldplicht aan de betrokkene; norm B is een preventieve en voortdurende governance-, monitoring- en evaluatieplicht voor bepaalde financiële entiteiten, zonder algemene verplichting om hetzelfde incident aan dezelfde soort ontvanger te melden.
verdict.criterion_fired: De kernactie, actorcategorie en inhoud verschillen wezenlijk: mededeling van een persoonsgegevensinbreuk aan de betrokkene versus inrichting en onderhoud van ICT-risicobeheer, monitoring, testen en evaluatie; de gedeelde incident-/ICT-risicocontext maakt dit hoogstens thematisch verwant.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Wanneer de inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens waarschijnlijk een hoog risico inhoudt voor de rechten en vrijheden van natuurlijke personen, deelt de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke de betrokkene de inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens onverwijld mee.
verdict.evidence_span_b: h) in voorkomend geval de relevante operationele conclusies die voortvloeien uit de in punt g) bedoelde tests en uit de analyse na een incident opnemen in het ICT-risicobeoordelingsproces

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require a telecommunications/domain-related entity to make information available to a public-facing recipient or authority, but the underlying actions differ: Norm A requires proactive public disclosure of non-personal domain-registration data; Norm B requires, on request, supplying a corporate-register extract and potentially conducting an investigation into a controlling-interest holder and its third-party ties.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an immediate, public disclosure duty triggered by domain registration. Norm B is a request-based cooperation duty triggered by suspected or anticipated controlling influence threatening the public interest, involving an extract and possibly an investigation supplied to the Minister.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in actor role, triggering event, core action, recipient, and information purpose; they are not the same compliance work repeated.
verdict.evidence_span_a: maken de domeinnaamregistratiegegevens, die geen persoonsgegevens zijn, onverwijld na de registratie van een domeinnaam openbaar
verdict.evidence_span_b: verstrekt een telecommunicatiepartij aan Onze Minister op verzoek om niet een uittreksel uit het door de rechtspersoon gehouden register met betrekking tot een recht op een aandeel

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both require an entity to communicate updated or otherwise relevant information to a public authority, but the duties concern different subject matter and regulatory purposes.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires designated essential or important entities to report changes to their previously submitted identification/contact and related registration details to the competent authorities. Norm B requires notified conformity-assessment bodies to inform the notifying authority about circumstances affecting the scope or conditions of their notification.
verdict.criterion_fired: The actor roles and triggering events differ: Norm A concerns changes in an entity’s registration particulars, while Norm B concerns circumstances affecting the scope or conditions of a conformity-assessment body’s notification. The shared act of informing an authority is too generic to create the same compliance duty.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De in lid 3 bedoelde entiteiten melden onmiddellijk elke wijziging in de bijzonderheden die zij op grond van de eerste alinea van dit lid hebben ingediend
verdict.evidence_span_b: omstandigheden die van invloed zijn op het toepassingsgebied van of de voorwaarden voor de aanmelding

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both require the entity to consider or assess ICT/security risks and the likelihood and severity of incidents when determining or evaluating risk-related measures. However, A concerns proportionality and selection of security measures, while B requires permanent identification and at least annual evaluation of ICT-risk sources, cyber threats, vulnerabilities, and risk scenarios.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a risk-proportionality factor within a duty to implement security measures; Norm B is an ongoing ICT-risk identification and assessment process for financial entities.
verdict.criterion_fired: Same broad ICT-risk/security-assessment subject matter and overlapping risk analysis, but the duties differ in actor scope, operational purpose, and required content: A informs proportionate security measures, whereas B mandates permanent identification and annual evaluation.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Ten aanzien van de evenredigheid van de maatregelen, bedoeld in het eerste lid, houdt de entiteit naar behoren rekening met de mate waarin zij aan risico’s is blootgesteld, de omvang van de entiteit en de kans dat zich incidenten voordoen en de ernst ervan
verdict.evidence_span_b: Financiële entiteiten identificeren permanent alle bronnen van ICT-risico, met name de wederzijdse risicoblootstelling ten aanzien van andere financiële entiteiten, en beoordelen de cyberdreigingen en ICT-kwetsbaarheden

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both provisions concern an authority or authority-facing access to information/documentation, but they do not impose the same underlying compliance action: Article 38 grants the lead overseer investigative powers, whereas Article 54 assigns the authorised representative duties to retain, provide, and cooperate regarding AI-model documentation.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an investigative power of the lead overseer; Norm B is a set of substantive duties of an authorised representative for general-purpose AI-model providers, including ten-year document availability and responding to reasoned requests.
verdict.criterion_fired: The provisions differ in actor, legal function, and operative duty: A authorises the lead overseer to investigate and obtain material, while B requires an authorised representative to perform mandate tasks, retain documentation, provide information on request, and cooperate with authorities.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De lead overseer is bevoegd om: a) registers, data, procedures en alle overig voor de uitvoering van zijn taken relevant materiaal te onderzoeken
verdict.evidence_span_b: c) het verstrekken aan het AI-bureau, na een met redenen omkleed verzoek, van alle informatie en documentatie, waaronder die in punt b), die nodig is om aan te tonen dat de verplichtingen van dit hoofdstuk worden nageleefd

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Geen gedeelde verb-level compliance-actie: norm A vereist het staven/documenteren van een beoordeling en passende waarborgen in het register van artikel 30; norm B vereist het bewaren van automatisch gegenereerde logs.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A betreft documentatie van een beoordeling en waarborgen voor een specifieke internationale doorgifte van persoonsgegevens; norm B betreft logretentie door aanbieders van hoog-risico-AI-systemen, met een minimumduur van zes maanden.
verdict.criterion_fired: De kernactie, het gereguleerde onderwerp, de actorrol en de inhoud verschillen wezenlijk; een gedeelde categorie van digitale compliance of mogelijke incidentcontext is niet uit de eigen teksten af te leiden.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De verwerkingsverantwoordelijke of de verwerker staaft de beoordeling en de in lid 1, tweede alinea, van dit artikel bedoelde passende waarborgen in het artikel 30 bedoelde register.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Aanbieders van AI-systemen met een hoog risico bewaren de in artikel 12, lid 1, bedoelde logs die automatisch worden gegenereerd door hun AI-systemen met een hoog risico voor zover dergelijke logs onder hun controle vallen.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A requires a provider to notify the affected subscriber about a measure taken (or to be taken) to address a threat to network, service, or terminal-device integrity and security. B requires financial entities to continuously identify ICT-risk sources and regularly assess cyber threats, ICT vulnerabilities, and risk scenarios. These are not the same underlying compliance action.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: A is an event-linked notification to an affected subscriber concerning a specific security measure; B is an ongoing internal ICT-risk identification and assessment process, with no notification recipient or incident-specific report.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms differ in core action, triggering context, actor role, recipient, and content: A concerns notifying an affected subscriber about a specific measure, while B concerns financial entities' continuous and periodic internal assessment of ICT risks and vulnerabilities.
verdict.evidence_span_a: doet de aanbieder melding aan de betrokken abonnee
verdict.evidence_span_b: identificeren permanent alle bronnen van ICT-risico

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both provisions concern maintaining or collecting records/data, but they impose different underlying duties: Norm A requires a processor to maintain a detailed register of processing activities; Norm B addresses collection of domain-name registration data and expressly seeks to prevent duplicate collection through cooperation.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an accountability record-keeping duty imposed on processors, whereas Norm B is a data-collection duplication-prevention rule concerning TLD registries and domain-name registration service entities.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in actor, subject matter, and purpose: processing-activity registers under GDPR versus domain-name registration-data collection under NIS2; the apparent similarity is only a broad records/data-maintenance pattern.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De verwerker, en, in voorkomend geval, de vertegenwoordiger van de verwerker houdt een register van alle categorieën van verwerkingsactiviteiten
verdict.evidence_span_b: De naleving van de in de leden 1 tot en met 5 vastgestelde verplichtingen mag er niet toe leiden dat domeinnaamregistratiegegevens tweemaal moeten worden verzameld.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern organizational measures/processes addressing ICT or network-and-information-system incidents and their risks, but A requires risk-proportionate security measures while B requires establishing and implementing an ICT-incident management process, including detection, management, and reporting.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a general risk-based security-measures duty, including consideration of exposure, entity size, incident likelihood and severity; Norm B is a specific incident-management-process duty for financial entities, expressly covering detection, management and reporting of ICT-related incidents.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ at the verb and actor-role level: A requires an essential or important entity to take and calibrate preventive/protective security measures, whereas B requires a financial entity to define, establish and implement an incident-management process. The shared incident-risk context is insufficient to establish duplicated compliance work.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Bij het nemen van de maatregelen houdt de entiteit in ieder geval rekening met de stand van de techniek, de uitvoeringskosten
verdict.evidence_span_b: Financiële entiteiten omschrijven een beheerproces voor ICT-gerelateerde incidenten, stellen dit vast en leggen dit ten uitvoer, om ICT-gerelateerde incidenten te detecteren, te beheren en te melden.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern regulated entities maintaining or making available information relevant to regulatory oversight, but they impose different underlying duties: A requires publication of policies and procedures for disclosing domain-registration data; B requires financial entities to maintain, report, and provide an ICT-services contractual-information register to competent authorities.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A concerns public disclosure policies and procedures for domain-registration data by registries/registration-service providers; Norm B concerns ICT third-party-contract registers, annual reporting, on-request supervisory access, and advance notification by financial entities.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in actor, subject matter, and operative action: A requires making disclosure policies and procedures public, whereas B requires financial entities to maintain, report, provide, and notify authorities about an ICT-contract information register.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De lidstaten schrijven voor dat het beleid en de procedures met betrekking tot de bekendmaking van dergelijke gegevens openbaar worden gemaakt.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Financiële entiteiten rapporteren ten minste jaarlijks aan de bevoegde autoriteiten over het aantal nieuwe overeenkomsten inzake het gebruik van ICT-diensten, de categorieën van derde aanbieders van ICT-diensten, het soort contractuele overeenkomsten en de ICT-diensten en -functies die worden geleverd.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A requires covered entities to establish and maintain an ICT-risk-management framework and mitigate ICT-risk impacts through resilient, up-to-date ICT systems and controls. B requires certain deployers of high-risk AI to conduct and, when necessary, update a fundamental-rights impact assessment. These are distinct substantive compliance actions.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A concerns ongoing ICT-risk management and resilience; Norm B concerns a fundamental-rights impact assessment for the use of a high-risk AI system and updating its information when relevant elements change.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern handling risks to information security in connection with a significant ICT/data incident: Norm A requires including the responsible reporting officer’s contact details in an early warning, while Norm B requires financial entities to implement ICT technologies and processes that prevent availability, authenticity, integrity, confidentiality, and data-loss risks.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an incident-triggered reporting-content duty; Norm B is an ongoing preventive ICT-security implementation duty, not a reporting obligation.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in both core action and event structure: A requires providing contact information as part of an early warning concerning a significant incident, whereas B requires implementing and operating preventive ICT-security measures. The shared security subject matter is insufficient to establish the same compliance work.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require preventive security/risk-management measures aimed at limiting or handling the consequences of security or ICT incidents. Norm A requires public electronic communications providers to take prescribed technical, operational, and organisational measures; Norm B requires certain financial entities to maintain a documented ICT-risk-management framework and ensure rapid detection and handling of ICT incidents.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A concerns providers of public electronic communications networks or services and specifically targets the effects of security incidents on national security or public order. Norm B concerns specified small or exempt financial entities and imposes a broad, ongoing ICT-risk-management framework, including detection, incident handling, continuity, testing, and documentation/evaluation; it does not require the same measure or address the same protected interests.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms do not impose the same core compliance action on the same actor role. They overlap only at a high level in addressing ICT/security incidents; Norm A requires sector-specific measures to limit incident consequences, while Norm B requires a comprehensive ICT-risk-management framework and operational controls for financial entities.

verdict.criterion_fired: Same actor and broadly overlapping incident-recording work, but the regimes cover different incident populations and require different records and purposes; the text does not establish that the same record can satisfy both duties without additional work.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require communicating information about a cyber/security threat or related protective measure, but they do not require the same communication: Norm A requires the provider to notify the affected subscriber of a measure taken (or, normally, before taking it, give the subscriber an opportunity to remove the threat), while Norm B requires essential/important entities to inform potentially affected service recipients about a significant cyber threat and possible response measures.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a provider-to-involved-subscriber notice tied to taking a network/service/device integrity or security measure, including an opportunity for the subscriber to remedy the threat; Norm B is an entity-to-service-recipient warning about a significant cyber threat and measures recipients can take in response.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties are not imposed on the same actor role: Norm A concerns an aanbieder/provider taking a security measure, whereas Norm B concerns essential and important entities warning their service recipients. Although both involve communicating about a security threat, the recipients and substantive purposes differ, so this is not the same compliance work repeated.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require the regulated actor to create or maintain compliance-related records/documentation, but they do not require the same underlying action: Norm A requires registering ICT-related incidents and significant cyber threats, while Norm B requires preparing and updating technical documentation for a high-risk AI system.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A concerns incident and cyber-threat registration within an ICT incident-management process; Norm B concerns pre-market/in-use technical documentation demonstrating conformity of a high-risk AI system and supporting conformity assessment.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties concern different actors, different triggering/event contexts, and materially different content and purposes; any superficial similarity in record-keeping does not create duplicated compliance work.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern compliance controls relating to regulated technology, but Norm A requires financial entities to register and manage ICT incidents, including identifying, documenting, and removing root causes; Norm B requires importers to verify specified conformity prerequisites before placing a high-risk AI system on the market, and in certain cases to withhold placement and notify specified parties and market-surveillance authorities.

Norm B is a pre-market conformity-verification duty for importers of high-risk AI systems, with a conditional non-placement and notification duty where non-compliance, falsification, or risk is suspected.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in actor, triggering event, and operative action: Norm A concerns recording and managing ICT-related incidents and cyber threats, while Norm B concerns importer verification of AI conformity before market placement. verdict.shared_compliance_action: Norm A imposes civil liability to compensate damage caused by unlawful processing; Norm B requires prompt notification of serious AI incidents to market-surveillance authorities, within at most 15 days after awareness (and after establishing, or reasonably likely, causation).

verdict.criterion_fired: The norms require fundamentally different actions, concern different triggering circumstances and purposes, and do not impose the same compliance work. Norm A concerns liability for damage caused by unlawful processing; Norm B concerns reporting a serious AI incident to market-surveillance authorities.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both concern access to or obtaining information/material relevant to a regulatory or legal function, but they do not impose the same operative compliance action: A requires disclosure-policy publication by domain-name registries/registration-service entities, while B grants the lead overseer investigative powers over ICT-service providers and other persons.

The latter is an authority power, not a matching publication or reporting duty.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Norm A requires domain-name registries and registration-service entities to establish and publish policies and procedures, including verification procedures, to ensure that registration-data databases contain accurate and complete information. Norm B empowers the lead overseer, during general investigations, to request telephone- and data-traffic overviews and to investigate or obtain copies of records, data, procedures, and other relevant material.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a substantive data-governance and policy/procedure obligation imposed on registries and registration-service entities; Norm B is an investigative power of the lead overseer concerning ICT-service providers and other persons or entities. It does not impose the same underlying action on the same actor.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms differ in both the core action and the duty-bearing actor: A requires establishing and publishing verification/data-quality policies and procedures, whereas B authorizes an overseer to investigate and obtain information or traffic overviews. The shared presence of data/procedures does not create the same compliance obligation.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both concern cybersecurity risk management in relation to an adverse cybersecurity event or risk: A requires considering suppliers’ vulnerabilities when selecting supply-chain security measures, while B requires investigating a serious incident, assessing its risks, and taking corrective measures.

verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in both core action and event family: A concerns preventive consideration of supplier vulnerabilities when adopting security measures, whereas B concerns post-incident investigation, risk assessment, corrective measures, and cooperation/notification constraints for an AI-system incident. verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern communicating information about serious/significant ICT-related incidents, but Norm A requires the entity to report each significant incident under the statutory incident-reporting procedure, whereas Norm B requires financial entities to maintain crisis-communication plans enabling responsible disclosure to clients, counterparties, and potentially the public.

verdict.criterion_fired: Different core action and different regulated actor role; the shared serious-incident context is insufficient to establish duplicated compliance work.
verdict.evidence_span_a: In het geval van een dergelijke uitbesteding blijft de financiële entiteit volledig verantwoordelijk voor het naleven van de vereisten inzake incidentrapportage.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A requires a critical ICT third-party provider to submit to on-site inspections ordered by the lead overseer; B concerns maintaining or extending AI-system certificates after a notified-body designation is withdrawn, including immediate notification to specified authorities and bodies. They do not impose the same underlying compliance action.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an inspection/cooperation duty imposed on a critical ICT third-party provider, whereas Norm B concerns certificate validity and assumption/completion of assessment responsibilities following withdrawal of a notified body's designation, with an immediate-notification duty.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms differ in actor role, triggering event, and operative action: A requires submission to an ordered on-site inspection; B addresses certificate continuation after withdrawal of a designation and related responsibility, assessment, and notification steps.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De kritieke derde aanbieder van ICT-diensten onderwerpt zich aan de inspecties ter plaatse die bij besluit van de lead overseer zijn gelast.
verdict.evidence_span_b: De nationale bevoegde autoriteit of de aangemelde instantie die de functies van de door de wijziging van de aanwijzing getroffen aangemelde instantie vervult, stelt de Commissie, de andere lidstaten en de andere aangemelde instanties hiervan onmiddellijk in kennis.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A requires the controller to report a personal-data breach to the competent supervisory authority within the specified timeframe (subject to the stated exception). B requires essential and important entities to implement proportionate technical, operational, and organisational cybersecurity-risk-management measures to prevent incidents or mitigate their effects; it is not a reporting duty.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: A is an ex post breach-notification obligation directed to a supervisory authority, whereas B is an ongoing preventive and mitigative security-measures obligation with no reporting recipient or deadline specified.
verdict.criterion_fired: The underlying actions and actor roles differ: A requires a controller to notify an authority about a personal-data breach; B requires essential or important entities to implement cybersecurity-risk-management measures. The shared incident/security context is insufficient to establish the same compliance work.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms involve responding to a justified request from an authority or legitimate requester by providing access to information or documentation. verdict.criterion_fired: The duties do not concern the same actor role or the same substantive event/family: Norm A is an access request for domain-registration data, whereas Norm B is an AI regulatory authority’s request for technical/compliance documentation and cooperation.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A lead overseer imposes a daily coercive fine on a critical third-party ICT service provider for non-compliance with supervisory measures; B is a notified conformity-assessment body suspending or withdrawing an AI-system certificate, or imposing limitations, when the system no longer meets specified requirements unless the provider takes corrective action.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: The norms concern different enforcement mechanisms, different triggering non-compliance contexts, and different actor roles: coercive monetary enforcement by a lead overseer versus certification action by a notified body.
verdict.criterion_fired: Different actor role and different enforcement duty/event family; the apparent similarity is only a broad non-compliance/enforcement pattern, not duplicated compliance work.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both concern communicating information about a significant/security-related incident, but A requires notifying affected data subjects, whereas B requires a staged incident-reporting process to a CSIRT or competent authority.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a GDPR communication to the data subject about a personal-data breach and its consequences/measures; Norm B is a NIS2 regulatory incident-reporting sequence to a CSIRT or competent authority, including early warning, incident notification, interim updates, and final reports.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in actor role, recipient, purpose, and substantive reporting content: A communicates a personal-data breach to the affected individual, while B requires regulated entities to report significant incidents to cybersecurity authorities through multiple reports.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Geen gedeelde concrete compliance-actie: norm A vereist het op verzoek ter beschikking stellen van een register aan een toezichthoudende autoriteit; norm B, voor zover geëxtraheerd, vereist dat aanbieders van hoog-risico-AI-systemen een kwaliteitsmanagementsysteem hebben. A ziet op het op verzoek verstrekken van een register aan een toezichthoudende autoriteit; B ziet op verplichtingen van aanbieders van hoog-risico-AI-systemen, met name het beschikken over een kwaliteitsmanagementsysteem.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern incident-related compliance, but A requires documenting personal-data breaches for supervisory compliance, whereas B requires rapid, staged reporting of significant incidents to a CSIRT or competent authority, including warnings, incident reports, updates, and final reports.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an internal documentation duty concerning personal-data breaches and enabling supervisory review; Norm B is an external, time-bound operational reporting sequence concerning significant incidents, with specified incident information and multiple reports.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties do not impose the same core action or substantially the same compliance work: A requires documenting all personal-data breaches, while B requires notifying/reporting significant incidents to a CSIRT or competent authority within specified deadlines. verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms involve providing information or documentation to a public authority upon request, but the requested material and regulatory purpose differ substantially.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires a telecommunications party to provide a company-register extract concerning a share right, or to investigate and report the identity and third-party links of a control holder, in response to suspected or potential overriding control threatening the public interest. Norm B requires an authorised representative of a provider of a general-purpose AI model to provide the AI Office, on a reasoned request, with all information and documentation needed to demonstrate compliance with the AI Act, including retained technical documentation.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in actor role, triggering regulatory context, and substantive content: Norm A concerns telecommunications-sector control/shareholding investigations for protection of the public interest; Norm B concerns an AI-model representative's compliance documentation and cooperation duties under the AI Act.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A requires the controller to provide specified information to the supervisory authority in a prior-consultation process; B requires certain financial entities to continuously monitor the security and operation of all ICT systems as part of an ICT-risk-management framework.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: A is an information-submission duty triggered by high-risk processing requiring prior consultation and directed to a supervisory authority. B is an ongoing ICT-security monitoring and risk-management measure, with no reporting to the authority in the provision itself.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ at the verb level, event/purpose level, and actor-role level: prior-consultation information provision by a GDPR controller versus continuous ICT-system security monitoring by specified financial entities.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Beide normen houden verband met het beheersen van cyberbeveiligingsrisico’s, maar A verplicht aanbieders tot het nemen van technische, operationele en organisatorische beveiligingsmaatregelen om de gevolgen van beveiligingsincidenten te beperken, terwijl B ziet op governance: bestuursorganen moeten maatregelen goedkeuren, toezicht houden op de uitvoering en mogelijk aansprakelijk zijn.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A legt een operationele beveiligingsmaatregelenplicht op aan aanbieders van openbare elektronische communicatienetwerken of -diensten; norm B legt lidstaten een governance- en aansprakelijkheidsverplichting op met betrekking tot bestuursorganen van essentiële en belangrijke entiteiten.
verdict.criterion_fired: Niet dezelfde actorrol en niet dezelfde kernhandeling: A betreft het implementeren van beveiligingsmaatregelen door aanbieders, B betreft het waarborgen van goedkeuring en toezicht door bestuursorganen via de lidstaten.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Beide normen verplichten de betrokken aanbieder/verwerkingsverantwoordelijke of verwerker passende technische en organisatorische beveiligingsmaatregelen te treffen om een passend, op het risico afgestemd beveiligingsniveau voor netwerken, diensten of verwerking te waarborgen.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm B concretiseert de beveiligingsmaatregelen voor persoonsgegevens en verwerking met specifieke elementen, zoals pseudonimisering, versleuteling, continuïteit, herstel na incidenten en periodieke tests. Norm A ziet op de veiligheid en beveiliging van aangeboden netwerken en diensten en bevat die concrete elementen niet.

Het gaat daarom niet om dezelfde complianceplicht die tweemaal moet worden uitgevoerd.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern organizational responsibility in the context of processing or ICT-related incidents, but they impose different actions: Norm A establishes civil liability and compensation for damage caused by unlawful processing, while Norm B requires financial entities to design, establish, implement, and operate an ICT-incident management process, including detection, management, and reporting.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a liability and damages-allocation rule triggered by damage caused by processing that infringes the GDPR; Norm B is a preventive and operational governance requirement for managing and reporting ICT-related incidents.
verdict.criterion_fired: The underlying duties, triggering events, and responsible actor categories differ materially: civil liability for unlawful processing versus implementation of an ICT-incident management process by financial entities.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Geen gedeelde compliance-actie: norm A betreft de tegenwerpelijkheid van een inschrijving in een aandeelhoudersregister na een verzoek tot uitlevering; norm B betreft voorwaarden voor verdere verwerking en delen van persoonsgegevens in een AI-testomgeving.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is een goederen-/registerrechtelijk gevolg van een aandelenuitleveringsverzoek, terwijl norm B een gegevensbeschermings- en AI-governance-regime voor verwerking, beveiliging, logging, bewaring en beperkte verdere deling voorschrijft.
verdict.criterion_fired: De normen hebben noch dezelfde kernhandeling, noch hetzelfde type gebeurtenis of dezelfde actorrol; een registerinschrijving die aan derden kan worden tegengeworpen is geen verwerking of verdere deling van persoonsgegevens in een AI-testomgeving.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Geen gedeelde compliance-actie: norm A vereist governance door bestuursorganen — goedkeuring en toezicht op cyberbeveiligingsrisicobeheersmaatregelen — terwijl norm B een lead overseer bevoegd maakt een dagelijkse dwangsom op te leggen om een kritieke ICT-dienstverlener tot naleving van toezichtmaatregelen te dwingen.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A betreft een preventieve/interne governance- en aansprakelijkheidsverplichting van bestuursorganen van essentiële en belangrijke entiteiten. Norm B betreft een handhavingssanctie door een toezichthouder wegens niet-naleving door kritieke derde ICT-dienstverleners, na een kennisgeving en een termijn van ten minste 30 dagen.
verdict.criterion_fired: De normen hebben niet dezelfde actorrol of kernhandeling: A ziet op bestuursorganen die maatregelen goedkeuren en toezicht houden; B ziet op een lead overseer die een dwangsom oplegt wegens niet-naleving van toezichtmaatregelen. De gedeelde cyberbeveiligingscontext is onvoldoende om van dezelfde compliance-last te spreken.
verdict.evidence_span_a: de bestuursorganen van essentiële en belangrijke entiteiten de door deze entiteiten genomen maatregelen voor het beheer van cyberbeveiligingsrisico’s goedkeuren om te voldoen aan artikel 21, toezien op de uitvoering ervan
verdict.evidence_span_b: neemt de lead overseer een besluit aan waarmee een dwangsom wordt opgelegd om de kritieke derde aanbieder van ICT-diensten tot nakoming van die maatregelen te dwingen

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both concern responding to risks or incidents involving information security, but Norm A requires notifying an affected individual of a personal-data breach, whereas Norm B requires financial entities to identify and assess ICT risks, cyber threats, vulnerabilities, and risk scenarios on an ongoing basis.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an urgent, individual-facing breach notification duty triggered by a personal-data breach likely to adversely affect privacy; Norm B is a continuous and periodic internal ICT-risk identification and assessment duty, with no notification recipient or incident-specific reporting requirement.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in core action, triggering/event structure, and actor role: Norm A requires notifying the affected data subject after a qualifying personal-data breach, while Norm B requires financial entities to identify and assess ICT risks and vulnerabilities as part of ongoing risk management.
