verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms impose a substantive prohibition/control obligation concerning the use or operation of regulated technology, but they do not require the same compliance work: Article 9 requires financial entities to implement documented ICT-security policies, procedures and controls, whereas Article 5 prohibits specified AI practices and uses.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an ICT-risk-management implementation duty for financial entities; Norm B is a prohibition on placing on the market, putting into service, or using specified AI systems and practices, including certain biometric categorisation systems.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms concern different underlying actions, actors, and regulatory subject matter: implementing ICT-security controls versus refraining from prohibited AI practices. They do not impose the same real-world compliance work, and there is no reporting or common recipient obligation.

verdict.distinguishing_factor: The norms concern fundamentally different duties, actors, and regulatory events: an inspected entity’s cooperation with supervisory inspection versus a notified body’s certification-enforcement decision following non-compliance.

verdict.distinguishing_factor: A concerns cooperation with product-safety risk-elimination measures at the Minister’s request; B concerns disclosure of domain-name registration data to legitimate access-seeking parties and publication of disclosure procedures.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms impose different duties on different actor roles in different regulatory contexts: product-risk mitigation cooperation versus domain-name registration-data access and transparency.

verdict.criterion_fired: The core action and actor role differ: A requires submission of an incident report, whereas B requires establishing and implementing an ICT-incident management process; the texts also identify different regulated-entity categories.

Norm A ziet op wijzigingen in eerder gemelde entiteitsgegevens onder de NIS2-richtlijn; norm B ziet op informatieverstrekking door aanbieders van hoog-risico-AI in verband met corrigerende maatregelen en artikel 20. verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern regulatory compliance and oversight of regulated technology providers, but Norm A governs cooperation with an investigation by a lead overseer, while Norm B imposes ongoing product-compliance duties on providers of high-risk AI systems.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A concerns exercising investigative powers and obtaining registers, data, procedures, materials, or answers from third-party ICT-service providers; Norm B requires high-risk AI providers to ensure conformity with substantive requirements, including before placing the system on the market or putting it into service.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms do not impose the same underlying action, event-triggered duty, or actor role: A concerns an overseer's investigation and compelled cooperation by third-party ICT-service providers, whereas B concerns providers' own conformity and lifecycle obligations for high-risk AI systems.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Beide normen leggen een informatie-/transparantiegerelateerde verplichting op, maar niet dezelfde concrete handeling: norm A vereist openbaarmaking van beleid en procedures voor bekendmaking van domeinnaamregistratiegegevens; norm B vereist het bijhouden, rapporteren en op verzoek verstrekken van een register van ICT-dienstcontracten aan de bevoegde autoriteit.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: De normen betreffen verschillende onderwerpen en doelen: publieke transparantie over domeinnaamgegevens versus ICT-risicobeheer en toezicht op contracten met ICT-dienstverleners.
verdict.criterion_fired: Verschillende kernhandeling, gebeurtenisfamilie en actorcontext; de gedeelde informatie-/publicatiekarakteristiek is te algemeen om dubbele compliance-last aan te nemen.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both provisions concern registration-related handling of numbering/domain-name information, but Norm A requires number holders to register number users within six months and place the number into the user's use; Norm B requires TLD registries and domain-registration service providers to make non-personal domain-registration data public without delay after domain registration.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A imposes a registration and consequential allocation/use duty concerning number users and telephone numbers; Norm B imposes an immediate public-disclosure duty concerning non-personal domain-name registration data.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties concern different regulated objects and event families, are imposed on different actor roles, and require different actions: registering number users and enabling number use versus publicly disclosing non-personal domain-registration data.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Nummerhouders registreren binnen zes maanden na de inwerkingtreding van artikel 4.9, derde lid, onderdeel b, de nummergebruikers.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A requires providers to implement technical, operational, and organisational measures to limit the consequences of security incidents; B requires affected entities to report significant incidents through early warnings and subsequent reports to a CSIRT or competent authority.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a preventive risk-management and mitigation duty, whereas Norm B is a time-bound incident-reporting duty with specified warning, incident, interim, and final-report content.
verdict.criterion_fired: The underlying actions differ: implementing security measures to limit incident consequences is not the same compliance work as submitting an early warning and incident reports to a CSIRT or competent authority.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms impose obligations concerning regulated products or systems, but they do not require the same compliance action: Norm A automatically causes an existing recognition to lapse when the issuer's recognition is withdrawn, whereas Norm B requires high-risk AI providers to perform multiple conformity, documentation, marking, registration, corrective-action, and information duties.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A requires the entity to implement and calibrate proportionate cybersecurity measures based on identified risks, including incident likelihood and severity. B requires financial entities to submit initial, interim/updated, and final reports on serious ICT-related incidents to the relevant competent authority within prescribed time limits.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a preventive, risk-based security-measures duty; Norm B is a post-incident reporting duty concerning specified serious ICT incidents and prescribed report content.
verdict.criterion_fired: The underlying verb-level actions and compliance purposes differ: A requires implementing and risk-calibrating security measures, whereas B requires reporting incident information to a competent authority. The shared incident/security context and broadly overlapping regulated-entity role do not make the duties the same.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De maatregelen, bedoeld in het eerste lid, zorgen voor een beveiligingsniveau van de netwerk- en informatiesystemen dat is afgestemd op de risico’s, bedoeld in het eerste lid.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Norm A requires domain-name registries and registration-service entities to establish and publish policies and procedures for disclosing specified domain-registration data, including access on a lawful and properly justified request by a legitimate party. Norm B requires number holders to register number users within six months and thereby place the number into the user's use.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A concerns establishing and publishing disclosure/access procedures for domain-registration data; Norm B concerns registering telecommunications number users and granting them use of a number.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties concern different actors, different subject matter, and different operative actions: domain-data disclosure-policy publication versus number-user registration and assignment/use of a number.
verdict.evidence_span_a: stellen het beleid en de procedures met betrekking tot de bekendmaking van de gegevens, bedoeld in het eerste lid, vast en maken dat beleid en die procedures openbaar
verdict.evidence_span_b: Nummerhouders registreren binnen zes maanden na de inwerkingtreding van artikel 4.9, derde lid, onderdeel b, de nummergebruikers.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms involve making information available in response to, or for use by, other parties, but they require materially different compliance work: Norm A requires a domain-name registry or registrar to answer a lawful, properly motivated access request for specific domain-registration data, promptly or within 72 hours. Norm B requires providers of general-purpose AI models to create and maintain extensive technical and user-facing documentation, copyright-compliance policies, and a public training-content summary.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an event-driven access-request response concerning specific domain-registration data; Norm B is an ongoing documentation, policy, disclosure, and publication regime for general-purpose AI-model providers.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in core action, triggering event, actor role, recipient relationship, and substantive content; any superficial similarity from information being made available does not establish duplicated compliance work.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Beide normen zien op het verstrekken of delen van informatie/documentatie over conformiteit of technische documentatie, maar A betreft informatieverstrekking aan de bevoegde minister op diens verzoek door een gemachtigde; B betreft het actief informeren van andere aangemelde instanties over geweigerde, ingetrokken, opgeschorte of beperkte certificaten.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: De actor, ontvanger en concrete functie verschillen: A is een verzoekgestuurde toezichts- en conformiteitsinformatieplicht van een gemachtigde aan de minister, terwijl B een proactieve inter-notified-body informatie-uitwisseling over specifieke certificaatbesluiten is.
verdict.criterion_fired: Niet dezelfde kernhandeling, actorrol of gebeurtenisfamilie; de beperkte overlap in informatie/documentatie is onvoldoende om dezelfde compliance-werkzaamheden aan te nemen.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A: the lead overseer may request reports from critical ICT third-party providers describing actions taken or corrective measures concerning recommendations. B: notified bodies must inform the notifying authority about circumstances affecting the scope or conditions of their notification.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: The norms concern different substantive duties: A is an oversight power to request remedial-action reports from critical ICT providers; B is a mandatory notification by conformity-assessment bodies concerning their notification status.
verdict.criterion_fired: Different actor roles and different event families/content: oversight follow-up on recommendations and corrective measures versus notification-authority reporting about circumstances affecting designation/notification conditions.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Beide normen vereisen een melding/kennisgeving in verband met een incident of bedreiging, maar norm A vereist een aanbieder om een abonnee over een voorgenomen maatregel te informeren (en gelegenheid tot herstel te geven), terwijl norm B financiële entiteiten verplicht ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incidenten aan een bevoegde autoriteit te rapporteren via eerste, tussentijdse/geactualiseerde en eindverslagen.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is een voorafgaande of spoedmelding aan de betrokken abonnee over een integriteits- of veiligheidsmaatregel; norm B is een inhoudelijk uitgewerkte, meerfasige incidentrapportage aan een bevoegde autoriteit, met informatie over de omvang en mogelijke grensoverschrijdende effecten van een ernstig ICT-incident.
verdict.criterion_fired: De normen hebben wel een vergelijkbare meldingshandeling en een brede ICT-/veiligheidscontext, maar niet dezelfde actorrol: norm A betreft een aanbieder die een abonnee informeert over een maatregel, terwijl norm B financiële entiteiten verplicht ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incidenten aan een bevoegde autoriteit te rapporteren. Bovendien verschillen ontvanger, doel, procedure en inhoud wezenlijk. Dit is daarom geen dubbele compliance-last.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern organizational handling of ICT/security events, but A requires an external early-warning notification while B requires internal monitoring and detection capabilities.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A imposes a time-bound reporting duty to the CSIRT and competent authority after a significant incident; Norm B imposes an ongoing monitoring/detection measure and does not require a report or identify a recipient.
verdict.criterion_fired: Same general ICT/security-incident family and financial/essential-entity-type operational role, but notification and monitoring are different compliance actions with different purposes and content; therefore not duplicate reporting work.
verdict.evidence_span_a: geeft ten behoeve van de melding, bedoeld in artikel 27, eerste lid, een vroegtijdige waarschuwing over het significante incident aan haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit
verdict.evidence_span_b: zetten voldoende middelen en capaciteiten in om toezicht te houden op activiteiten van gebruikers en het optreden van ICT-anomalieën en ICT-gerelateerde incidenten

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both concern implementing or maintaining cybersecurity risk-management measures, but Norm A specifically requires considering supplier/service-provider vulnerabilities, security quality, practices, and coordinated supply-chain risk assessments when selecting supply-chain measures; Norm B requires financial entities to establish and document broad ICT-security policies, procedures, controls, and related protections.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a supplier and supply-chain risk-assessment consideration duty; Norm B is a broad ICT-risk-management implementation duty for financial entities, including access control, authentication, encryption, change management, patching, and network segmentation.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms do not impose the same verb-level action or the same substantive compliance work: Norm A requires taking specified supply-chain factors into account when choosing measures, whereas Norm B requires financial entities to develop and implement documented ICT-security policies, procedures, controls, and infrastructure protections.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern domain/number registration information, but A requires number holders to register number users, whereas B requires registries and domain-name service providers to grant access to specified domain-registration data upon lawful, justified requests and to respond within 72 hours.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a one-time registration duty imposed on number holders after a statutory change; Norm B is an access-and-response duty imposed on domain-name registries and registration-service providers in response to requests from legitimate access-seeking parties.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in actor, operative action, triggering event, and compliance content; the shared registration-information subject matter is insufficient to establish duplicated compliance work.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Geen gedeelde concrete compliance-actie: norm A vereist het opstellen en bijhouden van een register van verwerkingsactiviteiten; norm B vereist op gemotiveerd verzoek toegang tot automatisch gegenereerde logs van een hoog-risico-AI-systeem.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A betreft interne documentatie/registratie van verwerkingsactiviteiten onder de AVG; norm B betreft het verstrekken van systeemlogs aan een bevoegde autoriteit voor toezicht op AI-conformiteit.
verdict.criterion_fired: De normen leggen verschillende handelingen op aan verschillende actorrollen en hebben geen hetzelfde triggering event: een register opstellen versus logs verstrekken op verzoek van een bevoegde autoriteit.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms involve obtaining or providing information in the context of regulatory oversight, but they do not impose the same compliance action: Article 38 empowers the lead overseer to request explanations from representatives, whereas Article 16 requires high-risk AI providers to demonstrate conformity to a national competent authority upon a reasoned request.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an investigative power of the lead overseer directed at representatives of critical third-party ICT service providers; Norm B is a provider obligation concerning proof of conformity of a high-risk AI system to a national competent authority.
verdict.criterion_fired: Different actor roles and different regulatory subject matter: an overseer's investigative request for explanations versus an AI provider's duty to demonstrate conformity.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both provisions concern conditions governing the handling or processing of personal data, but Norm A requires the controller to inform the supervisory authority about an exceptional transfer, whereas Norm B imposes safeguards and documentation/publication conditions for processing personal data in an AI regulatory sandbox.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an authority-notification duty triggered by an exceptional international transfer; Norm B is a set of operational safeguards and record/publication duties for AI-system development, training, and testing.
verdict.criterion_fired: Different core action and different event family; Norm A concerns notifying a supervisory authority of an exceptional third-country/international-organisation transfer, while Norm B concerns conditions for processing personal data in an AI regulatory sandbox.

verdict.distinguishing_factor: The norms concern different regulated objects, actors, duties, and event contexts: registration and allocation of telephone numbers versus preparation of AI-system technical documentation for conformity assessment.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require an actor to take a legally mandated measure, but Norm A requires the municipal authorities to decide on a consent application for cable works, whereas Norm B requires Member States to ensure that essential and important entities implement cybersecurity risk-management measures.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A concerns an administrative consent decision following a written notification about works on public land; Norm B concerns preventive and mitigating cybersecurity measures for network and information systems.
verdict.criterion_fired: Different core action, triggering context, and duty-bearing actor; the apparent similarity is not a duplicated compliance obligation.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern conformity-related compliance for regulated products, but Norm A requires an authorised representative to retain and, on request, provide conformity information/documentation to the Minister, whereas Norm B requires an importer to verify conformity prerequisites before placing a high-risk AI system on the market and, in specified circumstances, notify relevant parties and market-surveillance authorities.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an authorised representative’s information/document-retention and cooperation duty toward the Minister; Norm B is an importer’s pre-market verification duty, with a conditional notification duty for risks or suspected non-compliance. They do not require the same operational act or content.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in actor, triggering event, and core action: Norm A concerns responding to a Ministerial request and maintaining conformity records, while Norm B concerns an importer’s pre-market checks and conditional notifications. Similar conformity subject matter is insufficient to establish duplicate compliance work.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both provisions concern obtaining or making available information/documentation relevant to regulatory oversight or demonstrating compliance, but they allocate different functions: A imposes cooperation/document-retention duties on an authorised representative, while B grants investigative powers to the lead overseer.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an ongoing duty of the authorised representative to retain and, on request, provide conformity information/documentation and cooperate with risk-reduction measures. Norm B is an investigative authority empowering the lead overseer to inspect, copy, obtain, and request explanations from ICT-service providers and others.
verdict.criterion_fired: Different actor roles and different legal functions: A imposes duties on an authorised representative; B confers investigative powers on a supervisory authority. The provisions do not require the same compliance work to be performed twice.

verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A concerns investigative information-gathering powers exercised by a lead overseer against representatives of critical third-party ICT-service providers. Norm B concerns a mandatory inter-notified-body information-sharing duty about refused, suspended, withdrawn, or otherwise restricted quality-management approvals and technical-documentation certificates.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms differ in actor role, event family, and substantive action/content: an investigative request for explanations and records versus mandatory notification of regulatory approval/certification decisions.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require making conformity-related information and technical documentation available to a public authority upon request, but they assign that duty to different actor roles and concern different regulated products.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A concerns an appointed authorised representative for devices or radio equipment and includes a ten-year document-retention duty plus cooperation with risk-removal measures. Norm B concerns importers of high-risk AI systems and requires supplying information and documentation, in an understandable language, to the relevant competent authorities on a reasoned request, while ensuring technical documentation can be made available.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms share a request-based provision of conformity information/documentation to an authority, but they do not impose the duty on the same actor role and do not concern the same regulated-product/event family. The overlap is therefore not the same compliance work repeated under two legal bases.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern an AI/network-service provider taking action in response to a potentially serious security or integrity-related event, but A requires notifying the affected subscriber about a protective service measure, whereas B requires conducting an urgent investigation, risk assessment, corrective measures, and cooperation with authorities after a serious AI-system incident.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a subscriber-facing notice accompanying or following suspension/termination of internet access to address a threat to network, service, or device integrity and security. Norm B is an authority-facing post-incident investigation and remediation duty concerning a serious incident involving a high-risk AI system.
verdict.criterion_fired: The underlying actions and triggering events differ: A requires notifying the affected subscriber about a protective access measure, while B requires an urgent investigation and remediation after a serious high-risk-AI incident. The shared provider role and broad security context are insufficient to establish duplicated compliance work.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Voorafgaand aan het nemen van een maatregel, bedoeld in het eerste lid, onderdeel g, doet de aanbieder melding aan de betrokken abonnee
verdict.evidence_span_b: verricht de aanbieder onverwijld het nodige onderzoek in verband met het ernstige incident en het betrokken AI-systeem. Dit omvat een risicobeoordeling van het incident en corrigerende maatregelen.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both require the regulated actor to establish/prepare compliance-related material or measures, but the duties are substantively different: Norm A requires domain-name registries and registration-service entities to establish and publish policies and procedures ensuring accurate and complete registration data; Norm B requires providers of high-risk AI systems to prepare and update technical documentation demonstrating conformity and enabling assessment by authorities and notified bodies.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A concerns governance procedures for the accuracy and completeness of domain-name registration data, whereas Norm B concerns system-specific technical conformity documentation for high-risk AI systems.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties involve different actors, different subject matter, and different compliance outputs: domain-name data-governance policies and procedures versus high-risk-AI technical documentation.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De registers voor topleveldomeinnamen en de entiteiten die domeinnaamregistratiediensten verlenen stellen het beleid en de procedures vast, waaronder verificatieprocedures, om ervoor te zorgen dat de database, bedoeld in het eerste lid, juiste en volledige informatie bevat.
verdict.evidence_span_b: De technische documentatie van een AI-systeem met een hoog risico wordt opgesteld voordat dit systeem in de handel wordt gebracht of in gebruik wordt gesteld, en wordt geactualiseerd.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A requires the processor to inform the controller without undue delay after becoming aware of a personal-data breach. B requires the provider, after a serious-incident notification, to investigate the incident and AI system, including risk assessment and corrective measures, cooperate with authorities, and avoid certain system-modifying investigations without prior notice.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: A is an immediate personal-data-breach notification duty from processor to controller; B is a post-notification serious-AI-incident investigation/cooperation and non-interference duty, with prior notice only for a specified type of investigation.
verdict.criterion_fired: The underlying action, actor role, and operative event family differ: A concerns a processor notifying the controller of a personal-data breach, whereas B concerns an AI provider investigating a serious incident and coordinating with competent authorities.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De verwerker informeert de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke zonder onredelijke vertraging zodra hij kennis heeft genomen van een inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require an actor to create and maintain information or records, but they concern different subject matter and serve different compliance purposes: domain-name registration data in a database versus technical, user-facing, copyright, and training-content documentation for general-purpose AI models.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A concerns collecting and maintaining accurate and complete domain-name registration data; Norm B concerns documentation and information duties of providers of general-purpose AI models, including making specified information available to authorities and downstream AI-system providers.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in actor role, subject matter, and operative compliance action; the superficial similarity of maintaining information does not establish the same compliance work.
verdict.evidence_span_a: verzamelen nauwkeurige en volledige domeinnaamregistratiegegevens in een database en houden die gegevens bij
verdict.evidence_span_b: de technische documentatie van het model opstellen en up-to-date houden

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both concern an AI/NIS security-incident context and involve the provider/entity taking action in response to incident risk, but A requires preventive/mitigating security measures while B requires an immediate investigation, risk assessment, corrective measures, cooperation, and prior notice before certain system changes.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an ongoing risk-management and incident-impact-mitigation duty; Norm B is a post-serious-incident investigation and cooperation duty following a report under Article 73(1).
verdict.criterion_fired: The underlying actions and actor roles differ: A imposes a general duty on essential or important entities to implement measures limiting incident consequences, whereas B imposes a duty on an AI-system provider to investigate a serious incident immediately and cooperate with authorities.
verdict.evidence_span_a: neemt passende en evenredige technische, operationele en organisatorische maatregelen
verdict.evidence_span_b: verricht de aanbieder onverwijld het nodige onderzoek

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Beide normen betreffen het melden van informatie over een ICT-/veiligheidsincident aan een bevoegde instantie, maar norm A omvat daarnaast het bijhouden en documenteren van informatie en mogelijke corrigerende maatregelen, terwijl norm B een melding uit hoofde van artikel 19 van de verordening aan een sectorspecifiek CSIRT voorschrijft.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A geldt voor aanbieders van AI-modellen voor algemene doeleinden met een systeemrisico en ziet op ernstige incidenten en mogelijke corrigerende maatregelen; norm B geldt voor specifieke financiëlemarktactoren en betreft de melding van ICT-incidenten (waaronder een vrijwillige melding) aan een sectorspecifiek CSIRT.
verdict.criterion_fired: De actorrol verschilt wezenlijk: AI-modelaanbieders onder norm A tegenover banken en financiëlemarktinfrastructuur onder norm B. Bovendien verschillen de meldingsinhoud en de onderliggende wettelijke meldingsregeling; de gedeelde incident-trigger en het algemene werkwoord ‘melden’ zijn onvoldoende voor een dubbele compliance-last.
verdict.evidence_span_a: c) relevante informatie over ernstige incidenten en mogelijke corrigerende maatregelen bijhouden, documenteren en onverwijld rapporteren aan het AI-bureau en, in voorkomend geval, aan de nationale bevoegde autoriteiten;
verdict.evidence_span_b: Banken, handelsplatformen, centrale effectenbewaarinstellingen en centrale tegenpartijen doen de melding, bedoeld in artikel 19, eerste lid, eerste paragraaf, van de verordening, en de vrijwillige melding, bedoeld in artikel 19, tweede lid, eerste paragraaf, van de verordening, tevens bij het bij of krachtens artikel 16, eerste lid, van de Cyberbeveiligingswet aangewezen CSIRT voor de sectoren bankwezen en infrastructuur voor de financiële markt.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern maintaining or preparing compliance-related information/documentation, but they do not require the same underlying action: Norm A requires providing an ICT-services information register to a competent authority on request, whereas Norm B requires creating and updating technical documentation for a high-risk AI system to demonstrate conformity.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an on-request disclosure duty concerning contractual ICT-service arrangements of financial entities; Norm B is a documentation-production and updating duty concerning high-risk AI-system conformity, primarily for assessment by authorities and notified bodies.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in actor, subject matter, purpose, and operative action: an ICT-register disclosure to a competent authority versus preparation and updating of high-risk-AI technical documentation.

verdict.evidence_span_b: De technische documentatie van een AI-systeem met een hoog risico wordt opgesteld voordat dit systeem in de handel wordt gebracht of in gebruik wordt gesteld, en wordt geactualiseerd.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern making or obtaining information/documentation available for oversight or conformity assessment, but A authorizes an investigative power to obtain certified copies or extracts, whereas B imposes a proactive duty to prepare and update technical documentation for a high-risk AI system.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an investigative authority’s power to request or obtain certified copies/extracts from a critical ICT third-party provider’s records and other materials. Norm B is the provider/deployer-side obligation to prepare and update technical documentation before market placement or use, containing Annex IV information for conformity assessment.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in actor, event, and operative action: A concerns an investigation and the lead overseer’s power to obtain certified copies or extracts; B concerns advance preparation and updating of AI technical documentation. The shared information/documentation theme is insufficient to establish duplicated compliance work.

verdict.evidence_span_b: De technische documentatie van een AI-systeem met een hoog risico wordt opgesteld voordat dit systeem in de handel wordt gebracht of in gebruik wordt gesteld, en wordt geactualiseerd.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A concerns the legal effect/opposability of an entry in a shareholders’ register after a request for delivery of a shareholding; B requires preparation and updating of technical documentation for a high-risk AI system, including information enabling conformity assessment.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a property/securities-law rule about the effect of a register entry against later-acquiring deposit participants. Norm B is an AI-provider documentation and conformity-assessment obligation.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms concern different legal actions, triggering events, actors, and subject matter; neither requires the same compliance work as the other.

verdict.evidence_span_b: De technische documentatie van een AI-systeem met een hoog risico wordt opgesteld voordat dit systeem in de handel wordt gebracht of in gebruik wordt gesteld, en wordt geactualiseerd.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both provisions concern information or records relevant to regulatory oversight, but Norm A requires a processor to maintain a prescribed register, whereas Norm B empowers the lead overseer to investigate and obtain information from persons or entities.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a substantive record-keeping duty imposed on a processor; Norm B is an investigative power of the lead overseer, including hearing other persons or legal entities with their consent.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in actor, operative action, and legal function: maintaining a processing-activities register versus an overseer’s power to hear persons or legal entities during an investigation.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern an actor taking compliance-related action in relation to a regulated ICT/AI system or provider, but Norm A empowers an overseer to investigate and obtain information, whereas Norm B requires an importer to verify and ensure conformity before placing a high-risk AI system on the market, with notification only in the specified risk/non-conformity circumstances.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an investigative information-gathering power of a lead overseer directed at representatives and other persons; Norm B is a substantive pre-market conformity-verification duty of importers, including withholding market placement and, in a specified case, notifying the provider, authorised representatives, and market-surveillance authorities.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in actor, operative action, and event/purpose: investigative requests for explanations and records versus importer conformity checks and possible market-placement prohibition/notification.
verdict.evidence_span_a: c) vertegenwoordigers van kritieke derde aanbieder van ICT-diensten op te roepen en te verzoeken om mondelinge of schriftelijke toelichting te geven bij feiten of documenten die betrekking hebben op het onderwerp en het doel van het onderzoek
verdict.evidence_span_b: Alvorens een AI-systeem met een hoog risico in de handel wordt gebracht, zorgen de importeurs ervoor dat het systeem in overeenstemming is met deze verordening door na te gaan of:

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Beide normen betreffen het verstrekken of vastleggen van informatie, maar norm A vereist het staven van een beoordeling en passende waarborgen in een intern register; norm B vereist het verstrekken van identificatie-, contact-, sector- en dienstverleningsinformatie aan bevoegde autoriteiten en het melden van wijzigingen.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A ziet op documentatie in een artikel 30-register ter onderbouwing van een specifieke doorgifte van persoonsgegevens; norm B ziet op registratie-informatie voor de nationale lijst van essentiële en belangrijke entiteiten, inclusief wijzigingsmeldingen binnen twee weken.
verdict.criterion_fired: De normen hebben niet dezelfde kernhandeling, gebeurtenis of inhoud: A betreft het documenteren/staven van een doorgiftebeoordeling en waarborgen in een register, terwijl B betreft het verstrekken en actualiseren van entiteitsgegevens aan bevoegde autoriteiten voor een nationale entiteitenlijst.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De verwerkingsverantwoordelijke of de verwerker staaft de beoordeling en de in lid 1, tweede alinea, van dit artikel bedoelde passende waarborgen in het artikel 30 bedoelde register.
verdict.evidence_span_b: De in lid 3 bedoelde entiteiten melden onmiddellijk elke wijziging in de bijzonderheden die zij op grond van de eerste alinea van dit lid hebben ingediend, en in elk geval binnen twee weken na de datum van de wijziging.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A: the lead overseer may request telephone and data-traffic records as part of an investigation. B: the importer must, before placing a high-risk AI system on the market, verify specified compliance conditions, including that the provider has appointed an authorised representative; in certain circumstances it must also notify the provider, authorised representatives, and market-surveillance authorities of a risk.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A concerns investigative powers to obtain communications-traffic overviews; Norm B concerns an importer's pre-market compliance checks and, where a risk exists, notifications and a prohibition on placing the system on the market.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms do not impose the same underlying action, concern different triggering circumstances, and bind different actor roles: investigative information-gathering by a lead overseer versus importer's product-compliance checks and possible risk notification.

verdict.evidence_span_b: Alvorens een AI-systeem met een hoog risico in de handel wordt gebracht, zorgen de importeurs ervoor dat het systeem in overeenstemming is met deze verordening door na te gaan of:

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A requires essential and important entities to promptly communicate protective measures (and, if necessary, the significant cyber threat) to potentially affected service recipients. B requires financial entities to conduct post-incident ICT evaluations and, on request, non-micro financial entities to communicate changes implemented after those evaluations to competent authorities.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: A is an urgent outward communication to potentially affected service recipients about measures responding to a significant cyber threat; B is an internal post-incident evaluation and a conditional, request-based communication to competent authorities about implemented changes.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties do not share the same actor role or core compliance action: A concerns essential/important entities warning affected service recipients, whereas B concerns financial entities evaluating serious ICT disruptions and, if requested, informing competent authorities about resulting changes.
verdict.evidence_span_a: de ontvangers van hun diensten die mogelijkerwijs door een significante cyberdreiging worden getroffen, onverwijld meedelen welke maatregelen die ontvangers kunnen nemen in reactie op die dreiging
verdict.evidence_span_b: Andere financiële entiteiten dan micro-ondernemingen delen op verzoek de bevoegde autoriteiten de wijzigingen mee die na de in de eerste alinea bedoelde ICT-gerelateerde post-incidentevaluaties zijn doorgevoerd.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Norm A requires financial entities to maintain, annually report on, and on request provide an ICT-service contractual-register and related information to competent authorities. Norm B requires importers, before placing a high-risk AI system on the market, to verify the provider’s compliance documentation and markings, and in specified cases to withhold the system and notify the provider, authorised representatives, and market-surveillance authorities.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: The norms concern different regulated activities and event families: ICT-outsourcing register/reporting and supervisory disclosure in Norm A, versus pre-market conformity checks and conditional notification concerning high-risk AI systems in Norm B.
verdict.criterion_fired: Different actor roles and different event families; the duties are not the same compliance work merely directed through different channels.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Financiële entiteiten rapporteren ten minste jaarlijks aan de bevoegde autoriteiten over het aantal nieuwe overeenkomsten inzake het gebruik van ICT-diensten
verdict.evidence_span_b: Alvorens een AI-systeem met een hoog risico in de handel wordt gebracht, zorgen de importeurs ervoor dat het systeem in overeenstemming is met deze verordening door na te gaan of:

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Geen gedeelde compliance-handeling: norm A verplicht onverwijlde kennisgeving aan dienstontvangers; norm B legt civielrechtelijke aansprakelijkheid en schadevergoedings-/regresgevolgen op wegens onrechtmatige verwerking.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is een proactieve incidentmelding door een essentiële of belangrijke entiteit aan haar dienstontvangers; norm B is een aansprakelijkheidsregel voor verwerkingsverantwoordelijken en verwerkers, zonder meldings- of informatieplicht aan een ontvanger.
verdict.criterion_fired: Verschillende kernhandeling, gebeurtenisfamilie en actorrol; norm A betreft incidentcommunicatie, norm B betreft aansprakelijkheid voor schade door verwerkingsinbreuken.
verdict.evidence_span_a: stelt in voorkomend geval onverwijld de ontvangers van haar diensten in kennis van significante incidenten
verdict.evidence_span_b: is aansprakelijk voor de schade die wordt veroorzaakt door verwerking die inbreuk maakt op deze verordening

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A: the lead overseer’s written authorisation must state the applicable coercive fines. B: after reporting a serious incident, the AI provider must promptly investigate it and the AI system, including a risk assessment and corrective measures, while cooperating with authorities and observing restrictions on system changes.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: The norms regulate fundamentally different duties: A concerns the content of an investigative authorisation and possible coercive fines for failure to provide requested records, data, procedures, materials, or answers; B concerns the provider’s post-incident investigation, risk assessment, corrective measures, cooperation, and prior notice before potentially prejudicial system changes.
verdict.criterion_fired: Different core action, event family, and actor role; the apparent similarity is not a repeated compliance duty.
verdict.evidence_span_a: In deze machtiging worden eveneens de in artikel 35, lid 6, bedoelde dwangsommen genoemd
verdict.evidence_span_b: Na de melding van een ernstig incident op grond van lid 1 verricht de aanbieder onverwijld het nodige onderzoek in verband met het ernstige incident en het betrokken AI-systeem.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms involve an information-related compliance activity connected to regulatory oversight, but Norm A requires financial entities to register ICT-related incidents and significant cyber threats, whereas Norm B requires an authorised representative to provide a copy of its mandate to the AI Office upon request and to perform related documentation, information, and cooperation tasks.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an internal, comprehensive incident-and-threat registration and management duty imposed on financial entities; Norm B is an authorised representative’s on-request disclosure and regulatory-cooperation duty concerning an AI-model mandate and compliance documentation.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in actor, triggering event, and substantive action: Norm A concerns registration and management of ICT incidents/cyber threats by financial entities, while Norm B concerns an authorised representative providing mandate and compliance information to the AI Office on request.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Financiële entiteiten registreren alle ICT-gerelateerde incidenten en significante cyberdreigingen.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Hij legt op verzoek een kopie van het mandaat over aan het AI-bureau, in een van de officiële talen van de instellingen van de Unie.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Beide normen leggen een informatie-/documentatiegerichte complianceverplichting op, maar niet dezelfde: Norm A vereist toegangverlening tot specifieke domeinnaamregistratiegegevens na een rechtmatig en gemotiveerd verzoek; Norm B vereist het opstellen en actualiseren van technische documentatie voor een hoog-risico-AI-systeem.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A betreft reactieve verstrekking van domeinnaamregistratiegegevens aan legitieme toegangvragende partijen, met beantwoording binnen 72 uur. Norm B betreft proactieve technische documentatie voor conformiteitsbeoordeling door bevoegde autoriteiten en aangemelde instanties, met inhoud volgens bijlage IV.
verdict.criterion_fired: De normen betreffen verschillende actoren, verschillende compliance-objecten en verschillende doeleinden: toegang tot registratiegegevens op verzoek versus technische documentatie van hoog-risico-AI.
verdict.evidence_span_a: toegang verlenen tot specifieke met gegevens over de registratie van domeinnamen
verdict.evidence_span_b: De technische documentatie van een AI-systeem met een hoog risico wordt opgesteld voordat dit systeem in de handel wordt gebracht of in gebruik wordt gesteld, en wordt geactualiseerd.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Geen gedeelde concrete compliance-actie: norm A vereist medewerking aan en uitvoering van opdrachten van het militair gezag; norm B vereist het onder strikte voorwaarden verwerken, beveiligen, documenteren en verwijderen van bijzondere categorieën persoonsgegevens voor biasdetectie en -correctie.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A betreft een verplichting tot medewerking aan militair gezag bij toepassing van de Oorlogswet; norm B betreft voorwaarden voor uitzonderlijke verwerking van bijzondere persoonsgegevens door aanbieders van hoog-risico-AI-systemen.
verdict.criterion_fired: De normen hebben geen dezelfde kernhandeling, gebeurtenisfamilie of actorrol; zij regelen respectievelijk militaire medewerking en gegevensverwerking voor AI-biascorrectie.
verdict.evidence_span_a: verplicht het militair gezag alle medewerking te verlenen, daaronder begrepen het uitvoeren van door dat gezag gegeven opdrachten
verdict.evidence_span_b: mogen de aanbieders van dergelijke systemen uitzonderlijk bijzondere categorieën persoonsgegevens verwerken, mits passende waarborgen worden geboden

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A requires a telecommunications party, on request, to provide the Minister free of charge with an extract from a legal-entity register concerning a share right, and alternatively to investigate a controlling-interest holder's identity and third-party ties. B requires the provider of a high-risk AI system to prepare and update technical documentation before placing it on the market or putting it into service, demonstrating conformity and supplying information for conformity assessment by competent authorities and notified bodies.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: The norms concern fundamentally different duties and event families: A is an on-request information/investigation duty concerning suspected or anticipated dominant control threatening the public interest; B is ex ante and ongoing technical-documentation and conformity-demonstration duty for a high-risk AI system.
verdict.criterion_fired: Different event family, actor role, and core action; A concerns a telecommunications party responding to a Ministerial request about control over a legal entity, whereas B concerns preparation and updating of high-risk-AI technical documentation for conformity assessment.
verdict.evidence_span_a: verstrekt een telecommunicatiepartij aan Onze Minister op verzoek om niet een uittreksel uit het door de rechtspersoon gehouden register met betrekking tot een recht op een aandeel
verdict.evidence_span_b: De technische documentatie van een AI-systeem met een hoog risico wordt opgesteld voordat dit systeem in de handel wordt gebracht of in gebruik wordt gesteld, en wordt geactualiseerd.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A requires advance notification of cable-maintenance works on public land to the municipal mayor (or authorized official, with onward notification to the mayor). B requires investigation and risk-assessment/corrective measures after a serious AI incident, cooperation with authorities, and prior notice before conducting potentially causally compromising system modifications. These are not the same compliance action.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: A concerns advance notification of planned public-land cable-maintenance works; B concerns post-incident investigation and safeguards for an AI system, including prior notice of potentially compromising modifications.
verdict.criterion_fired: Different underlying action, triggering-event family, and regulated actor/context; the apparent similarity in notification language does not establish duplicated compliance work.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Ingeval de werkzaamheden in verband met de instandhouding van kabels worden verricht in of op openbare gronden, wordt hiervan door de aanbieder tevens voorafgaand aan de uit te voeren werkzaamheden melding gedaan bij de burgemeester van de gemeente binnen wiens grondgebied de werkzaamheden zullen plaatsvinden
verdict.evidence_span_b: verricht geen onderzoek waarbij het AI-systeem wordt gewijzigd op een wijze die van invloed kan zijn op de latere evaluatie van de oorzaken van het incident, zonder de bevoegde autoriteiten daarvan vooraf in kennis te stellen

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require post-incident investigative or evaluative work concerning a serious ICT/AI-related incident, but they require different substantive outputs: A requires a post-incident evaluation identifying causes and improvements, while B requires an immediate investigation including risk assessment and corrective measures, with cooperation and safeguards against altering the system before causal evaluation.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a retrospective ICT post-incident evaluation by a financial entity after disruption of core activities, including analysis of causes, procedural effectiveness, communications, and improvements. Norm B is an investigation by an AI-system provider after reporting a serious incident, including incident risk assessment and corrective measures, plus cooperation with authorities and a restriction on modifying the system before later causal evaluation.
verdict.criterion_fired: The actor role and substantive duty differ: financial entities must conduct a retrospective ICT post-incident evaluation after a disruption of core activities, whereas AI providers must promptly investigate a serious incident involving the AI system and perform a risk assessment and corrective measures. The shared incident-related context is insufficient to establish the same compliance work.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Financiële entiteiten verrichten ICT-gerelateerde post-incidentevaluaties na verstoringen van hun kernactiviteiten ten gevolge van een ernstig ICT-gerelateerd incident, analyseren daarbij de oorzaken van de verstoring en identificeren de verbeteringen die moeten worden aangebracht
verdict.evidence_span_b: Na de melding van een ernstig incident op grond van lid 1 verricht de aanbieder onverwijld het nodige onderzoek in verband met het ernstige incident en het betrokken AI-systeem. Dit omvat een risicobeoordeling van het incident en corrigerende maatregelen.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms impose ongoing organisational/documentation compliance duties on regulated entities, but they do not require the same underlying action: GDPR Article 30 requires maintaining a register of processing activities, while AI Act Article 16 contains multiple high-risk-AI provider obligations, including a quality-management system, documentation/log retention, conformity assessment, registration, corrective measures, and information provision.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a GDPR record-of-processing-activities duty for controllers and, where applicable, their representatives; Norm B is a bundle of product-governance and conformity obligations for providers of high-risk AI systems. The extracted action in B specifically concerns having a quality-management system.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms do not impose the same core action, concern the same event family, or bind the same actor role. A general documentation or organisational character is insufficient to establish duplicated compliance work.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Elke verwerkingsverantwoordelijke en, in voorkomend geval, de vertegenwoordiger van de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke houdt een register van de verwerkingsactiviteiten die onder hun verantwoordelijkheid plaatsvinden.
verdict.evidence_span_b: beschikken over een systeem voor kwaliteitsbeheer dat in overeenstemming is met artikel 17;

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both provisions assign an authorised representative a package of representative functions involving maintaining or providing compliance documentation and cooperating with authorities, but they do not impose the same concrete compliance work: A concerns devices/radio equipment and the Minister, while B concerns general-purpose AI models, the AI Office and competent authorities, and adds verification of the provider's obligations.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm B requires the representative to verify the provider's technical documentation and compliance with Articles 53/55, and its documentation/cooperation duties are tailored to general-purpose AI models and multiple authorities; Norm A concerns holding device/radio-equipment documentation, supplying information to the Minister on request, and assisting with risk-elimination measures.
verdict.criterion_fired: The actor role is similar, but the underlying regulated subject matter and duty package differ: A concerns devices/radio equipment and conformity/risk measures, whereas B concerns general-purpose AI models, provider-obligation verification, AI-office/national-authority documentation access, and AI-model measures.
verdict.evidence_span_a: b) het op verzoek van Onze Minister verstrekken van alle benodigde informatie en documentatie om de conformiteit van de apparaten of radioapparaten aan te tonen;
verdict.evidence_span_b: a) controleren of de aanbieder de in bijlage XI gespecificeerde technische documentatie heeft opgesteld en aan alle in artikel 53 en, indien van toepassing, artikel 55 bedoelde verplichtingen heeft voldaan;

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms involve risk-related measures following or addressing technology-related risks/incidents, but A requires regular testing of ICT-risk controls and continuity measures, whereas B requires the AI provider to investigate a serious incident, assess its risks, and take corrective measures.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a recurring preventive ICT-governance and testing obligation for specified financial entities; Norm B is an incident-triggered investigative and remedial obligation for an AI provider after reporting a serious incident.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in both the underlying action and actor role: A requires periodic testing of ICT-risk-management plans, measures, and controls, while B requires post-incident investigation, risk assessment, and corrective measures by an AI provider.
verdict.evidence_span_a: de in punt f) bedoelde plannen en maatregelen, alsmede de doeltreffendheid van de overeenkomstig de punten a) en c) uitgevoerde controles regelmatig testen
verdict.evidence_span_b: Dit omvat een risicobeoordeling van het incident en corrigerende maatregelen.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern maintaining or documenting information in connection with regulated ICT/AI operations, but they do not impose the same underlying compliance action: Norm A requires financial entities to keep accessible operational registers during activated ICT continuity/response plans, whereas Norm B permits exceptional processing of special-category personal data for bias detection and correction, subject to safeguards and recording the necessity reasons.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an operational record-keeping duty triggered by activation of ICT continuity and response/recovery plans; Norm B is a narrowly conditioned permission and safeguard regime for processing special-category personal data to detect and correct bias in high-risk AI systems.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms differ in actor, trigger, and substantive action: accessible incident/continuity registers versus exceptional sensitive-data processing and bias-mitigation safeguards.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Financiële entiteiten houden gemakkelijk toegankelijke registers bij van hun activiteiten vóór en tijdens storingen wanneer hun ICT-bedrijfscontinuïteitsplannen en ICT-respons- en herstelplannen worden geactiveerd.
verdict.evidence_span_b: mogen de aanbieders van dergelijke systemen uitzonderlijk bijzondere categorieën persoonsgegevens verwerken, mits passende waarborgen worden geboden voor de grondrechten en fundamentele vrijheden van natuurlijke personen.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both concern managing security/ICT risks and responding to security-related incidents, but A requires an urgent external notification of a qualifying personal-data security breach, whereas B requires ongoing ICT-risk-management measures and, where applicable, incorporation of operational lessons from testing and post-incident analysis into the risk-assessment process.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an event-triggered notification duty to the Dutch data-protection authority; Norm B is a continuing internal ICT-risk-management and resilience duty, with documentation/evaluation and possible submission of an evaluation report on request to the competent authority.
verdict.criterion_fired: The underlying action and actor role differ: A requires a public electronic communications service provider to notify the Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens of a qualifying security breach without delay; B requires specified financial entities to establish and maintain ICT-risk controls, monitor systems, mitigate risks, and incorporate operational conclusions. The shared security/incident context is insufficient to make the compliance work duplicative.
verdict.evidence_span_a: stelt de Autoriteit persoonsgegevens onverwijld in kennis van een inbreuk op de beveiliging
verdict.evidence_span_b: een degelijk en gedocumenteerd kader voor ICT-risicobeheer tot stand brengen en handhaven

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Geen gedeelde compliance-actie: norm A verplicht nummerhouders de nummergebruikers te registreren; norm B verplicht aanbieders van hoog-risico-AI-systemen technische documentatie op te stellen, te actualiseren en daarin conformiteitsinformatie te verstrekken.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: De normen betreffen verschillende gereguleerde objecten en verplichtingen: registratie van gebruikers van nummers versus technische documentatie voor hoog-risico-AI-systemen.
verdict.criterion_fired: Verschillende kernactie, actorrol en event-/objectfamilie; er is geen dubbele compliance-werkzaamheid.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Nummerhouders registreren binnen zes maanden na de inwerkingtreding van artikel 4.9, derde lid, onderdeel b, de nummergebruikers.
verdict.evidence_span_b: De technische documentatie van een AI-systeem met een hoog risico wordt opgesteld voordat dit systeem in de handel wordt gebracht of in gebruik wordt gesteld, en wordt geactualiseerd.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A concerns the lead overseer imposing a coercive fine on a critical ICT third-party provider for non-compliance with supervisory measures; B requires providers of systemic-risk general-purpose AI models to assess and mitigate risks, maintain and document information on serious incidents and corrective measures, report it urgently to the AI Office and possibly national authorities, and ensure cybersecurity protection.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: The norms concern fundamentally different duties and event families: enforcement of supervisory measures through a coercive fine versus incident-related information management and reporting by an AI-model provider.
verdict.criterion_fired: Different core action, event family, and actor role; A is an enforcement power exercised by a lead overseer, while B is a substantive incident-reporting and risk-management obligation imposed on an AI-model provider.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De in lid 6 bedoelde dwangsom wordt dagelijks opgelegd
verdict.evidence_span_b: relevante informatie over ernstige incidenten en mogelijke corrigerende maatregelen bijhouden, documenteren en onverwijld rapporteren aan het AI-bureau en, in voorkomend geval, aan de nationale bevoegde autoriteiten

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern supplying information or documentation to, and engaging with, public authorities in the AI/data-governance sphere, but they do not impose the same underlying compliance action. Norm A requires a controller to report a personal-data breach with specified incident details; Norm B requires an authorised representative to perform mandate-based tasks, retain technical documentation, provide information/documentation on reasoned request, and cooperate with authorities regarding a general-purpose AI model.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an incident-notification duty imposed on a personal-data controller and directed to a supervisory authority; Norm B is a broader representative-function duty concerning AI-model compliance, including document retention, production on request, and cooperation with the AI Office and competent authorities.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms differ in actor role, triggering event, and operative action: GDPR breach notification versus AI representative documentation, retention, and cooperation duties.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require maintaining or preparing documented information, but they concern different subject matter and serve different compliance purposes: ICT-service contractual-register documentation versus general-purpose AI-model documentation and disclosures.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Beide normen houden verband met ernstige/significante incidenten, maar norm A verplicht de entiteit tot onverwijlde melding/kennisgeving; norm B verplicht de aanbieder na een melding tot onderzoek, risicobeoordeling en corrigerende maatregelen.

verdict.evidence_span_a: Elke lidstaat zorgt ervoor dat essentiële en belangrijke entiteiten elk incident dat aanzienlijke gevolgen heeft voor de verlening van hun diensten als bedoeld in lid 3 (significant incident) onverwijld meldt bij zijn CSIRT of, indien van toepassing, zijn bevoegde autoriteit overeenkomstig lid 4.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Na de melding van een ernstig incident op grond van lid 1 verricht de aanbieder onverwijld het nodige onderzoek in verband met het ernstige incident en het betrokken AI-systeem. Dit omvat een risicobeoordeling van het incident en corrigerende maatregelen.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both provisions concern supplying information or reports to a public supervisory body in the digital/cyber domain, but they do not impose the same reporting duty. Norm A requires affected entities to report a significant incident through staged incident notifications and reports; Norm B empowers the lead overseer to request post-oversight reports describing actions or corrective measures taken in response to recommendations.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a mandatory, time-bound incident-reporting regime triggered by a significant incident and directed to the CSIRT or competent authority. Norm B is a supervisory power to request reports from critical ICT third-party providers after oversight activities, concerning actions or corrective measures relating to recommendations.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in both the triggering event and the actor role: A concerns affected entities reporting a significant incident, while B concerns critical ICT third-party providers responding to a lead overseer’s post-oversight request about corrective actions. The shared reporting/information-supply aspect and broadly supervisory recipients are insufficient to establish duplicate compliance work.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Beide normen houden verband met het verkrijgen of beschikbaar maken van informatie/documentatie, maar norm A betreft een toezichtsbevoegdheid om verkeersoverzichten op te vragen, terwijl norm B aanbieders verplicht technische en andere documentatie op te stellen, bij te houden en beschikbaar te stellen.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern managing risks associated with digital or data-processing activities, but Norm A requires prior consultation of a supervisory authority, whereas Norm B requires establishing and maintaining an ICT-risk-management framework, including identifying key dependencies on ICT third-party providers.

verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in core action, triggering context, and actor scope: prior consultation with a data-protection supervisory authority versus ongoing ICT-risk-management measures and mapping dependencies on ICT service providers.

verdict.criterion_fired: De normen leggen verschillende kernhandelingen op aan verschillende actoren in verschillende contexten: advies inwinnen voor een gegevensbeschermingseffectbeoordeling versus cyberbeveiligingsmaatregelen bepalen en daarbij toeleveringsketenrisico-informatie meewegen.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Wanneer een functionaris voor gegevensbescherming is aangewezen, wint de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke bij het uitvoeren van een gegevensbeschermingseffectbeoordeling diens advies in.
verdict.evidence_span_b: De lidstaten zorgen er ook voor dat de entiteiten, wanneer zij overwegen welke maatregelen als bedoeld in lid 2, punt d), passend zijn, rekening moeten houden met de resultaten van de overeenkomstig artikel 22, lid 1, uitgevoerde gecoördineerde beveiligingsrisicobeoordelingen van kritieke toeleveringsketens.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both involve handling or maintaining access to information, but A requires responding to a legitimate, reasoned request for access to specific domain-registration data, whereas B requires a processor to maintain a register containing specified categories of processing-activity information.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an external, time-limited access-response duty concerning specific domain-registration data; Norm B is an ongoing internal record-keeping duty concerning processing activities and specified GDPR compliance information.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in core action, triggering context, actor role, recipient relationship, and required content: A answers an access request within 72 hours, while B maintains a processing-activities register.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De registers voor topleveldomeinnamen en de entiteiten die domeinnaamregistratiediensten verlenen beantwoorden een verzoek om toegang als bedoeld in het eerste lid onverwijld of, indien dat niet mogelijk is, binnen 72 uur na ontvangst van het verzoek.
verdict.evidence_span_b: De verwerker, en, in voorkomend geval, de vertegenwoordiger van de verwerker houdt een register van alle categorieën van verwerkingsactiviteiten die zij ten behoeve van een verwerkingsverantwoordelijke hebben verricht.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Geen gedeelde compliance-actie: norm A verplicht nummerhouders tot registratie van nummergebruikers en rechtsgevolg voor nummergebruik; norm B betreft taken van een gemachtigde van een aanbieder van een AI-model voor algemene doeleinden, waaronder documentatiebeheer, informatieverstrekking en samenwerking met autoriteiten.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: De normen hebben verschillende onderwerpen, actoren, triggers en verplichtingen: nummerregistratie en ingebruikgeving van een nummer tegenover vertegenwoordiging en toezichtsondersteuning voor AI-modelaanbieders.
verdict.criterion_fired: Verschillende kernactie, gebeurtenisfamilie en actorrol; er is geen betekenisvolle overlap in de feitelijk te verrichten compliancewerkzaamheden.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Nummerhouders registreren binnen zes maanden na de inwerkingtreding van artikel 4.9, derde lid, onderdeel b, de nummergebruikers.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Hij legt op verzoek een kopie van het mandaat over aan het AI-bureau, in een van de officiële talen van de instellingen van de Unie.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require proactive cybersecurity risk-management capabilities, but Norm A requires implementing proportionate technical, operational, and organisational measures to manage network-and-information-system security risks and prevent or mitigate incidents, whereas Norm B requires deploying sufficient resources and capabilities to monitor user activity and detect ICT anomalies and ICT-related incidents.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a broad preventive and mitigating risk-management duty imposed on essential and important entities; Norm B is a financial-entity detection and monitoring duty focused on user activity, ICT anomalies, and ICT-related incidents.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties are not the same core action and do not bind the same actor role: A requires implementation of risk-management measures by essential and important entities, while B requires monitoring and detection capabilities by financial entities. The shared cybersecurity subject matter does not make the compliance work duplicative.
verdict.evidence_span_a: passende en evenredige technische, operationele en organisatorische maatregelen nemen om de risico’s voor de beveiliging van de netwerk- en informatiesystemen
verdict.evidence_span_b: voldoende middelen en capaciteiten in om toezicht te houden op activiteiten van gebruikers en het optreden van ICT-anomalieën en ICT-gerelateerde incidenten

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms involve maintaining or documenting information in a register, but they require different underlying compliance work: Norm A requires financial entities to document ICT-service contractual agreements and maintain an ICT third-party-service information register; Norm B requires providers of high-risk AI systems to record the reasons justifying exceptional processing of special-category personal data for bias detection and correction.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A concerns ICT outsourcing contracts and reporting or making an ICT-service register available to competent authorities; Norm B concerns the data-protection justification for exceptional processing of special-category personal data in high-risk AI systems.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties concern different subject matter, triggering circumstances, and actor roles: ICT-service contractual arrangements of financial entities versus exceptional processing of special-category personal data by high-risk-AI providers.
