verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A betreft een verzoekgestuurde verstrekking van een registeruittreksel over een aandeelhoudersrecht of een onderzoek naar de identiteit van een zeggenschapshouder in verband met mogelijke overwegende zeggenschap. Norm B betreft doorlopende technische documentatie over een AI-model voor algemene doeleinden, die op verzoek beschikbaar moet kunnen worden gesteld aan het AI-bureau en nationale bevoegde autoriteiten.
verdict.criterion_fired: De normen hebben niet dezelfde actorrol of gebeurtenisfamilie en vereisen inhoudelijk ander werk; een oppervlakkige overeenkomst in verstrekking aan een overheidsinstantie is onvoldoende voor een dubbele compliance-last.
verdict.evidence_span_a: verstrekt een telecommunicatiepartij aan Onze Minister op verzoek om niet een uittreksel uit het door de rechtspersoon gehouden register met betrekking tot een recht op een aandeel
verdict.evidence_span_b: de technische documentatie van het model opstellen en up-to-date houden, inclusief het trainings- en testproces en de resultaten van de evaluatie ervan, die ten minste de in bijlage XI vermelde informatie moet bevatten, zodat deze op verzoek aan het AI-bureau en de nationale bevoegde autoriteiten kunnen worden verstrekt

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require an actor to prepare or provide information/documentation, but Norm A requires registration information to be supplied to the Dutch minister, whereas Norm B requires AI-model providers to create, maintain, and make available technical and user-facing documentation, primarily for AI-system providers and on request for authorities.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A concerns supplying entity-identification and registration data for a national register, with changes reported within two weeks; Norm B concerns ongoing technical, compliance, and training-content documentation for general-purpose AI models and making it available to downstream AI-system providers and authorities on request.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in actor role, subject matter, purpose, and recipient: Norm A is a registration-information duty for covered entities, while Norm B is a documentation and disclosure duty for providers of general-purpose AI models. The apparent similarity is limited to information-related wording.
verdict.evidence_span_a: verstrekt ten behoeve van de registratie in het nationale register, bedoeld in artikel 43, aan Onze Minister de volgende informatie
verdict.evidence_span_b: informatie en documentatie opstellen, up-to-date houden en beschikbaar stellen voor aanbieders van AI-systemen die het AI-model voor algemene doeleinden in hun AI-systemen willen integreren

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require an entity to establish or maintain compliance-related information procedures or documentation, but they do not impose the same verb-level duty: Norm A requires setting and publishing policies and procedures to ensure accurate and complete domain-registration data; Norm B requires an authorised representative to keep specified AI technical documentation available for ten years and provide it to authorities on request.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A concerns establishing and publishing verification policies and procedures for a domain-name registration database. Norm B concerns retaining and supplying AI-model technical documentation and cooperating with authorities.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in actor role, subject matter, and core action: domain-name registries/registration-service entities must establish and publish database-accuracy procedures, whereas an AI-model provider's authorised representative must retain and furnish technical documentation to AI authorities.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De registers voor topleveldomeinnamen en de entiteiten die domeinnaamregistratiediensten verlenen stellen het beleid en de procedures vast, waaronder verificatieprocedures
verdict.evidence_span_b: een kopie van de in bijlage XI gespecificeerde technische documentatie beschikbaar houden voor het AI-bureau en de nationale autoriteiten gedurende een periode van tien jaar

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Geen gedeelde compliance-actie: norm A betreft de tegenwerpelijkheid van een inschrijving in een aandeelhoudersregister na een verzoek tot uitlevering; norm B betreft taken en bevoegdheden van een gemachtigde van een aanbieder van een AI-model voor algemene doeleinden, waaronder documentatiebeheer, informatieverstrekking en samenwerking met autoriteiten.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is een civielrechtelijk effect van een registerinschrijving in de context van uitlevering van een aandelenbelang; norm B legt organisatorische, documentatie- en medewerkingsverplichtingen op aan een AI-gemachtigde.
verdict.criterion_fired: De normen hebben noch dezelfde kernhandeling, noch dezelfde gebeurtenisfamilie of actorrol; de oppervlakkige overeenkomst in formulering/addressee leidt niet tot dezelfde compliance-last.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De inschrijving in het aandeelhoudersregister kan worden tegengeworpen aan een ieder
verdict.evidence_span_b: Hij legt op verzoek een kopie van het mandaat over aan het AI-bureau, in een van de officiële talen van de instellingen van de Unie.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A imposes a daily coercive fine on a critical ICT third-party provider for non-compliance with supervisory measures; B requires a system provider to confirm in writing to national competent authorities that another qualified notified body will temporarily monitor and assume responsibility for certificates during a suspension or restriction.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: The norms concern different actors, different event families, and different underlying actions: enforcement of supervisory measures versus arranging and confirming temporary certificate monitoring.
verdict.criterion_fired: Different actor role and different event family; the provisions impose distinct measures rather than repeated reporting or performance of the same compliance work.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De in lid 6 bedoelde dwangsom wordt dagelijks opgelegd tot aan de verplichtingen is voldaan
verdict.evidence_span_b: bevestigt de aanbieder van het systeem waarop het certificaat betrekking heeft binnen drie maanden na de schorsing of beperking aan de nationale bevoegde autoriteiten van de lidstaat waar hij zijn geregistreerde vestigingsplaats heeft via schriftelijke weg dat in plaats van de aangemelde instantie een andere gekwalificeerde aangemelde instantie tijdelijk de certificaten tijdens de periode van schorsing of beperking zal monitoren en er de verantwoordelijkheid voor zal dragen

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Geen gedeelde concrete compliance-actie: norm A verplicht het onverwijld openbaar maken van niet-persoonsgebonden domeinnaamregistratiegegevens; norm B verplicht het opstellen en actualiseren van technische documentatie voor een hoog-risico-AI-systeem.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A betreft publieke openbaarmaking van domeinnaamregistratiegegevens na registratie; norm B betreft interne technische documentatie en beschikbaarstelling daarvan aan bevoegde autoriteiten en aangemelde instanties voor conformiteitsbeoordeling.
verdict.criterion_fired: De normen hebben niet dezelfde kernhandeling, gebeurtenisfamilie of actorrol. A ziet op registers en aanbieders van domeinnaamregistratiediensten die gegevens openbaar maken; B ziet op aanbieders van hoog-risico-AI-systemen die technische documentatie opstellen en actualiseren.
verdict.evidence_span_a: onverwijld na de registratie van een domeinnaam, de domeinnaamregistratiegegevens die geen persoonsgegevens zijn, openbaar maken
verdict.evidence_span_b: De technische documentatie van een AI-systeem met een hoog risico wordt opgesteld voordat dit systeem in de handel wordt gebracht of in gebruik wordt gesteld, en wordt geactualiseerd.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A requires essential and important entities to provide identification, contact, sector/subsector, and cross-border service information to competent authorities, and to report changes. B concerns investigators' written authorisation specifying possible coercive fines if third-party ICT service providers fail to provide requested records, data, procedures, materials, or answers. It does not itself impose that provision duty on the same actor.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an entity-registration and change-notification obligation; Norm B is an investigative-authorisation rule concerning possible coercive fines for non-compliance with information requests to third-party ICT service providers.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms do not impose the same core action on the same actor in response to the same event. A requires entities to provide and update registry information; B regulates the contents of investigators' authorisations and possible fines relating to failure by third-party ICT service providers to answer investigative requests.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De in lid 3 bedoelde entiteiten melden onmiddellijk elke wijziging in de bijzonderheden die zij op grond van de eerste alinea van dit lid hebben ingediend, en in elk geval binnen twee weken na de datum van de wijziging.
verdict.evidence_span_b: In deze machtiging worden eveneens de in artikel 35, lid 6, bedoelde dwangsommen genoemd die kunnen worden opgelegd indien de vereiste registers, data, gedocumenteerde procedures of enig ander materiaal, dan wel de antwoorden op vragen van de onderzoekers aan vertegenwoordigers van derde aanbieders van ICT-diensten, niet of niet volledig worden verstrekt.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both provisions concern imposing a monetary coercive or punitive measure on an entity, but they do not require the same underlying compliance work: Norm A concerns a daily coercive penalty to compel a critical ICT third-party provider to comply with supervisory measures, while Norm B concerns fines imposed on an AI provider for an allegedly incorrect non-high-risk classification intended to evade Chapter III, Section 2 requirements.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an enforcement mechanism for non-compliance with supervisory measures after notice and a minimum 30-day period; Norm B is a sanction for intentional or otherwise improper AI-risk classification identified during market-authority review.
verdict.criterion_fired: Different underlying duty and event: the provisions impose distinct enforcement sanctions for distinct violations, involving different regulated actors and regulatory contexts; similarity of the phrase 'imposed' and monetary consequences is insufficient.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De in lid 6 bedoelde dwangsom wordt dagelijks opgelegd tot aan de verplichtingen is voldaan
verdict.evidence_span_b: worden aan de aanbieder overeenkomstig artikel 99 geldboeten opgelegd

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern organisational cybersecurity/ICT-risk-management measures, but A requires entities to take supplier-related cybersecurity considerations into account when selecting supply-chain measures, whereas B requires specified financial entities to develop staff cybersecurity-awareness and digital operational-resilience training programmes.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a supply-chain risk-assessment/design consideration concerning direct suppliers and service providers; Norm B is a personnel awareness and training programme obligation within a simplified ICT-risk-management framework.
verdict.criterion_fired: The underlying actions, subject matter, and operative duties differ: A concerns considering supplier vulnerabilities, product quality, and suppliers’ cybersecurity practices when determining supply-chain measures; B concerns developing cybersecurity-awareness and digital-operational-resilience training for personnel and managers. Neither imposes a reporting or notification duty, and the shared broad cybersecurity context is insufficient for duplicate burden.
verdict.evidence_span_a: rekening houden met de specifieke kwetsbaarheden van elke rechtstreekse leverancier en dienstverlener en met de algemene kwaliteit van de producten en de cyberbeveiligingspraktijken van hun leveranciers en dienstverleners, met inbegrip van hun veilige ontwikkelingsprocedures
verdict.evidence_span_b: bewustmakingsprogramma’s op het gebied van ICT-beveiliging en opleiding inzake digitale operationele weerbaarheid voor personeel en leidinggevenden ontwikkelen

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms impose an information/record-related compliance duty, but Norm A requires registration of number users, whereas Norm B requires importers to provide information and documentation to competent authorities on a reasoned request and ensure technical documentation is available.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a one-time registration duty concerning number users, with a six-month implementation deadline; Norm B is a request-triggered authority-information/documentation duty concerning high-risk AI-system conformity, supplemented by availability of technical documentation and related record-keeping context.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in actor role, triggering event, operative action, recipient relationship, and substantive content; they do not require the same compliance work to be repeated.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Nummerhouders registreren binnen zes maanden na de inwerkingtreding van artikel 4.9, derde lid, onderdeel b, de nummergebruikers.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Importeurs verstrekken ter staving van de conformiteit van een AI-systeem met een hoog risico met de eisen van afdeling 2, de relevante bevoegde autoriteiten op met redenen omkleed verzoek alle nodige informatie en documentatie

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Beide normen vereisen het nemen of bewerkstelligen van corrigerende maatregelen om een niet-conform systeem of beveiligingsmaatregel in overeenstemming te brengen. Norm B bevat daarnaast een afzonderlijke onmiddellijke kennisgevingsplicht aan de aanbieder/importeur en bevoegde autoriteiten, met een uitvoerige beschrijving van de non-conformiteit en maatregelen.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A betreft een entiteit die vaststelt dat zij niet voldoet aan cyberbeveiligingsrisicobeheersmaatregelen en vereist onverwijlde corrigerende maatregelen. Norm B betreft specifiek een distributeur van een hoog-risico-AI-systeem die non-conformiteit vaststelt; hij moet het systeem corrigeren, uit de handel nemen of terugroepen, dan wel ervoor zorgen dat andere marktdeelnemers dit doen, en bij een risico tevens onmiddellijk kennisgeven.
verdict.criterion_fired: De actorrol verschilt wezenlijk en de concrete verplichtingen hebben een andere sectorspecifieke inhoud: algemene cyberbeveiligingsmaatregelen van een entiteit tegenover markttoezicht- en productconformiteitsmaatregelen van een AI-distributeur. De gedeelde term 'corrigerende maatregelen' en een vergelijkbare non-conformiteitstrigger maken dit hoogstens oppervlakkig vergelijkbaar, niet dezelfde compliance-last.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De lidstaten zien erop toe dat een entiteit die vaststelt dat zij niet voldoet aan de in lid 2 bedoelde maatregelen, onverwijld alle noodzakelijke, passende en evenredige corrigerende maatregelen neemt.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Een distributeur die van mening is of redenen heeft om, op grond van de informatie waarover hij beschikt, aan te nemen dat een AI-systeem met een hoog risico dat hij op de markt heeft aangeboden, niet in overeenstemming is met de eisen van afdeling 2, neemt de noodzakelijke corrigerende maatregelen om dat systeem in overeenstemming te brengen met deze eisen, uit de handel te nemen of terug te roepen of zorgt ervoor dat de aanbieder, de importeur of een eventuele betrokken operator, waar passend, dergelijke corrigerende maatregelen treft.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Beide normen raken aan het delen of rapporteren van cyber-/incidentgerelateerde informatie, maar norm A stelt een vrijwillige informatie-uitwisselingsmogelijkheid vast, terwijl norm B aanbieders verplicht relevante informatie over ernstige incidenten en mogelijke corrigerende maatregelen bij te houden, te documenteren en onverwijld aan autoriteiten te rapporteren.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A betreft vrijwillige onderlinge uitwisseling van zeer brede cyberbeveiligingsinformatie tussen entiteiten; norm B betreft een verplichte, onverwijlde rapportage door aanbieders van AI-modellen met systeemrisico aan het AI-bureau en eventueel nationale bevoegde autoriteiten, met specifieke informatie over ernstige incidenten en corrigerende maatregelen.
verdict.criterion_fired: De normen hebben geen dezelfde actorrol en geen dezelfde kernverplichting: A verplicht lidstaten een vrijwillige uitwisselingsregeling mogelijk te maken, terwijl B AI-modelaanbieders verplichten informatie bij te houden, te documenteren en onverwijld aan autoriteiten te rapporteren.
verdict.evidence_span_a: op vrijwillige basis onderling relevante informatie over cyberbeveiliging kunnen uitwisselen, met inbegrip van informatie over cyberdreigingen, bijna-incidenten, kwetsbaarheden
verdict.evidence_span_b: relevante informatie over ernstige incidenten en mogelijke corrigerende maatregelen bijhouden, documenteren en onverwijld rapporteren aan het AI-bureau en, in voorkomend geval, aan de nationale bevoegde autoriteiten

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both involve communicating information to an authority or responsible entity concerning an incident, but A requires prompt notification of a personal-data breach, whereas B requires providing an estimate of aggregated annual costs and losses from serious ICT-related incidents upon request.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an immediate processor-to-controller notification duty triggered by knowledge of a personal-data breach; Norm B is a request-based financial-impact estimate supplied by certain financial entities to competent authorities and concerns aggregated annual costs and losses from serious ICT incidents.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in both actor role and core action/content: A requires informing the controller without undue delay about a personal-data breach, while B requires requested cost-and-loss estimation for serious ICT incidents to competent authorities.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De verwerker informeert de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke zonder onredelijke vertraging zodra hij kennis heeft genomen van een inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Andere financiële entiteiten dan micro-ondernemingen verstrekken de bevoegde autoriteiten op hun verzoek een raming van de geaggregeerde jaarlijkse kosten en verliezen als gevolg van ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incidenten.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both provisions concern regulatory oversight or certification-related compliance, but they do not require the same underlying action: Norm A requires submission to an on-site inspection, while Norm B requires confirmation and temporary reassignment of certificate monitoring responsibilities.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A imposes cooperation with an inspection ordered by the lead overseer; Norm B concerns the continued validity of certificates after suspension or limitation and, in specified circumstances, a written confirmation to national competent authorities that another qualified notified body will temporarily monitor them.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in actor, triggering situation, action, and purpose: inspection cooperation under Norm A versus certification-monitoring arrangements and confirmation following suspension or limitation under Norm B.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De kritieke derde aanbieder van ICT-diensten onderwerpt zich aan de inspecties ter plaatse die bij besluit van de lead overseer zijn gelast.
verdict.evidence_span_b: bevestigt de aanbieder van het systeem waarop het certificaat betrekking heeft binnen drie maanden na de schorsing of beperking aan de nationale bevoegde autoriteiten van de lidstaat waar hij zijn geregistreerde vestigingsplaats heeft via schriftelijke weg dat in plaats van de aangemelde instantie een andere gekwalificeerde aangemelde instantie tijdelijk de certificaten tijdens de periode van schorsing of beperking zal monitoren en er de verantwoordelijkheid voor zal dragen.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both provisions concern a formal regulatory action connected with a regulated activity, but A requires the municipal authority to issue an approval/consent decision, whereas B requires notified bodies to inform the notifying authority about specified conformity-assessment matters.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a municipal decision-making duty following a written cable-works notification; Norm B is an information-reporting duty by notified conformity-assessment bodies concerning certificates, accreditation conditions, requests, and activities.
verdict.criterion_fired: Different core action, triggering event, and actor role; the apparent similarity is not a duplicated compliance burden.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Burgemeester en wethouders nemen het instemmingsbesluit binnen acht weken na ontvangst van de schriftelijke melding
verdict.evidence_span_b: Aangemelde instanties brengen de aanmeldende autoriteit op de hoogte van:

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require maintaining and making technical documentation available, but they concern different regulated products, purposes, and information recipients. Norm A requires an authorised representative to retain an EU declaration of conformity and technical documentation for ten years and provide information/documentation to the Dutch Minister on request. Norm B requires providers of general-purpose AI models to prepare and keep updated extensive model documentation, make it available on request to the AI Office and national competent authorities, and provide documentation to AI-system providers for compliance purposes.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A concerns an authorised representative for apparatus/radio equipment and conformity documentation retained for a fixed ten-year period; Norm B concerns providers of general-purpose AI models and model-development, copyright, downstream-provider, and training-content documentation.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms do not impose the same underlying duty: although both mention technical documentation and possible provision to authorities, Norm A is a ten-year retention and on-request conformity-support duty for an authorised representative concerning apparatus/radio equipment, while Norm B imposes broader documentation, downstream-information, copyright-policy, and public-summary duties on AI-model providers.
verdict.evidence_span_a: het ter beschikking van Onze Minister houden van de EU-conformiteitsverklaring en de technische documentatie gedurende tien jaar nadat het apparaat of het radioapparaat in de handel is gebracht
verdict.evidence_span_b: de technische documentatie van het model opstellen en up-to-date houden, inclusief het trainings- en testproces en de resultaten van de evaluatie ervan, die ten minste de in bijlage XI vermelde informatie moet bevatten, zodat deze op verzoek aan het AI-bureau en de nationale bevoegde autoriteiten kunnen worden verstrekt

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern communicating information about an ICT/security incident, but A requires incident-notification content to include whether the incident may have cross-border effects, while B requires a crisis-communication plan enabling responsible disclosure of serious ICT incidents or vulnerabilities to clients, counterparties, and potentially the public.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a specific content requirement within an early-warning notification to an authority or other notification recipient; Norm B is an organisational planning and external-communication requirement directed at clients, counterparties, and potentially the public.
verdict.criterion_fired: Same incident family and actor role, but the underlying duties, recipients, purposes, and required content differ: A concerns stating the possible cross-border effects of a significant incident in an early warning; B concerns maintaining crisis-communication plans for responsible disclosure of serious ICT incidents or vulnerabilities to clients, counterparties, and possibly the public.
verdict.evidence_span_a: geeft de entiteit aan of het significante incident grensoverschrijdende gevolgen kan hebben
verdict.evidence_span_b: beschikken financiële entiteiten over crisiscommunicatieplannen die het mogelijk maken ten minste ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incidenten of kwetsbaarheden op verantwoordelijke wijze bekend te maken aan cliënten en tegenpartijen en, in voorkomend geval, aan het publiek

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms involve making information available to an authority or other entitled requester, but they do not require the same underlying compliance work: Norm A requires domain-registration entities to grant access to specific domain-registration data upon a lawful, justified request, within 72 hours; Norm B requires an AI-model provider's authorised representative to keep specified technical documentation and the provider's contact details available for ten years, and separately to provide information or cooperate upon request.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A concerns responding to access requests for domain-name registration data; Norm B concerns an authorised representative's AI-governance duties, especially long-term retention/availability of technical documentation and contact details.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in actor, subject matter, and operative action: Norm A imposes a 72-hour access-response duty on domain-name registries and registration-service providers, whereas Norm B imposes retention/availability and AI-compliance cooperation duties on an authorised representative of a general-purpose AI-model provider.
verdict.evidence_span_a: verzoeken om toegang onverwijld en in elk geval binnen 72 uur na ontvangst van het verzoek beantwoorden
verdict.evidence_span_b: een kopie van de in bijlage XI gespecificeerde technische documentatie beschikbaar houden voor het AI-bureau en de nationale autoriteiten gedurende een periode van tien jaar

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms involve providing information to a public authority, but Norm A requires registration information and updates to the national register, whereas Norm B concerns an authorised representative’s broader AI-compliance functions, including cooperation and supplying information or documentation on a reasoned request.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a standing registration-information duty for specified entities, including updates within two weeks of a change; Norm B is a mandate-based AI representative duty involving document retention, cooperation, and responsive disclosure to the AI Office and competent authorities.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in actor role, triggering context, and substantive content: Norm A concerns supplying entity-registration data to the national minister, while Norm B concerns an AI-model representative’s compliance, retention, cooperation, and requested disclosure duties.
verdict.evidence_span_a: verstrekt ten behoeve van de registratie in het nationale register, bedoeld in artikel 43, aan Onze Minister de volgende informatie middels het daarvoor opgezette mechanisme:
verdict.evidence_span_b: het verstrekken aan het AI-bureau, na een met redenen omkleed verzoek, van alle informatie en documentatie, waaronder die in punt b), die nodig is om aan te tonen dat de verplichtingen van dit hoofdstuk worden nageleefd;

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms involve an entity communicating or carrying out something for a public authority, but the underlying duties are not the same: A requires broad cooperation and execution of military-authority orders, whereas B requires supplying entity-identification details and promptly reporting changes to competent authorities.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an open-ended military-emergency cooperation and order-execution duty triggered by application of Article 31 of the Dutch War Act; Norm B is a specific cybersecurity-register information and update-reporting duty concerning entity particulars.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in both core action and event family: A concerns compliance with military-authority requests/orders during application of the War Act, while B concerns providing and updating registration information for cybersecurity-authority listing.
verdict.evidence_span_a: verplicht het militair gezag alle medewerking te verlenen, daaronder begrepen het uitvoeren van door dat gezag gegeven opdrachten
verdict.evidence_span_b: melden onmiddellijk elke wijziging in de bijzonderheden die zij op grond van de eerste alinea van dit lid hebben ingediend, en in elk geval binnen twee weken na de datum van de wijziging

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A requires making the GDPR processing-activities register available to a supervisory authority on request. B, as extracted, requires high-risk AI providers to perform multiple product-compliance duties; its specifically extracted action is to display the provider's name/trade name/trademark and contact address on the AI system, packaging, or accompanying documentation. These are not the same compliance action.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an on-request disclosure of a processing-activities register to a supervisory authority; Norm B concerns provider/product compliance and, in the extracted action, identification labelling of a high-risk AI system. The apparent similarity does not establish a shared triggering event or duplicated work.
verdict.criterion_fired: Different underlying action, event family, and actor role; the norms do not impose the same or substantially overlapping compliance work.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Desgevraagd stellen de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke of de verwerker en, in voorkomend geval, de vertegenwoordiger van de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke of de verwerker het register ter beschikking van de toezichthoudende autoriteit.
verdict.evidence_span_b: vermelden op het AI-systeem met een hoog risico of, wanneer dit niet mogelijk is, op de verpakking of in de bij het product gevoegde documentatie, naargelang het geval, hun naam, geregistreerde handelsnaam of geregistreerd merk en hun contactadres;

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Geen gedeelde compliance-actie: norm A verplicht een kritieke ICT-dienstaanbieder inspecties ter plaatse te ondergaan; norm B voorziet in het opleggen van geldboeten aan een AI-aanbieder na een onjuiste risicoclassificatie.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A betreft medewerking aan een door de lead overseer gelaste inspectie; norm B betreft een sanctie wegens het ten onrechte indelen van een AI-systeem als niet-hoog-risico. De mogelijke overeenkomst is slechts dat beide toezicht en handhaving betreffen.
verdict.criterion_fired: Verschillende kernactie, gebeurtenisfamilie en actorrol; dit is geen dubbele rapportage- of informatieverplichting.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De kritieke derde aanbieder van ICT-diensten onderwerpt zich aan de inspecties ter plaatse die bij besluit van de lead overseer zijn gelast.
verdict.evidence_span_b: worden aan de aanbieder overeenkomstig artikel 99 geldboeten opgelegd.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both concern handling communications about serious/significant ICT incidents, but A requires the affected entity to submit a progress report to a CSIRT or competent authority, whereas B requires a financial entity to maintain crisis-communication capability for disclosure to clients, counterparties, and potentially the public.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an incident-reporting duty to a cybersecurity authority during an ongoing significant incident; Norm B is a crisis-communication planning and disclosure duty directed to clients, counterparties, and possibly the public.
verdict.criterion_fired: Different actor role and materially different core action, recipients, purpose, and content; the shared ICT-incident context and possible financial-entity overlap do not make the duties the same compliance work.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Norm A requires telecommunications providers and spectrum users to cooperate with and carry out orders from the military authority under Article 31 of the Dutch War Act. Norm B permits and conditions the further processing of previously collected personal data for developing, training, and testing certain AI systems in a regulatory sandbox, subject to safeguards including monitoring, isolation, deletion, logging, documentation, and publication.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an emergency/public-authority cooperation and order-execution duty; Norm B is a conditional data-processing regime for AI testing, with associated safeguards and documentation/publication requirements.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms impose materially different actions on different actor categories in different regulatory contexts: military-authority cooperation and execution of orders versus conditional processing and governance of personal data for AI testing.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms address responding to serious/security incidents, but Norm A requires implementing preventive and mitigating security measures, whereas Norm B requires reporting a serious incident to market-surveillance authorities.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an ongoing risk-management and incident-impact mitigation duty; Norm B is an incident-notification duty with a specific 15-day deadline and an authority recipient.
verdict.criterion_fired: The underlying actions differ (implement measures versus submit a notification), and the actor roles differ: Norm A applies to essential or important entities, while Norm B applies to providers of high-risk AI systems and, where applicable, deployers. The shared incident-related context and authority-facing aspect do not make the compliance work duplicative.

verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in both actor role and core action: enabling voluntary information exchange versus internally analysing ICT-incident trends. The shared cybersecurity/incident subject matter is insufficient to create duplicate compliance work.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require the provider to make a notification/report connected to an adverse incident or threat, but they require different notifications serving different purposes and recipients.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires an internet-access provider to notify the affected subscriber about a contemplated or urgent protective termination/suspension measure and, where possible, give the subscriber an opportunity to remove the threat. Norm B requires a high-risk AI-system provider (or, where applicable, the deployer) to report a serious incident to the relevant market-surveillance authorities, with a deadline of immediately after establishing causation or reasonable likelihood and no later than 15 days after awareness.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms do not impose the same duty: although both involve a notification following a security-related adverse event, they concern different actor roles, different triggering circumstances, different recipients, and materially different content and purposes. Norm A is a customer warning tied to a protective service measure; Norm B is regulatory incident reporting concerning a serious AI-system incident.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both concern an incident-related communication/reporting duty, but A requires an essential or important entity to submit a progress report or final report about an ongoing/handled incident, while B requires a public electronic communications service provider to notify the Dutch Data Protection Authority immediately of a security breach affecting personal-data protection.

verdict.distinguishing_factor: The norms concern entirely different regulated objects, actors, and compliance activities: registration of number users versus preparation and updating of AI technical documentation.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in core action, triggering context, regulated object, and actor role; the apparent similarity is not a duplicated reporting or documentation burden.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern making information or documentation available in response to an information-access or information-request context, but they require different underlying compliance work: Norm A requires establishing and publishing policies and procedures for disclosure of domain-registration data; Norm B requires an authorised representative to provide specified information and documentation to the AI Office upon a reasoned request.

Norm B is a case-specific production duty imposed on an authorised representative, involving the AI model provider’s technical documentation and compliance information, and also includes cooperation with authorities.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in actor role, triggering context, and operative action: Norm A requires setting and publicly disclosing policies and procedures, whereas Norm B requires producing information and documentation to the AI Office on a reasoned request. The shared information-access theme is insufficient to establish the same compliance work.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A requires an entity to take supply-chain cybersecurity risks and supplier vulnerabilities into account when selecting appropriate measures; B prohibits placing on the market, putting into service, or using specified AI systems and practices.

verdict.criterion_fired: The norms impose different kinds of duties on different regulated conduct: A concerns cybersecurity risk-management measures relating to suppliers, while B prohibits specified AI-system practices. They do not require the same compliance work to be performed twice.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern managing risks arising from technology-related incidents, but A requires maintaining a general, documented ICT-risk-management framework, whereas B requires investigating a serious incident, assessing its risks, taking corrective measures, and cooperating with authorities.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a standing, entity-wide ICT-risk-governance and control obligation; Norm B is an incident-specific investigation and remediation obligation following notification of a serious AI incident.
verdict.criterion_fired: Same broad technology-risk/incident-management context and comparable provider/entity role, but the operative work differs: continuous framework maintenance and evaluation versus an immediate investigation, risk assessment, corrective measures, and authority cooperation.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Beide normen zien op onverwijlde actie naar aanleiding van een ernstig/significant incident, maar norm A vereist melding/informatieverstrekking aan dienstontvangers (en daarnaast autoriteiten), terwijl norm B een onderzoek, risicobeoordeling en corrigerende maatregelen door de aanbieder vereist.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A betreft het onverwijld informeren/rapporteren over een significant incident; norm B betreft het onverwijld onderzoeken van een ernstig incident en het nemen van corrigerende maatregelen, na een afzonderlijke melding aan markttoezichtautoriteiten.
verdict.criterion_fired: De normen hebben wel een vergelijkbare incidenttrigger, maar leggen verschillende kernhandelingen op en richten zich niet op dezelfde actorrol: A betreft essentiële/belangrijke entiteiten die melden/informeren; B betreft aanbieders die onderzoek doen, een risicobeoordeling uitvoeren en corrigerende maatregelen nemen.

verdict.evidence_span_b: Na de melding van een ernstig incident op grond van lid 1 verricht de aanbieder onverwijld het nodige onderzoek in verband met het ernstige incident en het betrokken AI-systeem.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both concern ongoing management of cybersecurity/ICT risk, including measures relating to resilience and incident consequences. Norm A requires an entity, when selecting supply-chain security measures, to take account of supplier vulnerabilities, supplier cybersecurity quality and coordinated critical-supply-chain risk assessments. Norm B requires specified financial entities to establish and maintain a documented ICT-risk-management framework and to implement, monitor, test and periodically evaluate ICT-risk controls and continuity measures.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a supply-chain risk-assessment consideration within a broader NIS2 security-duty framework; Norm B is a simplified but comprehensive ICT-risk-management regime for specified financial entities, including recurring testing and evaluation. Neither provision imposes the same specific act or reporting content.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms do not impose the same core action: A requires consideration of specified supplier and coordinated supply-chain risk information when selecting measures, whereas B requires establishment, maintenance, monitoring, testing and evaluation of an ICT-risk-management framework. Their triggering contexts and regulated actor categories also differ; the shared cybersecurity-risk subject matter is too general to establish duplicate compliance work.

Norm B is a request-triggered production of AI-compliance information and documentation, including retained technical documentation, by an authorised representative.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in actor role, triggering event, and substantive content: a controller reports a personal-data breach, whereas an authorised representative supplies AI-compliance information and documentation on the AI Office's reasoned request.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A requires an entity to report changes to previously submitted identification/contact and related registration information to the competent authorities. verdict.criterion_fired: The underlying action, triggering event, actor role, and required content are materially different; a shared authority-facing context and broad information/documentation theme do not create duplicate compliance work.

verdict.criterion_fired: The duties concern different regulated objects, different compliance purposes, and different actor roles. Norm A concerns registers and domain-registration service providers maintaining domain-registration databases; Norm B concerns providers of high-risk AI systems operating a quality-management system. verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern providing information to a competent authority in connection with serious/significant ICT-related incidents, but A requires an incident notification while B requires, on request, an estimate of aggregated annual costs and losses.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both concern organizational handling of ICT/security incidents, but A requires preventive and mitigating technical, operational, and organizational measures, while B requires establishing and implementing an ICT-incident management process for detection, management, and reporting.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both concern addressing the consequences of a security or personal-data incident, but Norm A requires implementing preventive and mitigating technical, operational, and organisational measures, whereas Norm B requires communicating specified breach information to the data subject.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both concern conformity-related compliance involving technical documentation and/or an EU conformity declaration, but A requires the authorised representative to keep and provide documentation on request, whereas B requires the provider to remedy formal non-conformity identified by a market-surveillance authority, potentially including making missing documentation or declaration available.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both provisions concern the handling or justification of personal-data processing, but A requires documenting/justifying an international transfer assessment and safeguards in a GDPR Article 30 record, whereas B authorizes and conditions further processing of personal data in an AI regulatory sandbox, including technical, organizational, documentation, logging, deletion, and publication measures.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms regulate or constrain conduct involving digital/ICT systems, but they do not require the same compliance action: Norm A requires covered entities to protect data availability, authenticity, integrity and confidentiality as part of ICT-risk management, whereas Norm B prohibits placing on the market, putting into service, or using specified AI systems.

Norm A concerns ongoing ICT-risk protection by certain financial entities; Norm B concerns prohibiting specified AI practices by actors placing AI systems on the market, putting them into service, or using them. verdict.shared_compliance_action: A requires covered entities to promptly inform their service recipients about significant cyber threats and possible response measures. B requires certain financial entities to establish and maintain an ICT-risk-management framework and related controls, including identifying and handling ICT incidents, continuity measures, testing, and incorporating operational lessons into risk assessment; the framework must also be documented and evaluated periodically and after serious ICT incidents, with a report supplied to the competent authority on request.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: A is an outward-facing, event-triggered communication duty to potentially affected service recipients; B is an ongoing ICT-risk-management and governance duty, with incident-related evaluation and improvement, not a duty to communicate the threat to recipients.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties do not impose the same core action or the same actor role: A requires prompt threat communication to service recipients, whereas B requires internal ICT-risk controls and governance, with possible documentation submitted to a competent authority on request. The shared cyber/ICT-risk context is insufficient to establish duplicated compliance work.

verdict.criterion_fired: The duties concern different registers, different regulatory subject matter, and different operative actions; the apparent similarity is limited to maintaining a register.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern handling or maintaining information in a regulated data-governance context, but they do not require the same compliance action: Norm A requires a processor to maintain a processing-activities register, while Norm B requires domain-name registries and registration-service providers to grant access to specific domain-registration data upon lawful, justified requests and respond within 72 hours.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an ongoing record-keeping duty concerning the processor's own processing activities; Norm B is an on-request disclosure/access duty concerning domain-name registration data for legitimate requesting parties.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in actor, operative action, subject matter, and trigger: maintaining a processing-activities register versus responding to access requests by providing domain-registration data.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms impose obligations on regulated entities, but A requires broad cooperation with military authorities, including carrying out their orders, whereas B imposes a specific set of AI-provider compliance duties, including retaining documentation and logs, conformity and corrective measures, and responding to competent-authority requests.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an event-contingent military-authority cooperation duty under application of the War Act; Norm B is an ongoing, product-specific compliance regime for providers of high-risk AI systems. Norm B's extracted action is document retention, not reporting or execution of authority orders.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in actor role, triggering context, and core action: A concerns telecommunications actors/users assisting military authority under the War Act, while B concerns high-risk AI providers maintaining AI compliance, including retaining specified documentation.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms impose ongoing compliance measures on regulated digital-sector providers, but Norm A requires collecting and maintaining complete domain-registration data, whereas Norm B requires high-risk AI providers to ensure conformity with applicable requirements and perform multiple related compliance tasks.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A concerns DNS/domain-registration databases and identification/contact data; Norm B concerns conformity, documentation, logging, corrective measures, and accessibility for high-risk AI systems.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties concern different regulated actors, different subject matter, and different underlying actions: domain-registration data collection and maintenance versus high-risk AI conformity and associated obligations.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A requires municipal approval of planned cable works; B requires financial entities to conduct post-incident ICT evaluations and, on request, communicate implemented changes to competent authorities.

verdict.criterion_fired: The norms impose different actions on different actor roles in response to different event families: municipal authorization of planned cable works versus post-incident ICT evaluation and related information-sharing.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern a financial/regulated entity dealing with the consequences of an ICT or significant incident, but Norm A requires an incident report to the CSIRT and competent authority, whereas Norm B requires an internal post-incident evaluation and, on request, communication of implemented changes to the competent authorities.

Norm B is an internal root-cause and effectiveness review, with possible later disclosure of resulting changes on request; it does not require the incident report prescribed by Norm A.
verdict.criterion_fired: Same incident family and broadly comparable regulated-entity role, but different core actions, purposes, and content: incident notification versus internal post-incident evaluation and disclosure of remediation changes.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both provisions concern compliance responses connected with regulatory oversight, but they do not impose the same operative duty: Norm A concerns stating possible coercive fines in an investigation authorisation, whereas Norm B requires a high-risk AI provider to take immediate corrective measures and notify specified supply-chain actors and, in some cases, authorities about non-conformity or risk.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an authorisation-content requirement imposed on the lead overseer or authorised investigators; Norm B is an immediate corrective-action and notification duty imposed on providers of high-risk AI systems.
verdict.criterion_fired: Different operative action, triggering context, and duty-bearing actor: an investigation authorisation's statement of potential coercive fines is not the provider's corrective-action and notification duty following AI-system non-conformity or risk.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both provisions concern serious/ICT-related incidents and, at a broad level, incident-related handling or information. However, Norm A does not impose an incident-reporting duty: it states that financial entities remain responsible for handling and consequences of incidents already reported under Article 19(1), while the authority may provide feedback. Norm B requires providers to keep, document, and promptly report information about serious incidents and possible corrective measures.

verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in both actor role and core action: Norm A concerns continuing responsibility and supervisory feedback after an ICT incident has been reported, whereas Norm B requires AI-model providers to retain, document, and promptly report serious-incident information and possible corrective measures.

verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in both core action and event family: A concerns selecting cybersecurity measures based on supplier vulnerabilities, supplier security quality, and coordinated supply-chain risk assessments; B concerns investigating a serious AI incident and restricting investigations that could alter the system without prior authority notice.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both concern handling or maintaining information in the digital/data-governance context, but A requires responding to a lawful, justified access request for specific domain-registration data, whereas B requires maintaining a register of processing activities and specified related information.

verdict.distinguishing_factor: A is an urgent outward notification to service recipients; B is an internal post-incident evaluation and, where requested, disclosure of resulting changes to competent authorities.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in core action, actor scope, recipient/purpose, and substantive content; the shared ICT-incident context is insufficient to create duplicate compliance work.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Beide normen betreffen het beschikbaar stellen of verstrekken van informatie/documentatie, maar A ziet op toegang tot domeinnaamregistratiegegevens op een rechtmatig verzoek; B ziet op het opstellen, bijhouden en beschikbaar stellen van AI-modeldocumentatie aan AI-systeemaanbieders en, op verzoek, autoriteiten.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: De normen hebben een andere materiële verplichting, een andere gebeurteniscontext en een andere actorrol: A betreft registers/registratiedienstverleners die reageren op toegangverzoeken om domeinnaamregistratiegegevens; B betreft aanbieders van AI-modellen voor algemene doeleinden die modeldocumentatie en trainingsinformatie opstellen en beschikbaar stellen.

verdict.criterion_fired: The provisions do not impose the same underlying action, concern different subject matter and purposes, and bind different actor roles; the superficial similarity is limited to data handling.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both require the regulated entity to implement and maintain cybersecurity/ICT-risk-management measures, but A specifically requires supply-chain risk considerations when selecting measures, whereas B requires a documented ICT-risk-management framework and related monitoring, continuity, testing, and improvement measures.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a supply-chain cybersecurity-risk consideration embedded in the selection of measures under NIS2 Article 21(2)(d), including supplier vulnerabilities, product quality, supplier cybersecurity practices, secure development, and coordinated supply-chain risk assessments. Norm B is a simplified but comprehensive ICT-risk-management framework duty for specified financial entities, including documentation, monitoring, incident handling, continuity, testing, and evaluation.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties do not impose the same core action on the same actor role: A concerns essential or important NIS2 entities considering supply-chain cybersecurity factors when selecting risk-management measures, while B concerns specified small or exempt financial entities establishing and maintaining a documented ICT-risk-management framework. The shared cybersecurity-risk subject matter is insufficient because the actor scope and operative duties differ materially.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both provisions concern obtaining or supplying information/documentation to support regulatory oversight, but they do not impose the same concrete compliance action: Article 38 empowers the lead overseer to obtain certified copies or extracts during an investigation, whereas Article 54 requires the authorised representative to maintain and provide technical documentation and cooperate with authorities.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Beide normen houden verband met het verstrekken/beschikbaar stellen van informatie of documentatie, maar A betreft een specifieke, verzoekgestuurde verstrekking aan de minister en eventueel een onderzoek naar een zeggenschapshouder; B betreft het structureel opstellen, actualiseren en beschikbaar stellen van technische en andere modeldocumentatie aan AI-systeemaanbieders, met mogelijke verstrekking aan autoriteiten op verzoek.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both require an entity to take operational measures concerning security or ICT incidents, but A requires risk-management measures to limit incident consequences, while B requires monitoring user activity and detecting ICT anomalies/incidents.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a preventive/resilience obligation for public electronic communications providers focused on managing network or service security risks and limiting consequences for national security or public order. Norm B is a financial-entity monitoring and detection obligation focused on user activity and ICT anomalies or incidents.
verdict.criterion_fired: Different actor roles and materially different operational duties: security-risk mitigation for public electronic communications providers versus monitoring and detection by financial entities.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern reporting a serious incident to a public authority, but they require different reporting regimes and substantially different report content.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires financial entities to prepare and submit an initial notification, interim updates, and a final report containing information needed to assess the ICT incident’s scope and cross-border effects. Norm B requires providers of EU-marketed high-risk AI systems (and, where applicable, deployers) to notify market-surveillance authorities of serious incidents, immediately after causation is established and no later than 15 days after awareness.
verdict.criterion_fired: The event family and broad verb are similar, but the duty-bearing actor role differs: financial entities under DORA versus providers (and potentially deployers) of high-risk AI systems under the AI Act. The reporting recipients, reporting regimes, and substantive content also differ materially. This is therefore not the same compliance duty merely repeated for an additional recipient.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Beide normen zien op het onverwijld verstrekken van informatie aan een externe ontvanger naar aanleiding van een digitale dreiging of incident, maar norm A betreft een verwerker die een persoonsgegevensinbreuk meldt aan de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke, terwijl norm B essentiële/belangrijke entiteiten verplichten ontvangers van hun diensten te informeren over een significante cyberdreiging en mogelijke maatregelen.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both provisions concern responses to adverse ICT/AI incidents, but A requires internal recovery-time data-integrity checks and reconciliations, whereas B requires external notification of serious incidents to market-surveillance authorities.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an internal control and data-reconstruction measure during recovery; Norm B is a time-limited regulatory notification duty triggered by awareness of a serious incident and, for the referenced duty, a causal link or reasonable likelihood involving a high-risk AI system.
verdict.criterion_fired: The underlying actions and actor roles differ: A requires financial entities to perform recovery/data-integrity controls, while B requires providers (or, where applicable, deployers) of high-risk AI systems to notify market-surveillance authorities. verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require maintaining information or records, but they concern different subject matter: domain-name registration data versus documentation for high-risk AI systems.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require an actor to take action toward a public authority or authority-like body, but Norm A requires broad cooperation and execution of military-authority orders, whereas Norm B requires supplying entity-identification and contact/sector/service information and updating it after changes.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a military-authority cooperation and order-execution duty triggered by application of Article 31 of the Dutch War Act; Norm B is a cybersecurity administrative registration/information-reporting duty for essential and important entities, including updates within two weeks of changes.
verdict.criterion_fired: The underlying action, triggering event, actor role, and required content differ materially; the fact that both involve providing assistance or information to public authorities does not make them the same compliance work.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms involve responding to a request from a public authority by supplying information or documentation, but the underlying duties are not the same: Norm A requires a telecommunications party to provide a company-register extract concerning a share right, while Norm B requires an authorised representative to cooperate with AI authorities and, on a reasoned request, provide AI-compliance information and documentation.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both provisions regulate or constrain the use of technology, but they do not require the same compliance action: Norm A requires financial entities to implement documented ICT-security policies, procedures and controls, whereas Norm B prohibits specified AI practices and imposes conditions on certain law-enforcement uses.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a preventive ICT-risk-management implementation duty imposed on financial entities; Norm B is a prohibition and authorization framework concerning specified AI uses, principally involving users, providers or law-enforcement authorities.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in actor role, operative action and subject matter: Norm A requires implementation of documented security controls, while Norm B prohibits or conditions particular AI-system uses; there is no same compliance work repeated.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Beide normen houden verband met het onverwijld rapporteren van informatie over ernstige/significante incidenten aan een overheids- of EU-toezichthoudende instantie. Norm A vereist echter een meerfasige incidentrapportage met waarschuwing, initiële melding, eventuele tussentijdse rapportage en eindverslag; norm B vereist daarnaast het bijhouden en documenteren van relevante informatie en mogelijke corrigerende maatregelen en het rapporteren daarvan.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A betreft betrokken entiteiten die significante incidenten melden aan het CSIRT of de bevoegde autoriteit, met gedetailleerde inhoud en meerdere rapportagemomenten. Norm B betreft aanbieders van AI-modellen voor algemene doeleinden met systeemrisico die ernstige incidenten en mogelijke corrigerende maatregelen rapporteren aan het AI-bureau en eventueel nationale bevoegde autoriteiten.
verdict.criterion_fired: De actorrol verschilt wezenlijk: norm A ziet op betrokken entiteiten onder de NIS2-incidentrapportage, terwijl norm B uitsluitend aanbieders van AI-modellen voor algemene doeleinden met systeemrisico betreft. Bovendien verschillen de rapportage-inhoud en het doel voldoende; de gedeelde incidentrapportage is daarom geen identieke compliance-taak die enkel opnieuw aan een extra ontvanger moet worden verricht.
verdict.evidence_span_a: een incidentmelding indienen met, indien van toepassing, een update van de in punt a) bedoelde informatie, een initiële beoordeling van het significante incident
verdict.evidence_span_b: relevante informatie over ernstige incidenten en mogelijke corrigerende maatregelen bijhouden, documenteren en onverwijld rapporteren aan het AI-bureau

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A grants the lead overseer investigative powers to examine relevant registers, data, procedures and other material, including obtaining explanations and copies. verdict.criterion_fired: The norms do not impose the same underlying action on the same actor in response to the same event. A concerns supervisory investigation powers; B concerns ongoing AI-model documentation, information provision, copyright policies, and publication duties.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms address handling ICT/data-security incidents, but Norm A requires prompt notification of an affected person, whereas Norm B requires financial entities to register incidents and significant cyberthreats and establish processes for monitoring, treatment, follow-up, and remediation.

verdict.criterion_fired: The underlying actions and actor roles differ: individual notification by a service provider versus internal registration and management processes by a financial entity. The shared incident-related context and broad addressee category do not make the compliance work the same.

verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in core action and actor role: A imposes communication to service recipients, while B imposes internal incident registration and management processes on financial entities. Norm B is an access, response-time, and transparency duty concerning domain-name registration data, triggered by a lawful and duly justified access request.

verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in actor, triggering context, and operative action: maintaining a register of processing activities versus verifying conformity and withholding market placement, with possible notifications.

Norm B is an internal post-incident review and improvement duty, with possible later disclosure of implemented changes to authorities.
verdict.criterion_fired: Same incident-related actor and broad event family, but different core actions and substantially different content and purpose; the duties are related rather than the same compliance work repeated.

verdict.criterion_fired: Different underlying duty and event family: A is an ongoing information/communication measure owed to the data subject; B is an update measure triggered by changes or obsolescence in elements of a high-risk AI fundamental-rights impact assessment. verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern responding to or mitigating the consequences of a serious/security incident, but Norm A requires ex ante or ongoing technical, operational, and organisational risk-control measures, whereas Norm B requires an AI provider, after reporting a serious incident, to investigate it, assess its risks, take corrective measures, cooperate with authorities, and avoid certain system modifications without prior notice.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a general preventive and impact-limitation duty for essential or important entities; Norm B is a post-incident investigation and corrective-action duty for an AI provider, including cooperation with authorities and procedural safeguards during the investigation.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties do not impose the same core action or actor role: Norm A requires security-risk management measures to prevent incidents or limit their consequences for service recipients and other services, while Norm B requires a provider's post-report investigation, risk assessment, corrective measures, and cooperation/notification safeguards concerning a serious incident involving an AI system.

verdict.evidence_span_b: Dit omvat een risicobeoordeling van het incident en corrigerende maatregelen.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both involve maintaining or supplying compliance-related information, but Norm A requires an entity to provide registration information to the Minister, whereas Norm B requires reasons for exceptional processing of special-category personal data to be recorded in a processing-activities register.

verdict.criterion_fired: The duties concern different actors, different triggering contexts, different purposes, and materially different content: national-register information supplied to the Minister versus internal documentation of exceptional personal-data processing.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern action following a security/integrity-related incident or threat, but A requires the provider to notify the affected subscriber and give an opportunity to remove the threat (or notify promptly after an urgent measure), whereas B requires investigation, risk assessment, corrective measures, cooperation with authorities, and prior notice before potentially compromising modifications.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a subscriber-facing notice and opportunity-to-remedy duty connected to a network/service/device security measure; Norm B is an incident-investigation, risk-assessment, corrective-action, cooperation, and authority-notification duty concerning a serious AI-system incident.
verdict.criterion_fired: Same security-related incident family and provider role, but the operative actions and required content/purpose differ substantially; this is related compliance work, not the same report or measure repeated.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Voorafgaand aan het nemen van een maatregel, bedoeld in het eerste lid, onderdeel g, doet de aanbieder melding aan de betrokken abonnee, en geeft de abonnee daarbij de gelegenheid de in dit onderdeel bedoelde bedreiging van de integriteit en veiligheid van netwerk, dienst of randapparaat weg te nemen.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Norm A authorizes the lead overseer to obtain certified copies or extracts of registers, data, documented procedures, and other relevant material during an investigation. Norm B requires the provider of a high-risk AI system to prepare and update technical documentation, containing at least the Annex IV elements, so authorities and notified bodies can assess conformity.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A concerns an investigative power to obtain copies or extracts of material from a critical ICT third-party service provider; Norm B concerns the ex ante and ongoing creation and updating of a specific technical-documentation package for a high-risk AI system.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in actor, legal function, and object: an investigator’s power to obtain certified copies during an investigation versus an AI provider’s obligation to prepare and update Annex IV technical documentation.

verdict.evidence_span_b: De technische documentatie van een AI-systeem met een hoog risico wordt opgesteld voordat dit systeem in de handel wordt gebracht of in gebruik wordt gesteld, en wordt geactualiseerd.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Beide normen houden verband met het verstrekken van informatie aan een bevoegde publieke instantie, maar norm A verplicht de entiteit zelf om wijzigingen in eerder verstrekte identificatie- en contactgegevens te melden; norm B verleent de lead overseer een onderzoeksbevoegdheid om vertegenwoordigers van kritieke derde aanbieders van ICT-diensten om mondelinge of schriftelijke toelichting te verzoeken en antwoorden vast te leggen.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is een proactieve, periodieke wijzigingsmelding door essentiële of belangrijke entiteiten aan bevoegde autoriteiten, met een termijn van twee weken. Norm B is een reactieve onderzoeksbevoegdheid van de lead overseer jegens vertegenwoordigers van kritieke derde ICT-dienstaanbieders, zonder specifieke termijn en met betrekking tot feiten of documenten die het onderzoek betreffen.
verdict.criterion_fired: De normen betreffen niet dezelfde kernhandeling, gebeurtenisfamilie of actorrol: A ziet op het melden van wijzigingen in entiteitsgegevens, terwijl B ziet op informatieverstrekking in het kader van een toezichthoudend onderzoek.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De in lid 3 bedoelde entiteiten melden onmiddellijk elke wijziging in de bijzonderheden die zij op grond van de eerste alinea van dit lid hebben ingediend, en in elk geval binnen twee weken na de datum van de wijziging.
verdict.evidence_span_b: vertegenwoordigers van kritieke derde aanbieder van ICT-diensten op te roepen en te verzoeken om mondelinge of schriftelijke toelichting te geven bij feiten of documenten die betrekking hebben op het onderwerp en het doel van het onderzoek

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern post-incident compliance activity involving ICT or personal-data incidents, but A requires documenting personal-data breaches for supervisory compliance, whereas B requires post-incident evaluation of serious ICT incidents and, for non-micro financial entities, communicating implemented changes to competent authorities on request.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a GDPR personal-data-breach documentation duty, including the breach facts, consequences, and corrective measures. Norm B is a DORA operational-resilience post-incident review duty focused on causes, procedures, effectiveness, improvements, and—where applicable—communicating resulting changes on request.
verdict.criterion_fired: Same broad incident-related compliance context and same regulated-entity role, but the operative actions and required content/purpose differ materially; A documents every personal-data breach for supervisory verification, while B evaluates serious ICT-related operational disruptions and identifies or communicates improvements.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De verwerkingsverantwoordelijke documenteert alle inbreuken in verband met persoonsgegevens, met inbegrip van de feiten omtrent de inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens, de gevolgen daarvan en de genomen corrigerende maatregelen.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Financiële entiteiten verrichten ICT-gerelateerde post-incidentevaluaties na verstoringen van hun kernactiviteiten ten gevolge van een ernstig ICT-gerelateerd incident, analyseren daarbij de oorzaken van de verstoring en identificeren de verbeteringen die moeten worden aangebracht in de ICT-activiteiten of in het kader van het ICT-bedrijfscontinuïteitsbeleid

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A requires a provider to promptly notify the Dutch Data Protection Authority of a security breach affecting personal-data protection.
