Norm B betreft verwerking van persoonsgegevens in een AI-testomgeving en transparantie door publicatie van projectinformatie.
verdict.criterion_fired: De normen verschillen zowel in de kernhandeling als in het onderwerp en de actorrol: risicobeperkende medewerking aan een ministeriële maatregel tegenover publicatie van AI-projectinformatie op een autoriteitenwebsite.
verdict.evidence_span_a: het op verzoek van Onze Minister verlenen van medewerking aan eventueel genomen maatregelen ter uitschakeling van de risico's van apparaten of radioapparaten waarvoor hij als gemachtigde is aangewezen
verdict.evidence_span_b: een korte samenvatting van het in de testomgeving ontwikkelde AI-project en de doelstellingen en verwachte resultaten ervan worden op de website van de bevoegde autoriteiten gepubliceerd

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Beide normen raken aan het verzamelen en aan autoriteiten verstrekken/rapporteren van informatie over ernstige incidenten, maar norm A vereist op verzoek een raming van geaggregeerde jaarlijkse kosten en verliezen; norm B vereist het bijhouden, documenteren en onverwijld rapporteren van relevante informatie over ernstige incidenten en mogelijke corrigerende maatregelen.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A betreft uitsluitend andere financiële entiteiten dan micro-ondernemingen en een kosten- en verliesraming op verzoek van bevoegde autoriteiten. Norm B betreft aanbieders van AI-modellen voor algemene doeleinden met een systeemrisico en vereist bredere incidentinformatie plus mogelijke corrigerende maatregelen, onverwijld gemeld aan het AI-bureau en eventueel nationale bevoegde autoriteiten.
verdict.criterion_fired: De actorrol verschilt wezenlijk en de vereiste inhoud en functie van de informatieverstrekking verschillen: financiële kostenraming op verzoek versus incidentrapportage met corrigerende maatregelen.
verdict.evidence_span_a: verstrekken de bevoegde autoriteiten op hun verzoek een raming van de geaggregeerde jaarlijkse kosten en verliezen als gevolg van ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incidenten
verdict.evidence_span_b: relevante informatie over ernstige incidenten en mogelijke corrigerende maatregelen bijhouden, documenteren en onverwijld rapporteren aan het AI-bureau en, in voorkomend geval, aan de nationale bevoegde autoriteiten

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms involve maintaining or making information/documentation available to public authorities, but they impose different substantive duties: A concerns a financial entity's ICT-service contract register and related reporting/access duties; B concerns an authorised representative's retention and availability of AI-model technical documentation and provider contact details.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: The duties concern different regulated subject matter, different actors, and different underlying compliance purposes: ICT third-party-service contracting versus general-purpose AI-model documentation and representation.
verdict.criterion_fired: Different actor role and different event/subject-matter family; the apparent similarity is limited to making information available to authorities.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Financiële entiteiten stellen de bevoegde autoriteit op verzoek het volledige informatieregister of desgevraagd specifieke onderdelen daarvan ter beschikking
verdict.evidence_span_b: een kopie van de in bijlage XI gespecificeerde technische documentatie beschikbaar houden voor het AI-bureau en de nationale autoriteiten gedurende een periode van tien jaar nadat het AI-model voor algemene doeleinden in de handel is gebracht

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Geen gedeelde compliance-actie: norm A vereist dat de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke de toezichthoudende autoriteit informeert over een uitzonderlijke doorgifte van persoonsgegevens; norm B betreft de taken en informatie-/samenwerkingsplichten van een gemachtigde van een aanbieder van een AI-model voor algemene doeleinden tegenover het AI-bureau en nationale autoriteiten.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A ziet op het melden van een specifieke internationale doorgifte van persoonsgegevens aan een toezichthoudende autoriteit. Norm B ziet op vertegenwoordiging, het bewaren van technische documentatie, het verstrekken van informatie en samenwerking met AI-toezichthouders op gemotiveerd verzoek.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both concern communicating ICT/security incidents or vulnerabilities, but Norm A requires the affected entity to report a significant incident to a CSIRT or competent authority, whereas Norm B requires a financial entity to maintain crisis-communication plans enabling responsible disclosure to clients, counterparties, and potentially the public.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an incident-reporting duty to public authorities with a 24-hour deadline and specified incident information; Norm B is a preventive ICT-risk-management planning duty aimed at communications to private stakeholders or the public, with no deadline or specified reporting package.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in core action, actor scope, recipients, purpose, and required content: an authority incident report is not the same compliance work as maintaining a crisis-communication plan for disclosure to clients, counterparties, or the public.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both concern managing cybersecurity/ICT risks through organizational and technical risk-management measures, including supply-chain or third-party risk considerations. Norm A requires an entity, when selecting supply-chain security measures, to take account of supplier vulnerabilities, supplier cybersecurity quality, and coordinated critical-supply-chain risk assessments. Norm B requires specified financial entities to establish and maintain a documented ICT-risk-management framework and related controls, with periodic and incident-triggered documentation and evaluation.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a specific supply-chain risk-assessment consideration within a broader NIS2 security-duty framework; Norm B is a simplified but comprehensive ICT-risk-management framework obligation for specified financial entities, including monitoring, incident handling, continuity, testing, and evaluation.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms do not impose the same underlying action: A requires taking specified supply-chain risk information into account when choosing measures, whereas B requires establishing and maintaining a documented ICT-risk-management framework and associated controls. They also address different actor categories and no common reporting recipient or deadline.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern incident-related compliance, but A requires an essential or important entity to report every significant incident under the procedures in Articles 26–29, whereas B requires providers of general-purpose AI models with systemic risk to keep and document relevant information about serious incidents and possible corrective measures and report it without delay to the AI Office and, where appropriate, national competent authorities.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm B is a broader, AI-specific incident-information, documentation, corrective-measures, and cybersecurity duty imposed on systemic-risk GPAI providers; Norm A is a significant-incident notification duty imposed on essential or important entities under the NIS2 implementation framework.
verdict.criterion_fired: The actor roles differ: A applies to essential or important entities, while B applies specifically to providers of general-purpose AI models with systemic risk. In addition, B requires keeping and documenting information, reporting possible corrective measures, and implementing related cybersecurity protection, while A requires reporting every significant incident under a separate procedure.

verdict.evidence_span_b: relevante informatie over ernstige incidenten en mogelijke corrigerende maatregelen bijhouden, documenteren en onverwijld rapporteren aan het AI-bureau en, in voorkomend geval, aan de nationale bevoegde autoriteiten

Norm B betreft het opstellen en actualiseren van technische documentatie vóór marktintroductie of ingebruikstelling, zodat conformiteit van een hoog-risico-AI-systeem kan worden beoordeeld.
verdict.criterion_fired: De normen leggen wezenlijk verschillende verplichtingen op aan verschillende actorrollen over verschillende onderwerpen: A ziet op entiteiten die voor cyberbeveiligingsdoeleinden bij bevoegde autoriteiten moeten worden geregistreerd en wijzigingen moeten melden; B ziet op aanbieders/verantwoordelijke partijen voor hoog-risico-AI-systemen die technische conformiteitsdocumentatie moeten opstellen en actualiseren.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De in lid 3 bedoelde entiteiten melden onmiddellijk elke wijziging in de bijzonderheden die zij op grond van de eerste alinea van dit lid hebben ingediend, en in elk geval binnen twee weken na de datum van de wijziging.
verdict.evidence_span_b: De technische documentatie van een AI-systeem met een hoog risico wordt opgesteld voordat dit systeem in de handel wordt gebracht of in gebruik wordt gesteld, en wordt geactualiseerd.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Norm A requires including the responsible reporting officer’s contact details in an early warning about a significant incident. verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in both actor role and core action: providing contact details in an early warning versus establishing and implementing an incident-management process.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern addressing security-related risks or incidents in digital/network systems, but Norm A requires notifying an affected subscriber about a contemplated or urgent service measure, whereas Norm B requires implementing and maintaining ICT-risk-management controls, including detecting anomalies and handling ICT incidents.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an event-triggered subscriber notification and opportunity-to-remedy duty linked to suspension or termination of internet access; Norm B is an ongoing organisational and technical ICT-risk-management duty for specified financial entities, with documentation/evaluation and possible submission to a competent authority on request.
verdict.criterion_fired: Different actor role and different core compliance action; the shared security-risk context and incident-related language do not make the notification duty and ICT-risk-management framework the same compliance work.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Geen gedeelde concrete compliance-actie: norm A vereist dat entiteiten cyberbeveiligingsmaatregelen voor de toeleveringsketen ontwerpen waarbij zij leverancierskwetsbaarheden, productkwaliteit en beveiligingspraktijken meewegen; norm B verbiedt bepaalde vormen van het in de handel brengen, in gebruik stellen of gebruiken van AI-systemen.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is een risicobeheer- en ontwerpverplichting voor essentiële en belangrijke entiteiten met betrekking tot netwerk- en informatiesystemen en hun leveranciers. Norm B is een materieel verbod op specifieke AI-praktijken, met mogelijke voorafgaande toestemming, registratie en waarborgen voor een beperkte uitzondering inzake realtime biometrische identificatie door rechtshandhavingsinstanties.
verdict.criterion_fired: De normen hebben niet dezelfde kernhandeling, actorrol of gebeurtenisfamilie. A betreft het nemen en onderbouwen van cyberbeveiligingsmaatregelen in de toeleveringsketen; B betreft het niet in de handel brengen, niet in gebruik stellen of niet gebruiken van verboden AI-systemen. Een oppervlakkige overlap in het woord 'kwetsbaarheden' maakt de verplichtingen niet gelijk of inhoudelijk verwant genoeg voor RELATED_BURDEN.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Beide normen vereisen dat de actor een risicogerelateerde beoordeling of maatregel uitvoert en daarbij relevante informatie in aanmerking neemt of actualiseert. Dat abstracte patroon is echter niet dezelfde concrete compliancehandeling: norm A betreft het meenemen van leveranciers- en dienstverlenerskwetsbaarheden bij cyberbeveiligingsmaatregelen voor de toeleveringsketen; norm B betreft een grondrechteneffectbeoordeling van het gebruik van een hoog-risico-AI-systeem en het actualiseren daarvan wanneer relevante elementen wijzigen.

A is een zorgplicht voor een essentiële of belangrijke entiteit inzake cyberbeveiligingsmaatregelen en de beoordeling van directe leveranciers/dienstverleners; B is een verplichting voor een gebruiksverantwoordelijke van een hoog-risico-AI-systeem om een grondrechteneffectbeoordeling uit te voeren en actuele informatie te behouden. Een eventuele algemene overeenkomst — beide betreffen risicobeoordeling — is onvoldoende voor RELATED_BURDEN of DUPLICATE_BURDEN.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern organisational/compliance activities by regulated digital-sector actors, but they do not impose the same underlying action: Norm A requires financial entities to establish integrated ICT-incident monitoring, handling and follow-up procedures, while Norm B assigns an authorised representative verification, document-retention/availability, information-production and cooperation duties concerning general-purpose AI models.

verdict.criterion_fired: The norms differ in the core action, triggering/event context, and actor role; any superficial similarity from both involving regulated digital compliance does not establish duplicated reporting or other compliance work.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern obligations involving regulated digital-system operators, but Norm A requires responding to a legitimate, reasoned request for access to specific domain-registration data, whereas Norm B imposes a broad set of ex ante and ongoing compliance obligations on providers of high-risk AI systems, including conformity, documentation, corrective-measure, and information duties.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a time-limited access-request response duty concerning specific domain-registration data; Norm B is a multi-part provider-compliance regime for high-risk AI systems, with no matching incident or access-request reporting obligation.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in core action, triggering event, actor role, and required content; any superficial similarity from both involving digital-law entities does not establish duplicated compliance work.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Norm A requires promptly notifying the affected person of a personal-data breach likely to adversely affect that person's privacy. Norm B requires exempt small/non-interconnected financial entities to establish and maintain ICT-risk controls, including monitoring, incident detection and response, continuity, testing, and related documentation/evaluation; on request, an evaluation report is submitted to the competent authority.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an incident-triggered notification to the affected data subject. Norm B is an ongoing ICT-risk-management and resilience framework duty, with documentation/evaluation obligations and possible submission to a competent authority; it does not require notifying affected persons of a breach.
verdict.criterion_fired: Same broad ICT/security-incident context and comparable regulated-entity role, but the operative actions, recipients, purposes, and required content differ substantially; this is related compliance work, not the same reporting obligation repeated.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern handling serious ICT/AI incidents, but Norm A requires establishing and implementing an incident-management process that includes reporting ICT-related incidents, whereas Norm B requires the provider to promptly investigate a serious incident, conduct a risk assessment, take corrective measures, cooperate with authorities, and give prior notice before certain system modifications. They do not require the same core compliance work.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a financial entity's general ICT-incident management and reporting-process obligation; Norm B is a high-risk AI provider's post-report investigation, risk-assessment, corrective-measures, cooperation, and procedural-notice obligation.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in both actor role and core action: Norm A concerns financial entities implementing a process to detect, manage, and report ICT incidents; Norm B concerns AI providers promptly investigating a serious incident and taking related follow-up measures. The shared incident context and authority-facing setting do not make the compliance work duplicative.

Norm B requires the provider, following a market-surveillance finding, to remedy formal non-conformity within a period set by that authority, potentially followed by market restrictions, recall, or withdrawal.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A concerns the content of a data-breach notification; Norm B concerns corrective action against formal non-conformity in an AI system, not reporting the incident or supplying equivalent information.
verdict.criterion_fired: The underlying actions, triggering events, and actor roles differ: a controller's breach-notification information duty versus an AI provider's remediation duty imposed after a market-surveillance finding.

verdict.criterion_fired: The duties concern different regulated subject matter, actors, and compliance purposes: product conformity and ministerial market-surveillance cooperation versus maintaining a GDPR processing-activities register.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require post-incident investigative or control activity concerning the integrity, causes, risks, or remediation of systems/data: Norm A requires financial entities to perform necessary checks and reconciliations during ICT-incident recovery, while Norm B requires an AI provider to promptly investigate a serious incident, assess its risks, take corrective measures, cooperate with authorities, and avoid altering the AI system in a way that could affect later causal evaluation without prior notice.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A concerns data-integrity checks and reconciliations during recovery from an ICT-related incident, including reconstruction of external-stakeholder data. Norm B concerns an AI provider’s prompt investigation and risk assessment of a serious AI incident, corrective measures, cooperation with authorities, and preservation of the system’s evidentiary state unless authorities are notified in advance.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties do not impose the same core action on the same actor role: Norm A requires recovery-stage data-integrity controls by financial entities, whereas Norm B requires investigation and related safeguards by providers of AI systems. The shared incident-related context is insufficient to establish duplicated compliance work.

verdict.evidence_span_b: Na de melding van een ernstig incident op grond van lid 1 verricht de aanbieder onverwijld het nodige onderzoek in verband met het ernstige incident en het betrokken AI-systeem.

verdict.criterion_fired: De normen hebben noch dezelfde kernhandeling, noch hetzelfde type trigger of dezelfde actorrol; een registratieplicht voor nummergebruikers is niet dezelfde verplichting als een jurisdictietoewijzingsregel.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern taking measures in response to a risk or disruption affecting a network or service, but Norm A authorizes targeted orders to secure cooperation with a suspension or prevent misuse/outage, whereas Norm B requires an entity to take corrective cybersecurity-risk-management measures when it finds that it is not complying with prescribed measures.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A concerns compliance with orders issued by an appointed person in the context of a specific suspension and prevention of misuse or service/network outage; Norm B concerns an entity’s own corrective action after identifying non-compliance with broad cybersecurity risk-management measures.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in actor, legal mechanism, and operative purpose: Norm A empowers an appointed person to issue orders to a party involved in a suspension, while Norm B requires a regulated entity to take corrective cybersecurity measures after detecting its own non-compliance. The shared reference to network/service disruption or cybersecurity risk is too general to establish the same event family or duplicated compliance work.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require the regulated actor to create and maintain written records or documentation, but they concern different subject matter and serve different compliance purposes: GDPR processing-activity records versus technical documentation and related information for a general-purpose AI model.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern ongoing management of cyber/ICT security risks through organisational and technical risk-management measures. Neither provision requires the same report or submission to the same authority.

The shared cyber-risk subject matter is insufficient to create duplicate compliance work.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern handling ICT/AI-related incidents, but Norm A requires preventive ICT-risk detection and rapid incident handling, whereas Norm B requires the AI provider to investigate a serious incident, assess its risks, take corrective measures, cooperate with authorities, and avoid altering the system in a way that could affect later causal evaluation without prior notice.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a general, ongoing ICT-risk-management and incident-detection/handling measure for specified financial entities; Norm B is a post-serious-incident investigation and non-interference duty for an AI provider.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties do not impose the same core action or fall on the same actor role: Norm A requires financial entities to establish and operate ICT-risk controls that identify/detect anomalies and enable rapid handling, while Norm B requires an AI provider, after a serious incident has been reported, to investigate without impermissibly modifying the AI system and to cooperate with authorities.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A requires an essential/important entity to give an early warning about a significant incident to its CSIRT and competent authority within 24 hours. B requires a financial entity to design, establish, and implement an ICT-related-incident management process for detecting, managing, and reporting such incidents.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an incident-triggered, time-bound early-warning notification duty; Norm B is an ex ante organisational/process-implementation duty, not a duty to submit a particular incident report.
verdict.criterion_fired: The underlying actions and actor roles differ: A requires immediate incident notification, while B requires implementing an incident-management process. The shared ICT/security-incident subject matter is insufficient to establish duplicate compliance work.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit geeft ten behoeve van de melding, bedoeld in artikel 27, eerste lid, een vroegtijdige waarschuwing over het significante incident aan haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Financiële entiteiten omschrijven een beheerproces voor ICT-gerelateerde incidenten, stellen dit vast en leggen dit ten uitvoer, om ICT-gerelateerde incidenten te detecteren, te beheren en te melden.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both involve providing information to a public authority, but Norm A requires making the GDPR processing-activities register available on request, whereas Norm B requires notified bodies to inform the notifying authority about specified conformity-assessment matters and activities.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A concerns access to a register of processing activities by a controller or processor; Norm B concerns statutory notifications by notified bodies about conformity-assessment certificates, status changes, accreditation circumstances, authority requests, and activities including cross-border work and subcontracting.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties involve different actors, different subject matter, and different event families: GDPR processing-activity records versus AI Act conformity-assessment information and notifications.

B prohibits specified AI practices, including certain uses or placing on the market/putting into service of AI systems; for real-time remote biometric identification, it also requires specified safeguards and prior authorization. These are not the same compliance action.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a cybersecurity supply-chain risk-management duty for essential or important entities; Norm B is a prohibition on specified AI practices and related conditions for law-enforcement biometric identification.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms impose different kinds of duties on different regulated activities: A requires consideration of supplier and supply-chain cybersecurity risks as part of implementing security measures, whereas B prohibits specified AI-system practices and regulates exceptional biometric-identification use. There is no repeated reporting, notification, retention, information-provision, or other identical compliance work.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both concern communicating information about a security/personal-data incident, but A requires an early warning to the entity’s CSIRT and competent authority, whereas B specifies the content of a communication to the affected data subject.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an incident warning to institutional recipients within 24 hours; Norm B is a substantive communication to the data subject, in clear and simple language, describing the personal-data breach and specified information and measures.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in core action, actor role, recipient, and required content: A concerns an essential or important entity’s early warning to a CSIRT and competent authority, while B concerns a controller’s communication to the affected data subject.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit geeft ten behoeve van de melding, bedoeld in artikel 27, eerste lid, een vroegtijdige waarschuwing over het significante incident aan haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Beide normen voorzien in het verstrekken of beschikbaar stellen van informatie/documentatie aan een bevoegde overheidsinstantie, maar zij betreffen niet dezelfde concrete compliancehandeling: norm A vereist entiteitsregistratiegegevens en het melden van wijzigingen; norm B betreft een gemachtigde die op verzoek een mandaatkopie en, bij een gemotiveerd verzoek, AI-modeldocumentatie of andere nalevingsinformatie verstrekt.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A ziet op algemene identificatie- en registratiegegevens van essentiële of belangrijke entiteiten, inclusief wijzigingsmeldingen binnen twee weken. Norm B ziet op de taken van een gemachtigde van een aanbieder van een AI-model voor algemene doeleinden, waaronder het op verzoek overleggen van het mandaat en het beschikbaar houden of verstrekken van technische documentatie.
verdict.criterion_fired: De normen leggen geen dezelfde kernverplichting op: zij hebben verschillende actoren, verschillende inhoud en verschillende juridische doeleinden. De oppervlakkige overeenkomst dat informatie aan een overheidsinstantie wordt verstrekt, is onvoldoende.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De in lid 3 bedoelde entiteiten melden onmiddellijk elke wijziging in de bijzonderheden die zij op grond van de eerste alinea van dit lid hebben ingediend, en in elk geval binnen twee weken na de datum van de wijziging.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Hij legt op verzoek een kopie van het mandaat over aan het AI-bureau, in een van de officiële talen van de instellingen van de Unie.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Beide normen leggen documentatie-/informatiegerelateerde compliance-verplichtingen op, maar niet dezelfde concrete handeling: norm A vereist het onderbouwen van een beoordeling en passende waarborgen in een register; norm B omvat onder meer het verstrekken van informatie die krachtens artikel 20 vereist is, naast diverse andere AI-aanbiedersverplichtingen.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A betreft de onderbouwing en registratie van waarborgen voor een specifieke doorgifte van persoonsgegevens naar een derde land of internationale organisatie. Norm B betreft algemene product- en conformiteitsverplichtingen van aanbieders van hoog-risico-AI-systemen, waaronder het verstrekken van artikel 20-informatie.
verdict.criterion_fired: De normen hebben geen dezelfde kernhandeling, gebeurtenisfamilie of actorrol. Norm A ziet op een specifieke internationale doorgifte van persoonsgegevens en registratie/onderbouwing daarvan; norm B ziet op aanbieders van hoog-risico-AI en algemene conformiteits- en informatieverplichtingen. Een eventuele oppervlakkige overlap in documenteren of informatie verstrekken maakt de compliance-werkzaamheden niet hetzelfde.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De verwerkingsverantwoordelijke of de verwerker staaft de beoordeling en de in lid 1, tweede alinea, van dit artikel bedoelde passende waarborgen in het artikel 30 bedoelde register.
verdict.evidence_span_b: nemen de noodzakelijke corrigerende maatregelen en verstrekken de uit hoofde van artikel 20 vereiste informatie

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require a notification/report, but they concern different notifications: A requires an essential or important entity to report every significant incident under Articles 26–29; B requires an internet-access provider to notify the affected subscriber about a protective service measure, or as soon as possible afterward where urgency prevents prior notice.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an incident-reporting duty under the NIS framework, while Norm B is a customer-notification duty tied to taking a measure to protect network, service, or end-device integrity and security.
verdict.criterion_fired: Different actor role and materially different duty: A concerns reporting significant incidents to the authorities/procedures under Articles 26–29, whereas B concerns notifying the affected subscriber about a provider-initiated protective measure. The shared word-level action and broad security context do not make the compliance work the same.

Wanneer dit wegens de vereiste spoed niet voorafgaand aan het nemen van de maatregel mogelijk is, doet de aanbieder zo snel mogelijk melding van de maatregel.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require maintaining or making available structured records/information, but A requires a processor's register of processing activities, whereas B requires financial entities to maintain and provide an ICT third-party-contract information register, including reporting and notifications to competent authorities.

verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in actor role, subject matter, and operative purpose: A is a processor's record-keeping duty concerning processing activities, while B is a financial entity's ICT-contract register, supervisory disclosure, annual reporting, and notification duty.

verdict.criterion_fired: The duties concern different regulated actors and different subject matter: domain-name registration data versus high-risk AI-system logs. The shared request-for-access mechanism is not enough to establish the same compliance burden.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require prompt communication to potentially affected service recipients/clients about a cyber-related threat or incident and protective or mitigating measures.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A concerns essential or important entities informing service recipients about measures in response to a significant cyber threat, with optional notice of the threat itself. Norm B concerns financial entities informing clients about measures for a significant cyber threat or, separately, notifying clients of a serious ICT-related incident affecting clients’ financial interests and the mitigation measures taken.
verdict.criterion_fired: Same broad cyber-threat/incident communication pattern and same client/service-recipient audience, but the actor categories and operative content differ: A covers essential/important entities and recommended recipient measures in response to a significant cyber threat; B covers financial entities, including incident notification and mitigation measures or protective measures.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit deelt de ontvangers van haar diensten, die mogelijkerwijs door een significante cyberdreiging in relatie tot het ontvangen van die diensten worden getroffen, onverwijld mee welke maatregelen die ontvangers kunnen nemen in reactie op die dreiging.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Wanneer een ernstig ICT-gerelateerd incident optreedt en gevolgen heeft voor de financiële belangen van cliënten, stellen financiële entiteiten, zodra zij het incident hebben opgemerkt, hun cliënten onverwijld in kennis van het ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incident en van de maatregelen die zijn genomen om de negatieve gevolgen van een dergelijk incident te beperken.

verdict.evidence_span_a: Elke verwerkingsverantwoordelijke en, in voorkomend geval, de vertegenwoordiger van de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke houdt een register van de verwerkingsactiviteiten die onder hun verantwoordelijkheid plaatsvinden.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern communicating information about a cyber-related event, but A requires informing potentially affected service recipients about a significant cyber threat and possible protective measures, whereas B requires financial entities to prepare and submit prescribed notifications and reports about serious ICT-related incidents to a competent authority.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a recipient-facing warning/information duty concerning a significant cyber threat; Norm B is regulatory incident reporting concerning a serious ICT-related incident, using prescribed models and containing information needed by the competent authority to assess scope and cross-border effects.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties do not impose the same core action on the same actor role: A requires an essential or important entity to inform its service recipients about a significant cyber threat and possible response measures, while B requires a financial entity to prepare and submit formal incident notifications/reports to a competent authority. The different recipient and materially different content/purpose reinforce that this is not duplicated compliance work.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit deelt de ontvangers van haar diensten, die mogelijkerwijs door een significante cyberdreiging in relatie tot het ontvangen van die diensten worden getroffen, onverwijld mee welke maatregelen die ontvangers kunnen nemen in reactie op die dreiging.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms involve making information or documentation available to public authorities in the context of regulatory oversight, but they do not impose the same underlying compliance action.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires financial entities to maintain and update an ICT-service contractual information register and report specified aggregate information at least annually, with the register available on request. Norm B requires an authorised representative of a general-purpose AI-model provider to perform delegated tasks, retain technical documentation for ten years, provide information and documentation to the AI Office on a reasoned request, and cooperate with authorities on measures concerning the model.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in actor role, subject matter, and operative action: Norm A concerns a financial entity's ICT third-party-contract register and recurring supervisory reporting; Norm B concerns an authorised representative's AI-model documentation, cooperation, and assistance duties.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Financiële entiteiten rapporteren ten minste jaarlijks aan de bevoegde autoriteiten over het aantal nieuwe overeenkomsten inzake het gebruik van ICT-diensten, de categorieën van derde aanbieders van ICT-diensten, het soort contractuele overeenkomsten en de ICT-diensten en -functies die worden geleverd.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both provisions concern enforcement measures intended to compel an addressee to remedy non-compliance: A imposes a coercive fine on a critical ICT third-party provider, while B requires an AI provider to take corrective measures to bring an AI system into compliance.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a lead overseer’s coercive-fine decision triggered by failure to comply with oversight measures; Norm B is a market-surveillance authority’s substantive corrective-action order triggered by finding that an AI system is high-risk. The duties, purposes, and compliance work therefore differ substantially.
verdict.criterion_fired: Different actor role and different enforcement event/duty: A concerns non-compliance with lead-overseer measures and payment of a coercive fine; B concerns bringing an AI system into regulatory conformity through corrective measures.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both involve communicating information about an event to a public authority, but they do not require the same compliance work: Norm A requires advance notice of planned cable-maintenance works on public land, whereas Norm B requires structured incident reporting about a significant incident, including warnings, incident details, assessments, mitigation measures, and final reports.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A concerns prior notification of planned cable-maintenance works to a municipal mayor or delegate; Norm B concerns multiple reports about a significant incident to a CSIRT or competent authority.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern demonstrating or maintaining compliance of regulated products, but they do not impose the same concrete compliance action. verdict.shared_compliance_action: Geen gedeelde concrete compliance-actie: norm A vereist de toezichthoudende autoriteit te informeren over een specifieke, niet-repetitieve doorgifte van persoonsgegevens; norm B vereist een gemachtigde een kopie van technische documentatie beschikbaar te houden voor het AI-bureau en nationale autoriteiten gedurende tien jaar.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A betreft een incidentele melding aan een toezichthoudende autoriteit naar aanleiding van een uitzonderlijke internationale doorgifte van persoonsgegevens. Norm B betreft een voortdurende bewaarplicht voor technische AI-documentatie ten behoeve van mogelijke verzoeken van meerdere autoriteiten.
verdict.criterion_fired: De normen leggen verschillende kernhandelingen op (informeren versus beschikbaar houden/bewaren), zien op verschillende gebeurtenissen en hebben verschillende verantwoordelijke actoren: de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke tegenover de gemachtigde van een aanbieder van een AI-model voor algemene doeleinden.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De verwerkingsverantwoordelijke informeert de toezichthoudende autoriteit over de doorgifte.
verdict.evidence_span_b: een kopie van de in bijlage XI gespecificeerde technische documentatie beschikbaar houden voor het AI-bureau en de nationale autoriteiten gedurende een periode van tien jaar

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms involve reporting information about serious incidents to public authorities, but Norm A requires a structured, staged report of a serious ICT-related incident, whereas Norm B requires keeping, documenting, and promptly reporting relevant information about serious incidents and possible corrective measures.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A concerns serious ICT-related incidents affecting financial entities and requires initial, interim/updated, and final notifications containing information needed to assess scope and cross-border effects. Norm B concerns providers of general-purpose AI models with systemic risk and requires reporting relevant information about serious incidents and possible corrective measures to the AI Office and, where applicable, national competent authorities.
verdict.criterion_fired: The actor roles are different and the duties arise under different regulatory regimes: financial entities must submit staged ICT-incident notifications, while systemic-risk GPAI-model providers must maintain/document and promptly report incident and corrective-measure information. The shared incident-reporting theme does not establish the same compliance work.
verdict.evidence_span_a: een tussentijds verslag na de eerste kennisgeving als bedoeld in punt a), zodra de status van het oorspronkelijke incident ingrijpend is gewijzigd
verdict.evidence_span_b: relevante informatie over ernstige incidenten en mogelijke corrigerende maatregelen bijhouden, documenteren en onverwijld rapporteren aan het AI-bureau

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A requires domain-name registries and registration-service entities to answer lawful access requests for specific domain-registration data within 72 hours. B requires notified bodies to inform other notified bodies about certain refused, suspended, withdrawn, or otherwise limited quality-management-system approvals and certain technical-documentation assessment certificates.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: The norms concern different actors, different triggering events, different information, and different underlying actions: responding to access requests for domain-registration data versus notifying peer notified bodies about certification or approval decisions.
verdict.criterion_fired: Different actor role and different event family; the duties are not the same compliance work.
verdict.evidence_span_a: verzoeken om toegang onverwijld en in elk geval binnen 72 uur na ontvangst van het verzoek beantwoorden

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Beide normen leggen een informatie-/rapportageverplichting aan een bevoegde autoriteit op, maar over wezenlijk verschillende onderwerpen: A vereist een voortgangs- of eindverslag over een incident; B vereist meldingen/informatie over certificaten, aanmelding en conformiteitsbeoordelingsactiviteiten.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A betreft de afhandeling van een voortduring of beëindiging van een incident en vereist een verslag met de in artikel 29, eerste lid, bedoelde aspecten. Norm B betreft informatieverplichtingen van aangemelde instanties over hun certificaten, aanmeldingsvoorwaarden en conformiteitsbeoordelingsactiviteiten.
verdict.criterion_fired: De normen zien niet op dezelfde gebeurtenis of dezelfde actorrol: A geldt voor een essentiële of belangrijke entiteit bij een incident, terwijl B geldt voor een aangemelde instantie en informatie over conformiteitsbeoordeling en aanmelding betreft.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Zij dient een eindverslag in binnen één maand nadat het incident is afgehandeld.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Aangemelde instanties brengen de aanmeldende autoriteit op de hoogte van:

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both provisions concern the handling or obtaining of information in a regulatory/compliance context, but Norm A requires an essential entity to bear the cost of an independent targeted security audit, whereas Norm B requires a high-risk AI deployer to use information supplied under Article 13 when carrying out a data-protection impact assessment.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A concerns payment for a targeted cybersecurity audit imposed by a competent authority; Norm B concerns using AI-system information to perform a data-protection impact assessment. They do not impose the same underlying compliance work.
verdict.criterion_fired: Different core action, event family, and actor role; the apparent similarity is only an information/compliance-context overlap and does not establish duplicated reporting or assessment work.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De kosten van een dergelijke gerichte door een onafhankelijke instantie uitgevoerde beveiligingsaudit worden betaald door de gecontroleerde entiteit
verdict.evidence_span_b: gebruiken gebruiksverantwoordelijken van AI-systemen met een hoog risico de informatie die op grond van artikel 13 van deze verordening wordt verstrekt om hun verplichting na te komen om een gegevensbeschermingseffectbeoordeling uit te voeren

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern telecommunications/digital-sector entities handling information, but Norm A requires a telecommunication party, upon ministerial request, to provide a specific register extract or investigate a controller’s identity and third-party links. Norm B requires domain-name registries and registration-service providers to collect and maintain accurate, complete domain-registration data in a database, supported by verification policies and procedures.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an on-request information-production/investigation duty triggered by suspected or potential dominant control threatening the public interest; Norm B is an ongoing data-collection, database-maintenance, and verification duty concerning domain-name registration records.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in core action, triggering event, actor role, and purpose: Norm A concerns responding to a ministerial request connected to suspected dominant control, whereas Norm B concerns maintaining a DNS registration database as an ongoing security, stability, and resilience measure.
verdict.evidence_span_a: verstrekt een telecommunicatiepartij aan Onze Minister op verzoek om niet een uittreksel uit het door de rechtspersoon gehouden register met betrekking tot een recht op een aandeel
verdict.evidence_span_b: de registers voor topleveldomeinnamen en de entiteiten die domeinnaamregistratiediensten verlenen, met de nodige zorgvuldigheid nauwkeurige en volledige domeinnaamregistratiegegevens verzamelen en bijhouden in een speciale database

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Beide normen leggen geen gelijksoortige meldings- of informatieverstrekkingsplicht op. Norm A vereist dat beleid en procedures over openbaarmaking openbaar worden gemaakt; norm B betreft voorwaarden voor verwerking van persoonsgegevens in een AI-testomgeving, waaronder wissen, logging, documentatie en publicatie van een projectsamenvatting.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is een transparantieplicht voor registers en domeinnaamregistratiedienstverleners; norm B is een gegevensverwerkingsregime voor AI-testomgevingen, met onder meer beveiliging, verwijdering, logging, documentatie en beperkte publicatie.
verdict.criterion_fired: De normen hebben geen dezelfde kernactie, actorrol of gebeurtenisfamilie: A ziet op het openbaar maken van beleid en procedures over domeinnaamregistratiegegevens, terwijl B ziet op voorwaarden en waarborgen voor verwerking van persoonsgegevens bij AI-ontwikkeling, inclusief wissen en documentatie.
verdict.evidence_span_a: stellen het beleid en de procedures met betrekking tot de bekendmaking van de gegevens, bedoeld in het eerste lid, vast en maken dat beleid en die procedures openbaar
verdict.evidence_span_b: in het kader van de testomgeving verwerkte persoonsgegevens worden beschermd met passende technische en organisatorische maatregelen en worden gewist nadat de deelname aan de testomgeving is beëindigd of de periode van bewaring van de persoonsgegevens ten einde is gekomen

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern maintaining or ensuring the accuracy/completeness of an information database or register, but they impose different operational duties: Norm A requires domain-name registries and registration-service entities to have and publish policies and procedures, including verification procedures, ensuring accurate and complete domain-registration data; Norm B requires financial entities to maintain and update a register of contractual ICT-service arrangements, document and classify those arrangements, report specified aggregate information annually, provide the register on request, and notify authorities of certain planned arrangements or changes.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A concerns DNS domain-registration data and policies/procedures for its accuracy and completeness; Norm B concerns financial entities' registers of contractual ICT-service arrangements and related reporting, disclosure, and notification duties.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties concern different subject matter, different regulated actors, and different compliance purposes: DNS data accuracy and verification procedures versus ICT-outsourcing contract-register management and supervisory reporting/notification.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De lidstaten schrijven voor dat de registers voor topleveldomeinnamen en de entiteiten die domeinnaamregistratiediensten verlenen, over beleidslijnen en procedures, waaronder verificatieprocedures, beschikken om ervoor te zorgen dat de in lid 1 bedoelde databases juiste en volledige informatie bevatten.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Financiële entiteiten rapporteren ten minste jaarlijks aan de bevoegde autoriteiten over het aantal nieuwe overeenkomsten inzake het gebruik van ICT-diensten, de categorieën van derde aanbieders van ICT-diensten, het soort contractuele overeenkomsten en de ICT-diensten en -functies die worden geleverd.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require the regulated actor to provide information to a public authority, but they concern different information and different compliance purposes: Norm A requires rapid reporting of a significant incident affecting a trust service to the CSIRT and competent authority, while Norm B requires notified bodies to inform the notifying authority about conformity-assessment certificates, status changes, notification circumstances, authority requests, and activities within their notification scope.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an incident-reporting duty triggered by a significant incident affecting provision of a trust service, with a 24-hour deadline and specified incident information. Norm B is an ongoing/conditional information duty concerning conformity-assessment activities and related certificates or notification matters, including information supplied on request; no deadline is specified.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties do not concern the same event family or the same actor role. Norm A applies to an essential or important entity offering a trust service and concerns a significant incident; Norm B applies to a notified body and concerns conformity-assessment and notification information. The shared act of informing an authority is too generic to establish duplicated compliance work.
verdict.evidence_span_a: een essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit die een vertrouwensdienst aanbiedt onverwijld of, indien dat niet mogelijk is, binnen 24 uur nadat zij kennis heeft gekregen van het significante incident een melding van het significante incident in bij haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit
verdict.evidence_span_b: Aangemelde instanties brengen de aanmeldende autoriteit op de hoogte van:

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Beide normen voorzien in het vastleggen of meedelen van informatie, maar niet in dezelfde concrete compliancehandeling: norm A vereist interne registratie en incidentbeheer; norm B vereist kennisgeving aan andere aangemelde instanties over specifieke goedkeuringen en beoordelingscertificaten.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A betreft registratie en opvolging van ICT-gerelateerde incidenten en significante cyberdreigingen door financiële entiteiten. Norm B betreft interinstitutionele kennisgeving door aangemelde instanties over geweigerde, opgeschorte, ingetrokken, beperkte of verleende goedkeuringen en certificaten.
verdict.criterion_fired: De normen verschillen zowel qua kernactie, actorrol als gebeurtenis en inhoud; een oppervlakkige overeenkomst rond informatieverwerking of kennisgeving creëert geen dubbele compliance-last.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Financiële entiteiten registreren alle ICT-gerelateerde incidenten en significante cyberdreigingen.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Geen gedeelde compliance-actie: norm A betreft het vermelden van mogelijke dwangsommen in een schriftelijke onderzoeksvolmacht; norm B betreft voorwaarden en beperkingen voor verdere verwerking en delen van persoonsgegevens in een AI-testomgeving.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A regelt onderzoeksbevoegdheden en de vermelding van sancties bij het niet verstrekken van registers, data, procedures of antwoorden. Norm B regelt rechtmatigheid, beveiliging, monitoring, bewaring, documentatie en beperkte verdere deling van persoonsgegevens bij AI-ontwikkeling, training en testen.
verdict.criterion_fired: De normen hebben geen dezelfde verb-level actie, geen dezelfde trigger en geen voldoende overeenkomstige compliance-inhoud; A ziet op een onderzoeks- en sanctiemechanisme, B op gegevensverwerking in een AI-testomgeving.
verdict.evidence_span_a: In deze machtiging worden eveneens de in artikel 35, lid 6, bedoelde dwangsommen genoemd
verdict.evidence_span_b: aanbieders kunnen de oorspronkelijk verzamelde gegevens alleen verder delen in overeenstemming met het Unierecht inzake gegevensbescherming

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both concern taking or requiring corrective action in response to regulatory concerns, but Norm A is a power of the lead overseer to request reports on actions or corrective measures already taken, whereas Norm B requires the AI provider to take adequate corrective measures within a prescribed period.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A concerns oversight reporting by critical ICT third-party providers regarding measures taken in response to recommendations; Norm B concerns substantive remediation by an AI provider to bring an AI system into compliance after a market-surveillance finding.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in actor, event, and operative action: Norm A involves a critical ICT third-party provider reporting corrective actions to a lead overseer, while Norm B involves an AI provider taking corrective measures after a high-risk/non-compliance assessment.
verdict.evidence_span_a: na afloop van de oversightactiviteiten te verzoeken om verslagen met vermelding van de ondernomen acties of de corrigerende maatregelen die door de kritieke derde aanbieders van ICT-diensten zijn genomen
verdict.evidence_span_b: Indien de aanbieder van het betrokken AI-systeem niet binnen de in lid 2 van dit artikel bedoelde termijn adequate corrigerende maatregelen neemt

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms impose an information/documentation-related compliance duty, but A requires an authorised representative to keep conformity materials available and provide them to the Minister on request, while B requires high-risk AI providers to retain automatically generated logs.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A concerns conformity documentation and cooperation with a minister; Norm B concerns retention of automatically generated AI-system logs for at least six months.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in actor, subject matter, and operative action: A concerns an authorised representative's retention/provision of conformity information and cooperation with measures, whereas B concerns a high-risk AI provider's retention of system logs.
verdict.evidence_span_a: het ter beschikking van Onze Minister houden van de EU-conformiteitsverklaring en de technische documentatie gedurende tien jaar nadat het apparaat of het radioapparaat in de handel is gebracht
verdict.evidence_span_b: Aanbieders van AI-systemen met een hoog risico bewaren de in artikel 12, lid 1, bedoelde logs die automatisch worden gegenereerd door hun AI-systemen met een hoog risico voor zover dergelijke logs onder hun controle vallen.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Beide normen leggen een vorm van documentatie-/transparantieverplichting op, maar niet dezelfde concrete handeling: norm A vereist openbaarmaking van beleid en procedures voor domeinnaamregistratiegegevens; norm B vereist bewaring van een volledige, gedetailleerde beschrijving en onderbouwing van AI-training, -testing en -validatie als technische documentatie.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A betreft publieke bekendmaking van verificatie- en andere procedures door domeinnaamregisters en registratiedienstverleners; norm B betreft interne bewaring van AI-testdocumentatie door aanbieders binnen een gereglementeerde AI-testomgeving.
verdict.criterion_fired: De normen verschillen zowel qua actor en onderwerp als qua kernhandeling: openbaarmaking van domeinnaamregistratiebeleid tegenover bewaring van AI-ontwikkelings- en testdocumentatie. Er is daarom geen dubbele compliance-last.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Zij maken dat beleid en die procedures openbaar.
verdict.evidence_span_b: een volledige en gedetailleerde beschrijving van het proces en de onderbouwing van het trainen, testen en valideren van het AI-systeem wordt samen met de testresultaten bewaard als onderdeel van de in bijlage IV bedoelde technische documentatie

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Norm A authorizes the lead overseer to hear or question persons to collect information during an investigation. Norm B imposes conditions on processing personal data in an AI regulatory sandbox, including a prohibition on decisions or measures affecting data subjects; it does not impose an information-gathering or reporting duty.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A concerns an investigative authority's power to obtain information from persons; Norm B concerns safeguards and limitations on personal-data processing for AI-system development, including preventing effects on data subjects.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms do not impose the same verb-level action, concern different subject matter and event families, and place the relevant legal power or obligation on different actor roles.

verdict.evidence_span_b: de verwerking van persoonsgegevens in het kader van de testomgeving mag niet leiden tot maatregelen of besluiten die gevolgen hebben voor de betrokkenen

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms involve an information-related duty triggered by circumstances or decisions relevant to regulatory oversight, but the underlying actions differ: Norm A requires a telecommunications party, on ministerial request, to provide a register extract or investigate/control-holder identity and third-party links; Norm B requires a notified body to inform other notified bodies about specified quality-management approvals and Union technical-documentation assessment certificates, including refusals, suspensions, withdrawals, limitations, and certain grants on request.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a request-based disclosure/investigation duty concerning control over a telecommunications party and possible threats to the public interest; Norm B is a mandatory inter-notified-body information-sharing duty concerning the status of approvals and technical-documentation certificates.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in actor role, triggering event, recipient, and substantive content; the apparent similarity is only a broad information/oversight theme, not the same compliance work repeated.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require the addressee to take a compliance-related action concerning a regulated digital subject, but Norm A requires answering access requests for domain-registration data, whereas Norm B requires an importer to verify and ensure a high-risk AI system’s conformity before placing it on the market, with notification only if a risk exists.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an on-request information-access response duty with a 72-hour deadline; Norm B is a pre-market conformity-verification duty for importers, supplemented by a conditional notification duty to specified parties where the system poses a relevant risk.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties concern different actors, different triggering events, and different core actions: responding to a legitimate request for domain-registration data versus verifying and ensuring conformity of a high-risk AI system before placing it on the market.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms involve maintaining or making information/documentation available to public authorities, but they do not impose the same underlying compliance action: Norm A requires collecting and maintaining accurate, complete domain-registration data in a database, whereas Norm B requires an authorised representative to perform specified oversight, retention, production, and cooperation tasks for an AI provider.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A concerns systematic collection and maintenance of domain-name registration data for DNS security and identification/contact purposes; Norm B concerns an authorised representative's AI Act mandate, including retaining technical documentation and supplying or cooperating with authorities on reasoned request.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both provisions impose obligations involving regulated ICT/AI-system providers, but they do not require the same compliance action: Article 38 empowers the lead overseer to investigate and request information or explanations, whereas Article 16 requires high-risk AI providers to perform a broad set of compliance, documentation, conformity, corrective-action, and information duties.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A concerns supervisory investigative powers and compelled cooperation; Norm B concerns substantive obligations of providers of high-risk AI systems, including compliance management, recordkeeping, conformity assessment, corrective measures, and demonstrating conformity on request.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms differ in both actor role and core duty: A authorizes a lead overseer to investigate critical third-party ICT-service providers and obtain explanations, while B imposes ongoing product-compliance obligations on providers of high-risk AI systems.
verdict.evidence_span_a: vertegenwoordigers van kritieke derde aanbieder van ICT-diensten op te roepen en te verzoeken om mondelinge of schriftelijke toelichting te geven bij feiten of documenten die betrekking hebben op het onderwerp en het doel van het onderzoek

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Norm A requires financial entities to register ICT-related incidents and significant cyber threats and establish processes for their monitoring, handling, and follow-up. verdict.criterion_fired: De normen hebben niet dezelfde kernactie, gebeurtenisfamilie of actorrol. A ziet op openbaarmaking door domeinnaamregisters en registratiedienstverleners; B op beperkingen en waarborgen voor persoonsgegevensverwerking in een AI-testomgeving.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Beide normen houden verband met openbaarmaking/publicatie van informatie, maar A vereist dat domeinnaamregistratiegegevens openbaarmakingsbeleid en -procedures openbaar worden gemaakt, terwijl B vereist dat een korte samenvatting van een AI-project, met doelstellingen en verwachte resultaten, op de website van bevoegde autoriteiten wordt gepubliceerd.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A betreft transparantie over beleid en procedures voor bekendmaking van domeinnaamregistratiegegevens; norm B betreft publicatie van inhoudelijke informatie over een AI-testproject en de resultaten/doelstellingen daarvan.
verdict.criterion_fired: De normen hebben geen voldoende gemeenschappelijke actor- en gebeurteniscontext en vereisen inhoudelijk verschillende openbaarmakingen; een oppervlakkige overeenkomst in het werkwoord 'openbaar maken/publiceren' volstaat niet.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De lidstaten schrijven voor dat het beleid en de procedures met betrekking tot de bekendmaking van dergelijke gegevens openbaar worden gemaakt.
verdict.evidence_span_b: een korte samenvatting van het in de testomgeving ontwikkelde AI-project en de doelstellingen en verwachte resultaten ervan worden op de website van de bevoegde autoriteiten gepubliceerd

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms involve making information or documentation available to an external party, but A requires a mandated representative to retain and provide conformity materials to the Minister, whereas B requires domain-name registries/registration-service providers to grant access to registration data to legitimate requesting parties and respond within 72 hours.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: The duties concern different actors, different subject matter, and different purposes: conformity-assessment records and regulatory cooperation under A versus domain-registration data access under B.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms do not impose the same underlying action on the same actor for the same event or content; A concerns retaining/providing conformity documentation and cooperating with risk-reduction measures, while B concerns granting access to domain-registration data on justified requests.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A requires making non-personal domain-name registration data public immediately after domain registration; B requires high-risk AI providers to demonstrate, upon a reasoned request from a national competent authority, that the AI system complies with Section 2 requirements.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: The norms concern different regulated objects and different compliance actions: public disclosure of domain-registration data versus demonstrating AI-system conformity to a competent authority.
verdict.criterion_fired: Different event family, actor role, regulated object, recipient context, and core action; the apparent similarity does not establish a duplicated reporting or disclosure burden.

verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in both core action and actor role: A concerns Member States enabling voluntary cybersecurity information exchange among entities; B concerns financial entities evaluating serious ICT disruptions and potentially reporting implemented changes to competent authorities.

verdict.evidence_span_a: onverwijld meedelen welke maatregelen die ontvangers kunnen nemen in reactie op die dreiging
verdict.evidence_span_b: relevante informatie over ernstige incidenten en mogelijke corrigerende maatregelen bijhouden, documenteren en onverwijld rapporteren aan het AI-bureau

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Geen gedeelde concrete compliance-actie: norm A betreft governance, goedkeuring en toezicht op cyberbeveiligingsrisicobeheersmaatregelen; norm B betreft toezichthouderfeedback en de blijvende verantwoordelijkheid van financiële entiteiten voor reeds gerapporteerde ICT-incidenten.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern a provider or other regulated actor taking action in response to a situation involving an external authority, but Norm A requires requesting an ACM decision on a dispute about a statutory tolerance obligation, whereas Norm B requires investigating a serious AI incident, assessing its risks, taking corrective measures, cooperating with authorities, and in some cases giving prior notice before altering the system.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an optional, time-limited request for an ACM decision after failure to reach agreement concerning a gedoogplicht or the location, timing, or method of works. Norm B is an immediate substantive incident-response investigation and remediation duty following a serious AI incident, with cooperation and procedural safeguards.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in core action, triggering event, actor role, and substantive purpose; the superficial similarity of involving an authority and a provider does not establish duplicated compliance work.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms regulate or constrain the use/operation of ICT or AI systems, but they do not require the same compliance action: Norm A requires continuous monitoring of the security and functioning of all ICT systems, while Norm B prohibits or conditions specified real-time remote biometric-identification uses in public spaces for law enforcement.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A imposes an ongoing ICT-security monitoring and risk-management duty on certain financial entities; Norm B imposes substantive prohibitions and authorization, impact-assessment, registration, and safeguards requirements on law-enforcement use of real-time remote biometric identification.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms do not impose the same underlying action, concern different regulated activities and actor roles, and have no common reporting recipient or deadline. Similarity at the broad level of regulating ICT/AI systems is insufficient for duplicate burden.

verdict.criterion_fired: The underlying retention duties are imposed on different actor roles, concern different information and regulatory objects, and serve different compliance purposes; the apparent similarity is limited to the generic idea of keeping information.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms impose obligations connected to regulated digital-system activity, but A requires immediate public disclosure of non-personal domain-registration data, whereas B requires an importer to verify and ensure conformity of a high-risk AI system before placing it on the market, with possible notification to specified parties and market-surveillance authorities if a risk or non-compliance is identified.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: The underlying duties, triggering events, and compliance outputs differ: A is a transparency/publication duty triggered by domain registration; B is a conformity-check and market-placement duty triggered before placing a high-risk AI system on the market, supplemented by a conditional notification duty.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms do not impose the same core action on the same actor in response to the same event. A concerns registries/domain-registration service entities making non-personal registration data public immediately after registration; B concerns importers verifying and ensuring AI-system conformity before market placement, and conditionally notifying specified parties and market-surveillance authorities.

Norm B requires notified bodies to inform other notified bodies about specified quality-management approvals and technical-documentation assessment certificates, including refusals, suspensions, withdrawals, restrictions, or issued certificates on request.

verdict.criterion_fired: The norms do not impose the same underlying compliance work: Norm A concerns entities supplying or updating organisational/contact and service-location information to competent authorities, while Norm B concerns notified bodies exchanging approval and certificate information with other notified bodies.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms impose governance and data-management compliance duties, but they require different substantive measures: A requires establishing and publishing policies and procedures to ensure accurate and complete domain-registration data; B permits exceptional processing of special-category personal data only subject to strict necessity, safeguards, access controls, non-disclosure, deletion, and record-keeping conditions.

verdict.criterion_fired: The norms do not impose the same underlying action on the same actor in response to the same kind of event. A requires domain-name registries and registration-service entities to establish and publish policies and procedures, while B sets conditions and safeguards for exceptional processing of special-category personal data by high-risk AI-system providers.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A requires the controller to report a personal-data breach to the competent supervisory authority. B concerns competent authorities’ enforcement powers, including ordering essential entities to remedy identified deficiencies or infringements; it does not itself impose the same breach-reporting duty on the entity.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a direct, time-bound breach-notification obligation imposed on a controller and addressed to a supervisory authority. Norm B is a framework obligation on Member States concerning enforcement powers of authorities, including remedial orders against essential entities; any reporting under B is either compliance with Article 23 reporting obligations or reporting on implementation of ordered measures, not the Article 33 notification itself.
verdict.criterion_fired: Different actor role and different core action: A requires breach notification; B requires Member States to empower authorities to enforce and order remediation, rather than requiring the entity to make the Article 33 notification.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both require the responsible actor to create and maintain structured documentation containing specified information: a GDPR record of processing activities and an AI Act technical file for a high-risk AI system.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: The duties concern different subject matter, purposes, and substantive contents: processing-activity records for GDPR accountability versus technical documentation demonstrating conformity of a high-risk AI system.
verdict.criterion_fired: The underlying documentation verbs are broadly similar, but the duties do not concern the same triggering event, actor role, or compliance content. Article 30 requires controllers or their representatives to maintain records of processing activities; Article 11 requires providers of high-risk AI systems to prepare and update technical documentation before placing the system on the market or putting it into service.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A requires an essential or important entity to submit a progress report while a reportable incident is still ongoing, followed by a final report after resolution. B requires a financial entity to conduct a post-incident ICT evaluation after a serious ICT-related incident, including analysis of causes, improvements, procedural compliance, measure effectiveness, and specified response and communication aspects; certain entities must communicate resulting changes to competent authorities on request.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: A is an incident-reporting duty with a progress-report/final-report sequence and a specified submission point. B is primarily an internal post-incident evaluation and improvement duty, with subsequent changes communicated to authorities only on request; its content is evaluative and remedial rather than a status report on the incident.
verdict.criterion_fired: Same incident family and broadly comparable regulated-entity role, but the core actions and required content differ: A requires progress/final incident reports, whereas B requires post-incident evaluation and identification of improvements, with only resulting changes communicated on request.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Norm A requires information to be supplied in an early warning about a significant incident: whether it was probably caused by an unlawful or malicious act, whether it may have cross-border effects, and the contact details of the person responsible for the report. Norm B requires financial entities to conduct post-incident evaluations after serious ICT-related incidents, analyze causes and needed improvements, assess whether procedures and measures were effective, and—on request for non-micro-enterprises—communicate implemented changes to competent authorities.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an early-warning reporting-information duty concerning the characterization and possible cross-border effects of a significant incident. Norm B is a post-incident review, remediation, and possible follow-up information duty concerning causes, procedural compliance, effectiveness, and implemented improvements.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms concern a broadly related ICT-incident context, but they impose different core actions on different actor categories: an entity must provide specified early-warning information under Norm A, whereas a financial entity must perform a post-incident evaluation and potentially communicate resulting changes under Norm B. The reporting content and compliance purpose are not the same.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms impose security-related measures on an entity/provider, but A requires considering suppliers’ cybersecurity quality and secure-development practices when selecting supply-chain measures, whereas B requires investigating a serious incident, including risk assessment and corrective measures, while avoiding certain system-altering investigations without prior notice.

verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in core action and event family: A is a preventive supply-chain security consideration duty, while B is a serious-incident investigation and non-interference/prior-notice duty.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern information-related compliance in a digital/data context, but A requires informing a supervisory authority about an exceptional international data transfer, whereas B requires making domain-registration-data disclosure policies and procedures public (and, in the broader provision, responding to access requests).

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both require the provider/entity to communicate information about an incident, but A requires an early warning to cybersecurity authorities, while B requires notifying affected individuals about a personal-data breach likely to adversely affect their privacy.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: The recipient, purpose, and required substance differ: A is an early-warning report to the CSIRT and competent authority concerning a significant incident; B is a privacy-impact notification to the affected data subject concerning a personal-data breach.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A requires a telecommunications party, upon the Minister’s request, to provide a register extract concerning a share right (and, in the alternative, investigate a controller’s identity and third-party ties). B permits high-risk AI providers, under strict conditions, to process special-category personal data to detect and correct bias, with security, access-control, deletion, and record-keeping requirements.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: A is a request-based information/investigation duty directed to a Minister concerning control over a telecommunications entity; B is an exceptional data-processing permission and safeguard regime for high-risk AI providers, with no reporting or provision of information to an authority.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms do not impose the same underlying action, concern different triggering circumstances and regulatory purposes, and bind different actor roles. A concerns ministerial scrutiny of potentially threatening control; B concerns exceptional processing of sensitive personal data for AI-bias detection and correction.

verdict.distinguishing_factor: The duties concern different subject matter and purposes: domain-registration identification/contact data for DNS security and resilience versus technical conformity documentation for high-risk AI systems.
verdict.criterion_fired: The underlying duties differ in actor, subject matter, and compliance purpose.
