verdict.shared_compliance_action: A requires a public electronic communications service provider to promptly notify the Dutch Data Protection Authority of a security breach affecting personal-data protection. B concerns the lead overseer’s power to request reports from critical ICT third-party providers about actions or corrective measures taken in response to oversight recommendations; it is an oversight/information-request mechanism, not a provider’s incident-notification duty.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: A is an urgent, provider-initiated notification of a qualifying personal-data security breach to the data-protection authority. B is a lead-overseer-initiated request for post-oversight reports on actions or corrective measures, potentially followed by transmission to other authorities and enforcement for non-compliance.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in actor, triggering event, action, purpose, and content: A requires breach notification by an electronic communications provider; B empowers a lead overseer to request corrective-action reports from critical ICT third-party providers.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern maintaining or preparing technical documentation connected with demonstrating conformity of a regulated product or system. However, Norm A requires an authorised representative to keep specified existing documents available for the Minister for ten years and provide them on request; Norm B requires the provider of a high-risk AI system to create and update technical documentation before market placement or putting into service, containing Annex IV information for conformity assessment.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a retention-and-on-request availability duty imposed on an authorised representative and directed to the Minister; Norm B is a substantive preparation and updating duty imposed on the high-risk AI-system provider, with documentation intended for assessment by competent authorities and notified bodies.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in core action, triggering context, and obligated actor: A concerns ten-year retention and request-based provision of conformity documents after market placement, while B concerns prior preparation and ongoing updating of AI technical documentation.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A requires the controller to seek the data protection officer’s advice when carrying out a data protection impact assessment. B requires certain financial entities to establish and maintain a documented ICT-risk-management framework and related ICT-security, resilience, monitoring, continuity, testing, and improvement measures; on request, an evaluation report is submitted to the competent authority.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: A is an internal consultation duty connected to a data protection impact assessment and addressed to the data protection officer; B is an ongoing ICT-risk-management and operational-resilience regime for specified financial entities, with possible documentation and submission to a competent authority.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms impose different core actions on different duty-bearer roles and concern different event or compliance families: internal DPO consultation during a DPIA versus establishment and maintenance of an ICT-risk-management framework and resilience controls.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A requires essential and important entities to implement proportionate technical, operational, and organisational cybersecurity-risk-management measures to prevent incidents or limit their effects. B requires financial entities to conduct post-incident ICT evaluations, analyse causes and improvements, and—where applicable—communicate implemented changes to competent authorities on request. These are not the same underlying compliance action.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an ongoing preventive and risk-management obligation concerning network and information-system security measures; Norm B is a post-incident review, improvement-identification, and (for certain entities) on-request communication obligation.
verdict.criterion_fired: Same broad ICT/cyber-incident context and broadly comparable regulated-entity role, but the duties require materially different work: preventive risk-management measures versus post-incident evaluation and possible communication of resulting changes. The different recipient does not determine the result; the low content overlap does.

verdict.distinguishing_factor: The recipient, purpose, and required reporting content differ: A is a risk-based data-breach communication to the data subject; B is supervisory reporting of serious ICT-related incidents, including initial, interim/updated, and final reports.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties do not impose the same core compliance action on the same actor role: GDPR Article 34 concerns a controller communicating a personal-data breach to the affected data subject, while DORA Article 19 concerns a financial entity reporting serious ICT-related incidents to a competent authority.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Beide normen houden een actor verplicht tot het verstrekken van informatie aan een overheidsinstantie, maar de inhoud en het doel van die verstrekking verschillen wezenlijk: norm A betreft op verzoek conformiteitsinformatie en -documentatie over apparaten; norm B betreft identificatie-, contact-, sector- en dienstverleningsinformatie voor het opstellen en bijhouden van een entiteitenlijst, inclusief wijzigingen binnen twee weken.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A ziet op het aantonen van productconformiteit door een gemachtigde op verzoek van de minister; norm B ziet op registratie/listing van essentiële of belangrijke entiteiten en het melden van wijzigingen in hun basisgegevens aan bevoegde autoriteiten.
verdict.criterion_fired: De normen hebben wel een vergelijkbare verbale handeling (informatie verstrekken aan een autoriteit), maar niet dezelfde actorrol of hetzelfde soort triggering event/compliance-doel. Norm A betreft een gemachtigde voor radioapparatuur en een verzoek om conformiteitsdocumentatie; norm B betreft essentiële/belangrijke entiteiten en initiële of gewijzigde registratiegegevens voor een cyberbeveiligingslijst. Dit is geen herhaling van dezelfde compliancewerkzaamheden.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern ongoing management of ICT/cybersecurity risk, including security measures and monitoring, but A requires an entity to take account of coordinated supply-chain security-risk assessments when selecting measures, whereas B requires specified small financial entities to maintain and operate a simplified ICT-risk-management framework, including continuous monitoring of ICT-system security and operation.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a supply-chain risk-assessment consideration within a broader cybersecurity duty; Norm B is a sector-specific, ongoing ICT-risk-management and monitoring framework duty for specified financial entities.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties do not impose the same underlying action: A concerns considering coordinated critical-supply-chain security-risk-assessment results when choosing measures, while B concerns continuously monitoring all ICT systems and maintaining a documented ICT-risk-management framework. They also apply to different actor categories and are not triggered by the same event.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Norm A requires domain-name registration data registries and registration-service entities to grant access to specific registration data upon lawful, duly justified requests and answer within 72 hours. Norm B permits high-risk-AI providers, only exceptionally and subject to safeguards, to process special categories of personal data to detect and correct bias, including access controls, non-disclosure, deletion, and recording the necessity and reasons for the processing.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: The norms concern different compliance actions and different subject matters: responding to justified access requests for domain-registration data versus internally processing sensitive personal data for bias detection and correction in high-risk AI systems.
verdict.criterion_fired: Different core action, event family, and actor role; neither norm requires the same compliance work to be performed twice.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Beide normen leggen geen identieke rapportage- of meldingsplicht op: norm A betreft registratie van nummergebruikers en het rechtswege in gebruik geven van een nummer; norm B betreft het bijhouden van een register van verwerkingsactiviteiten met voorgeschreven inhoud.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is een sectorspecifieke registratie- en nummergebruiksplicht voor nummerhouders; norm B is een gegevensbeschermingsplicht voor verwerkingsverantwoordelijken en hun vertegenwoordigers om verwerkingsactiviteiten te documenteren.
verdict.criterion_fired: De normen betreffen verschillende kernhandelingen, verschillende soorten gereguleerde activiteiten en niet noodzakelijk dezelfde actorrol; een eventuele overlap in persoonsgegevens of registratie is onvoldoende om dezelfde compliance-werkzaamheden aan te nemen.

verdict.evidence_span_b: Elke verwerkingsverantwoordelijke en, in voorkomend geval, de vertegenwoordiger van de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke houdt een register van de verwerkingsactiviteiten die onder hun verantwoordelijkheid plaatsvinden.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern handling ICT/security incidents, but A requires prompt external reporting of significant incidents and relevant cross-border-impact information, whereas B requires internal ICT-risk controls to detect anomalies and handle ICT-related incidents quickly.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an incident-reporting and notification duty to a CSIRT or competent authority (and, where applicable, service recipients); Norm B is an ongoing ICT-risk-management, detection, and incident-response control duty with no reporting recipient or incident-reporting deadline.
verdict.criterion_fired: The underlying duties differ: A requires external notification/reporting of significant incidents, while B requires establishing and maintaining internal ICT-risk-management measures, including detection and rapid handling of incidents. The shared incident/security context is insufficient for duplicate burden, and the actor populations are not the same.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Norm A requires an entity, as part of an early warning concerning a significant incident, to provide the contact details of the official responsible for the report. Norm B requires financial entities to continuously identify ICT-risk sources and assess relevant cyber threats and ICT vulnerabilities, including at least annual evaluation of risk scenarios.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A concerns incident-related early-warning content and provision of a reporting official’s contact details; Norm B concerns ongoing ICT-risk identification and cybersecurity risk assessment, not incident reporting.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in core action, triggering context, and compliance purpose: incident early-warning information versus continuous and annual ICT-risk assessment.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A requires entities to report changes to previously submitted identification/contact/sector information to competent authorities; B requires providers of general-purpose AI models to prepare, maintain, and make available technical and other documentation/information for AI-system providers, and to make a training-content summary public.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: The norms concern different duties and different substantive information: A is a time-limited change notification to competent authorities, while B is ongoing AI-model documentation and disclosure to downstream AI-system providers, authorities on request, and the public.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern action following a serious/significant ICT-related operational incident, but A requires urgent notification to service recipients, whereas B requires a post-incident evaluation, causal analysis, identification of improvements, and—on request for non-micro financial entities—communication of implemented changes to competent authorities.

verdict.criterion_fired: The event family is related, but the core actions, actor categories, recipients, and compliance purposes differ: immediate customer/service-recipient notification versus post-incident evaluation and authority-facing disclosure of implemented changes.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Norm A empowers the lead overseer to investigate and obtain explanations or information from representatives of critical third-party ICT service providers; Norm B imposes conditions on processing personal data in an AI regulatory sandbox, including security, deletion, logging, documentation, and publication requirements.

verdict.criterion_fired: The norms do not impose the same underlying action, concern the same event family, or bind the same actor in the same role. One is an investigative authority power; the other is a set of conditions and safeguards for personal-data processing in an AI regulatory sandbox.

verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in actor, subject matter, and purpose: GDPR processing-activity records versus general-purpose AI-model documentation and information. verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both provisions concern addressing the consequences or implications of security/significant incidents, but Norm A requires an entity to state information in an early warning, while Norm B requires communications providers to implement technical, operational, and organisational security measures.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an information-disclosure element of an early warning about a significant incident, specifically whether it may have cross-border effects; Norm B is a preventive/mitigative security-measures duty aimed at limiting incident consequences for national security or public order.
verdict.criterion_fired: Different underlying action and actor role: Norm A concerns reporting information about a significant incident, whereas Norm B concerns implementing security measures to mitigate security-incident consequences.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern responding to a significant/serious incident, but Norm A requires an early warning to the entity’s CSIRT and competent authority, whereas Norm B requires the AI provider to investigate the incident and AI system, conduct a risk assessment, take corrective measures, cooperate with authorities, and give prior notice before potentially compromising modifications.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an incident-warning/reporting duty; Norm B is a post-incident investigation, risk-assessment, corrective-action, cooperation, and procedural-notice duty.
verdict.criterion_fired: The event family is broadly similar, but the core actions and actor roles differ: Norm A imposes an early-warning duty on essential or important entities, while Norm B imposes investigation and remediation duties on an AI provider.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit geeft ten behoeve van de melding, bedoeld in artikel 27, eerste lid, een vroegtijdige waarschuwing over het significante incident aan haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Na de melding van een ernstig incident op grond van lid 1 verricht de aanbieder onverwijld het nodige onderzoek in verband met het ernstige incident en het betrokken AI-systeem.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms involve an actor supplying or making information available to a public authority, but the underlying duties are not the same: A concerns cooperation with risk-elimination measures and, separately, information/documentation proving product conformity on request; B concerns initial entity-identification information and prompt updates to competent authorities.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A applies to an appointed representative for devices/radio equipment and requires cooperation with measures eliminating product risks (with related on-request conformity documentation duties). Norm B applies to entities covered by the NIS2 listing mechanism and requires registration details and updates, including a two-week maximum for changes.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms do not impose the same underlying action, concern different triggering circumstances and regulatory purposes, and bind different actor roles. Any superficial similarity consists only in interaction with a public authority; a different recipient alone would not have been decisive, but here the duties and event families are materially different.
verdict.evidence_span_a: het op verzoek van Onze Minister verlenen van medewerking aan eventueel genomen maatregelen ter uitschakeling van de risico's van apparaten of radioapparaten waarvoor hij als gemachtigde is aangewezen

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Norm A requires entities to report changes to previously submitted identification/contact information to the competent authorities within two weeks. Norm B permits providers of high-risk AI systems, under strict conditions, to process special categories of personal data to detect and correct bias, including safeguards, access controls, deletion, and register documentation.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a time-bound change-notification duty to competent authorities; Norm B is a substantive data-processing permission subject to safeguards and documentation, with no reporting duty or deadline.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms impose different kinds of obligations concerning different subject matter and purposes: administrative notification of changed entity details versus controlled processing of sensitive personal data for bias detection and correction.
verdict.evidence_span_a: melden onmiddellijk elke wijziging in de bijzonderheden die zij op grond van de eerste alinea van dit lid hebben ingediend, en in elk geval binnen twee weken na de datum van de wijziging

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both provisions involve maintaining or including information in a register of processing activities, but Norm A requires a processor's comprehensive register, whereas Norm B requires that an existing GDPR-related register contain specific reasons justifying exceptional processing of special-category data for bias detection and correction.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a standalone processor record-keeping duty covering all processing-activity categories and specified particulars; Norm B is a narrowly targeted documentation requirement concerning the necessity and alternatives analysis for processing special-category data in high-risk AI systems.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in actor scope, triggering context, and required content: Norm A concerns a processor's general register of processing activities, while Norm B concerns documenting the justification for exceptional special-category-data processing by providers of high-risk AI systems. A shared reference to a processing-activities register is insufficient to establish the same compliance work.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern organisational handling of technology-related risk or incidents, but A requires maintaining and documenting an ICT-risk-management framework, including mapping key dependencies on ICT third-party providers, whereas B requires an AI provider to investigate a serious incident and cooperate with competent authorities or a notified body.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a standing ICT-risk-governance and dependency-mapping obligation for specified financial entities; Norm B is a post-serious-incident investigation and cooperation obligation for an AI provider.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both require the responsible entity to implement appropriate technical and organisational measures, but A concerns securing and ultimately deleting legally retained telecommunications data, while B concerns data protection by design/default and data minimisation for personal-data processing.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is tied to retained telecommunications data and expressly covers security, authorised access, protection against specified forms of compromise, and destruction after the retention period. Norm B applies to the controller's processing generally and requires measures ensuring that only personal data necessary for each specific purpose are processed, including limits on quantity, processing extent, storage period, and accessibility, with particular emphasis on preventing unrestricted access without human intervention.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms share a generic measure-taking verb, but they do not impose the same compliance duty: A applies to public telecommunications providers and retained traffic/data records, whereas B applies to a controller and governs privacy-by-design/default, purpose-specific data minimisation, and accessibility across processing. The retention-period destruction requirement in A does not make the duties the same as B's broader storage-limitation requirement.

verdict.evidence_span_b: De verwerkingsverantwoordelijke treft passende technische en organisatorische maatregelen om ervoor te zorgen dat in beginsel alleen persoonsgegevens worden verwerkt die noodzakelijk zijn voor elk specifiek doel van de verwerking.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Beide normen leggen een informatie-/documentatiegerichte activiteit op, maar niet dezelfde concrete handeling: norm A machtigt de toezichthouder om bestaande registers, data en ander materiaal te onderzoeken en gewaarmerkte kopieën of uittreksels daarvan te maken of te verkrijgen; norm B verplicht AI-modelaanbieders om technische documentatie en andere informatie op te stellen, bij te houden, beschikbaar te stellen en een trainingscontentsamenvatting openbaar te maken.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A betreft onderzoeksbevoegdheden van een lead overseer jegens een kritieke derde aanbieder van ICT-diensten; norm B betreft doorlopende documentatie-, informatieverstrekking- en openbaarmakingsverplichtingen van aanbieders van AI-modellen voor algemene doeleinden.
verdict.criterion_fired: De normen hebben niet dezelfde actorrol of gebeurtenisfamilie en leggen geen identieke kernhandeling op. A ziet op toezichthoudend onderzoek en het verkrijgen van gewaarmerkte kopieën; B op het opstellen, actualiseren, beschikbaar stellen en openbaar maken van AI-modeldocumentatie.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require the relevant provider/entity to carry out an assessment or investigation connected with ICT/AI-system risk or incidents, but they do not require the same concrete compliance action.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires a recurring, at-least-annual assessment of all legacy ICT systems, including assessments before and after specified technology, application, or system connections. Norm B requires an immediate, incident-specific investigation after a serious incident report, including incident risk assessment, corrective measures, cooperation with authorities, and restrictions on altering the AI system during the investigation.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties concern different actors, different triggering circumstances, and different substantive work: periodic legacy-ICT risk assessment versus urgent post-serious-incident AI-system investigation.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Andere financiële entiteiten dan micro-ondernemingen verrichten regelmatig en ten minste eenmaal per jaar een specifieke ICT-risicobeoordeling op alle legacy-ICT-systemen
verdict.evidence_span_b: Na de melding van een ernstig incident op grond van lid 1 verricht de aanbieder onverwijld het nodige onderzoek in verband met het ernstige incident en het betrokken AI-systeem.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern compliance controls connected to regulated operational activity, but they require different actions: Norm A requires financial entities to maintain accessible records during activation of ICT continuity/response-and-recovery plans; Norm B requires importers to verify specified conformity conditions before placing a high-risk AI system on the market, and, where a risk exists, to notify specified parties and market-surveillance authorities.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an incident-continuity recordkeeping duty triggered by activation of ICT response and recovery plans. Norm B is a pre-market product-conformity verification duty for importers, supplemented by a conditional notification duty concerning a risky, non-compliant, counterfeit, or falsely documented high-risk AI system.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in actor role, triggering event, and verb-level action: maintaining accessible operational records during ICT disruptions versus verifying AI conformity before market placement (and conditionally notifying authorities and other parties).

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A requires an ongoing significant-incident progress report to be submitted to the CSIRT or competent authority; B requires post-incident evaluation, including analysis of disruption causes, and (for non-micro financial entities) communication of implemented changes to competent authorities on request.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: A is an external incident-reporting duty with a contemporaneous progress-report submission; B is an internal post-incident review and improvement duty, with possible later disclosure of resulting changes on request.
verdict.criterion_fired: Same incident family and broadly similar regulated-entity role, but the operative actions and required content differ: incident-status reporting to an authority versus internal causal analysis and improvement assessment.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both provisions concern making information or documentation available to a public authority, but A imposes an ongoing document-retention/availability duty on an authorised representative, whereas B grants an overseer investigative powers to inspect, copy, question, and request traffic records.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a substantive, time-limited retention and production duty tied to conformity documentation; Norm B is an authority's investigative power covering potentially broad materials and communications-traffic records, with no corresponding retention duty or specified deadline.
verdict.criterion_fired: Different core action, event/trigger structure, and actor role; A concerns an authorised representative's ten-year retention and on-request provision of conformity records, while B concerns the lead overseer's power to request traffic overviews and conduct a general investigation.

verdict.criterion_fired: Different core action, event family, and actor role; the apparent similarity is not a duplicated reporting or record-keeping obligation.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Geen gedeelde concrete compliance-actie: norm A vereist dat bij het kiezen van maatregelen rekening wordt gehouden met leveranciers- en ketenrisicobeoordelingsresultaten; norm B vereist onderzoek naar een ernstig AI-incident, risicobeoordeling, corrigerende maatregelen en samenwerking met autoriteiten.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: NORM A requires an internet-access provider to notify the affected subscriber before, or as soon as possible after, taking a protective suspension or termination measure. NORM B requires essential and important entities to implement proportionate technical, operational, and organisational cybersecurity risk-management measures to prevent incidents and limit their effects.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: A is an individual subscriber notification tied to a specific service suspension or termination; B is a general preventive and mitigative cybersecurity-control obligation, with no reporting or notification duty.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in both actor role and core action: A is provider-to-subscriber notification concerning a specific protective service measure, whereas B concerns entities implementing cybersecurity risk-management measures. The shared security-related context is insufficient to establish duplicated compliance work.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both concern supplying information or documentation to a public authority in a broad sense, but Norm A imposes a standing entity-registration/update duty, whereas Norm B grants an investigative power to the lead overseer to obtain copies or extracts of records and other material.

verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in actor role, triggering context, and substantive content: Norm A concerns entity identification and updates for a Member State list; Norm B concerns investigative document-copying powers exercised by the lead overseer.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern organisational ICT/cybersecurity risk-management measures, but A requires considering direct suppliers’ vulnerabilities and related supply-chain security factors when selecting measures, whereas B requires exempt small financial entities to establish and maintain a documented ICT-risk-management framework and related controls, including staff awareness and training.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a supply-chain risk-assessment input within a broader NIS2 security-measures duty; Norm B is a simplified ICT-risk-management framework and control regime for specified financial entities, including monitoring, continuity, testing, and training.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties do not impose the same core action on the same actor role: A concerns an essential or important entity taking supplier vulnerabilities and supply-chain security into account, while B concerns specified exempt financial entities establishing and maintaining a documented ICT-risk-management framework and associated controls.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require the regulated entity to establish or prepare compliance-related internal material: ICT-incident management procedures/processes under Norm A, and technical documentation for a high-risk AI system under Norm B.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A concerns ongoing ICT-incident monitoring, handling, follow-up, and root-cause remediation by financial entities; Norm B concerns pre-market and updated technical documentation demonstrating conformity of a high-risk AI system and supporting conformity assessment.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern maintaining technical documentation and making it available to a public authority on request, but they do not require the same substantive documentation or serve the same regulatory purpose.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires the appointed representative to keep the EU declaration of conformity and technical documentation available for ten years and, on request, provide all information and documentation needed to demonstrate conformity of specified radio/electrical equipment. Norm B requires providers of general-purpose AI models to create and keep up to date model documentation, including training, testing and evaluation information, so it can be supplied to the AI Office and national competent authorities on request, alongside broader duties concerning downstream providers, copyright compliance and publication of a training-content summary.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties concern different regulated objects and regulatory regimes, are imposed on different actor roles, and require materially different documentation: equipment conformity records versus AI-model lifecycle, training, testing and evaluation documentation. The shared availability/provision mechanism is not enough to establish duplicated compliance work.
verdict.evidence_span_a: het ter beschikking van Onze Minister houden van de EU-conformiteitsverklaring en de technische documentatie gedurende tien jaar nadat het apparaat of het radioapparaat in de handel is gebracht

verdict.criterion_fired: The norms do not impose the same underlying action, concern different actors and purposes, and are not triggered by the same event. Any overlap in the word 'registers' is incidental and does not establish duplicated compliance work.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Elke verwerkingsverantwoordelijke en, in voorkomend geval, de vertegenwoordiger van de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke houdt een register van de verwerkingsactiviteiten die onder hun verantwoordelijkheid plaatsvinden.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Beide normen vereisen dat een gereguleerde entiteit informatie aan bevoegde autoriteiten verstrekt of daarvoor beschikbaar stelt, maar zij zien op verschillende soorten informatie en verschillende compliance-doeleinden.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms involve supplying information or documentation to a public authority, but they do not require the same underlying compliance work: Norm A requires registration information and updates for a national register, while Norm B requires an authorised representative to maintain technical documentation and provide information/documentation to the AI Office or national authorities on a reasoned request.

verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in actor role, triggering context, purpose, and substantive content. verdict.criterion_fired: De normen betreffen verschillende kernhandelingen, actoren en juridische situaties: een doorgiftemelding onder de AVG tegenover een onderzoeks- en informatieverzamelingsbevoegdheid onder DORA.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms involve communicating information about a security/integrity-related event or measure, but A requires notice to an affected subscriber about a provider’s protective service measure, whereas B requires structured incident reporting by covered entities to a CSIRT or competent authority.

verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in core action, actor role, recipient, purpose, and required content; the shared security-related context and notification/reporting vocabulary do not make them the same compliance work.

verdict.criterion_fired: Different core action, event/role, and compliance purpose; the apparent similarity is not a duplicated reporting or documentation burden.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both involve providing or responding with information, but A requires domain-name registration entities to answer a lawful, duly justified access request for specific domain-registration data, whereas B requires high-risk AI providers to provide information required under Article 20 and, separately, to demonstrate conformity on a reasoned request from a national competent authority.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: The duties concern different regulatory subject matter and purposes: access to domain-registration data for a legitimate requesting party versus AI-provider corrective-action and Article 20 information obligations within the high-risk AI regime.
verdict.criterion_fired: Different event family and actor role; the apparent similarity is limited to a broad information-provision verb and does not establish the same compliance work.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A requires controllers (and, where applicable, their representatives) to maintain a register containing specified processing-activity information. verdict.criterion_fired: The underlying actions, triggering events, and actor roles differ: A concerns reporting changes in entity information, whereas B concerns remedying formal non-conformity identified by a market-surveillance authority.

verdict.criterion_fired: The duties concern different subject matter, actors, and compliance purposes: product conformity and market-surveillance cooperation versus maintaining a personal-data processing-activities register.

verdict.criterion_fired: Same representative role, same ten-year post-market-placement retention pattern, and related request-based information/cooperation duties, but different regulated products, documents, authorities, and substantive compliance purposes mean the obligations are not simply the same work repeated.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both concern reporting a significant/ICT incident to a cybersecurity incident-response authority, but Norm B specifically extends certain EU-regulation reports (including voluntary reports) to the designated sectoral CSIRT, while Norm A imposes a general significant-incident reporting duty on essential or important entities under Articles 26–29.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a general duty on essential or important entities to report every significant incident under the Cybersecurity Act framework; Norm B is an additional-recipient rule for specified financial-sector actors, covering reports required or voluntarily made under Article 19 of the EU regulation.
verdict.criterion_fired: Same reporting action, incident family, and broadly comparable regulated-entity role, but the provisions do not establish the same report content or the same underlying reporting duty: Norm A covers every significant incident, whereas Norm B redirects/adds reporting of specified EU-regulation ICT-incident reports, including voluntary reports, to a sectoral CSIRT.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit meldt overeenkomstig de artikelen 26 tot en met 29 ieder significant incident.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both involve communicating information about a security-related incident after the actor becomes aware of it, but Norm A requires the processor to inform the controller, whereas Norm B requires covered entities to submit a structured series of reports to a CSIRT or competent authority.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a prompt processor-to-controller notification of a personal-data breach; Norm B is a multi-stage, authority-facing reporting regime for significant incidents, with specified warning, incident, interim, and final reports and substantially more detailed content.
verdict.criterion_fired: The event family is broadly related, but the actor role, recipient, core reporting duty, and required content differ materially; this is not the same compliance work repeated.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both concern handling ICT/security incidents, but Norm A requires including specific incident information in an early warning, whereas Norm B requires maintaining ICT-risk-management capabilities to detect anomalies and handle ICT-related incidents quickly.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an incident-triggered early-warning information duty; Norm B is an ongoing preventive and operational ICT-risk-management duty, with periodic and serious-incident-related evaluation and possible submission of an evaluation report on request.
verdict.criterion_fired: Same incident/security-risk family and broadly comparable regulated-entity role, but the duties require materially different compliance work: incident-warning content versus an ongoing ICT-risk-management framework and operational controls.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern post-incident risk-management activity, but A requires incorporating operational lessons from incident testing/analysis into an ICT-risk-assessment process, whereas B requires investigating a serious incident and AI system, including risk assessment and corrective measures, while avoiding certain system modifications and cooperating with authorities.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a continuing internal ICT-risk-management and lessons-learned measure for specified financial entities; Norm B is an immediate investigation and procedural safeguard following notification of a serious AI incident.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties do not have the same core action or actor role: A concerns specified financial-sector entities integrating incident-analysis conclusions into ICT-risk assessment, while B concerns an AI provider investigating a serious incident and refraining from unnotified system modifications.
verdict.evidence_span_a: in voorkomend geval de relevante operationele conclusies die voortvloeien uit de in punt g) bedoelde tests en uit de analyse na een incident opnemen in het ICT-risicobeoordelingsproces

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern handling ICT/security incidents, but A requires reporting a specific significant incident to a CSIRT and competent authority, whereas B requires financial entities to establish and implement an incident-management process for detecting, managing, and reporting ICT-related incidents.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an incident-triggered external notification duty with specified report content and a 72-hour deadline (or 24 hours for the related trust-service exception). Norm B is an ongoing organizational/process-management duty and does not itself require a particular incident report to a recipient.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in both actor role and core action: A imposes an immediate incident-reporting obligation on essential or important entities, while B imposes a process-design, adoption, implementation, detection, management, and reporting obligation on financial entities. The shared ICT-incident subject matter is insufficient to make the compliance work duplicative.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both involve compliance-related information handling, but Norm A requires informing a supervisory authority about an exceptional personal-data transfer, whereas Norm B requires providers of general-purpose AI models to create and maintain technical documentation and other materials, making them available or public as specified.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an authority notification triggered by an exceptional international personal-data transfer; Norm B is an ongoing documentation, information-sharing, policy, and publication regime for providers of general-purpose AI models.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in core action, triggering event, actor role, recipient/purpose, and substantive content; Norm A concerns notifying a supervisory authority of a specific exceptional data transfer, while Norm B concerns maintaining and disseminating AI-model documentation and related information.

verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an incident report by an essential or important entity to cybersecurity authorities, including information for assessing cross-border effects; Norm B is a clear-language communication to the data subject about the nature of a personal-data breach and specified information and measures under GDPR Article 33(3)(b)–(d).
verdict.criterion_fired: Same broad incident-reporting/notification family, but different actor-duty framing, recipients, purposes, and required content; therefore related burden rather than repeated identical compliance work.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A requires an essential or important entity to promptly inform potentially affected service recipients about measures they can take in response to a significant cyber threat and, if necessary, to inform them of the threat itself. B concerns the lead overseer imposing a coercive fine on a critical ICT third-party provider for non-compliance with supervisory measures, after at least 30 calendar days, with the fine imposed daily until compliance (subject to the stated maximum period and procedural safeguards).
verdict.distinguishing_factor: A is a substantive cyber-threat communication duty owed to service recipients; B is an enforcement and sanctioning power exercised by a supervisory authority against a critical ICT third-party provider for failure to comply with supervisory measures.
verdict.criterion_fired: Different core action, triggering event, and actor role; B is a supervisory sanction rather than a report, notification, or information duty comparable to A.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit deelt de ontvangers van haar diensten, die mogelijkerwijs door een significante cyberdreiging in relatie tot het ontvangen van die diensten worden getroffen, onverwijld mee welke maatregelen die ontvangers kunnen nemen in reactie op die dreiging.
verdict.evidence_span_b: neemt de lead overseer een besluit aan waarmee een dwangsom wordt opgelegd om de kritieke derde aanbieder van ICT-diensten tot nakoming van die maatregelen te dwingen.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms involve responding to or supplying information in response to a request, but they require different substantive compliance work: Norm A requires granting access to specific domain-name registration data, whereas Norm B requires notified conformity-assessment bodies to inform the notifying authority about specified certification, accreditation, authority-request, and activity matters.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an access request concerning specific domain-name registration data made by a legitimate party; Norm B is an information-notification duty concerning conformity-assessment activities and related certification or designation matters, owed to the notifying authority.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in both actor role and substantive event/content: domain-name registries or registration-service entities must answer a legitimate data-access request within 72 hours, while notified conformity-assessment bodies must notify the notifying authority about specified conformity-assessment and certification matters, with no deadline stated here.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Norm A requires the controller, when conducting a data-protection impact assessment, to seek the data protection officer’s advice. Norm B prohibits specified AI practices, including placing on the market, putting into service, or using prohibited AI systems; it does not impose a reporting, consultation, or impact-assessment duty on the same actor.

verdict.criterion_fired: The norms do not impose the same verb-level action, concern different triggering circumstances, and do not place the duty on the same actor role. Norm A requires seeking advice from a data protection officer; Norm B prohibits specified conduct involving AI systems.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms impose substantive controls on the use or management of technology, but they do not require the same compliance action: Article 16 requires covered financial entities to establish and operate ICT-risk-management measures, whereas Article 5 prohibits specified AI practices, including certain biometric categorisation uses.

verdict.criterion_fired: The norms concern different regulated conduct, different actor roles, and different legal mechanisms: ongoing ICT-risk controls versus prohibition of specified AI practices. They do not require the same work to be performed twice.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Beide normen leggen een verplichting op rond het omgaan met gegevens, maar norm A vereist het verzamelen en bijhouden van nauwkeurige en volledige domeinnaamregistratiegegevens in een database; norm B vereist bescherming van persoonsgegevens die in een AI-testomgeving worden verwerkt, als onderdeel van verdere verwerking voor AI-ontwikkeling, -training en -testing.

Norm B betreft technische en organisatorische bescherming van persoonsgegevens binnen een geïsoleerde AI-testomgeving, met aanvullende beperkingen op verwerking, delen en gebruik.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require an organizational information-governance measure: establishing/maintaining procedures or an information register. However, Norm A requires domain-name registries and registration-service entities to establish and publish policies and procedures ensuring accurate and complete registration data, while Norm B requires financial entities to maintain, document, report on, and provide an ICT-contract information register to competent authorities.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both involve supplying information to a public authority: A requires the authorised representative to provide the Minister with information and documentation on request to demonstrate product conformity; B requires the controller to inform the supervisory authority about a non-routine international data transfer and separately inform the data subject about the transfer and interests pursued.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: The duties concern different substantive subject matter and purposes: product-conformity documentation and cooperation with a minister versus justification and notification of an exceptional personal-data transfer to a supervisory authority.
verdict.criterion_fired: The underlying event, actor role, and required content are materially different; the superficial similarity is limited to informing or providing information to an authority.

verdict.evidence_span_b: De verwerkingsverantwoordelijke informeert de toezichthoudende autoriteit over de doorgifte.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require the regulated actor to create and maintain structured documentation or records, but they concern different subject matter and serve different compliance purposes: domain-registration databases versus high-risk-AI technical documentation demonstrating conformity.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A concerns accurate and complete domain-name registration data identifying registrants and domain-management contacts; Norm B concerns technical documentation demonstrating that a high-risk AI system complies with applicable requirements and enabling conformity assessment by authorities and notified bodies.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in actor role, subject matter, and compliance purpose. Norm A applies to top-level-domain registries and domain-registration service providers and requires maintaining registration data in a database. Norm B applies to providers of high-risk AI systems and requires preparing and updating technical conformity documentation before placing the system on the market or putting it into service.

verdict.evidence_span_b: De technische documentatie van een AI-systeem met een hoog risico wordt opgesteld voordat dit systeem in de handel wordt gebracht of in gebruik wordt gesteld, en wordt geactualiseerd.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Beide normen houden verband met het beschikbaar stellen van informatie voor juridische/regulatoire doeleinden, maar A vereist toegangverlening tot domeinnaamregistratiegegevens op een gemotiveerd verzoek, terwijl B vereist dat technische documentatie over een hoog-risico-AI-systeem wordt opgesteld en bijgewerkt (en voor bepaalde kmo’s eventueel een formulier wordt gebruikt).
verdict.distinguishing_factor: A betreft een reactieve toegangverlening aan legitieme verzoekers binnen 72 uur; B betreft proactieve technische documentatie voor conformiteitsbeoordeling vóór marktintroductie of ingebruikname en daarna actualisering.
verdict.criterion_fired: De normen hebben niet dezelfde kernhandeling, gebeurtenisfamilie of actorrol: A ziet op registers en domeinnaamregistratiedienstverleners die registratiegegevens op verzoek toegankelijk maken; B ziet op de aanbieder/verantwoordelijke voor een hoog-risico-AI-systeem die technische documentatie opstelt en actualiseert.
verdict.evidence_span_a: verzoeken om toegang onverwijld en in elk geval binnen 72 uur na ontvangst van het verzoek beantwoorden
verdict.evidence_span_b: De technische documentatie van een AI-systeem met een hoog risico wordt opgesteld voordat dit systeem in de handel wordt gebracht of in gebruik wordt gesteld, en wordt geactualiseerd.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A requires implementing and maintaining proportionate technical, operational, and organisational security measures, including risk assessment and consideration of incident likelihood and severity; B requires immediate notification of the Dutch Data Protection Authority of a qualifying security breach affecting personal-data protection.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a preventive, risk-based security-measures duty, whereas Norm B is a reactive notification duty triggered by a personal-data-impacting security breach.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ at the verb and compliance-work level: A requires taking security measures and accounting for risks; B requires notifying the supervisory authority of a qualifying breach. The shared security/incident context and broadly similar regulated-entity setting do not make the underlying obligation the same.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A requires domain-name registries and domain-name registration service entities to make non-personal domain-registration data public immediately after domain registration. B requires an authorised representative to keep an EU declaration of conformity and technical documentation available to the Minister for ten years, provide information and documentation on request to demonstrate conformity, and cooperate with risk-elimination measures on request.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: The norms concern different regulated objects and compliance purposes: public disclosure of domain-registration data after registration versus product-conformity record retention, information provision, and cooperation with safety measures.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in actor, regulated subject matter, triggering event, action, and purpose; A is immediate public disclosure after domain registration, while B concerns an authorised representative's retention, on-request conformity information, and cooperation regarding device risks.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms involve an entity or representative providing information or documentation to a public authority, but they do not require the same compliance work: A concerns maintaining and, on request, supplying conformity evidence and cooperating with risk-reduction measures; B concerns supplying entity-identification and contact information for inclusion in a national register, and promptly updating changes.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a product-conformity representative's ongoing document-retention, on-request evidence/cooperation duty; Norm B is an essential or important entity's registration-information and change-notification duty for a cybersecurity-entity list.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in actor role, triggering context, and substantive content: A concerns conformity assessment and product-risk measures, while B concerns cybersecurity-entity registration and updates. Similarity in supplying information to an authority is insufficient.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern regulatory handling of a risk-related situation, but Norm A requires prior consultation with a data-protection supervisory authority, while Norm B requires the AI provider to investigate a serious incident, perform an incident risk assessment, take corrective measures, cooperate with authorities, and give prior notice before certain system-changing investigations.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an ex ante GDPR consultation duty concerning planned high-risk personal-data processing, with specified information to be supplied. Norm B is an ex post AI Act serious-incident investigation and remediation duty, including cooperation and safeguards against compromising the later causal evaluation.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in both the triggering event and the operative action: prior consultation about intended high-risk processing versus investigation and remediation after a serious AI incident.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern making information or documentation available in response to an information-access or disclosure-related context, but Norm A requires establishing and publishing policies and procedures, whereas Norm B requires an authorised representative to provide a mandate copy on request and perform broader documentation, information, retention, and cooperation tasks.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a general policy-and-procedure publication duty for domain-name registries and registration-service entities concerning disclosure of registration data; Norm B is a representative's document-production and compliance-support duty for providers of general-purpose AI models, directed to the AI Office and authorities.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in actor, event/purpose, and operative action: Norm A requires setting and publicly disclosing policies and procedures, while Norm B requires producing a mandate copy on request and undertaking AI-compliance documentation, information, retention, and cooperation tasks.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern maintaining or preparing technical documentation capable of demonstrating product/system conformity, but they impose different duties: Norm A requires an authorised representative to keep the EU declaration of conformity and technical documentation available to the Minister for ten years and provide information/documentation on request; Norm B requires the high-risk AI system’s technical documentation to be prepared before placing on the market or putting into service, updated, and sufficiently complete and clear for conformity assessment by competent authorities and notified bodies.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a post-market retention and on-request cooperation duty of an authorised representative concerning an apparatus or radio apparatus; Norm B is an ex ante and ongoing documentation-production/update duty concerning a high-risk AI system, with specified Annex IV content and conformity-assessment purposes.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in actor role, regulated subject matter, timing, and operative action: Norm A requires keeping and supplying existing conformity documents to a Minister, whereas Norm B requires creating and updating AI technical documentation for conformity assessment.

verdict.evidence_span_b: De technische documentatie van een AI-systeem met een hoog risico wordt opgesteld voordat dit systeem in de handel wordt gebracht of in gebruik wordt gesteld, en wordt geactualiseerd.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms involve supplying information or documentation to a public authority, but they do not impose the same underlying compliance action: A specifies the contents of a personal-data-breach notification, while B concerns an authorised representative's provision of a mandate copy or other compliance information/documentation to the AI Office or authorities on request.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires a controller's breach notification containing incident-specific information; Norm B requires an authorised representative to provide a mandate copy or, on a reasoned request, information/documentation demonstrating compliance with GPAI-model obligations, and also to retain documentation and cooperate with authorities.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in actor, triggering event, and substantive content: A concerns notifying a supervisory authority of a personal-data breach; B concerns an authorised representative's mandate/documentation and cooperation duties for a general-purpose AI model.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern managing risks arising from technology-related incidents, but A requires maintaining a broad ICT-risk-management framework and resilient ICT systems, whereas B requires the AI provider, after reporting a serious incident, to investigate it, perform an incident risk assessment, and take corrective measures.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a standing, preventive ICT-risk-management and resilience obligation for specified financial entities; Norm B is a post-incident investigation and remediation obligation for an AI provider, including cooperation with authorities.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties are not the same because the actor roles differ and the operative actions differ: A requires ongoing ICT-risk controls and resilient systems, while B requires a post-incident investigation, risk assessment, and corrective measures.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both provisions concern obligations arising in the context of regulatory oversight of a provider, but Norm A establishes procedural hearing and access-to-file rights for a critical ICT third-party provider, whereas Norm B requires an AI provider to investigate a serious incident, including risk assessment and corrective measures, and to cooperate with authorities.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an authority's procedural duty safeguarding the investigated provider's right to be heard; Norm B is the provider's substantive post-incident investigation and remediation duty.
verdict.criterion_fired: Different core action, event context, and duty-bearing actor: a lead overseer must provide an opportunity to be heard in an enforcement procedure, while an AI provider must investigate a serious incident and undertake risk assessment and corrective measures.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Alvorens een dwangsom op grond van lid 6 op te leggen, stelt de lead overseer de vertegenwoordigers van de kritieke derde aanbieder van ICT-diensten die aan de procedure is onderworpen, in de gelegenheid te worden gehoord
verdict.evidence_span_b: verricht de aanbieder onverwijld het nodige onderzoek in verband met het ernstige incident en het betrokken AI-systeem. Dit omvat een risicobeoordeling van het incident en corrigerende maatregelen.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Norm A requires number holders to register number users within six months and thereby place the number into the user's use; Norm B requires processors (and, where applicable, their representatives) to maintain a register of processing-activity categories and specified related information.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A concerns registration and allocation/use of telecommunications numbers by number holders; Norm B concerns maintaining records of processing activities for GDPR accountability and documentation.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms impose different verb-level duties on different actor roles concerning unrelated subject matter: number-user registration and number allocation versus maintaining a GDPR processing-activities register.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Beide normen leggen een organisatorische/documentaire compliance-verplichting op, maar niet dezelfde concrete handeling: A vereist het instellen van procedures en processen voor ICT-incidentbeheer; B vereist het opstellen, bijhouden, beschikbaar stellen en openbaar maken van AI-modeldocumentatie en beleid.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both concern implementing and maintaining ICT/cybersecurity risk-management measures, including supply-chain or third-party risk considerations, but A requires an entity to take account of coordinated supply-chain security-risk assessments when selecting measures, whereas B requires specified financial entities to establish, maintain, monitor, test, and improve a documented ICT-risk-management framework and related controls.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a supply-chain risk-assessment consideration within a broader NIS2 security-duty; Norm B is a simplified ICT-risk-management framework duty for specified financial entities, including ongoing monitoring, incident handling, continuity, testing, and evaluation.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms do not impose the same underlying action on the same actor role: A concerns considering coordinated critical-supply-chain security-risk assessments when choosing measures, while B imposes a broader documented ICT-risk-management framework and operational control obligations on specified financial entities. The shared cybersecurity subject matter is insufficient to establish duplicate compliance work.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both provisions concern consequences or corrective action following a problem involving a regulated digital credential/system, but they do not impose the same compliance action: Norm A automatically terminates related recognitions when a recognition is withdrawn, whereas Norm B requires a distributor to take or procure corrective measures and, where there is a risk, notify the provider/importer and competent authorities with detailed information.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an automatic legal consequence of withdrawal of a recognition and concerns the status of business and organisational means; Norm B is an active distributor duty triggered by suspected non-conformity or risk, involving corrective measures, withdrawal/recall, and potentially detailed notifications.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms differ in both the triggering event and the duty-bearing actor: Norm A concerns withdrawal of a recognition by a means issuer and automatic lapse of associated recognitions; Norm B concerns a distributor's suspected high-risk AI non-conformity and requires corrective action and possible notification.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Met de intrekking van een erkenning van een middelenuitgever vervalt tevens de erkenning van de bedrijfs- en organisatiemiddelen die door die middelenuitgever worden uitgegeven.
verdict.evidence_span_b: neemt de noodzakelijke corrigerende maatregelen om dat systeem in overeenstemming te brengen met deze eisen, uit de handel te nemen of terug te roepen

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A verplicht financiële entiteiten om beleidslijnen, procedures en controles voor ICT-toegang in te voeren en te beheren. B verplicht een aanbieder na een ernstig incident onderzoek te verrichten, inclusief risicobeoordeling en corrigerende maatregelen, en daarbij bepaalde wijzigingen zonder voorafgaande kennisgeving aan autoriteiten niet uit te voeren.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A betreft structurele, preventieve ICT-governance en toegangsbeheer; norm B betreft onderzoek en corrigerende maatregelen na een ernstig AI-incident, met samenwerking met autoriteiten en een beperking op wijzigingen tijdens dat onderzoek.
verdict.criterion_fired: De normen leggen verschillende kernhandelingen op aan verschillende actorrollen en zien niet op hetzelfde soort gebeurtenis: A vereist preventieve ICT-beleids- en controlemaatregelen, terwijl B onderzoek en incidentgerelateerde beperkingen voorschrijft.
verdict.evidence_span_a: zij voeren beleidslijnen en protocollen in voor strenge authenticatiemechanismen
verdict.evidence_span_b: verricht geen onderzoek waarbij het AI-systeem wordt gewijzigd op een wijze die van invloed kan zijn op de latere evaluatie van de oorzaken van het incident

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both concern supplying information or reports to support regulatory oversight after a cybersecurity-related matter, but Norm A requires incident reporting by an affected entity, whereas Norm B concerns the lead overseer’s power to request post-oversight reports from critical ICT third-party providers about actions or corrective measures.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a mandatory, time-bound multi-stage significant-incident reporting duty to a CSIRT or competent authority. Norm B is an oversight power enabling the lead overseer to request reports concerning actions or corrective measures following recommendations; it is not itself an incident-reporting duty and has no fixed deadline in the provision.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in actor role, triggering context, and substantive purpose/content: A concerns reporting a significant incident and its evolution; B concerns reports requested after oversight activities about actions or corrective measures relating to recommendations.

verdict.evidence_span_b: na afloop van de oversightactiviteiten te verzoeken om verslagen met vermelding van de ondernomen acties of de corrigerende maatregelen

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require an organisation to prepare/provide information relevant to regulatory oversight, but they impose different underlying duties: A requires an entity to submit identification and registration-related information to competent authorities, while B requires providers of high-risk AI systems to create and maintain technical documentation demonstrating conformity.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an immediate or change-triggered information submission for inclusion in a Member State’s entity list; Norm B is pre-market and ongoing technical-documentation preparation for conformity assessment of a high-risk AI system.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties concern different actor roles, different regulatory subject matter and different event families: cybersecurity-entity registration/details versus high-risk-AI technical conformity documentation. Any broad similarity in providing information to authorities is insufficient to establish duplicated compliance work.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De in lid 3 bedoelde entiteiten melden onmiddellijk elke wijziging in de bijzonderheden die zij op grond van de eerste alinea van dit lid hebben ingediend, en in elk geval binnen twee weken na de datum van de wijziging.
verdict.evidence_span_b: De technische documentatie van een AI-systeem met een hoog risico wordt opgesteld voordat dit systeem in de handel wordt gebracht of in gebruik wordt gesteld, en wordt geactualiseerd.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both concern responding to security-related incidents, but Norm A requires preventive/risk-management measures to limit incident consequences, whereas Norm B requires a processor to inform the controller of a personal-data breach without undue delay.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an ongoing technical, operational, and organisational risk-control duty directed at limiting consequences for service recipients and other services; Norm B is an incident-triggered notification duty by a processor to the controller.
verdict.criterion_fired: The underlying actions and actor roles differ: Norm A requires an essential or important entity to implement measures, while Norm B requires a processor to inform the controller after learning of a personal-data breach.
