verdict.evidence_span_a: Financiële entiteiten registreren alle ICT-gerelateerde incidenten en significante cyberdreigingen.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Gebruiksverantwoordelijken van AI-systemen met een hoog risico bewaren de logs die automatisch worden gegenereerd door dat AI-systeem met een hoog risico

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Beide normen leggen een informatie-/communicatieverplichting aan een overheidsinstantie op, maar A betreft het beschikbaar houden en op verzoek verstrekken van conformiteitsinformatie en documentatie door een gemachtigde; B betreft het melden door een aangemelde instantie van specifieke certificerings-, aanmeldings- en conformiteitsbeoordelingskwesties aan de aanmeldende autoriteit.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: De actorrol, de concrete informatie, het doel en de aard van de verplichting verschillen: A is een gemachtigde die documentatie bewaart en op verzoek verstrekt of aan maatregelen meewerkt; B is een aangemelde instantie die uit eigen beweging specifieke gebeurtenissen en activiteiten aan de aanmeldende autoriteit meldt.
verdict.criterion_fired: Niet dezelfde kernverplichting: de normen hebben niet dezelfde actorrol of hetzelfde type trigger en vereisen wezenlijk verschillende informatie-/compliancewerkzaamheden. Het feit dat beide een overheidsinstantie als informatieontvanger hebben, maakt de verplichtingen niet dubbel.
verdict.evidence_span_a: b) het op verzoek van Onze Minister verstrekken van alle benodigde informatie en documentatie om de conformiteit van de apparaten of radioapparaten aan te tonen;
verdict.evidence_span_b: b) weigering, beperking, schorsing of intrekking van een beoordelingscertificaat technische documentatie van de Unie of een goedkeuring voor systemen voor kwaliteitsbeheer afgegeven overeenkomstig de eisen van bijlage VII;

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A requires the controller/processor’s register of processing activities to be prepared in written or electronic form. B requires an AI provider, following a market-surveillance finding, to remedy specified formal non-conformities within a period set by the authority, potentially followed by market restriction, prohibition, recall, or withdrawal.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A concerns maintaining a written/electronic register of processing activities; Norm B concerns remedial enforcement of AI regulatory formalities such as CE marking, an EU declaration of conformity, database registration, an authorised representative, or technical documentation.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms do not impose the same underlying action, concern different event families and regulatory purposes, and bind different actor roles. A is a record-keeping/form requirement; B is an authority-directed remediation and possible enforcement measure.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Het in de leden 1 en 2 bedoelde register is in schriftelijke vorm, waaronder in elektronische vorm, opgesteld.
verdict.evidence_span_b: schrijft zij de betrokken aanbieder voor dat deze binnen een door haar vast te stellen termijn een einde maakt aan deze non-conformiteit

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms involve providing access to, or information from, records at the request of another party. However, Norm A requires a telecommunications party to provide a company-register extract concerning a share right, or to investigate the identity and third-party links of a control holder, upon request by the Minister. Norm B requires domain-name registries and registration-service providers to grant legitimate requesters access to specific domain-registration data and answer access requests within 72 hours, with public disclosure procedures.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: The duties concern different records, different requesting parties and purposes, and different regulated actors: ministerial investigation of potentially threatening control in Norm A versus lawful access to domain-name registration data in Norm B.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms do not impose the same underlying action on the same actor in response to the same event. Norm A concerns minister-requested corporate-control information or an investigation by a telecommunications party; Norm B concerns domain-registration-data access by registries or registration-service providers for legitimate access seekers.
verdict.evidence_span_a: verstrekt een telecommunicatiepartij aan Onze Minister op verzoek om niet een uittreksel uit het door de rechtspersoon gehouden register met betrekking tot een recht op een aandeel
verdict.evidence_span_b: de registers voor topleveldomeinnamen en de entiteiten die domeinnaamregistratiediensten verlenen, op rechtmatige en naar behoren gemotiveerde verzoeken van legitieme toegangvragende partijen toegang verlenen tot specifieke met gegevens over de registratie van domeinnamen

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Geen gedeelde concrete compliance-actie: norm A verplicht openbaarmaking van beleid en procedures; norm B stelt cumulatieve voorwaarden aan verwerking, beveiliging, logging, bewaring en beperkte publicatie van persoonsgegevens in een AI-testomgeving.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A betreft transparantie over procedures voor bekendmaking van domeinnaamregistratiegegevens. Norm B betreft rechtmatige verdere verwerking van persoonsgegevens voor AI-ontwikkeling, met operationele waarborgen en documentatievereisten.
verdict.criterion_fired: De normen hebben noch dezelfde kernhandeling, noch dezelfde trigger of actorrol; een eventuele publicatieverplichting in norm B ziet op een AI-projectsamenvatting en is niet dezelfde openbaarmaking als in norm A.
verdict.evidence_span_a: stellen het beleid en de procedures met betrekking tot de bekendmaking van de gegevens, bedoeld in het eerste lid, vast en maken dat beleid en die procedures openbaar
verdict.evidence_span_b: in het kader van de testomgeving te verwerken persoonsgegevens bevinden zich in een functioneel gescheiden, geïsoleerde en beschermde omgeving voor dataverwerking onder de controle van de potentiële aanbieder

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Geen gedeelde concrete compliance-actie: norm A vereist het opstellen van een register van verwerkingsactiviteiten; norm B bevat een reeks product-, documentatie-, registratie-, conformiteits- en informatieverplichtingen voor aanbieders van hoog-risico-AI-systemen.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A betreft het schriftelijk, ook elektronisch, opstellen van een register van verwerkingsactiviteiten. Norm B betreft aanbiedersverplichtingen voor hoog-risico-AI, waaronder het vermelden van naam/handelsnaam/merk en contactadres, het bewaren van documentatie en logs, conformiteitsbeoordeling, registratie, corrigerende maatregelen en het verstrekken van informatie.
verdict.criterion_fired: De normen hebben geen dezelfde kernhandeling, gebeurtenisfamilie of actorrol. A gaat over het opstellen en bijhouden van een register van verwerkingsactiviteiten; B over verplichtingen van aanbieders van hoog-risico-AI-systemen. Er is geen gedeelde rapportage- of informatieverplichting die opnieuw zou moeten worden uitgevoerd.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Het in de leden 1 en 2 bedoelde register is in schriftelijke vorm, waaronder in elektronische vorm, opgesteld.
verdict.evidence_span_b: vermelden op het AI-systeem met een hoog risico of, wanneer dit niet mogelijk is, op de verpakking of in de bij het product gevoegde documentatie, naargelang het geval, hun naam, geregistreerde handelsnaam of geregistreerd merk en hun contactadres

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Geen gedeelde concrete compliance-actie: norm A bepaalt welke lidstaat jurisdictie heeft, terwijl norm B een bewaarplicht voor automatisch gegenereerde AI-systeemlogs oplegt.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is een jurisdictie- en territorialiteitsregel, met eventueel de aanwijzing van een vertegenwoordiger in de Unie; norm B is een inhoudelijke documentatie- en bewaarplicht met een minimale bewaartermijn van zes maanden.
verdict.criterion_fired: De normen leggen verschillende soorten verplichtingen op aan niet-overlappende actorrollen: A bepaalt toepasselijke jurisdictie, B verplicht gebruiksverantwoordelijken van hoog-risico-AI-systemen logs te bewaren. Er is dus geen herhaalde rapportage, informatieverstrekking of andere identieke compliance-werkzaamheid.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Binnen het toepassingsgebied van deze richtlijn vallende entiteiten worden geacht onder de jurisdictie te vallen van de lidstaat waar zij zijn gevestigd
verdict.evidence_span_b: Gebruiksverantwoordelijken van AI-systemen met een hoog risico bewaren de logs die automatisch worden gegenereerd door dat AI-systeem met een hoog risico

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both provisions concern regulated digital/ICT entities and their relationship with public authorities, but they impose fundamentally different obligations: Norm A allocates supervisory jurisdiction territorially, while Norm B requires financial entities to document, maintain, report, disclose, and notify information about ICT-service contracts.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a jurisdiction-allocation rule and does not require a compliance submission or operational measure; Norm B imposes concrete information-management and authority-reporting/notification duties concerning contractual ICT arrangements.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms do not impose the same underlying action or address the same triggering event: Norm A determines which Member State has jurisdiction, whereas Norm B requires financial entities to maintain records and provide specified ICT-contract information to competent authorities.
verdict.evidence_span_a: worden geacht onder de jurisdictie te vallen van de lidstaat waar zij zijn gevestigd
verdict.evidence_span_b: Financiële entiteiten rapporteren ten minste jaarlijks aan de bevoegde autoriteiten over het aantal nieuwe overeenkomsten inzake het gebruik van ICT-diensten

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Beide normen bevatten verplichtingen rond het beheersen van ICT-/gegevensrisico’s, maar norm A vereist incidentregistratie en procedures voor incidentopvolging en herstel, terwijl norm B voorwaarden stelt aan de verwerking, beveiliging, bewaring en het delen van persoonsgegevens in een AI-testomgeving.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A ziet op het registreren en behandelen van ICT-gerelateerde incidenten en significante cyberdreigingen; norm B ziet op rechtmatige verdere verwerking en het niet buiten de testomgeving delen van in de testomgeving aangemaakte persoonsgegevens.
verdict.criterion_fired: De normen hebben geen dezelfde kernhandeling of hetzelfde triggering event: A betreft incidentmanagement en het opsporen, documenteren en wegnemen van onderliggende oorzaken; B betreft beperkingen en waarborgen voor persoonsgegevensverwerking en gegevensdeling in een AI-testomgeving.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Financiële entiteiten registreren alle ICT-gerelateerde incidenten en significante cyberdreigingen.
verdict.evidence_span_b: persoonsgegevens die in de testomgeving worden aangemaakt mogen niet buiten de testomgeving worden gedeeld

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Norm A concerns identifying and stating possible coercive fines in an investigation authorisation; Norm B concerns deleting personal data processed in an AI regulatory sandbox after participation ends or the retention period expires. They do not require the same compliance work.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an investigative-authorisation measure concerning possible coercive fines for failure to provide requested records, data, procedures, materials, or answers. Norm B is a data-governance obligation to erase personal data after sandbox participation or the applicable retention period.
verdict.criterion_fired: Different underlying action, event context, and actor role; the apparent similarity is not a duplicated compliance obligation.
verdict.evidence_span_a: In deze machtiging worden eveneens de in artikel 35, lid 6, bedoelde dwangsommen genoemd
verdict.evidence_span_b: in het kader van de testomgeving verwerkte persoonsgegevens worden beschermd met passende technische en organisatorische maatregelen en worden gewist

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Beide normen vereisen het vastleggen/documenteren van informatie binnen de organisatie, maar Norm A vereist een register met gegevens over verwerkingsactiviteiten, terwijl Norm B registratie en processen voor het beheer en de opvolging van ICT-gerelateerde incidenten vereist.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A ziet op een doorlopende inventarisatie van verwerkingsactiviteiten door verwerkers; Norm B ziet op ICT-incidenten en significante cyberdreigingen, inclusief monitoring, behandeling, follow-up en het wegnemen van onderliggende oorzaken.
verdict.criterion_fired: De normen betreffen niet dezelfde gebeurtenis of hetzelfde type compliancewerk: Norm A gaat over registers van verwerkingsactiviteiten door verwerkers, Norm B over ICT-incidentbeheer door financiële entiteiten.
verdict.evidence_span_a: houdt een register van alle categorieën van verwerkingsactiviteiten
verdict.evidence_span_b: registreren alle ICT-gerelateerde incidenten en significante cyberdreigingen

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern maintaining or making information available, but they impose different underlying duties: Norm A requires collecting and maintaining accurate, complete domain-name registration data in a database; Norm B requires an authorised representative to keep specified conformity documents available to the Minister for ten years, and also provide information/documentation or cooperate with risk-reduction measures on request.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a standing data-collection and database-maintenance obligation for domain-name registries and registration-service entities. Norm B is a product-compliance document-retention and regulatory-cooperation obligation for an authorised representative, directed to the Minister.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in actor, subject matter, and operative action: domain-registration data collection/database maintenance versus retention and regulatory provision of product-conformity documentation. They are not the same compliance work repeated.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De registers voor topleveldomeinnamen en de entiteiten die domeinnaamregistratiediensten verlenen verzamelen nauwkeurige en volledige domeinnaamregistratiegegevens in een database en houden die gegevens bij.
verdict.evidence_span_b: het ter beschikking van Onze Minister houden van de EU-conformiteitsverklaring en de technische documentatie gedurende tien jaar nadat het apparaat of het radioapparaat in de handel is gebracht;

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Beide normen betreffen geen identieke rapportage- of informatieverstrekkingstaak: norm A verleent de lead overseer een onderzoeksbevoegdheid om personen te horen en informatie te verzamelen, terwijl norm B de aanbieder verplicht een gedetailleerde beschrijving en onderbouwing van AI-training, -testing en -validatie met testresultaten te bewaren als technische documentatie.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is een toezichthoudende onderzoeksbevoegdheid gericht op het horen van personen; norm B is een inhoudelijke documentatie- en bewaarplicht voor AI-testactiviteiten. Zij verschillen zowel in actorrol als in gebeurtenis/doel en vereiste inhoud.
verdict.criterion_fired: De normen leggen niet dezelfde kernhandeling op en betreffen niet dezelfde actorrol of gebeurtenisfamilie; een onderzoeksverhoor door de lead overseer is geen documentatiebewaarplicht van een AI-aanbieder.
verdict.evidence_span_a: vertegenwoordigers van kritieke derde aanbieder van ICT-diensten op te roepen en te verzoeken om mondelinge of schriftelijke toelichting te geven
verdict.evidence_span_b: een volledige en gedetailleerde beschrijving van het proces en de onderbouwing van het trainen, testen en valideren van het AI-systeem wordt samen met de testresultaten bewaard

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require an entity to make information available to others, but A requires immediate public disclosure of non-personal domain-registration data, whereas B requires ten-year retention and availability of specified high-risk AI-system documentation to national competent authorities.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: The duties differ fundamentally in purpose, information, timing, and access model: public disclosure immediately after domain registration versus controlled regulatory record retention for ten years after placing or putting an AI system into service.
verdict.criterion_fired: Different underlying action, event family, actor role, recipient relationship, deadline, and content; the superficial similarity that both involve making information available does not establish duplicated compliance work.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De registers voor topleveldomeinnamen en de entiteiten die domeinnaamregistratiediensten verlenen maken de domeinnaamregistratiegegevens, die geen persoonsgegevens zijn, onverwijld na de registratie van een domeinnaam openbaar.
verdict.evidence_span_b: De aanbieder houdt gedurende een periode van tien jaar nadat het AI-systeem met een hoog risico in de handel is gebracht of in gebruik is gesteld de volgende elementen ter beschikking van de nationale bevoegde autoriteiten:

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A requires domain-name registries and domain-registration service providers to answer a lawful, properly reasoned access request for specific domain-registration data, promptly or within 72 hours. B requires number holders to register number users within six months and thereby place the number into the user's use.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: The norms concern different regulated objects and duties: responding to access requests for domain-registration data versus registering telecommunications number users and granting use of the number.
verdict.criterion_fired: Different core action, triggering event, and actor role; A concerns responding to an access request, while B concerns registration of number users and allocation of a number.
verdict.evidence_span_a: beantwoorden een verzoek om toegang als bedoeld in het eerste lid
verdict.evidence_span_b: Nummerhouders registreren binnen zes maanden na de inwerkingtreding van artikel 4.9, derde lid, onderdeel b, de nummergebruikers

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Norm A requires an essential or important entity to report every significant incident under Articles 26–29. Norm B requires financial entities to deploy sufficient resources and capabilities to monitor user activity and the occurrence of ICT anomalies and ICT-related incidents, especially cyberattacks.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an external incident-reporting duty; Norm B is an internal detection and monitoring measure. They concern potentially related ICT incidents, but require different actions and serve different compliance purposes.
verdict.criterion_fired: Different core action and different actor role: reporting significant incidents versus implementing monitoring/detection capabilities.
verdict.evidence_span_a: meldt overeenkomstig de artikelen 26 tot en met 29 ieder significant incident
verdict.evidence_span_b: zetten voldoende middelen en capaciteiten in om toezicht te houden op activiteiten van gebruikers en het optreden van ICT-anomalieën en ICT-gerelateerde incidenten

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms impose ongoing organizational compliance duties on regulated entities, but they do not require the same underlying action: Norm A requires supplying and promptly updating entity-identification information to competent authorities, while Norm B requires high-risk AI providers to maintain a quality-management system (among other duties).
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A concerns registration/listing information and updates to competent authorities; Norm B concerns an internal quality-management system for high-risk AI systems.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in actor scope, subject matter, and operative action: Norm A concerns entities supplying or updating identification and service information for a cybersecurity-authority list, whereas Norm B concerns providers of high-risk AI systems maintaining a quality-management system. They are not the same event-driven reporting or compliance work.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De in lid 3 bedoelde entiteiten melden onmiddellijk elke wijziging in de bijzonderheden die zij op grond van de eerste alinea van dit lid hebben ingediend, en in elk geval binnen twee weken na de datum van de wijziging.
verdict.evidence_span_b: beschikken over een systeem voor kwaliteitsbeheer dat in overeenstemming is met artikel 17

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Geen gedeelde compliance-actie: norm A bepaalt de toepasselijke jurisdictie; norm B stelt voorwaarden en beperkingen aan verdere verwerking van persoonsgegevens in een AI-testomgeving, waaronder een verbod op delen buiten die omgeving.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is een jurisdictie-/territorialiteitsregel zonder meldings-, rapportage- of uitvoeringsplicht; norm B is een materiële gegevensverwerkingsregel met beveiligings-, bewaarbehoud-, logging-, documentatie- en publicatieverplichtingen.
verdict.criterion_fired: De normen leggen niet dezelfde verb-level actie op en zien niet op dezelfde soort gebeurtenis of compliancehandeling. Het feit dat beide bepalingen een entiteit en een lidstaat/testomgeving als context noemen, creëert geen dubbele compliance-last.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Binnen het toepassingsgebied van deze richtlijn vallende entiteiten worden geacht onder de jurisdictie te vallen van de lidstaat waar zij zijn gevestigd
verdict.evidence_span_b: persoonsgegevens die in de testomgeving worden aangemaakt mogen niet buiten de testomgeving worden gedeeld

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Beide normen vereisen het bijhouden van gestructureerde gegevens, maar niet dezelfde gegevens of voor hetzelfde compliance-doel: norm A vereist een register van verwerkingsactiviteiten; norm B vereist het verzamelen en bijhouden van domeinnaamregistratiegegevens in een database, met verificatiebeleid en openbaarmaking daarvan.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A ziet op verantwoordingsinformatie over verwerkingsactiviteiten onder verantwoordelijkheid van de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke. Norm B ziet op identificatie- en contactgegevens van domeinnaamhouders en beheercontactpunten ten behoeve van DNS-beveiliging, -stabiliteit en -weerbaarheid.
verdict.criterion_fired: De normen leggen verschillende gegevensbeheer- en documentatieplichten op aan verschillende actorrollen, met een verschillend doel en een lage inhoudelijke overlap; er is geen dubbele uitvoering van dezelfde compliancewerkzaamheden.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Elke verwerkingsverantwoordelijke en, in voorkomend geval, de vertegenwoordiger van de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke houdt een register van de verwerkingsactiviteiten die onder hun verantwoordelijkheid plaatsvinden.
verdict.evidence_span_b: de registers voor topleveldomeinnamen en de entiteiten die domeinnaamregistratiediensten verlenen, met de nodige zorgvuldigheid nauwkeurige en volledige domeinnaamregistratiegegevens verzamelen en bijhouden in een speciale database

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern an information-related compliance activity, but they do not impose the same underlying duty: Norm A requires number holders to register number users, while Norm B requires financial entities to maintain, report on, and provide an ICT-contract information register to the competent authority.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a one-time registration of number users by number holders; Norm B is an ICT-outsourcing governance and supervisory-information regime for financial entities, including maintaining a register and supplying it or related information to the competent authority.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in actor, subject matter, and operative action: registration of number users versus maintaining/reporting/providing an ICT-services contract register for supervision.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Nummerhouders registreren binnen zes maanden na de inwerkingtreding van artikel 4.9, derde lid, onderdeel b, de nummergebruikers.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Financiële entiteiten stellen de bevoegde autoriteit op verzoek het volledige informatieregister of desgevraagd specifieke onderdelen daarvan ter beschikking, samen met alle informatie die noodzakelijk wordt geacht om doeltreffend toezicht op de financiële entiteit mogelijk te maken.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both require the relevant provider/controller to implement appropriate technical and organizational (and, for Norm A, potentially operational) security or data-protection measures. They do not require the same specific measure or address the same compliance purpose.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A concerns managing security risks to public electronic communications services and minimizing the effects of security incidents on users and other networks/services. Norm B concerns privacy by design and by default: implementing data-protection principles and safeguards for data subjects throughout processing.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties are preventive measure-implementation obligations, but they arise from different regulatory domains, protect different interests, and apply to different actor roles: providers of public electronic communications services versus a controller determining and carrying out processing.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Aanbieders van openbare elektronische communicatiediensten nemen passende en evenredige technische, operationele en organisatorische maatregelen om de risico’s voor de beveiliging van hun diensten te beheersen
verdict.evidence_span_b: treft de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke, zowel bij de bepaling van de verwerkingsmiddelen als bij de verwerking zelf, passende technische en organisatorische maatregelen

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Beide normen betreffen het openbaar maken/bewaren van informatie of documentatie in brede zin, maar leggen niet dezelfde concrete compliancehandeling op: norm A vereist onverwijlde openbaarmaking van niet-persoonsgebonden domeinnaamregistratiegegevens; norm B vereist bewaring van een volledige en gedetailleerde beschrijving van AI-ontwikkeling, samen met testresultaten, als technische documentatie.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A ziet op onmiddellijke publieke openbaarmaking van domeinnaamregistratiegegevens door domeinnaamregisters en registratiedienstverleners. Norm B ziet op interne documentatiebewaring door AI-aanbieders binnen een gereglementeerde AI-testomgeving, als onderdeel van technische documentatie.
verdict.criterion_fired: De normen verschillen wezenlijk in kernactie, triggering context, actorrol en inhoud: publieke gegevensopenbaarmaking na domeinregistratie versus documentatiebewaring tijdens AI-ontwikkeling, -training en -testing.
verdict.evidence_span_a: de registers voor topleveldomeinnamen en de entiteiten die domeinnaamregistratiediensten verlenen, onverwijld na de registratie van een domeinnaam, de domeinnaamregistratiegegevens die geen persoonsgegevens zijn, openbaar maken
verdict.evidence_span_b: een volledige en gedetailleerde beschrijving van het proces en de onderbouwing van het trainen, testen en valideren van het AI-systeem wordt samen met de testresultaten bewaard als onderdeel van de in bijlage IV bedoelde technische documentatie

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern obligations relating to maintaining or recording accurate information in a registration context, but A requires number holders to register number users, whereas B requires domain-name registries and registration-service entities to establish policies and verification procedures and make them public.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a one-time registration duty imposed on number holders, with a six-month implementation deadline; Norm B is an ongoing governance, verification, database-accuracy, and transparency duty imposed on domain-name registries and registration-service entities.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in actor role and core action: A requires registration of number users, while B requires policies and procedures for accurate and complete domain-name registration databases, including verification and publication.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Nummerhouders registreren binnen zes maanden na de inwerkingtreding van artikel 4.9, derde lid, onderdeel b, de nummergebruikers.
verdict.evidence_span_b: De lidstaten schrijven voor dat de registers voor topleveldomeinnamen en de entiteiten die domeinnaamregistratiediensten verlenen, over beleidslijnen en procedures, waaronder verificatieprocedures, beschikken om ervoor te zorgen dat de in lid 1 bedoelde databases juiste en volledige informatie bevatten.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A requires a public electronic communications provider to notify the Dutch Data Protection Authority without delay of a security breach affecting personal-data protection. B requires a financial entity to conduct post-incident ICT evaluations, analyse the causes of a disruption, identify improvements, and—where applicable for non-micro-enterprises—communicate implemented changes to competent authorities on request.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: A is an urgent breach notification to a data-protection authority; B is an internal post-incident review and improvement process, with possible later disclosure of resulting changes to competent authorities on request.
verdict.criterion_fired: The actor role and core compliance action differ: A imposes immediate external notification of a security breach, while B imposes post-incident evaluation, causal analysis, and improvement identification (with possible disclosure of changes on request). The shared ICT/security-incident context is insufficient to create duplicate reporting work.
verdict.evidence_span_a: stelt de Autoriteit persoonsgegevens onverwijld in kennis van een inbreuk op de beveiliging
verdict.evidence_span_b: verrichten ICT-gerelateerde post-incidentevaluaties na verstoringen van hun kernactiviteiten ten gevolge van een ernstig ICT-gerelateerd incident, analyseren daarbij de oorzaken van de verstoring en identificeren de verbeteringen die moeten worden aangebracht

verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an anti-duplication rule concerning collection and cooperation for domain-name registration data; Norm B is a retention obligation for automatically generated high-risk-AI logs.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties involve different actors, different information, and different compliance actions: avoiding duplicate collection of domain-registration data versus retaining AI-system logs.

verdict.criterion_fired: Different core action, event family, and actor role; the apparent similarity is not sufficient to establish duplicated or merely related compliance work.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms involve communicating information to an external body, but Norm A requires financial entities to establish and operate an ICT-incident management process that includes reporting ICT-related incidents, whereas Norm B requires notified bodies to inform the notifying authority about certification, accreditation, scope, market-surveillance, and conformity-assessment matters.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A concerns reporting ICT-related incidents as part of an incident-management process; Norm B concerns notified bodies' information duties regarding their notification, conformity-assessment activities, and related certification or scope matters.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in actor, triggering subject matter, and substantive content: ICT-incident management/reporting by financial entities versus notification-related information reporting by notified bodies to the notifying authority.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require the responsible entity to establish or document compliance-related information, but they do not require the same underlying work: Norm A requires domain-name registries/registration-service entities to establish and publish policies and procedures for disclosing domain-registration data, while Norm B requires a controller or processor to substantiate an assessment and appropriate safeguards in the Article 30 record.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A concerns publicly establishing procedures governing access/disclosure of domain-registration data; Norm B concerns documenting the assessment and safeguards supporting a specific international personal-data transfer derogation.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties concern different subject matter, triggering circumstances, and actor roles. Norm A is a policy/procedure-publication duty for domain-name registries and registration-service entities in the context of justified requests for domain-registration data. Norm B is an internal-record substantiation duty for controllers/processors concerning exceptional transfers of personal data to third countries or international organisations.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern handling or obtaining information/data, but they impose different actions: Norm A empowers the lead overseer to obtain certified copies or extracts during an investigation; Norm B requires high-risk AI providers to satisfy safeguards and conditions when exceptionally processing special categories of personal data.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an investigative authority's power to obtain copies or extracts from records and other materials; Norm B is a provider's substantive data-processing compliance regime for bias detection and correction, including security, access controls, non-disclosure, deletion, and documentation.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms do not impose the same duty: they involve different actors, different legal functions, and different underlying actions. Norm A concerns supervisory investigation and obtaining certified copies or extracts; Norm B concerns conditions governing exceptional processing of special-category personal data by high-risk AI providers.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A requires registers and domain-name registration service entities to make non-personal domain-registration data public immediately after registration. B requires importers, before placing a high-risk AI system on the market, to verify specified compliance elements, including that the provider has appointed an authorised representative; in certain risk/non-compliance situations, the importer must notify the provider, authorised representatives, and market-surveillance authorities.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: The norms concern different regulated objects and compliance actions: publication of domain-registration data versus pre-market conformity checks and, in a specified risk situation, notification and withholding market placement of a high-risk AI system.
verdict.criterion_fired: The underlying action, triggering event, actor role, regulated object, and compliance purpose differ materially; any superficial similarity in timing or addressee category does not establish duplicated compliance work.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Norm A requires an essential or important entity to submit an interim progress report when an incident is still ongoing at the final-report deadline, followed by a final report within one month after resolution. Norm B requires financial entities to implement their digital operational resilience strategy and monitor and analyse the frequency, types, scale, evolution, and patterns of ICT-related incidents to improve risk awareness and preparedness.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an incident-triggered reporting duty to an authority or other recipient, whereas Norm B is an internal governance, monitoring, analysis, and resilience-improvement duty; it does not require submission of a report to the same recipient or channel.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties do not impose the same core action or actor role: A requires incident reporting by essential/important entities, while B requires financial entities to analyse ICT incidents as part of internal digital operational resilience management.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A requires communicating a personal-data breach to the affected data subject, including a clear description of the breach and specified information and measures. B requires financial entities to conduct post-incident ICT evaluations after serious ICT-related disruptions, identify causes and improvements, and—where applicable—share implemented changes with competent authorities on request. These are not the same compliance action.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: A is an external breach communication to the data subject; B is an internal post-incident evaluation and, for non-micro financial entities, disclosure of resulting changes to competent authorities on request.
verdict.criterion_fired: Same broad ICT/security-incident family and broadly comparable regulated-entity role, but the duties differ in action, purpose, recipient, and required content; therefore this is related rather than duplicated work.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Neither norm imposes the same underlying compliance action. Norm A concerns the opposability of a shareholder-register entry to persons who later become participants in a deposit; Norm B requires preparation, updating, and substantive maintenance of technical documentation for a high-risk AI system, including information enabling conformity assessment.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Norm A requires an essential or important entity to submit a progress report instead of a final report while an incident continues, followed by a final report within one month after the incident is handled. Norm B establishes civil liability for damage caused by processing that infringes the GDPR, including limited processor liability; it does not require reporting, notification, retention, information provision, or implementation of a measure.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an incident-reporting duty with a post-incident deadline; Norm B is a substantive liability and compensation rule concerning unlawful processing and damage.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms do not impose the same type of compliance action, concern different triggering events, and bind different actor categories: incident reporting by essential/important entities versus liability for controllers/processors causing damage through GDPR-infringing processing.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both require the responsible entity/controller to implement appropriate technical and organizational measures, but the measures serve different regulatory objectives: network and information-system security under A, versus data-protection principles and data-subject rights under B.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a cybersecurity risk-management duty for essential or important entities, including prevention and mitigation of incidents affecting services; Norm B is a privacy-by-design and by-default duty for controllers, focused on lawful, data-minimizing processing and safeguards for individuals’ rights.
verdict.criterion_fired: The apparent similarity is limited to the generic verb-level requirement to take technical and organizational measures. The duties address different risk domains, different regulatory purposes, and different obligated actor roles; therefore they are not the same compliance work repeated.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both concern ICT/security risk management in financial or digital-service contexts, but A requires incident reporting and B requires preventive protective ICT measures.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a time-bound, multi-stage report about a significant incident to a CSIRT or competent authority; Norm B is an ongoing preventive obligation to deploy ICT technologies and processes that protect availability, authenticity, integrity, confidentiality, and data.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ at the verb and compliance-work level: A requires submitting a progress report during an ongoing significant incident, whereas B requires implementing and using preventive ICT security technologies and processes. The shared cybersecurity subject matter does not make the underlying event, actor duty, or work the same.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require the regulated entity to take a compliance measure in response to a risk-related regulatory context, but Norm A requires providing specified information to a supervisory authority before high-risk processing, whereas Norm B requires developing and documenting an information-security policy and other ICT-risk controls.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a prior-consultation information-supply duty directed to a supervisory authority; Norm B is an ongoing ICT-security governance and control-implementation duty with no reporting or recipient requirement.
verdict.criterion_fired: The underlying actions, triggering contexts, and compliance outputs differ: prior consultation and provision of DPIA-related information to a supervisory authority versus implementation and documentation of ICT-security measures by financial entities.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern compliance activity following an ICT/data-related incident, but A requires notifying a supervisory authority, whereas B requires conducting a post-incident evaluation, analysing disruption causes, identifying improvements, and—on request for non-micro financial entities—communicating implemented changes to competent authorities.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an incident-notification duty to the Article 55 supervisory authority, with a 72-hour deadline. Norm B is an internal post-incident review and improvement duty, with possible later disclosure of resulting changes on request; its related paragraph concerns ICT-security training, not incident notification.
verdict.criterion_fired: The underlying actions and compliance purposes differ: A reports a personal-data breach to a supervisory authority; B performs an ICT post-incident evaluation and analyses causes/improvements, with any authority communication limited to changes made after that evaluation. The actor categories also differ: A concerns a data controller, while B concerns financial entities.

verdict.evidence_span_b: Financiële entiteiten verrichten ICT-gerelateerde post-incidentevaluaties na verstoringen van hun kernactiviteiten ten gevolge van een ernstig ICT-gerelateerd incident, analyseren daarbij de oorzaken van de verstoring en identificeren de verbeteringen die moeten worden aangebracht

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern cybersecurity-related activity following or addressing incidents: Norm A enables voluntary exchange of relevant cybersecurity information, while Norm B requires the provider to promptly investigate a serious incident, assess its risks, take corrective measures, cooperate with authorities, and give prior notice before certain system-changing investigations. They do not impose the same operative compliance action.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A establishes a voluntary information-sharing framework among entities; Norm B imposes a mandatory, prompt investigation and related cooperation/corrective-measures duty on high-risk AI-system providers after reporting a serious incident.
verdict.criterion_fired: Different core action and actor role; the shared incident/cybersecurity context is insufficient to establish duplicated compliance work.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A: registers bijhouden van activiteiten vóór en tijdens storingen wanneer ICT-continuïteits- en respons-/herstelplannen worden geactiveerd. B: persoonsgegevens verwerken in een AI-testomgeving onder cumulatieve voorwaarden, waaronder het publiceren op de website van bevoegde autoriteiten van een korte projectsamenvatting met doelstellingen en verwachte resultaten.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A betreft interne registratie tijdens ICT-storingen door financiële entiteiten; norm B betreft gereguleerde verwerking van persoonsgegevens voor AI-ontwikkeling en een publicatieverplichting over het AI-project.
verdict.criterion_fired: De normen leggen geen dezelfde verb-level actie op, zien niet op hetzelfde soort triggering event en richten zich niet op dezelfde actorrol. De oppervlakkige overeenkomst dat informatie wordt bijgehouden/gepubliceerd is onvoldoende voor een gedeelde compliance-verplichting.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both involve supplying information to public authorities, but Norm A requires a breach notification containing specified personal-data-breach details, while Norm B requires importers to provide, or make available, information and documentation substantiating conformity of a high-risk AI system, upon a reasoned request.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: The duties concern different triggering events, actors, purposes, and substantive content: a personal-data breach notification versus an authority's reasoned request for AI-system conformity information and technical documentation.
verdict.criterion_fired: Different event family and different actor role; the shared feature of providing information to authorities is too generic to establish duplicate compliance work.

verdict.evidence_span_b: de relevante bevoegde autoriteiten op met redenen omkleed verzoek alle nodige informatie en documentatie

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern post-incident activity by a regulated provider/entity following a serious ICT/AI-related incident: A requires a post-incident evaluation and, on request, communication of resulting changes; B requires an immediate investigation, including risk assessment and corrective measures, with cooperation and safeguards concerning the investigation.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an internal post-incident evaluation of disruption to core activities, focused on causes, procedural compliance, effectiveness, and improvements, with possible disclosure of implemented changes to competent authorities. Norm B is an immediate investigation of a serious incident involving a high-risk AI system, including risk assessment and corrective measures, and cooperation with authorities without altering the system in a way that could affect later causal evaluation.
verdict.criterion_fired: Same broad serious-incident family, but different actor roles and materially different investigative/evaluative duties and purposes; therefore related burden rather than repeated identical compliance work.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Financiële entiteiten verrichten ICT-gerelateerde post-incidentevaluaties na verstoringen van hun kernactiviteiten ten gevolge van een ernstig ICT-gerelateerd incident, analyseren daarbij de oorzaken van de verstoring en identificeren de verbeteringen die moeten worden aangebracht
verdict.evidence_span_b: Na de melding van een ernstig incident op grond van lid 1 verricht de aanbieder onverwijld het nodige onderzoek in verband met het ernstige incident en het betrokken AI-systeem. Dit omvat een risicobeoordeling van het incident en corrigerende maatregelen.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Norm A requires avoiding duplicate collection of domain-name registration data through cooperation between registries and domain-name registration service entities. Norm B requires importers of high-risk AI systems to verify specified compliance conditions before placing the system on the market, including conformity assessment, technical documentation, CE marking, EU declaration/instructions, and an authorised representative; in certain risk cases it also requires notification to specified parties and market-surveillance authorities.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: The norms concern fundamentally different compliance duties, actors, and subject matter: preventing duplicate collection of domain-registration data versus pre-market conformity verification and, in a specified risk case, notification concerning a high-risk AI system.
verdict.criterion_fired: Different event family and different actor role; the apparent similarity does not establish the same compliance obligation.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms impose an information-related compliance duty on regulated digital/technical actors, but the underlying actions differ: Norm A requires immediate public disclosure of non-personal domain-registration data; Norm B requires an authorised representative to provide information and documentation to the Minister on request to demonstrate conformity, alongside retention and cooperation duties.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is proactive public disclosure after domain registration, whereas Norm B is reactive provision of conformity evidence to a minister upon request (with related retention and risk-mitigation cooperation duties).
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties concern different actors, different triggering events, different recipients/purposes, and materially different actions and content; the apparent similarity is not a repeated compliance burden.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A requires a telecommunications party, upon the Minister’s request, to provide a register extract concerning a share right and potentially investigate a controller’s identity and third-party ties. B requires a provider/deployer responsible for a high-risk AI system to prepare and update technical documentation demonstrating conformity and containing Annex IV information, for assessment by competent authorities or notified bodies.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: A is an on-request information-production/investigation duty triggered by suspected or anticipated dominant control threatening the public interest; B is an ex ante and ongoing technical-documentation duty for a high-risk AI system, tied to market placement or putting into service and conformity assessment.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms concern different actors, different triggering events, and materially different actions and information: a telecommunications party must respond to a Ministerial request about share-control ownership, whereas the responsible AI-system actor must create and update technical conformity documentation.
verdict.evidence_span_a: verstrekt een telecommunicatiepartij aan Onze Minister op verzoek om niet een uittreksel uit het door de rechtspersoon gehouden register met betrekking tot een recht op een aandeel

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms involve an entity providing information to a public authority, but they do not require the same underlying compliance action: A requires, upon request, supplying a register extract and/or conducting an investigation into a controller's identity and third-party links; B requires reporting changes to previously submitted entity information.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an on-request investigation/information-production duty triggered by suspected or impending dominant control threatening the public interest. Norm B is a proactive, time-limited update-reporting duty triggered by changes in the entity's registered particulars.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in both the triggering event and the substantive action/content: A concerns suspected dominant control and requires a register extract or investigation; B concerns changes in registration particulars and requires an update to competent authorities within two weeks.
verdict.evidence_span_a: stelt een telecommunicatiepartij op verzoek van Onze Minister een onderzoek in naar de identiteit van een houder van zeggenschap en de banden die deze heeft met derden.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern compliance following a significant/serious incident, but Norm A requires including specified information in an early warning, whereas Norm B requires the provider to promptly investigate the serious incident and AI system, including a risk assessment and corrective measures, while cooperating with authorities.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an information-reporting/early-warning content duty; Norm B is an investigation, risk-assessment, corrective-measures, and cooperation duty following a serious-incident report.
verdict.criterion_fired: Same incident family and actor role, but different core actions and substantially different compliance content; the duties are related incident-response burdens rather than the same work repeated.
verdict.evidence_span_a: geeft de entiteit aan of het significante incident vermoedelijk door een onrechtmatige of kwaadwillige handeling is veroorzaakt
verdict.evidence_span_b: verricht de aanbieder onverwijld het nodige onderzoek in verband met het ernstige incident en het betrokken AI-systeem

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern handling ICT/AI-related incidents, but they impose different core actions: Norm A requires financial entities to establish and implement an incident-management process for detecting, managing, and reporting ICT-related incidents; Norm B requires AI providers, after reporting a serious incident, to promptly investigate it, conduct a risk assessment, take corrective measures, cooperate with authorities, and avoid compromising the later causal evaluation.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a general, ongoing incident-management-process obligation for financial entities, whereas Norm B is a post-report investigation, risk-assessment, remediation, cooperation, and evidence-preservation obligation for providers of high-risk AI systems.
verdict.criterion_fired: The event family overlaps because both concern serious/ICT-related incidents, but the actor roles and verb-level duties differ: process establishment and incident detection/management/reporting versus prompt post-notification investigation and corrective action.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Financiële entiteiten omschrijven een beheerproces voor ICT-gerelateerde incidenten, stellen dit vast en leggen dit ten uitvoer, om ICT-gerelateerde incidenten te detecteren, te beheren en te melden.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Na de melding van een ernstig incident op grond van lid 1 verricht de aanbieder onverwijld het nodige onderzoek in verband met het ernstige incident en het betrokken AI-systeem.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both involve supplying or maintaining information/documentation relevant to regulatory oversight, but they do not require the same underlying compliance work: A requires an entity to provide registration information to the national minister, while B requires preparation and updating of technical documentation for a high-risk AI system.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a registration-information disclosure duty to the national minister, including entity identity, contact, sector, service-location and information-sharing details, with changes reported within two weeks. Norm B is an ongoing technical-documentation and conformity-demonstration duty for a high-risk AI system, intended for assessment by competent authorities and notified bodies.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in actor scope, subject matter, purpose, and core action: A concerns registration information about an entity; B concerns technical documentation demonstrating an AI system’s conformity. The apparent similarity of regulatory information provision is insufficient to establish duplicate or related burden.
verdict.evidence_span_a: verstrekt ten behoeve van de registratie in het nationale register, bedoeld in artikel 43, aan Onze Minister de volgende informatie
verdict.evidence_span_b: De technische documentatie van een AI-systeem met een hoog risico wordt opgesteld voordat dit systeem in de handel wordt gebracht of in gebruik wordt gesteld, en wordt geactualiseerd.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Norm A requires notifying service recipients of significant incidents; Norm B requires deploying sufficient resources and capabilities to monitor user activity, ICT anomalies, and ICT-related incidents.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an incident-notification duty directed to service recipients, whereas Norm B is an ongoing ICT monitoring and detection measure with no external recipient.
verdict.criterion_fired: Same actor and broadly related ICT/security-incident context, but the underlying actions and compliance outputs differ: notification versus monitoring/detection.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern responding to a serious/significant incident, but A requires the entity to submit a structured incident report and follow-up reports, whereas B requires the AI provider to investigate the incident, assess its risks, take corrective measures, and cooperate with authorities.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a time-bound reporting duty to a CSIRT or competent authority; Norm B is an investigation and remediation duty following a serious incident, with cooperation and prior-notification safeguards. The reporting duty referenced in B's related paragraph is not the action imposed by B itself.
verdict.criterion_fired: The underlying action and actor role differ: A requires affected entities to submit a detailed incident notification within 72 hours, while B requires providers to investigate an incident and implement corrective measures without delay. The shared incident trigger is insufficient to establish duplicated compliance work.
verdict.evidence_span_a: onverwijld en in elk geval binnen 72 uur nadat zij kennis hebben gekregen van het significante incident, een incidentmelding indienen
verdict.evidence_span_b: verricht de aanbieder onverwijld het nodige onderzoek in verband met het ernstige incident en het betrokken AI-systeem

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern managing risks arising from technology-related incidents, but A requires maintaining business continuity and response/recovery measures, whereas B requires investigating a serious AI incident, including risk assessment and corrective measures.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a standing ICT-risk-management and business-continuity obligation for specified financial entities; Norm B is an incident-triggered investigation and cooperation obligation for an AI provider after a serious incident has been reported.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in both actor role and core action: A requires ensuring continuity through business-continuity, response and recovery measures, while B requires investigating a serious incident, conducting a risk assessment, and taking corrective measures. The shared technology-incident/risk context is insufficient to establish duplicated compliance work.
verdict.evidence_span_a: de continuïteit van kritieke of belangrijke functies waarborgen door middel van bedrijfscontinuïteitsplannen en respons- en herstelmaatregelen
verdict.evidence_span_b: verricht de aanbieder onverwijld het nodige onderzoek in verband met het ernstige incident en het betrokken AI-systeem. Dit omvat een risicobeoordeling van het incident en corrigerende maatregelen.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both provisions concern obtaining information or explanations from an addressee in connection with regulatory oversight: A requires the authorised representative to provide requested information and documentation to the Minister to demonstrate conformity; B empowers the lead overseer to request oral or written explanations from ICT-service-provider representatives, and to hear other persons or legal entities, to collect information for an investigation. They do not impose the same underlying duty.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A imposes a substantive cooperation/supply duty on an authorised representative, on request by the Minister, concerning conformity information and documentation. Norm B grants an investigative power to the lead overseer to hear persons or entities and obtain explanations or information for an investigation; it is primarily an authority power rather than the same addressee-facing reporting obligation.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms differ in actor role, legal function, and operative action: A requires an authorised representative to provide conformity information/documentation to a Minister, whereas B authorises a lead overseer to hear persons or entities during an investigation. The apparent similarity is limited to information-gathering.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern maintaining/documenting information or records in connection with regulated ICT/AI activities, but they do not impose the same underlying compliance action: A requires a financial entity to maintain, update, and report/provide an ICT third-party-contract information register; B permits exceptional processing of special-category personal data subject to safeguards and requires the processing register to record the justification for that processing.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A concerns an ICT third-party-contract register and related reporting or supervisory disclosure by financial entities; Norm B concerns exceptional processing of special-category personal data by providers of high-risk AI systems to detect and correct bias, with safeguards and justification in a processing register.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms do not impose the same core action, concern different regulatory subject matter and triggering circumstances, and bind different actor roles; any superficial similarity from record-keeping does not create duplicated compliance work.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Financiële entiteiten rapporteren ten minste jaarlijks aan de bevoegde autoriteiten over het aantal nieuwe overeenkomsten inzake het gebruik van ICT-diensten, de categorieën van derde aanbieders van ICT-diensten, het soort contractuele overeenkomsten en de ICT-diensten en -functies die worden geleverd.
verdict.evidence_span_b: mogen de aanbieders van dergelijke systemen uitzonderlijk bijzondere categorieën persoonsgegevens verwerken, mits passende waarborgen worden geboden voor de grondrechten en fundamentele vrijheden van natuurlijke personen.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A requires the controller to consult the supervisory authority before processing where a DPIA indicates high residual risk. B requires the provider, after a serious-incident notification, to investigate the incident and AI system, assess risks, take corrective measures, cooperate with competent authorities, and refrain from certain system-altering investigations without prior notice.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: A is a pre-processing supervisory consultation based on high-risk processing and includes supplying specified information about the proposed processing. B is a post-serious-incident investigation and remediation duty concerning an AI system, including a restriction on potentially prejudicial system modifications and cooperation with authorities.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms do not impose the same core action and concern different triggering-event families, actors, and compliance purposes: prior consultation for high-risk planned processing versus post-incident investigation and remediation for an AI provider.

verdict.evidence_span_b: verricht de aanbieder onverwijld het nodige onderzoek in verband met het ernstige incident en het betrokken AI-systeem

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern documented data-processing governance, but A requires maintaining a comprehensive register of processing activities, whereas B requires satisfying safeguards for exceptional processing of special categories of personal data and adding specific necessity reasons to an existing processing-activities register.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a general record-keeping duty covering all processing activities and specified register fields. Norm B is a conditional substantive safeguard regime for high-risk AI providers processing special-category data to detect or correct bias; its register requirement is only one additional content item within that regime.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms do not impose the same underlying action or concern the same triggering event: A requires controllers or their representatives to maintain a general processing-activities register, while B conditionally requires providers of high-risk AI systems to meet safeguards for exceptional special-category-data processing, including recording the reasons for necessity in an existing register.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Elke verwerkingsverantwoordelijke en, in voorkomend geval, de vertegenwoordiger van de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke houdt een register van de verwerkingsactiviteiten die onder hun verantwoordelijkheid plaatsvinden.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Voor zover dit strikt noodzakelijk is om de opsporing en correctie van vertekeningen te waarborgen in verband met de AI-systemen met een hoog risico overeenkomstig lid 2, punten f) en g), van dit artikel, mogen de aanbieders van dergelijke systemen uitzonderlijk bijzondere categorieën persoonsgegevens verwerken, mits passende waarborgen worden geboden voor de grondrechten en fundamentele vrijheden van natuurlijke personen.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require the regulated entity to take account of or avoid practices involving vulnerabilities, but they impose fundamentally different duties: Norm A requires a cybersecurity risk-management assessment concerning suppliers and service providers; Norm B prohibits placing on the market, putting into service, or using specified AI practices.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a supply-chain cybersecurity risk-assessment consideration duty, whereas Norm B is a prohibition on specified AI-system practices, including exploitation of vulnerabilities and manipulative conduct.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms do not impose the same underlying action or address the same compliance event: Norm A concerns an entity's cybersecurity measures and supplier vulnerabilities, while Norm B prohibits specified AI practices and uses.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern establishing or verifying compliance-related information procedures/documentation, but they do not require the same underlying compliance action. Norm A requires domain-name registries and registration-service entities to establish and publish policies and procedures for disclosing domain-registration data. Norm B requires an authorised representative of a general-purpose AI-model provider to perform delegated compliance tasks, including checking technical documentation, retaining it, supplying information/documentation to the AI Office on reasoned request, and cooperating with authorities.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a general policy-and-procedure publication duty concerning access to domain-registration data; Norm B is an authorised-representative function involving verification, ten-year retention, provision of compliance evidence, and cooperation with AI authorities.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms differ in actor, subject matter, and operative duty: Norm A concerns domain-name data-disclosure policies and procedures, while Norm B concerns an AI-model provider's authorised representative and AI Act compliance documentation and cooperation.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De registers voor topleveldomeinnamen en de entiteiten die domeinnaamregistratiediensten verlenen stellen het beleid en de procedures met betrekking tot de bekendmaking van de gegevens, bedoeld in het eerste lid, vast en maken dat beleid en die procedures openbaar.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Geen gedeelde compliance-actie: norm A verplicht de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke advies in te winnen van de functionaris voor gegevensbescherming bij een gegevensbeschermingseffectbeoordeling; norm B verplicht bepaalde financiële entiteiten onder meer de belangrijkste afhankelijkheden van derde aanbieders van ICT-diensten in kaart te brengen binnen een ICT-risicobeheerkader.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A betreft intern advies binnen een gegevensbeschermingseffectbeoordeling; norm B betreft structureel ICT-risicobeheer en het identificeren van afhankelijkheden van ICT-dienstverleners, met periodieke evaluatie en mogelijke indiening van een evaluatieverslag bij de bevoegde autoriteit.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require the regulated entity to perform an information-related compliance activity, but A requires responding to access requests for domain-registration data, whereas B requires maintaining accessible records of activities before and during disruptions when ICT continuity and response/recovery plans are activated.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A concerns responding to a legitimate access request for specific domain-registration data within 72 hours; Norm B concerns keeping records of activities surrounding activation of ICT continuity and response/recovery plans during disruptions.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in both the underlying action and triggering event: A requires answering an external access request, while B requires internal record-keeping during ICT disruptions. They therefore do not impose the same compliance work.

verdict.evidence_span_b: houden gemakkelijk toegankelijke registers bij van hun activiteiten vóór en tijdens storingen

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Geen gedeelde concrete compliance-actie: norm A verplicht een doorlopend ICT-risicobeheerkader en het gebruik van robuuste, weerbare en actuele ICT-systemen, protocollen en instrumenten; norm B verplicht tijdens onderzoek naar een ernstig AI-incident geen onderzoek uit te voeren dat het AI-systeem op een evaluatiebeïnvloedende wijze wijzigt, naast onderzoek, risicobeoordeling, corrigerende maatregelen en samenwerking.

verdict.criterion_fired: De normen verschillen zowel in kernactie als in actorrol en gebeurteniscontext: A ziet op structureel ICT-risicobeheer en systeemweerbaarheid; B op het niet wijzigen van een AI-systeem tijdens onderzoek naar een ernstig incident.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both provisions concern supplying or making compliance-related information/documentation available to a public authority, but they do not impose the same underlying duty: Article 33 requires a personal-data-breach notification with specified incident details, while Article 54 requires an authorised representative to perform AI Act compliance tasks, including providing AI-model documentation and information to the AI Office on request.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: The norms address different event families and different substantive purposes: a GDPR personal-data breach versus verification and enforcement of obligations concerning a general-purpose AI model.
verdict.criterion_fired: Different event family and different actor role; the apparent similarity in authority-facing information duties does not establish the same compliance work.

verdict.evidence_span_b: het verstrekken aan het AI-bureau, na een met redenen omkleed verzoek, van alle informatie en documentatie

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms involve communicating information connected with a cyber/ICT-related threat or incident, but A requires proactive notification and recommended protective measures to potentially affected service recipients, whereas B requires providing authorities, on request, with an estimate of aggregated annual costs and losses from serious ICT-related incidents.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a customer/service-recipient warning duty concerning a significant cyber threat and possible response measures; Norm B is an authority-facing, request-based provision of quantified annual loss and cost information concerning serious ICT-related incidents.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in both actor role and substantive action/content: A concerns an essential or important entity warning potentially affected service recipients and explaining possible measures, while B concerns financial entities supplying authorities on request with an aggregated annual cost-and-loss estimate. The shared cyber/ICT context and broad information-sharing character do not make the compliance work the same.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit deelt de ontvangers van haar diensten, die mogelijkerwijs door een significante cyberdreiging in relatie tot het ontvangen van die diensten worden getroffen, onverwijld mee welke maatregelen die ontvangers kunnen nemen in reactie op die dreiging.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Andere financiële entiteiten dan micro-ondernemingen verstrekken de bevoegde autoriteiten op hun verzoek een raming van de geaggregeerde jaarlijkse kosten en verliezen als gevolg van ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incidenten.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms involve supplying information or documentation to a public authority, but they do not require the same underlying compliance action: Norm A requires an entity to report changes to previously submitted registration/details information, whereas Norm B requires an authorised representative, on request, to provide the AI Office with a copy of its mandate.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a proactive change-reporting duty triggered by a change in the entity's submitted particulars and subject to a two-week deadline; Norm B is a request-based document-production duty concerning the representative's mandate, with no stated deadline.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in actor, trigger, purpose, and content: NIS2 entities must report changes in registration particulars to competent authorities, while an AI-model provider's authorised representative must provide a mandate copy to the AI Office on request.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De in lid 3 bedoelde entiteiten melden onmiddellijk elke wijziging in de bijzonderheden die zij op grond van de eerste alinea van dit lid hebben ingediend, en in elk geval binnen twee weken na de datum van de wijziging.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Hij legt op verzoek een kopie van het mandaat over aan het AI-bureau, in een van de officiële talen van de instellingen van de Unie.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Norm A requires number holders to register number users within six months after the specified provision enters into force; Norm B requires the processing-activities register referred to in Article 30(1) and (2) to be maintained in written or electronic form.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: They concern entirely different compliance objects and triggering contexts: numbering administration versus documentation of processing activities.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Norm A requires maintaining a written/electronic register of processing activities; Norm B requires entities to provide identification/contact/scope information to competent authorities and promptly report changes to that information.

verdict.criterion_fired: The norms impose different core actions on different regulatory subjects for different purposes: a GDPR processing-activities register versus NIS2 entity identification and change reporting to competent authorities.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both require ICT/cybersecurity risk-management measures that address risks involving ICT systems and third parties, but A specifically requires considering suppliers’ product quality and cybersecurity practices when selecting supply-chain security measures, whereas B requires simplified financial-entity ICT-risk-management controls, including identifying key ICT-service-provider dependencies and incorporating post-incident/test conclusions into the risk-assessment process.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a supplier-risk consideration within NIS2 supply-chain security measures; Norm B is a broader, documented ICT-risk-management framework for specified financial entities, with monitoring, continuity, testing, and post-incident follow-up.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms do not impose the same core action on the same actor role: A concerns an essential or important entity assessing direct suppliers and service providers when choosing supply-chain security measures; B concerns specified small or exempt financial entities establishing and maintaining a simplified ICT-risk-management framework and related controls. Their subject matter overlaps only at a broad cybersecurity-risk level, not as the same compliance work.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern ICT/cybersecurity risk management in relation to incidents: A requires reporting significant incidents and relevant cross-border-impact information; B requires maintaining and operating an ICT-risk-management framework, including identifying, detecting and handling ICT incidents and incorporating lessons from incident analysis.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an urgent external incident-reporting and notification duty triggered by a significant incident. Norm B is an ongoing internal ICT-risk-management and resilience duty, including post-incident learning, with no reporting of the incident itself required by the quoted provision.
verdict.criterion_fired: Same general ICT/security-incident family and broadly comparable regulated-entity role, but the operative actions and compliance outputs differ: external reporting to a CSIRT/competent authority versus internal risk-management, monitoring, response, testing and incorporation of operational conclusions.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A requires the entity to promptly take necessary, appropriate and proportionate corrective measures after finding non-compliance with cybersecurity-risk-management measures. B concerns confirmation by an authority or notified body of responsibility for AI systems and completion of an assessment within twelve months after withdrawal of a designation, plus related notifications and certificate-validity consequences.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: The norms concern different substantive duties and event families: cybersecurity non-compliance requiring remediation versus withdrawal/change of an AI notified body's designation requiring responsibility confirmation and assessment.
verdict.criterion_fired: Different core action, triggering event, and actor role; the apparent similarity does not establish duplicated compliance work.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both concern handling or communicating information about ICT/data incidents, but A requires the processor to inform the controller, whereas B requires financial entities to establish and implement an incident-management process for detecting, managing, and reporting ICT-related incidents.

verdict.criterion_fired: The underlying action and actor role differ: A imposes a specific notification duty on a processor, while B imposes a broader incident-management process duty on financial entities. The shared incident-related context is insufficient to establish duplicated compliance work.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Norm A requires the entity to pay the costs of an independent targeted security audit; Norm B requires covered entities to establish and maintain an ICT-risk-management framework and protect data, including periodic evaluation and submission of an evaluation report on request.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A concerns payment for a supervisory security audit, whereas Norm B concerns ongoing ICT-risk-management and data-protection measures by regulated financial entities.
verdict.criterion_fired: The extracted duties do not impose the same verb-level action, concern different regulatory subjects and purposes, and do not require the same compliance work. Norm A's audit-cost payment is not the same as Norm B's ICT-risk-management and data-protection obligations.
