verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern cybersecurity-related information or risk, but A requires enabling voluntary information exchange, while B requires financial entities to identify and assess ICT risks, cyber threats, and vulnerabilities.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a Member State obligation to facilitate voluntary inter-entity cybersecurity information sharing; Norm B is a direct, ongoing and at-least-annual risk-identification and assessment duty for financial entities.
verdict.criterion_fired: The underlying actions, triggering context, and duty-bearing actors differ: A concerns voluntary information-sharing arrangements, whereas B concerns internal ICT-risk identification and assessment by financial entities.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A requires an essential or important entity to implement proportionate technical, operational, and organisational security measures to prevent incidents and limit their consequences. B empowers the lead overseer to impose a coercive fine on a critical ICT third-party provider for non-compliance with supervisory measures; it is an enforcement action by the authority, not the provider’s underlying security-measure duty.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a substantive preventive risk-management and incident-impact-limitation obligation imposed on essential or important entities. Norm B is an administrative enforcement power exercised by the lead overseer against critical ICT third-party providers after non-compliance with supervisory measures.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms differ in actor, operative action, and legal function: A requires security measures by regulated entities, whereas B authorises a lead overseer to impose a coercive fine for failure to comply with supervisory measures.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A permits the provider, rights-holder, or manager to request a decision from the Dutch Authority for Consumers and Markets within two weeks after failure to reach agreement. B requires financial entities to classify ICT-related incidents and assess their effects using specified criteria.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: A is an optional procedural request to an authority concerning a statutory tolerance obligation or the location, timing, and method of works; B is a substantive incident-classification and impact-assessment duty with no recipient or deadline specified.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms impose different core actions on different actor roles and concern different triggering situations: an unresolved agreement about works versus classification of an ICT-related incident.

verdict.distinguishing_factor: The norms concern fundamentally different compliance actions and subject matter: access-request response versus documentation retention and controlled personal-data processing for AI testing.
verdict.criterion_fired: Different core action, event family, and actor role; the norms do not require the same compliance work.

verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a substantive breach-notification content obligation, whereas Norm B is a jurisdiction-allocation rule, with a possible representative requirement for certain entities established outside the EU.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms do not impose the same core action and do not concern the same event family: A concerns communicating personal-data-breach details to a supervisory authority; B concerns determining the competent Member State and jurisdiction.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms involve an actor being required to provide cooperation or assistance to a public authority, but Norm A requires broad cooperation with military authorities when Article 31 of the Dutch War Act is applied, whereas Norm B requires an authorised representative to perform AI Act-specific verification, retention, information-production, and cooperation tasks for the AI Office and competent authorities.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an emergency/military-authority cooperation duty triggered by application of the War Act; Norm B is a standing AI-governance mandate involving technical-documentation verification, ten-year retention, production of information on reasoned request, and cooperation concerning a general-purpose AI model.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in actor role, triggering event, subject matter, and operative content; the superficial similarity of cooperation with authorities does not establish duplicated compliance work.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both provisions concern a response to a legally relevant situation, but A requires the provider to notify the affected subscriber about a contemplated or urgent network/service/device-security measure, whereas B empowers the lead overseer to impose a coercive fine on a critical ICT third-party provider for non-compliance with supervisory measures.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a provider-to-subscriber notification duty linked to a protective suspension or termination measure; Norm B is an authority’s enforcement power and coercive-fine procedure directed at securing compliance with supervisory measures.
verdict.criterion_fired: The provisions do not impose the same underlying action on the same actor: A requires subscriber notification, while B concerns a lead overseer’s imposition of a daily coercive fine after non-compliance with supervisory measures.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both concern submitting incident-related information or a report, but Norm A requires an ongoing/final incident report to the competent authority under the NIS2 framework, while Norm B requires the relevant DORA notification, including voluntary notifications, also to the sectoral CSIRT.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a progress-report/final-report substitution and follow-up duty when an incident remains unresolved; Norm B is an additional transmission of specified DORA ICT-incident notifications to a sectoral CSIRT, including voluntary notifications.
verdict.criterion_fired: The event family is broadly the same (an ICT/security incident), but the actor scope and operative duties differ: Norm A applies to essential or important entities and requires a progress report or later final report, whereas Norm B applies specifically to banks, trading venues, central securities depositories and central counterparties and requires specified DORA notifications to an additional sectoral CSIRT. The texts do not establish that the same actor must repeat the same report content.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both provisions concern handling or maintaining data, but Norm A requires collecting and maintaining accurate, complete domain-registration data in a database, whereas Norm B permits and regulates further processing of previously collected personal data for developing, training, and testing specified AI systems in a regulatory sandbox, subject to extensive safeguards.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A imposes a database collection and maintenance duty on domain-name registries and registration-service entities; Norm B establishes conditions and safeguards for further processing of personal data in an AI regulatory sandbox, including isolation, monitoring, deletion, logging, documentation, and publication requirements.
verdict.criterion_fired: The provisions do not impose the same underlying action, concern the same triggering event, or bind the same actor role. Norm A concerns domain-registration data collection and maintenance; Norm B concerns conditional further processing of personal data for AI-system development and associated safeguards.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern regulated entities' compliance with supervisory/regulatory requirements, but they do not impose the same concrete action: A concerns identifying possible coercive fines in an investigation authorisation, while B imposes broad high-risk-AI provider obligations, including conformity, documentation, corrective measures, and information provision.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an investigative-authorisation requirement concerning the possible imposition of coercive fines on third-party ICT-service providers; Norm B is a substantive, ongoing compliance regime for providers of high-risk AI systems.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms differ in the underlying action, triggering context, and actor role; any superficial similarity from regulated digital-sector addressees is insufficient. Norm A concerns an overseer’s written authorisation and possible coercive fines in an investigation, whereas Norm B concerns providers’ substantive obligations for high-risk AI systems.

verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in actor, subject matter, and operative action: maintaining conformity documentation for regulatory inspection versus creating and maintaining a processing-activities register. They do not concern the same triggering event or repeated compliance work.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A requires an authorised representative to cooperate with measures taken to eliminate risks from devices/radio equipment, on request of the Minister. B requires a notified body to inform other notified bodies about specified refused, suspended, withdrawn, limited, or—on request—issued approvals/certificates.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: The duties concern different actors, different triggering events, different actions, and different recipients: risk-mitigation cooperation for an authorised representative versus inter-notified-body information sharing about conformity-assessment approvals or certificates.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms impose ongoing documentation-related compliance duties, but A requires an authorised representative to keep conformity materials available and provide them to the Minister on request, whereas B requires high-risk AI deployers to retain automatically generated logs under their control for an appropriate period or at least six months.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both concern cybersecurity/ICT incident-related information or handling, but Norm A requires enabling voluntary inter-entity cybersecurity information exchange, whereas Norm B requires financial entities to establish and implement an ICT-incident management process that includes reporting incidents.

verdict.criterion_fired: The actor role and core compliance action differ: Norm A addresses Member States ensuring voluntary information exchange by covered and, where applicable, other entities; Norm B addresses financial entities implementing an ICT-incident management process. The shared incident/cybersecurity context is insufficient to establish duplicated compliance work.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Beide normen houden verband met het openbaar maken of verstrekken van informatie, maar leggen niet dezelfde concrete handeling op: norm A vereist dat beleid en procedures over bekendmaking van domeinnaamregistratiegegevens openbaar worden gemaakt; norm B vereist dat aangemelde instanties specifieke certificerings-, autorisatie- en conformiteitsbeoordelingsinformatie aan de aanmeldende autoriteit melden.

Norm B betreft meldingen door aangemelde instanties aan een aanmeldende autoriteit over certificaten, goedkeuringen, wijzigingen in de aanmelding en conformiteitsbeoordelingsactiviteiten.
verdict.criterion_fired: De normen hebben niet dezelfde actor, niet dezelfde concrete actie en niet hetzelfde type informatie of doel: norm A ziet op publieke transparantie over procedures voor gegevensbekendmaking, terwijl norm B ziet op institutionele rapportage door aangemelde instanties aan een aanmeldende autoriteit.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require the addressee to take a compliance-related measure concerning regulated conduct: A requires an entity to take supplier and service-provider cybersecurity factors into account when selecting supply-chain security measures; B prohibits placing on the market, putting into service, or using specified AI systems. They do not require the same underlying compliance work.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a risk-based supply-chain cybersecurity due-diligence and measure-selection obligation, whereas Norm B is a substantive prohibition on specified AI practices, including biometric categorisation.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms concern different actors, different regulated conduct, and different compliance purposes: cybersecurity risk management of suppliers versus prohibition of specified AI-system practices.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern ICT/cyber-risk management in a broad sense, but Norm A requires affected entities to submit a formal significant-incident report to the CSIRT or competent authority, whereas Norm B requires financial entities to identify and periodically assess ICT risks, cyber threats, and vulnerabilities internally. They do not require the same compliance action.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an externally directed, incident-triggered reporting duty with specified reporting stages and deadlines; Norm B is an ongoing internal risk-identification and assessment duty, including at least annual evaluation.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in core action, triggering event, and actor scope: incident reporting by affected entities to an authority/CSIRT versus continuous and annual ICT-risk assessment by financial entities.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both provisions involve making a notification/report connected to an incident or threat affecting network or service security, but A requires an essential or important entity to submit an interim progress report (and later a final report) to address specified incident aspects, whereas B requires a provider to notify the affected subscriber about a contemplated or emergency security measure and give an opportunity to remedy the threat.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an incident-reporting duty to the competent authority or other legally designated recipient, covering the incident's specified aspects and continuing status. Norm B is a customer-facing procedural notice about a specific security measure, including an opportunity to remove the threat; it is not an incident progress report.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in both actor role and core action/content: A concerns an essential or important entity submitting a progress report during an ongoing incident, while B concerns a provider notifying the affected subscriber before or promptly after taking a security measure.

verdict.distinguishing_factor: The duties concern different regulatory subject matter and purposes: GDPR processing-activity records versus AI Act technical, quality-management, conformity, and notified-body documentation retained for authority access.
verdict.criterion_fired: Different core action, event/regulatory subject matter, actor role, recipient relationship, and required content; the superficial similarity is limited to maintaining records or documentation.

Norm B betreft gerichte meldingen door aangemelde instanties aan een aanmeldende autoriteit over hun conformiteitsbeoordelingsactiviteiten en relevante gebeurtenissen.
verdict.criterion_fired: De normen hebben niet dezelfde kernhandeling, gebeurtenisfamilie of actorrol; bovendien is de ontvanger/publiek verschillend en overlapt de inhoud slechts beperkt.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Norm A requires describing or communicating the specified details of a personal-data breach in a notification to the supervisory authority. Norm B requires cooperation so that domain-name registration data need not be collected twice; it concerns avoiding duplicate collection, not reporting a breach.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: The norms concern different underlying actions and event families: breach-notification content versus prevention of duplicate collection of domain-name registration data.
verdict.criterion_fired: Different core action and different event family; Norm B is an anti-duplication rule for collecting domain-name registration data, whereas Norm A specifies the contents of a personal-data-breach notification.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Beide normen houden verband met een reactie op een door een bevoegde autoriteit vastgestelde of te melden situatie, maar de feitelijke verplichtingen verschillen: norm A verplicht de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke een toezichthoudende autoriteit over een internationale doorgifte te informeren; norm B verplicht een aanbieder een formele AI-non-conformiteit te beëindigen binnen een door de markttoezichtautoriteit vastgestelde termijn.

Norm B betreft een herstel-/beëindigingsbevel van een markttoezichtautoriteit aan een AI-aanbieder wegens formele non-conformiteit.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms impose obligations on regulated digital-sector actors, but they do not require the same compliance action: Norm A requires prompt public disclosure of non-personal domain-registration data after domain registration, whereas Norm B imposes a broad set of high-risk-AI-provider obligations, with the extracted action specifically requiring a quality-management system.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A concerns immediate public disclosure of non-personal domain-registration data following a domain registration; Norm B concerns providers' ongoing governance and conformity obligations for high-risk AI systems, including quality management.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms differ in the regulated actor, operative action, triggering event, and compliance purpose. Norm A concerns domain-name registration and public disclosure; Norm B concerns high-risk AI providers' quality-management systems and related conformity duties.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require the regulated entity to provide or demonstrate compliance-related information to a competent authority upon request: A requires making the ICT information register and necessary supervisory information available; B requires demonstrating that a high-risk AI system complies with Section 2 requirements upon a reasoned request from a national competent authority.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A concerns a financial entity's ICT third-party-contract information register and supervisory information; Norm B concerns a high-risk AI provider's demonstration of AI-system conformity. The actors, subject matter, and underlying regulatory regimes differ.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties concern different actor roles and different subject matter/event families: maintaining and supplying an ICT-outsourcing register for financial supervision versus demonstrating conformity of a high-risk AI system. Similarity of a possible authority request is insufficient to establish duplicated compliance work.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Beide normen houden verband met het melden van een gebeurtenis, maar norm A vereist een voorafgaande melding van kabelwerkzaamheden aan de burgemeester; norm B vereist dat financiële entiteiten een intern proces vaststellen en uitvoeren om ICT-gerelateerde incidenten onder meer te melden.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A betreft een voorafgaande gemeentelijke melding van werkzaamheden in of op openbare gronden. Norm B betreft het opzetten en uitvoeren van een intern ICT-incidentbeheerproces; de bepaling schrijft hier niet zelf een concrete melding aan dezelfde ontvanger voor.
verdict.criterion_fired: De normen verschillen zowel in de trigger (kabelwerkzaamheden versus ICT-incidenten) als in de kernhandeling en actorcontext (vooraf melden aan een burgemeester versus een financieel-intern incidentbeheerproces).
verdict.evidence_span_a: voorafgaand aan de uit te voeren werkzaamheden melding gedaan bij de burgemeester van de gemeente
verdict.evidence_span_b: om ICT-gerelateerde incidenten te detecteren, te beheren en te melden

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Geen gedeelde compliance-actie: norm A verplicht nummerhouders gebruikers te registreren en het nummer daardoor aan de nummergebruiker in gebruik te geven; norm B verplicht aanbieders van hoog-risico-AI-systemen, op gemotiveerd verzoek, logs aan een bevoegde autoriteit toegankelijk te maken.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A betreft registratie en ingebruikgeving van nummers aan nummergebruikers; norm B betreft toegang tot automatisch gegenereerde AI-systeemlogs voor toezicht door een bevoegde autoriteit.
verdict.criterion_fired: De normen hebben verschillende actoren, handelingen, begunstigden/toezichthoudende ontvangers en onderwerpen; een gedeelde gebeurtenis of compliance-inhoud blijkt niet uit de teksten.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Nummerhouders registreren binnen zes maanden na de inwerkingtreding van artikel 4.9, derde lid, onderdeel b, de nummergebruikers.
verdict.evidence_span_b: verlenen aanbieders die verzoekende bevoegde autoriteit, indien van toepassing, toegang tot de in artikel 12, lid 1, bedoelde logs

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A: onverwijld significante incidenten melden aan het CSIRT/de bevoegde autoriteit en, waar relevant, ontvangers van de diensten informeren, met informatie over mogelijke grensoverschrijdende gevolgen. B: de lead overseer kan verslagen opvragen over ondernomen acties of corrigerende maatregelen naar aanleiding van aanbevelingen; daarnaast kunnen ICT-dienstverleners informatie over uitbesteding toezenden.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is een incident-triggered reporting/information duty concerning significant incidents, while Norm B is an oversight power concerning requested reports and outsourcing information, not a duty to report the same incident.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms do not impose the same underlying action on the same actor in response to the same event: A concerns urgent significant-incident reporting/information, whereas B concerns oversight requests for reports on remedial actions and outsourcing information.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Elke lidstaat zorgt ervoor dat essentiële en belangrijke entiteiten elk incident dat aanzienlijke gevolgen heeft voor de verlening van hun diensten als bedoeld in lid 3 (significant incident) onverwijld meldt bij zijn CSIRT of, indien van toepassing, zijn bevoegde autoriteit overeenkomstig lid 4.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A requires registers and domain-name registration service providers to answer legitimate access requests for specific domain-registration data within 72 hours. B governs conditions for processing previously collected personal data in an AI regulatory sandbox, including safeguards, logging, retention/deletion, documentation, and publication.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: A is a time-bound access-request response duty concerning domain-registration data; B is a conditional data-processing regime for AI-system development and testing, with multiple safeguards and documentation/publication requirements.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms do not impose the same underlying action, concern the same triggering event, or bind the same actor role. A concerns responding to legitimate requests for domain-registration data; B concerns processing personal data in an AI regulatory sandbox subject to cumulative conditions.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms involve making information available, but A requires registers/domain-registration service providers to grant access to specific domain-registration data and publish disclosure procedures, whereas B requires high-risk AI providers to take corrective measures and provide information required under Article 20, including in the broader context of provider obligations.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A concerns access to domain-name registration data and transparency of disclosure procedures; Norm B concerns information provision connected to corrective measures for high-risk AI systems and compliance with the AI Act.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties concern different actors, different regulatory subject matter, and different operative purposes: domain-registration data access and disclosure procedures versus high-risk-AI corrective measures and Article 20 information.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms involve providing information to an authority-like recipient, but A requires a financial entity to make its ICT-outsourcing information register available to the competent authority on request, whereas B requires a notified body to inform other notified bodies about specified decisions and certificates.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: The duties concern different actors, different event families, and materially different information: ICT-service contractual-register disclosure versus inter-notified-body communication about quality-management approvals and technical-documentation certificates.
verdict.criterion_fired: Different actor role and different event family; the shared information-transmission feature is too generic, and the required content and regulatory purposes are distinct.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both provisions concern regulated digital/ICT compliance, but A requires an investigation authorisation to state applicable coercive fines, whereas B requires high-risk AI providers to retain automatically generated logs.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an investigative-authorisation/procedural requirement concerning possible coercive fines for third-party ICT-service providers; Norm B is a substantive record-retention duty for providers of high-risk AI systems.
verdict.criterion_fired: The underlying actions, triggering contexts, and obligated actor roles differ: A concerns stating coercive fines in an investigation authorisation, while B concerns retaining AI-system logs for at least six months.
verdict.evidence_span_a: In deze machtiging worden eveneens de in artikel 35, lid 6, bedoelde dwangsommen genoemd
verdict.evidence_span_b: Aanbieders van AI-systemen met een hoog risico bewaren de in artikel 12, lid 1, bedoelde logs

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both concern reporting ICT/security incidents, but A requires the affected entity to submit a specific incident notification and follow-up reports to a CSIRT or competent authority; B requires a financial entity to establish and operate an internal ICT-incident management process that includes reporting incidents.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an external, time-bound notification and reporting duty concerning a significant incident, with detailed prescribed content and deadlines. Norm B is an internal governance/process obligation to detect, manage, and report ICT-related incidents, without specifying an external recipient, prescribed report content, or deadline.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in their core action and actor role: A requires an affected entity to submit a detailed external incident notification within 72 hours, while B requires financial entities to implement an internal incident-management process that includes reporting.
verdict.evidence_span_a: binnen 72 uur nadat zij kennis hebben gekregen van het significante incident, een incidentmelding indienen
verdict.evidence_span_b: Financiële entiteiten omschrijven een beheerproces voor ICT-gerelateerde incidenten, stellen dit vast en leggen dit ten uitvoer, om ICT-gerelateerde incidenten te detecteren, te beheren en te melden.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A requires a public electronic communications service provider to promptly notify the Dutch Data Protection Authority of a qualifying security breach affecting personal-data protection. B requires financial entities to implement and use ICT technologies, processes, policies, and controls to prevent or mitigate availability, authenticity, integrity, confidentiality, and data-loss risks; it is a preventive security measure, not an incident-notification duty.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: A is an urgent, authority-directed breach notification duty; B is an ongoing preventive ICT-security and resilience obligation for financial entities, with no reporting recipient or deadline.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms differ in both the operative action and the duty-bearing actor: A requires incident notification by a public electronic communications provider, while B requires preventive ICT-risk controls by financial entities. The shared security subject matter is insufficient to establish the same event family or duplicated compliance work.

verdict.evidence_span_b: voorkomen een gebrek aan beschikbaarheid, de aantasting van de authenticiteit en integriteit, de inbreuken op de vertrouwelijkheid en het verlies van gegevens

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Beide normen voorzien in het beschikbaar stellen of verkrijgen van informatie/documentatie voor toezicht, maar niet in dezelfde concrete compliancehandeling: A betreft onderzoeksbevoegdheden van de lead overseer, waaronder het opvragen/verkrijgen van materiaal en toelichtingen; B betreft de gemachtigde die technische documentatie gedurende tien jaar beschikbaar houdt en die op gemotiveerd verzoek aan het AI-bureau verstrekt.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A verleent een toezichthouder onderzoeksbevoegdheden tegenover kritieke derde aanbieders van ICT-diensten; norm B legt aan een gemachtigde van een aanbieder van een algemeen AI-model een documentbewaar- en verstrekkingstaak op, met specifieke technische documentatie en een bewaartermijn van tien jaar.
verdict.criterion_fired: De normen verschillen wezenlijk in actorrol, event family en kernactie: A is een algemene onderzoeksbevoegdheid die wordt uitgeoefend wanneer een onderzoek plaatsvindt, terwijl B een doorlopende bewaarplicht en verzoekgebonden informatieverstrekking over AI-modeldocumentatie oplegt.
verdict.evidence_span_a: c) vertegenwoordigers van kritieke derde aanbieder van ICT-diensten op te roepen en te verzoeken om mondelinge of schriftelijke toelichting te geven bij feiten of documenten die betrekking hebben op het onderwerp en het doel van het onderzoek
verdict.evidence_span_b: b) een kopie van de in bijlage XI gespecificeerde technische documentatie beschikbaar houden voor het AI-bureau en de nationale autoriteiten gedurende een periode van tien jaar

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Beide normen zien op het delen of melden van cyberbeveiligingsinformatie, maar norm A verplicht niet tot een concrete melding: zij verlangt dat lidstaten vrijwillige onderlinge informatie-uitwisseling mogelijk maken. Norm B verplicht financiële entiteiten daarentegen tot het indienen van eerste, tussentijdse en eindrapporten over ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incidenten bij een bevoegde autoriteit.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A betreft een vrijwillig, onderling informatie-uitwisselingskader met een breed scala aan cyberbeveiligingsinformatie; norm B betreft een verplichte, formele incidentrapportage door financiële entiteiten aan een bevoegde autoriteit, met voorgeschreven opeenvolgende rapportagemomenten en informatie over de incidentomvang en grensoverschrijdende effecten.
verdict.criterion_fired: De kernactie en de actorrol verschillen: A legt een lidstaat een faciliteringsplicht op voor vrijwillige informatie-uitwisseling tussen entiteiten, terwijl B financiële entiteiten rechtstreeks verplicht tot formele rapportage aan een bevoegde autoriteit. De gedeelde cyberincidentcontext en mogelijke autoriteitsrelatie maken dit hoogstens thematisch verwant, niet dezelfde compliance-werkzaamheden.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De lidstaten zorgen ervoor dat ... entiteiten ... op vrijwillige basis onderling relevante informatie over cyberbeveiliging kunnen uitwisselen
verdict.evidence_span_b: Financiële entiteiten dienen ... bij de relevante bevoegde autoriteit het volgende in: ... b) een tussentijds verslag

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Geen gedeelde concrete compliance-actie: norm A verplicht medewerking aan en uitvoering van opdrachten van het militair gezag; norm B legt aanbieders van hoog-risico-AI een breed pakket product-, kwaliteits-, documentatie-, registratie-, conformiteits- en correctieve verplichtingen op.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is een contextafhankelijke verplichting tot gehoorzaamheid en medewerking aan het militair gezag bij toepassing van de Oorlogswet. Norm B betreft doorlopende ex-ante en product-complianceverplichtingen van aanbieders van hoog-risico-AI, waaronder kwaliteitsbeheer.
verdict.criterion_fired: De normen verschillen zowel in actorrol als in kernactie en event/context: militaire bevelsuitvoering en algemene medewerking versus AI-aanbiedersverplichtingen inzake conformiteit en kwaliteitsbeheer.
verdict.evidence_span_a: zijn ... verplicht het militair gezag alle medewerking te verlenen, daaronder begrepen het uitvoeren van door dat gezag gegeven opdrachten
verdict.evidence_span_b: beschikken over een systeem voor kwaliteitsbeheer dat in overeenstemming is met artikel 17

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require the regulated actor to provide information to a public authority, but the duties concern different subject matter and purposes: A requires staged reporting of serious ICT-related incidents, whereas B requires notified bodies to inform the notifying authority about conformity-assessment activities and related matters.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A concerns incident reporting by financial entities, including initial, interim/updated, and final reports containing information needed to assess an ICT incident and its effects. Norm B concerns information supplied by notified bodies about conformity-assessment certificates, changes to notification status, requests from market-surveillance authorities, and activities within the scope of notification, often on request.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties are not meaningfully the same because they involve different actor roles and different event/content domains: serious ICT-related incidents versus conformity-assessment activities and certificates.
verdict.evidence_span_a: een tussentijds verslag na de eerste kennisgeving als bedoeld in punt a), zodra de status van het oorspronkelijke incident ingrijpend is gewijzigd
verdict.evidence_span_b: op verzoek, de binnen het toepassingsgebied van hun aanmelding verrichte conformiteitsbeoordelingsactiviteiten en andere activiteiten, waaronder grensoverschrijdende activiteiten en onderaanneming

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern taking action in response to a circumstance involving infrastructure or services, but Norm A requires ongoing preventive and mitigating cybersecurity measures, whereas Norm B requires advance notification of cable-maintenance works on public land to the municipal mayor (or an authorized official). They do not impose the same compliance work.

verdict.criterion_fired: Different underlying action, event/context, and actor role; the superficial overlap is limited to information/data handling.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms involve an actor carrying out a registration-related compliance action: number holders must register number users, while providers of high-risk AI systems must comply with registration obligations under Article 49(1).
verdict.distinguishing_factor: The duties concern different subject matter and different registration schemes: telecommunications number users versus high-risk AI systems. Norm B is also a broad bundle of provider obligations, and its registration duty is only one item within that bundle.
verdict.criterion_fired: The underlying registration verbs are superficially similar, but the regulated actors, objects of registration, regulatory domains, and triggering frameworks differ; therefore the norms do not impose the same compliance work.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Beide normen bevatten een informatie-/documentatiegerichte verplichting in brede zin, maar A vereist het bijhouden, documenteren en op verzoek of periodiek verstrekken van ICT-contractinformatie aan bevoegde autoriteiten; B vereist publicatie van een korte samenvatting van een AI-project en de doelstellingen en verwachte resultaten op de website van bevoegde autoriteiten.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: De normen zien op wezenlijk verschillende compliance-objecten en doeleinden: ICT-outsourcingregisters en toezichtinformatie bij A tegenover transparantie over AI-testprojecten en resultaten bij B.
verdict.criterion_fired: De verplichtingen betreffen niet dezelfde kernactie, niet dezelfde gebeurtenis/familie en niet dezelfde actorrol; bovendien is de ontvangerrelatie niet die van dezelfde of verschillende autoriteiten met dezelfde rol, maar een niet-vergelijkbare publicatie-/toezichtcontext.

verdict.evidence_span_b: een korte samenvatting van het in de testomgeving ontwikkelde AI-project en de doelstellingen en verwachte resultaten ervan worden op de website van de bevoegde autoriteiten gepubliceerd

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern compliance-related action connected to a regulated legal situation, but A requires a telecommunications party to provide a corporate-register extract or investigate control-holder identity on ministerial request, whereas B requires an importer to verify an AI system's conformity before placing it on the market and, where a risk exists, notify specified parties and market-surveillance authorities.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a request-based information/investigation duty concerning potentially threatening control over a telecommunications entity; Norm B is a pre-market AI conformity-verification and, in a specified risk case, notification duty imposed on importers.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in actor role, triggering event, and operative action: A concerns ministerial suspicion of potentially threatening control and provision of register information or an investigation; B concerns an importer's pre-market conformity checks for a high-risk AI system, with a separate risk-based notification obligation.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Beide normen gebruiken het werkwoord “verstrekken” (informatie verstrekken), maar zij regelen niet dezelfde concrete compliancehandeling: norm A vereist proactieve informatieverstrekking aan de abonnee over een overstapproces; norm B vereist het verstrekken van door een bevoegde instantie gevraagde informatie, met verantwoordelijkheid voor volledigheid, juistheid en niet-misleiding.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A betreft consumenteninformatie vóór en tijdens een overstapproces; norm B betreft het beantwoorden van een informatieverzoek door een kritieke derde ICT-dienstaanbieder, kennelijk in het toezichtskader van DORA.
verdict.criterion_fired: De concrete trigger, actorrol, ontvanger en inhoud/purpose verschillen wezenlijk; een gedeeld werkwoord (“verstrekken”) en een algemene informatiecomponent maken de verplichtingen niet dezelfde.
verdict.evidence_span_a: verstrekken de abonnee vóór en tijdens het overstapproces toereikende informatie over het overstapproces
verdict.evidence_span_b: verstrekken de gevraagde informatie

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Beide normen gebruiken een kennisgevings-/informatieverstrekkingsactie, maar zij verplichten verschillende informatieverstrekking: norm A vereist dat essentiële en belangrijke entiteiten hun ontvangers informeren over een significante cyberdreiging en mogelijke maatregelen; norm B vereist dat aangemelde instanties de aanmeldende autoriteit informeren over conformiteitsbeoordelingscertificaten, wijzigingen in hun aanmelding, ontvangen informatieverzoeken en activiteiten.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A betreft communicatie over een significante cyberdreiging aan mogelijk getroffen dienstontvangers; norm B betreft periodieke of op verzoek verstrekte toezicht- en conformiteitsbeoordelingsinformatie aan de aanmeldende autoriteit.
verdict.criterion_fired: De normen hebben wel een vergelijkbare verbale actie (informatie/kennisgeving verstrekken), maar verschillen in actorrol, triggering event, ontvanger en inhoud. Norm A ziet op een significante cyberdreiging; norm B op conformiteitsbeoordelingsactiviteiten en aanmeldingsstatus. Dit is dus geen dubbele compliance-last.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Indien nodig stellen de entiteiten die ontvangers ook in kennis van de significante cyberdreiging zelf.
verdict.evidence_span_b: op verzoek, de binnen het toepassingsgebied van hun aanmelding verrichte conformiteitsbeoordelingsactiviteiten en andere activiteiten, waaronder grensoverschrijdende activiteiten en onderaanneming.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require the regulated actor to establish or perform compliance-related controls, but they do not require the same underlying action: Norm A requires maintaining policies and procedures, including verification procedures, for accurate and complete domain-registration databases; Norm B requires importers to verify specified conformity conditions before placing a high-risk AI system on the market, with a related notification duty if a risk is identified.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A concerns governance and verification procedures for the accuracy and completeness of domain-registration data, whereas Norm B concerns an importer's pre-market conformity checks and, in a specified case, notification to the provider, representatives, and market-surveillance authorities.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties concern different actors, different subject matter, and different compliance actions: domain-name registries/registration-service providers must maintain and publish data-accuracy policies and procedures, while importers must check high-risk AI conformity before placing it on the market. The apparent similarity is not a repeated reporting or notification burden.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms address protection against data-related security risks, but A requires reporting a qualifying personal-data breach to a supervisory authority, whereas B requires financial entities to implement/use ICT technologies and processes to prevent or mitigate ICT and data-security risks.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an incident-triggered, time-limited notification duty to a supervisory authority; Norm B is an ongoing preventive ICT-security implementation duty with no reporting recipient or deadline.
verdict.criterion_fired: The underlying actions and actor roles differ: A requires a controller to notify an authority after a personal-data breach, while B requires financial entities to implement/use preventive ICT technologies and processes. The shared data-security subject matter does not make the compliance work duplicative.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A requires the controller to document personal-data breaches, including facts, consequences, and corrective measures, so the supervisory authority can verify compliance. B primarily governs supervisory feedback and confirms that financial entities remain responsible for handling and consequences of ICT incidents reported under Article 19(1); it does not impose the same documentation duty.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A imposes a record-keeping/documentation obligation on the controller; Norm B states continuing responsibility and regulates supervisory feedback after an ICT-incident notification, without imposing an equivalent reporting or documentation action.
verdict.criterion_fired: Different core action and actor role: A is a controller's documentation duty concerning personal-data breaches, whereas B concerns a financial entity's continuing responsibility for ICT incidents and supervisory feedback.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De verwerkingsverantwoordelijke documenteert alle inbreuken in verband met persoonsgegevens, met inbegrip van de feiten omtrent de inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens, de gevolgen daarvan en de genomen corrigerende maatregelen.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A requires financial entities to maintain accessible records of activities before and during disruptions when ICT continuity/response and recovery plans are activated. B requires notified bodies to inform the notifying authority about specified conformity-assessment certificates, approvals, changes affecting notification, information requests, and activities, including on request.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: The norms concern different actors, different triggering circumstances, different actions, and different compliance outputs: operational record-keeping during ICT-plan activation versus regulatory information reporting by notified bodies.
verdict.criterion_fired: Different actor role and different event family; the duties are record retention/accessibility versus notification of conformity-assessment information to a notifying authority.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both involve making information or policies available in connection with data-related activities, but Norm A requires publication of domain-name registration data-disclosure policies and procedures, whereas Norm B requires informing a supervisory authority about an exceptional international personal-data transfer and also informing the data subject about that transfer and interests pursued.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a proactive transparency/publication duty imposed on domain-name registries and registration-service providers; Norm B is a conditional GDPR safeguard/reporting duty imposed on a controller for a specific exceptional transfer to a third country or international organisation.
verdict.criterion_fired: Different underlying action, event family, and actor role; Norm A concerns publishing general policies and procedures, while Norm B concerns notifying authorities and data subjects about a particular exceptional international data transfer.
verdict.evidence_span_a: stellen het beleid en de procedures met betrekking tot de bekendmaking van de gegevens, bedoeld in het eerste lid, vast en maken dat beleid en die procedures openbaar

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A requires essential and important entities to implement proportionate technical, operational, and organisational cybersecurity-risk-management measures; B concerns retaining responsibility for compliance with ICT-incident-reporting requirements despite outsourcing them.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a preventive and risk-management measure duty, whereas Norm B is an accountability rule concerning incident-reporting obligations and outsourcing.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms do not impose the same underlying action or address the same event: A requires implementation of cybersecurity measures by essential/important entities, while B preserves a financial entity’s responsibility for incident-reporting compliance after outsourcing.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both concern addressing security incidents or their consequences, but A requires implementing proportionate technical, operational, and organisational security measures, whereas B requires promptly notifying the Dutch Data Protection Authority of a qualifying security breach.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a preventive/mitigating security-measures duty directed at protecting service recipients and other services; Norm B is an urgent breach-notification duty directed to the Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens and limited to breaches adversely affecting personal-data protection.
verdict.criterion_fired: The underlying actions and actor scopes differ: A imposes risk-management and incident-impact mitigation measures on essential or important entities, while B imposes an urgent notification duty on providers of public electronic communications services. The shared security-incident context and broad service-provider relationship do not make the compliance work the same.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Beide normen leggen brede cyber-/ICT-risicobeheersmaatregelen op, maar norm A vereist specifiek dat bij de keuze van toeleveringsketenmaatregelen rekening wordt gehouden met leverancierskwetsbaarheden en cyberbeveiligingspraktijken, terwijl norm B een vereenvoudigd, gedocumenteerd ICT-risicobeheerkader en operationele ICT-controles vereist.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A betreft een specifieke beoordelingsfactor binnen de beveiliging van de toeleveringsketen; norm B betreft een omvattend ICT-risicobeheer- en weerbaarheidskader voor bepaalde financiële entiteiten.
verdict.criterion_fired: De normen verschillen zowel naar actorrol als naar de concrete kernhandeling: norm A ziet op essentiële/belangrijke entiteiten die leverancierskwetsbaarheden meewegen bij passende maatregelen, terwijl norm B ziet op specifieke vrijgestelde financiële entiteiten die een ICT-risicobeheerkader moeten instellen, onderhouden en operationeel uitvoeren. De gedeelde cyberrisicocontext maakt dit hoogstens thematisch verwant, niet dezelfde compliance-werkzaamheden.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Wanneer de entiteit overweegt welke maatregelen als bedoeld in het derde lid, onderdeel d, passend zijn, houdt zij rekening met: a. de specifieke kwetsbaarheden van elke rechtstreekse leverancier en dienstverlener;
verdict.evidence_span_b: moeten de in de eerste alinea vermelde entiteiten: a) een degelijk en gedocumenteerd kader voor ICT-risicobeheer tot stand brengen en handhaven

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Norm A requires number holders to register number users within six months. Norm B requires importers, before placing a high-risk AI system on the market, to verify and ensure regulatory conformity, including conformity assessment, technical documentation, CE marking, EU declaration and instructions, and—where a risk exists—to notify the provider, authorised representatives and market-surveillance authorities.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: The norms concern fundamentally different regulated activities and event families: registration of number users versus pre-market conformity checks and possible risk notification for high-risk AI systems.
verdict.criterion_fired: Different event family and different actor role; the duties do not require the same compliance work to be repeated.

verdict.evidence_span_b: Alvorens een AI-systeem met een hoog risico in de handel wordt gebracht, zorgen de importeurs ervoor dat het systeem in overeenstemming is met deze verordening door na te gaan of:

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A concerns the legal effect of registration in a shareholders’ register; B requires importers to provide information and documentation, and ensure technical documentation is available, to competent authorities upon a reasoned request.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an opposability rule concerning a shareholders-register entry and persons who later become participants in a depot; Norm B is an importer’s information/documentation duty concerning conformity of a high-risk AI system.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms do not impose the same underlying action, concern different triggering circumstances and actors, and require materially different legal outcomes or compliance work.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require the regulated actor to establish or prepare compliance-related documentation/procedures: Norm A requires domain-name registries and registration-service entities to establish and publish policies and procedures for disclosing domain-registration data; Norm B requires providers of high-risk AI systems to prepare and update technical documentation demonstrating conformity and enabling assessment by authorities and notified bodies.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A concerns establishing and publishing access/disclosure policies and procedures for domain-registration data, whereas Norm B concerns creating and updating substantive technical documentation for a high-risk AI system's conformity assessment.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties concern different subject matter, different regulated actors, and different compliance purposes: domain-name data-disclosure procedures versus high-risk-AI technical conformity documentation.
verdict.evidence_span_a: stellen het beleid en de procedures met betrekking tot de bekendmaking van de gegevens, bedoeld in het eerste lid, vast en maken dat beleid en die procedures openbaar
verdict.evidence_span_b: De technische documentatie van een AI-systeem met een hoog risico wordt opgesteld voordat dit systeem in de handel wordt gebracht of in gebruik wordt gesteld, en wordt geactualiseerd.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both provisions concern obligations or measures connected with regulatory oversight of a provider after a legally relevant event, but they do not require the same compliance action: Norm A concerns the lead overseer imposing a coercive fine for non-compliance, whereas Norm B requires an AI provider to investigate a serious incident, assess its risks, take corrective measures, cooperate with authorities, and give prior notice before certain system-changing investigations.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an enforcement power exercised by a lead overseer against a critical ICT third-party service provider after non-compliance; Norm B is an incident-response duty imposed on an AI provider following a serious incident.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms differ in actor role, operative action, and event family: A concerns an authority's coercive-fine enforcement measure following non-compliance, while B concerns a provider's investigation and remediation duties following a serious AI incident.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De in lid 6 bedoelde dwangsom wordt dagelijks opgelegd tot aan de verplichtingen is voldaan
verdict.evidence_span_b: verricht de aanbieder onverwijld het nodige onderzoek in verband met het ernstige incident en het betrokken AI-systeem. Dit omvat een risicobeoordeling van het incident en corrigerende maatregelen.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms involve maintaining or documenting information in a register, but they do not impose the same underlying compliance action: Norm A requires the controller or processor to substantiate an assessment and safeguards in the Article 30 record, whereas Norm B requires the processing-activities record to contain reasons justifying strictly necessary processing of special-category data for bias detection and correction.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A concerns documenting an assessment and safeguards supporting a specific international data transfer derogation; Norm B concerns documenting the necessity and justification for processing special-category personal data by providers of high-risk AI systems to detect or correct bias.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties concern different substantive compliance purposes and different actor roles: Norm A applies to a controller or processor documenting transfer-related safeguards, while Norm B applies to providers of high-risk AI systems documenting justification for exceptional processing of special-category data. Any superficial register/documentation similarity does not make the underlying work the same.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De verwerkingsverantwoordelijke of de verwerker staaft de beoordeling en de in lid 1, tweede alinea, van dit artikel bedoelde passende waarborgen in het artikel 30 bedoelde register.
verdict.evidence_span_b: het register op grond van Verordeningen (EU) 2016/679 en (EU) 2018/1725 en Richtlijn (EU) 2016/680 van verwerkingsactiviteiten bevat de redenen waarom de verwerking van bijzondere categorieën persoonsgegevens strikt noodzakelijk was om vertekeningen op te sporen en waarom die doelstelling niet kon worden bereikt door de verwerking van andere data.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both provisions concern obtaining information or documentary material in connection with an authority-led inquiry, but Norm A imposes a request-based duty on a telecommunications party to provide a specific register extract or conduct an identity/control investigation, whereas Norm B grants the lead overseer investigative powers to inspect, copy, summon, question, and obtain information.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an obligation imposed on a telecommunications party and concerns suspected or impending overriding control that may threaten the public interest. Norm B is an empowerment of the lead overseer to conduct general investigations concerning critical third-party ICT service providers; it does not itself impose a matching reporting or disclosure duty on the provider.
verdict.criterion_fired: The provisions do not impose the same compliance work: Norm A requires a telecommunications party, upon ministerial request, to provide a specific shareholder-rights register extract or investigate a controller's identity and connections; Norm B authorizes the lead overseer to investigate and obtain material or explanations as part of a general supervisory investigation.
verdict.evidence_span_a: verstrekt een telecommunicatiepartij aan Onze Minister op verzoek om niet een uittreksel uit het door de rechtspersoon gehouden register met betrekking tot een recht op een aandeel
verdict.evidence_span_b: vertegenwoordigers van kritieke derde aanbieder van ICT-diensten op te roepen en te verzoeken om mondelinge of schriftelijke toelichting te geven bij feiten of documenten

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require the regulated actor to prepare and maintain information/documentation, but Norm A principally requires responding to access requests for domain-registration data, whereas Norm B requires AI-model providers to create and maintain technical and other documentation and make it available to specified recipients.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A concerns disclosure of specific domain-registration data by registries/registration-service entities in response to a lawful, justified access request, with a 72-hour response deadline. Norm B concerns ongoing documentation, information-sharing, copyright-compliance policies, and publication duties of providers of general-purpose AI models.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in actor, event/context, purpose, and substantive content; the superficial similarity of providing information/documentation does not amount to the same compliance work.
verdict.evidence_span_a: de registers voor topleveldomeinnamen en de entiteiten die domeinnaamregistratiediensten verlenen ... toegang verlenen tot specifieke met gegevens over de registratie van domeinnamen
verdict.evidence_span_b: Aanbieders van AI-modellen voor algemene doeleinden moeten: a) de technische documentatie van het model opstellen en up-to-date houden

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern access to information/documentation in a regulatory oversight or conformity-assessment context, but they do not impose the same underlying compliance action: Article 38 concerns investigators exercising investigative powers and obtaining requested records, data, procedures, materials, or answers; Article 11 requires providers of high-risk AI systems to prepare and update technical documentation demonstrating conformity and containing Annex IV information.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Article 38 is an investigative-access and cooperation mechanism directed at third-party ICT-service providers during an overseer’s investigation, whereas Article 11 is a standing technical-documentation duty for high-risk AI-system providers, intended to support conformity assessment by authorities and notified bodies.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in actor role, triggering context, and core action: investigative cooperation in an overseer-led investigation versus preparation and updating of AI technical documentation.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De functionarissen van de lead overseer en andere door hem voor de uitvoering van de in lid 1 bedoelde onderzoeken gemachtigde personen oefenen hun bevoegdheden uit na overlegging van een schriftelijke machtiging waarin het onderwerp en het doel van het onderzoek zijn vermeld.
verdict.evidence_span_b: De technische documentatie van een AI-systeem met een hoog risico wordt opgesteld voordat dit systeem in de handel wordt gebracht of in gebruik wordt gesteld, en wordt geactualiseerd.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Geen gedeelde concrete compliance-actie: Norm A vereist het ontwikkelen en documenteren van informatiebeveiligingsbeleid als onderdeel van ICT-risicobeheer; Norm B vereist na melding van een ernstig incident onderzoek, risicobeoordeling, corrigerende maatregelen en samenwerking met autoriteiten, met een beperking op onderzoek dat het AI-systeem kan wijzigen.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is een doorlopende preventieve governance- en beleidsverplichting voor financiële entiteiten. Norm B is een incidentresponsverplichting voor aanbieders van AI-systemen na een ernstig incident, inclusief onderzoek en samenwerking met bevoegde autoriteiten.
verdict.criterion_fired: De normen verschillen zowel in kernactie als in actorrol en gebeurtenisfamilie: preventief informatiebeveiligingsbeleid tegenover post-incident onderzoek en corrigerende maatregelen bij een ernstig AI-incident.
verdict.evidence_span_a: zij ontwikkelen en documenteren een beleid inzake informatiebeveiliging waarin regels worden vastgesteld ter bescherming van de beschikbaarheid, authenticiteit, integriteit en vertrouwelijkheid van gegevens, informatie- en ICT-activa
verdict.evidence_span_b: Na de melding van een ernstig incident op grond van lid 1 verricht de aanbieder onverwijld het nodige onderzoek in verband met het ernstige incident en het betrokken AI-systeem. Dit omvat een risicobeoordeling van het incident en corrigerende maatregelen.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A vereist dat essentiële en belangrijke entiteiten wijzigingen in eerder verstrekte identificatie- en registratiegegevens aan de bevoegde autoriteiten melden. B vereist dat aanbieders technische documentatie voor hoog-risico-AI-systemen opstellen en actualiseren, zodat conformiteit kan worden aangetoond en autoriteiten/aangemelde instanties de conformiteit kunnen beoordelen.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: A is een tijdgebonden wijzigingsmelding van entiteits- en contactgegevens aan bevoegde autoriteiten; B is doorlopende technische conformiteitsdocumentatie voor een hoog-risico-AI-systeem, opgesteld vóór marktintroductie of ingebruikname en geactualiseerd daarna.
verdict.criterion_fired: De normen betreffen verschillende actoren, gebeurtenissen en kernhandelingen: wijzigingsmelding van registratiegegevens versus opstellen en actualiseren van technische conformiteitsdocumentatie.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De in lid 3 bedoelde entiteiten melden onmiddellijk elke wijziging in de bijzonderheden die zij op grond van de eerste alinea van dit lid hebben ingediend, en in elk geval binnen twee weken na de datum van de wijziging.
verdict.evidence_span_b: De technische documentatie van een AI-systeem met een hoog risico wordt opgesteld voordat dit systeem in de handel wordt gebracht of in gebruik wordt gesteld, en wordt geactualiseerd.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Beide normen leggen een verplichting op die verband houdt met het beheer van risico’s na of in verband met een incident: norm A vereist governance, goedkeuring en toezicht op cyberbeveiligingsrisicomaatregelen; norm B vereist na melding van een ernstig incident onderzoek, een incidentrisicobeoordeling en corrigerende maatregelen.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A betreft een doorlopende governance- en verantwoordingsplicht van bestuursorganen van essentiële en belangrijke entiteiten met betrekking tot cyberbeveiligingsrisicobeheersmaatregelen. Norm B betreft een aanbieder die na melding van een ernstig incident onverwijld een specifiek incidentonderzoek uitvoert, inclusief risicobeoordeling en corrigerende maatregelen, en daarbij met autoriteiten samenwerkt.
verdict.criterion_fired: De normen verschillen zowel in kernactie als in actorrol en event/context: A is bestuursgovernance en toezicht op algemene cyberbeveiligingsmaatregelen; B is incidentonderzoek en herstelmaatregelen door een AI-aanbieder na een ernstig incident. De beperkte thematische overlap rond risicobeheer maakt dit geen dubbele compliance-last.
verdict.evidence_span_a: de bestuursorganen van essentiële en belangrijke entiteiten de door deze entiteiten genomen maatregelen voor het beheer van cyberbeveiligingsrisico’s goedkeuren om te voldoen aan artikel 21, toezien op de uitvoering ervan en aansprakelijk kunnen worden gesteld
verdict.evidence_span_b: verricht de aanbieder onverwijld het nodige onderzoek in verband met het ernstige incident en het betrokken AI-systeem. Dit omvat een risicobeoordeling van het incident en corrigerende maatregelen.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require an entity to prepare and provide or make information/documentation available, but they concern different substantive duties: registration information for a national register versus AI-model documentation and transparency obligations.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A concerns essential/important entities and domain-name registration service providers supplying registration data and updates to the Dutch Minister; Norm B concerns providers of general-purpose AI models preparing, maintaining, supplying, and publishing technical, user-facing, copyright, and training-content information.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in actor role, subject matter, and purpose. Norm A is an ongoing national-register information-supply duty, including updates within two weeks; Norm B imposes multiple AI-model documentation, disclosure, copyright-policy, and publication duties, with no comparable registration-reporting obligation.

verdict.evidence_span_b: Aanbieders van AI-modellen voor algemene doeleinden moeten: a) de technische documentatie van het model opstellen en up-to-date houden ... b) informatie en documentatie opstellen, up-to-date houden en beschikbaar stellen ... d) een voldoende gedetailleerde samenvatting opstellen en openbaar maken

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A concerns supplying specified information in an early warning about a significant incident, including whether the incident may have cross-border effects. B concerns conducting post-incident evaluations after serious ICT-related disruptions, assessing causes and effectiveness, identifying improvements, and—on request for non-micro financial entities—communicating implemented changes to competent authorities.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: A is an early-warning information disclosure about the incident’s possible cross-border effects; B is an internal post-incident review and improvement process, with possible later communication of resulting changes.
verdict.criterion_fired: Same broad ICT/security-incident family and actor role, but different operative actions and substantially different content and purpose; therefore related rather than duplicated work.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern internal organisational/data-governance measures by regulated entities, but they do not require the same compliance action: Norm A requires establishing procedures and processes for monitoring, handling and following up ICT incidents, while Norm B permits exceptional processing of special-category personal data for detecting and correcting bias, subject to safeguards and documentation.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A addresses ICT-incident management and root-cause remediation; Norm B addresses exceptional processing and protection of special-category personal data for bias detection and correction in high-risk AI systems.
verdict.criterion_fired: Different underlying action, event family, and regulated actor role; the apparent similarity does not establish duplicated compliance work.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms involve obtaining or checking information/material relevant to regulatory compliance, but they impose fundamentally different actions: the lead overseer conducts a broad investigative examination, while the importer verifies specified conformity conditions before placing a high-risk AI system on the market.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A grants an investigative power to a supervisory authority; Norm B imposes a pre-market verification duty on an importer, with a conditional notification duty only where the importer has sufficient reasons to suspect non-compliance, falsification, or a relevant risk.
verdict.criterion_fired: Different actor role and different event family/core duty: an authority's general investigative examination is not the importer's pre-market conformity verification or conditional notification obligation.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms involve producing or providing information/documentation, but A requires a telecommunications party, upon ministerial request, to provide a register extract or investigate a controlling-interest holder; B requires providers of general-purpose AI models to create and maintain extensive technical and related documentation, make some of it available to downstream providers, and provide it on request to the AI Office and national authorities.

The triggering events, actors, purposes, recipients, and substantive content differ: A concerns suspected or anticipated controlling influence threatening the public interest, whereas B imposes standing AI-model documentation and transparency duties.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms do not concern the same event family or the same actor role, and their required information serves materially different purposes and contains different subject matter; a superficial shared information-provision verb is insufficient.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A requires affected entities to submit a progress report on an ongoing significant incident to the CSIRT or competent authority; B requires financial entities to conduct post-incident ICT evaluations and, for non-micro-enterprises, communicate implemented changes to competent authorities on request.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: A is an external incident-reporting duty during an ongoing significant incident, with prescribed incident-status content and timing. B is an internal post-incident evaluation and improvement duty, with a possible later, request-based communication of changes; it does not require submission of an incident progress report.
verdict.criterion_fired: Same incident family and broadly comparable regulated-entity role, but different core actions, purposes, timing, and content: external progress reporting versus internal post-incident evaluation and improvement, with only a conditional request-based communication of changes.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A requires a critical ICT third-party provider to submit to an on-site inspection ordered by the lead overseer, including compliance with the inspection decision. B requires an AI provider, after reporting a serious incident, to promptly investigate the incident and AI system, assess risks, take corrective measures, cooperate with authorities, and give prior notice before certain system-changing investigations.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: A concerns submission to and procedural compliance with a supervisory on-site inspection; B concerns post-incident investigation, risk assessment, corrective action, and cooperation/notice duties. They do not impose the same operational work.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in actor role, triggering context, and core action: inspection compliance under supervisory orders versus post-serious-incident investigation and remediation.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A requires the entity to take immediate necessary, appropriate and proportionate corrective measures after finding that it does not comply with cybersecurity-risk-management measures. B requires a critical ICT third-party provider to submit to an on-site inspection ordered by the lead overseer; the listed items are contents of the overseer’s decision, not a reporting duty imposed on the provider.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: The norms concern fundamentally different duties: corrective remediation of cybersecurity non-compliance versus cooperation with an on-site supervisory inspection.
verdict.criterion_fired: Different core action, event family, and actor role; B is an inspection/cooperation obligation, not a corrective-measures obligation.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms involve an actor taking a formal step before or with a public authority, but A is an optional request to the ACM for a decision in a failed agreement, whereas B requires staged incident reporting to a CSIRT or competent authority.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A concerns requesting an ACM decision about the applicability, location, timing, or method of works after negotiations fail; Norm B concerns mandatory, detailed reporting of a significant incident, including warnings, incident updates, interim/final reports, and mitigation information.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms involve making information or documentation available to competent authorities, but A primarily requires financial entities to maintain/update an ICT-service contract information register and report specified aggregate information, whereas B requires importers to provide information and documentation substantiating conformity of a high-risk AI system, and to ensure technical documentation can be made available.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: The duties concern different regulated subject matters and purposes: ICT third-party-service oversight and register/reporting under A versus high-risk AI conformity substantiation and technical documentation under B.
verdict.criterion_fired: Different actor role and different event/duty family; any superficial overlap is limited to supplying information to competent authorities, while the underlying compliance work, subject matter, and purpose differ.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A requires a telecommunications party, upon ministerial request, to provide a register extract free of charge and/or investigate the identity and third-party links of a control holder. B requires the provider of a high-risk AI system to prepare and update technical documentation demonstrating conformity and containing Annex IV information, so that competent authorities and notified bodies can assess conformity.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: The norms concern different regulated actors, different triggering events, and materially different compliance work: a control/ownership investigation or register disclosure versus preparation and maintenance of AI-system technical documentation.
verdict.criterion_fired: Different event family and different actor role; the duties are not the same compliance work, and the recipient relationship is unrelated.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require prompt communication concerning a cyber/data-related threat or incident, but A requires a processor to inform the controller about a personal-data breach, whereas B requires essential or important entities to inform potentially affected service recipients about protective measures and, if necessary, the significant cyber threat itself.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: The duties differ in both actor-recipient relationship and communication purpose/content: A is processor-to-controller notification of a personal-data breach; B is entity-to-service-recipient warning and guidance concerning a significant cyber threat.
verdict.criterion_fired: Different actor role and materially different recipient relationship and content; the shared incident/threat context and prompt communication do not make the underlying compliance work the same.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both require the regulated actor to create or make information available: Norm A requires publication of non-personal domain-name registration data, while Norm B requires preparation and updating of technical documentation for a high-risk AI system.

verdict.criterion_fired: The duties concern different regulated actors, different triggering events, and materially different outputs and purposes: publication of domain-registration data versus preparation of AI technical documentation for conformity assessment.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern action following an ICT/data-related incident, but Norm A requires urgent communication of the personal-data breach to affected individuals, whereas Norm B requires financial entities to conduct a post-incident evaluation, assess causes and effectiveness, identify improvements, and—on request for non-micro entities—communicate implemented changes to competent authorities.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an urgent breach notification to the data subject; Norm B is an internal post-incident review and improvement process, with possible authority-facing disclosure of resulting changes.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern compliance steps connected with regulated entities or products, but A requires an entity to provide/update identification and contact information to competent authorities, whereas B requires importers to verify high-risk AI-system conformity before placing it on the market and, in specified cases, notify the provider, authorised representatives, and market-surveillance authorities.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern handling or obtaining information/data, but Norm A requires domain-registration entities to collect and maintain accurate, complete registration data in a database, whereas Norm B empowers a supervisory authority to investigate and obtain records, data, explanations, and traffic overviews.
