verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both provisions assign an authorised representative a package of representative duties involving retention or provision of technical information/documentation and cooperation with authorities. However, Norm B additionally requires the representative to provide a copy of the mandate and contains AI-specific verification, documentation, and cooperation duties.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A concerns representatives for devices/radio equipment and requires keeping the EU declaration of conformity and technical documentation available to the Minister, supplying information/documentation on request, and cooperating with risk-elimination measures. Norm B concerns representatives for providers of general-purpose AI models and requires mandate disclosure to the AI Office, verification of AI-specific obligations, retention of AI technical documentation for the AI Office and national authorities, provision of information on a reasoned request, and cooperation concerning AI-model measures.
verdict.criterion_fired: The provisions concern different regulated subject matters and different substantive compliance regimes: devices/radio equipment under Norm A versus general-purpose AI models under Norm B. Although both use an authorised-representative structure and include authority-facing information/documentation and cooperation duties, they do not impose the same duty for the same regulated object or compliance purpose.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A requires the controller to provide specified information to the data-protection supervisory authority in a prior-consultation process. B requires financial entities to implement and document ICT-security, network/infrastructure, access-control, authentication, change-management, and patch/update measures.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: A is an information-provision duty triggered by a planned high-risk processing activity and addressed to a supervisory authority; B is an ongoing ICT-risk-management and security-controls duty triggered by the entity's risk-management framework, not a reporting or information-provision duty.

verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in core action, triggering subject matter, and actor role: Norm A concerns supplying ENISA-register information by specified digital-service entities, while Norm B concerns internal incident registration and management by financial entities. verdict.criterion_fired: The duties do not concern the same event or compliance work: A concerns registration in an ENISA-related register, while B concerns an exceptional international transfer of personal data and associated notifications.

verdict.criterion_fired: The duties concern different actors, different triggering circumstances, and different substantive actions: publication of domain-registration data versus conformity assessment of high-risk AI systems.

Norm B concerns notified bodies informing the notifying authority about specified conformity-assessment matters and activities, including cross-border work and subcontracting, with no deadline stated here.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both require an entity to communicate information concerning a cyber/ICT-related incident or threat, but A requires an early warning to a CSIRT and competent authority, while B requires notice to potentially affected clients, including mitigation or protective measures.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: The recipients and substantive purpose/content differ: A is an early regulatory/CSIRT warning about a significant incident; B is client-facing information about a serious ICT incident and mitigation measures, or protective measures for a significant cyber threat.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties do not impose the same compliance work: they involve different actor categories, recipients, and communication content/purposes. The shared ICT/cyber-incident context and notification verb are insufficient to establish duplicate burden.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit geeft ten behoeve van de melding, bedoeld in artikel 27, eerste lid, een vroegtijdige waarschuwing over het significante incident aan haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit.
verdict.evidence_span_b: stellen financiële entiteiten, zodra zij het incident hebben opgemerkt, hun cliënten onverwijld in kennis van het ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incident en van de maatregelen die zijn genomen om de negatieve gevolgen van een dergelijk incident te beperken.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both provisions concern making information or documentation available to a public authority in connection with regulatory oversight or compliance verification, but they do not impose the same concrete action: Norm A requires the appointed representative to retain and, on request, provide conformity information/documentation and cooperate with risk-reduction measures; Norm B empowers the lead overseer to inspect or obtain records and other material and to question persons during an investigation.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A imposes duties on an appointed representative, including ten-year retention and responding to ministerial requests. Norm B grants investigative powers to a lead overseer concerning critical third-party ICT-service providers and other persons; it is not itself a matching reporting or information-supply duty.
verdict.criterion_fired: The provisions do not impose the same actor-side compliance obligation: A is a representative's retention/provision/cooperation duty, while B is an authority's investigative power to examine or obtain material and hear persons.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Geen gedeelde concrete compliance-actie: norm A vereist het aanwijzen van een vertegenwoordiger; norm B vereist het opstellen en actualiseren van technische documentatie voor een hoog-risico-AI-systeem.

A ziet op het ontbreken van een EU-vertegenwoordiger bij bepaalde entiteiten; B ziet op het opstellen en actualiseren van technische documentatie vóór marktintroductie of ingebruikname van een hoog-risico-AI-systeem.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require an entity to provide information to a public authority, but they concern materially different information and purposes: Norm A requires covered digital-service entities to submit registration information for ENISA’s register through the designated mechanism; Norm B requires a telecommunications party, on request, to provide a company-register extract concerning a share right to the Minister, and separately may require an investigation into a controlling-interest holder.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a standing, sector-specific registration-information submission for the ENISA register, covering entity identity, classification, addresses, contact details, Member States of operation, and IP ranges. Norm B is an on-request disclosure connected to suspected or anticipated dominant control threatening the public interest, concerning a share-right register extract (and potentially an investigation into the controller’s identity and affiliations).
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms do not concern the same triggering event or the same actor role: Norm A applies to specified essential or important digital-service entities for ENISA-register information, while Norm B applies to a telecommunications party responding to a Ministerial request arising from suspected or prospective overwegende zeggenschap. The shared act of providing information to an authority is insufficient for duplicate burden, and the required information and purposes substantially differ.
verdict.evidence_span_a: verstrekken de volgende entiteiten aan het centrale contactpunt de informatie, bedoeld in het derde lid van dit artikel, middels het daarvoor opgezette mechanisme
verdict.evidence_span_b: verstrekt een telecommunicatiepartij aan Onze Minister op verzoek om niet een uittreksel uit het door de rechtspersoon gehouden register met betrekking tot een recht op een aandeel

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both provisions involve an actor taking a formal step toward a public authority, but A requires an incident warning/report while B permits a request for an administrative decision concerning a statutory access obligation and works.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an urgent cybersecurity-incident warning by an essential or important entity to its CSIRT and competent authority; Norm B is an optional escalation request by an infrastructure provider, rights-holder, or manager to the ACM after failed negotiations about a gedoogplicht and related works.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties concern different triggering events, actor roles, purposes, recipients, and substantive content; the shared presence of a formal communication to an authority is not enough to establish duplicated compliance work.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit geeft ten behoeve van de melding, bedoeld in artikel 27, eerste lid, een vroegtijdige waarschuwing over het significante incident aan haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit.
verdict.evidence_span_b: kan de aanbieder alsmede de rechthebbende of de beheerder, bedoeld in artikel 5.2, binnen 2 weken de Autoriteit Consument en Markt verzoeken een beschikking te geven over de toepasselijkheid van de gedoogplicht of de plaats, het tijdstip en de wijze van de uit te voeren werkzaamheden.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A: een besluit onverwijld nemen na ontvangst van een melding. B: kennisgeving doen van de aanwijzing als kritieke ICT-dienstverlener en de aanvangsdatum van oversightactiviteiten, met daarnaast een mogelijkheid voor de aanbieder om een gemotiveerde verklaring in te dienen.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A betreft het nemen van een besluit na ontvangst van een melding; norm B betreft kennisgevingen over een aanwijzing als kritieke ICT-dienstverlener en de start van toezicht, plus een afzonderlijke procedure voor opmerkingen en aanvullende informatie.
verdict.criterion_fired: De normen hebben niet dezelfde kernhandeling, gebeurtenis, actorrol of inhoud; een besluit nemen na ontvangst van een melding is wezenlijk anders dan kennisgeving doen van een aanwijzing en toezichtstart.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Het besluit wordt onverwijld na het tijdstip van ontvangst van de melding genomen.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Nadat een derde aanbieder van ICT-diensten als cruciaal is aangewezen, stellen de ETA’s de derde aanbieder van ICT-diensten via het Gemengd Comité in kennis van die aanwijzing alsook van de aanvangsdatum vanaf wanneer zij daadwerkelijk aan oversightactiviteiten zullen worden onderworpen.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both provisions concern follow-up compliance after a serious/security-type incident: A requires an interim update report during an incident notification process, while B requires the provider to promptly investigate the serious incident and AI system, including risk assessment and corrective measures, and to cooperate with authorities.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A imposes a requested interim reporting duty to a CSIRT or competent authority; Norm B imposes an immediate investigation, risk-assessment, corrective-measures, cooperation, and prior-notification duty on an AI-system provider. The duties are not the same work.
verdict.criterion_fired: The core actions and responsible actor roles differ: A requires an essential or important entity to submit an interim report with relevant situation updates when requested, whereas B requires an AI provider to investigate the incident and system, assess risks, take corrective measures, cooperate with authorities, and give prior notice before potentially compromising investigative changes.

The different authority channel is not the decisive factor.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require the addressee to take a proactive compliance measure concerning ICT/AI-related risks: Norm A requires financial entities to implement network and infrastructure-management controls, while Norm B prohibits specified AI-system activities and, for certain real-time biometric-identification uses, requires authorization and safeguards.

verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in actor, triggering context, core action, purpose, and required content: cybersecurity risk-control measures versus a high-risk AI fundamental-rights assessment and regulatory notification.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern submitting an interim report or update concerning a serious ICT/security incident to a competent authority. However, Norm A requires an interim report on relevant updates only when requested by the entity’s CSIRT or competent authority, whereas Norm B requires financial entities to submit a structured interim report after the initial notification when the incident status or handling materially changes, with further updates and a final report under specified conditions.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a request-based supplementary report under the NIS2-style incident-reporting process and may be addressed to either a CSIRT or competent authority. Norm B is a mandatory DORA reporting sequence for financial entities, addressed to the relevant competent authority, using prescribed reporting stages and containing information needed to assess incident scope and cross-border effects.
verdict.criterion_fired: Same incident-update reporting pattern and broadly overlapping interim-reporting work, but different regulated actor categories and materially different reporting frameworks, triggers, procedures, and required content prevent a finding that the same compliance work is simply repeated.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern communications connected with digital/ICT regulatory oversight, but they do not impose the same underlying compliance action: Norm A requires the entity to submit a substantive post-incident final report, while Norm B concerns notification of a critical designation and its oversight start date.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an incident-reporting duty imposed on an essential or important entity and addressed to its CSIRT and competent authority. Norm B is a designation notification involving the lead overseer/ETAs, the critical ICT third-party provider, and the provider’s financial-entity customers; it is not an incident report.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms differ in the operative action, triggering event, and duty-bearing actor: A requires an entity to file a detailed final incident report within one month after an incident notification; B concerns notification of a regulatory designation and oversight commencement, with a separate customer-notification consequence.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit dient uiterlijk één maand na de melding, bedoeld in artikel 27, eerste lid, een eindverslag in bij haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Aansprakelijkheid voor schade door onrechtmatige verwerking (Norm A) versus het uitvoeren van post-incidentevaluaties en identificeren van verbeteringen in ICT-activiteiten of bedrijfscontinuïteitsbeleid (Norm B). Er is geen gedeelde concrete compliancehandeling.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both provisions involve obtaining or supplying information or records, but A imposes a specific information-submission duty on domain-name registration service providers, whereas B grants the lead overseer investigative powers to inspect or obtain materials and copies during general investigations.

Norm B is an authority's investigative power to examine or obtain records, copies, and other material from critical third-party ICT service providers; it is not the same reporting obligation.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in actor role and operative action: A requires entities providing domain-name registration services to provide specified register information; B empowers the lead overseer to investigate and obtain records or copies in an investigation. The shared information theme is insufficient to establish duplicated compliance work.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms impose information/documentation-related duties, but they require different underlying work: domain-name registration service entities must provide registry-identification information to the central contact point, while providers of general-purpose AI models must create and maintain extensive model technical documentation and make it available to specified AI authorities or system providers.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a targeted registry-information submission by domain-name registration service providers, covering entity, contact, location, service-territory, and IP-range details. Norm B is a substantive AI-governance documentation duty covering the model’s technical documentation, training and testing process, evaluation results, and related information/documentation obligations.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties concern different regulated actors and different substantive obligations: Norm A requires supplying registry data to the NIS2 central contact point; Norm B requires preparing and maintaining technical AI-model documentation and related materials, with possible provision to AI authorities or AI-system providers. Similarity as information-related duties and authority-facing channels is insufficient for duplicate burden.
verdict.evidence_span_a: verstrekken entiteiten die domeinnaamregistratiediensten verlenen aan het centrale contactpunt de informatie, bedoeld in het derde lid van dit artikel, middels het daarvoor opgezette mechanisme

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Norm A requires covered entities to report significant incidents to a CSIRT or competent authority through warnings, incident reports, updates and final reports. verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both provisions concern manufacturer/provider compliance responsibilities for regulated products or systems, but they do not impose the same concrete action: A concerns appointing an authorised representative in writing, while B sets out multiple high-risk-AI provider obligations, including corrective measures and information provision.

Norm B bevat bovendien afzonderlijke jaarlijkse rapportage- en voorafgaande kennisgevingsplichten.
verdict.criterion_fired: De onderliggende informatieverstrekking lijkt op hoog abstractieniveau vergelijkbaar, maar de concrete actor, het gereguleerde onderwerp, de trigger en de inhoud/doelstelling van de informatie verschillen wezenlijk. verdict.shared_compliance_action: A requires entities to incorporate relevant operational conclusions from testing and post-incident analysis into the ICT-risk-assessment process; B requires an AI provider, after reporting a serious incident, to investigate it and the AI system, assess risks, take corrective measures, cooperate with competent authorities/notified bodies, and give prior notice before certain system-changing investigations.

The shared incident-related context is insufficient for duplicate burden.

Die kennisgeving bevat de informatie die nodig is om aan te tonen dat aan de desbetreffende eis is voldaan.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A requires the controller/processor to make its processing-activities register available to a supervisory authority on request. B requires a provider of certain high-risk AI systems to follow specified conformity-assessment procedures, potentially involving a notified body; it does not impose the same reporting or information-supply action.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: The norms concern fundamentally different compliance duties: GDPR record disclosure to a supervisory authority versus AI Act conformity assessment of a high-risk AI system.
verdict.criterion_fired: Different core action, event family, and actor role; A concerns disclosure of a processing register on request, while B concerns selecting/following a conformity-assessment procedure for a high-risk AI system.

verdict.evidence_span_b: volgt de aanbieder de conformiteitsbeoordelingsprocedure van bijlage VII

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Beide normen omvatten het opstellen/beschikbaar houden of verstrekken van technische informatie en documentatie, maar zij leggen geen identieke rapportage- of documentatietaak op. Norm A betreft een gemachtigde die documentatie tien jaar bewaart en op verzoek aan de minister verstrekt om conformiteit aan te tonen; norm B betreft aanbieders van algemene AI-modellen die uitgebreide model-, trainings- en evaluatiedocumentatie opstellen en bijhouden, onder meer voor AI-systeemaanbieders en op verzoek voor het AI-bureau en nationale bevoegde autoriteiten.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A ziet op de wettelijke vertegenwoordiger van een apparaat- of radioapparaatfabrikant en op conformiteitsdocumentatie gedurende tien jaar, terwijl norm B ziet op aanbieders van algemene AI-modellen en op model-, trainings-, test- en evaluatie-informatie, plus informatie voor integrerende AI-systeemaanbieders en een auteursrechtbeleid en publieke trainingscontentsamenvatting.
verdict.criterion_fired: De normen hebben niet dezelfde actorrol, niet dezelfde inhoudelijke compliance-doelstelling en geen hetzelfde soort trigger: A betreft doorlopende conformiteitsbewaring en verzoekgestuurde medewerking rond apparaten/radioapparaten; B betreft doorlopende governance-, documentatie- en transparantieverplichtingen voor algemene AI-modellen.
verdict.evidence_span_a: het ter beschikking van Onze Minister houden van de EU-conformiteitsverklaring en de technische documentatie gedurende tien jaar nadat het apparaat of het radioapparaat in de handel is gebracht
verdict.evidence_span_b: de technische documentatie van het model opstellen en up-to-date houden, inclusief het trainings- en testproces en de resultaten van de evaluatie ervan

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern compliance activity connected with ICT/security incidents, but A requires an incident-related progress report (and later final report), whereas B requires documentation and evaluation of an ICT-risk-management framework and submission of its evaluation report on request.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an incident-reporting duty for an essential or important entity, including a progress report when the incident is still ongoing. Norm B is a governance/control-framework documentation and evaluation duty, with an evaluation report submitted to the competent authority on request.
verdict.criterion_fired: The underlying actions and responsible actor categories differ: A requires reporting the status/aspects of a continuing incident, while B requires documenting and evaluating an ICT-risk-management framework and, on request, submitting its evaluation report. The shared ICT-incident context is insufficient to establish the same compliance work.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Beide normen leggen een informatie-/transparantieverplichting op, maar niet dezelfde: norm A vereist onmiddellijke openbare beschikbaarstelling van niet-persoonsgebonden domeinnaamregistratiegegevens; norm B vereist het bijhouden van een ICT-contractenregister en rapportage/terbeschikkingstelling aan de bevoegde autoriteit.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern ICT/security-incident handling, but Norm A requires the affected entity to submit incident reports and updates to a CSIRT or competent authority, whereas Norm B requires a financial entity to establish and implement an internal ICT-incident management process for detection, management, and reporting.

verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in both the core action and actor role: A requires incident submissions by affected entities to an authority/CSIRT, while B requires financial entities to create and implement an internal incident-management process. Similar incident subject matter is insufficient for duplicate burden.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern post-incident ICT/AI risk handling, but Norm A requires financial entities to establish and maintain preventive ICT-security and risk-management controls, whereas Norm B requires an AI provider to investigate a serious incident, assess its risks, take corrective measures, cooperate with authorities, and avoid prejudicial system changes.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a standing preventive governance and control framework obligation; Norm B is an incident-triggered investigation, remediation, cooperation, and procedural-preservation obligation for AI providers.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in both actor role and core action: financial entities must implement/document preventive ICT-security measures, while AI providers must promptly investigate a serious incident and undertake related corrective and cooperation steps. The apparent similarity is not enough to establish duplicated compliance work.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both impose obligations involving making resources or cooperation available to a public authority, but A requires active cooperation and execution of military-authority orders, whereas B requires retaining specified high-risk-AI documentation and keeping it available to national competent authorities for ten years.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: A is an event-contingent cooperation duty during application of the Dutch War Act; B is a fixed ten-year documentation-retention and availability duty following placing a high-risk AI system on the market or putting it into service.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties concern different actors, triggering events, and substantive actions: military-authority cooperation and execution of orders versus retention and availability of specified AI compliance documentation.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both concern addressing ICT/security incidents: Norm A requires implementing preventive and mitigating security measures, while Norm B requires preparing and submitting incident notifications and reports to a competent authority.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an ongoing risk-management and incident-prevention/impact-mitigation duty; Norm B is an incident-reporting duty involving specified notifications and reports to an authority, including information on scope and cross-border effects.
verdict.criterion_fired: The underlying actions and actor roles differ: Norm A requires an essential or important entity to implement technical, operational and organisational measures, whereas Norm B requires a financial entity to report serious ICT-related incidents and prepare prescribed reports for a competent authority. The shared ICT/security-incident context is insufficient to make the compliance work duplicative.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both provisions concern regulatory oversight or demonstrating compliance to public authorities, but they do not impose the same underlying compliance action: Article 38 concerns investigators exercising investigative powers and obtaining requested records, data, procedures, materials, or answers; Article 16(k) requires high-risk AI providers to demonstrate conformity with Section 2 upon a reasoned request from a national competent authority.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Article 38 governs the authority's exercise of investigative powers and the investigated ICT service provider's provision of requested information or materials, whereas Article 16(k) imposes a substantive demonstration-of-conformity duty on high-risk AI providers.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in actor role, operative action, and subject matter: one concerns an overseer's investigation and requested responses from representatives of third-party ICT service providers; the other concerns a high-risk AI provider demonstrating conformity with Section 2 to a national competent authority.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms involve an obligation directed to an external authority, but Norm A requires broad cooperation and execution of military-authority orders, whereas Norm B requires notified bodies to inform the notifying authority about specified conformity-assessment matters and activities.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a broad cooperation/assistance duty triggered by application of Article 31 of the Dutch War Act; Norm B is a structured information-reporting duty concerning conformity-assessment activities and related certification or notification matters.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in core action, triggering context, actor role, recipient authority, and substantive content; any superficial similarity from involving an authority-directed obligation is insufficient for duplicate burden.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms impose a positive compliance action on a regulated provider-type actor: Norm A requires answering a lawful, properly justified request for access to specific domain-registration data; Norm B requires the provider of a high-risk AI system to follow an applicable conformity-assessment procedure to demonstrate compliance.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A concerns responding to an external access request for specific domain-registration data, whereas Norm B concerns selecting and carrying out a conformity-assessment procedure for a high-risk AI system. They do not concern the same operational work.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in both event family and core action: Norm A is an access-request response duty for domain-registration data, while Norm B is an AI conformity-assessment duty. verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern compliance-related information/process obligations for regulated entities, but A requires providing entity-identification and registration information to a central contact point, whereas B requires establishing internal ICT-incident management procedures and processes (and, in the fuller provision, registering ICT incidents and significant cyber threats).
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an external information-supply duty for domain-name registration service providers concerning ENISA's register; Norm B is an internal ICT-incident governance and management duty for financial entities.
verdict.criterion_fired: The underlying action, triggering subject matter, and actor role differ: A requires domain-name registration service providers to provide specified entity information to a central contact point, while B requires financial entities to establish internal procedures and processes for monitoring, handling, and following up ICT-related incidents.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Documenting or carrying out conditions for processing or transferring personal data: Norm A requires substantiating an assessment and safeguards in a GDPR register; Norm B requires satisfying and operationalising extensive safeguards for processing personal data in an AI regulatory sandbox, including monitoring, isolation, logging, deletion, documentation, and publication.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A concerns documenting an assessment and appropriate safeguards for exceptional transfers of personal data to a third country or international organisation. Norm B concerns the substantive conditions and safeguards for further processing personal data to develop, train, and test certain AI systems in a regulatory sandbox.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms do not impose the same underlying action or address the same triggering event. Norm A is a controller/processor recordkeeping and substantiation duty linked to an exceptional international data transfer; Norm B is a set of conditions and safeguards governing AI-sandbox processing, with no comparable reporting or registration duty to the same recipient.

Norm A concerns an authorised representative’s ongoing support and documentation duties, while Norm B concerns an AI provider’s selection and use of a conformity-assessment procedure.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Beide normen houden verband met toezicht/compliance rond gereguleerde digitale activiteiten, maar norm A vereist het informeren van de toezichthoudende autoriteit en de betrokkene over een specifieke doorgifte; norm B betreft controle, beschikbaar houden en op verzoek verstrekken van AI-documentatie en samenwerking met autoriteiten.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A ziet op een internationale doorgifte van persoonsgegevens en bevat een meldings-/informatieplicht. Norm B ziet op de gemachtigde van een aanbieder van een AI-model voor algemene doeleinden en diens documentatie-, verificatie- en samenwerkingsverplichtingen.
verdict.criterion_fired: De normen betreffen niet dezelfde kernhandeling, niet dezelfde trigger en niet dezelfde actorrol: A betreft informeren over een doorgifte van persoonsgegevens door de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke, terwijl B de gemachtigde van een AI-aanbieder verplicht technische documentatie te controleren en die op verzoek aan het AI-bureau of bevoegde autoriteiten beschikbaar te stellen.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De verwerkingsverantwoordelijke informeert de toezichthoudende autoriteit over de doorgifte. De verwerkingsverantwoordelijke informeert de betrokkene
verdict.evidence_span_b: controleren of de aanbieder de in bijlage XI gespecificeerde technische documentatie heeft opgesteld en aan alle in artikel 53 en, indien van toepassing, artikel 55 bedoelde verplichtingen heeft voldaan

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Norm A requires a controller to describe or communicate specified information in a personal-data-breach notification to a supervisory authority. Norm B requires conditions and safeguards for processing personal data in an AI regulatory sandbox, including preventing decisions affecting data subjects; it also includes retention, deletion, logging, documentation, and publication requirements.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an incident-notification content duty triggered by a personal-data breach; Norm B is a substantive data-processing authorization/safeguard regime for AI-system development, training, and testing, not a breach-reporting duty.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms do not impose the same underlying action or concern the same triggering event: A concerns reporting a personal-data breach to a supervisory authority, while B governs safeguards and conditions for processing personal data in an AI regulatory sandbox.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms involve communicating information about a security-related situation, but Norm A requires an internet-access provider to notify the affected subscriber before, or as soon as possible after, taking a protective service measure; Norm B requires an affected entity to submit structured incident reports and updates about a significant incident to a CSIRT or competent authority.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a subscriber notice accompanying a provider's suspension or termination measure to protect network, service, or device integrity and security. Norm B is a regulatory incident-reporting regime involving early warnings, incident reports, interim updates, and final reports to cybersecurity authorities, with specified deadlines and detailed content.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties do not impose the same core action on the same actor role: Norm A concerns provider-to-subscriber notice of a protective access-service measure, while Norm B concerns regulated-entity-to-CSIRT/competent-authority reporting of a significant incident. The shared security context and broad communication element are insufficient because the recipients, purposes, reporting content, and procedural duties materially differ.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Beide normen vereisen dat een entiteit een incident aan een bevoegde autoriteit meldt, maar norm A betreft een onverwijlde vroegtijdige waarschuwing naast een CSIRT-melding, terwijl norm B een eerste kennisgeving en verdere incidentrapportages aan de relevante financiële toezichthouder vereist.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A ziet op essentiële of belangrijke entiteiten en een vroegtijdige waarschuwing over een significant incident binnen 24 uur aan zowel CSIRT als bevoegde autoriteit. Norm B ziet op financiële entiteiten en vereist een eerste kennisgeving, tussentijdse/geactualiseerde rapportages en een eindverslag over een ernstig ICT-gerelateerd incident, met inhoud gericht op de omvang en grensoverschrijdende effecten van het incident.
verdict.criterion_fired: De actorcategorieën en wettelijke regimes verschillen wezenlijk: norm A legt de plicht op aan essentiële of belangrijke entiteiten onder het NIS2-kader, terwijl norm B financiële entiteiten onder DORA betreft. Bovendien verschillen de rapportage-inhoud en rapportagecyclus wezenlijk: een vroege waarschuwing binnen 24 uur tegenover een reeks financiële incidentrapporten met eerste, tussentijdse en eindrapportage.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit geeft ten behoeve van de melding, bedoeld in artikel 27, eerste lid, een vroegtijdige waarschuwing over het significante incident aan haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Norm A requires domain-name registries and registration-service entities to collect and maintain accurate, complete domain-registration data, with policies and verification procedures. Norm B governs and restricts the further processing of lawfully collected personal data in an AI regulatory sandbox, including safeguards, deletion, logging, documentation, and publication requirements.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A concerns maintaining a domain-registration database; Norm B concerns conditions and safeguards for processing personal data to develop, train, and test certain AI systems in a regulatory sandbox.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms impose different verb-level duties on different operational activities and do not concern the same triggering event or compliance work. A is a data-collection and database-maintenance obligation for domain-name registries and registration-service entities; B is a conditional data-processing regime for AI sandbox activities, including safeguards and documentation/publication requirements.

verdict.distinguishing_factor: The norms concern fundamentally different actions and subject matter: appointment of an authorised representative for specified manufacturer obligations versus disclosure of a GDPR processing-activities register to a supervisory authority.
verdict.criterion_fired: Different core action, event family, and actor role; no duplicated compliance work is apparent.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms regulate handling or movement of personal data, but Norm A requires the controller to inform the supervisory authority and the data subject about a transfer to a third country or international organisation, whereas Norm B prohibits sharing personal data created in the AI regulatory sandbox outside that sandbox and imposes broader processing safeguards.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an exceptional international-transfer notification duty; Norm B is a containment and governance requirement for personal-data processing in an AI regulatory sandbox.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms do not impose the same verb-level action or address the same triggering event: A concerns an exceptional third-country/international-organisation transfer and notification, while B concerns further processing and prohibition of sharing data outside an AI test environment.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require making information available to another party: A requires public disclosure of non-personal domain-registration data, while B requires providing the processing-activities register to a supervisory authority upon request.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an automatic, immediate public-disclosure duty concerning non-personal domain-registration data after domain registration; Norm B is a request-based duty to make a processing-activities register available to a supervisory authority.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties concern different actors, different triggering events, different recipients, and materially different information: public domain-registration data versus a processing-activities register supplied to a supervisory authority.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require making information and technical documentation available to a public authority on request to support or assess regulatory conformity. However, Norm A imposes this duty on an appointed representative for devices/radio equipment, while Norm B imposes it on importers of high-risk AI systems and includes a broader, reasoned-request information package in an understandable language.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: The duties concern different regulated products and different responsible actor roles: an appointed representative under the radio-equipment regime versus an importer under the AI Act. Norm B also expressly requires provision of all necessary information and documentation, including specified additional material, and availability of technical documentation to the authorities.
verdict.criterion_fired: The actor role is different and the norms regulate different product/compliance regimes; the overlap in authority-requested conformity documentation is not enough to make them the same duty.

verdict.criterion_fired: The duties concern different actors, different subject matter, and different compliance actions: representative appointment versus preparation and updating of technical documentation.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms involve an entity maintaining or supplying information, but they do not impose the same underlying compliance action: Norm A requires domain-name registration service providers to provide specified entity and service information to the central contact point for the ENISA register; Norm B requires providers of high-risk AI systems to document, in a processing register, why processing special-category personal data was strictly necessary to detect bias and why other data would not suffice.

verdict.criterion_fired: The duties concern different actors, different subject matter and purposes, and different compliance actions: registry information submission versus internal justification and safeguards for exceptional processing of special-category personal data.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both concern handling ICT/security incidents, but Norm A requires staged external incident reporting with substantive incident information, whereas Norm B requires internal registration of incidents and cyber threats as part of an ICT-incident management process.

verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in core action, actor scope, recipient/purpose, and required content: external staged reporting of significant incidents versus internal registration of all ICT-related incidents and significant cyber threats.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern handling information related to digital-domain or ICT events, but Norm A requires providing specific domain-registration data in response to a lawful, justified request, whereas Norm B requires financial entities to register ICT-related incidents and significant cyber threats and establish incident-management processes.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an access/disclosure duty triggered by a request from a legitimate party; Norm B is an internal incident-recording and management duty triggered by ICT incidents or significant cyber threats.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern organizational responses to ICT/AI-related risks or incidents, but they do not impose the same concrete action: Norm A requires financial entities to establish and maintain a broad ICT-risk-management and protection framework, while Norm B requires an AI provider, after a serious incident has been reported, to investigate it, assess its risks, take corrective measures, and cooperate with authorities or a notified body.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a standing preventive and governance obligation covering policies, controls, infrastructure, access, authentication, change management, and patching. Norm B is a post-incident investigation, remediation, and cooperation obligation for an AI provider.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in core action, triggering event, and actor role: Norm A imposes ongoing preventive ICT-security measures on financial entities; Norm B imposes post-serious-incident investigation, corrective-action, and cooperation duties on AI providers.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms involve providing information in connection with a legally significant situation, but they do not require the same underlying compliance work: A requires a telecommunications party, on ministerial request, to investigate a controller's identity and relationships (and provide a register extract), whereas B requires a controller to inform the supervisory authority and the data subject about an exceptional third-country transfer and its compelling legitimate interests.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a ministerial-requested investigation/information-production duty concerning control over a telecommunications entity and a possible threat to the public interest; Norm B is a GDPR derogation and notification duty concerning an exceptional international personal-data transfer, including information to both the supervisory authority and the data subject.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in actor role, triggering event, and substantive action/content; the superficial presence of an information-related verb does not make them the same reporting or investigative obligation.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms impose an operational compliance duty on a regulated actor, but the duties are fundamentally different: Norm A requires broad cooperation with military authorities, including carrying out their orders; Norm B requires retention of automatically generated high-risk AI-system logs under the provider’s control for at least six months.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an authority-directed cooperation/assistance duty triggered by application of the Dutch War Act, whereas Norm B is a record-retention duty concerning AI logs, with a minimum six-month retention period.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern organizational responses to ICT/AI-related risks or incidents, but Norm A requires implementing documented preventive security policies, procedures, and controls, whereas Norm B requires an urgent post-incident investigation, risk assessment, corrective measures, and cooperation with authorities.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a standing preventive ICT-risk-management and security-control obligation for financial entities; Norm B is an incident-triggered investigation and cooperation obligation for providers of high-risk AI systems following a serious-incident report.
verdict.criterion_fired: The underlying action, triggering event, and regulated actor differ: Norm A requires financial entities to implement preventive policies/procedures/controls, while Norm B requires AI providers to investigate a serious incident urgently and cooperate with authorities.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both provisions concern handling or supplying information/data, but they impose materially different duties: Norm A requires specified entities to provide identifying and network/service information to a central contact point for the ENISA register; Norm B regulates the further processing, sharing, safeguarding, retention, logging, documentation, and publication of personal data in an AI regulatory sandbox.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a mandatory information-supply duty to a central authority for registry purposes. Norm B is a set of conditions governing further processing of previously collected personal data for AI-system development, including restrictions on sharing and publication; it is not a duty to provide the same information to the same type of authority.
verdict.criterion_fired: The provisions do not impose the same underlying action, concern the same triggering event, or assign the same role-based duty. Norm A requires registry information to be supplied to a central contact point, whereas Norm B governs permissible further processing and related safeguards for personal data in an AI test environment.

verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a request-based interim update within the NIS2 incident-reporting process; Norm B is the DORA reporting regime for financial entities, with prescribed initial, interim, and final reports and specified incident-assessment content.
verdict.criterion_fired: The actor role is not the same: Norm A applies to essential or important entities, while Norm B applies to financial entities. verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern responding to security-related risks or incidents affecting network, information-system, service, or device security, but A requires preventive/risk-management measures while B requires advance or prompt notice to an affected subscriber and an opportunity to remedy a threat before a provider takes a specified measure.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both concern reporting an ICT/significant incident to a CSIRT, but Norm A requires a structured, multi-stage significant-incident reporting package, while Norm B requires the relevant financial-sector entities to make the Article 19 mandatory or voluntary ICT-incident report additionally to the designated sectoral CSIRT.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A covers the full NIS2 significant-incident reporting sequence and detailed content (early warning, incident notification, updates, interim and final reports) for affected entities generally; Norm B is a Dutch additional-recipient rule for specified financial entities and refers to the separate DORA Article 19 mandatory/voluntary reporting regime.
verdict.criterion_fired: Same reporting action, incident family, and actor role, but the provisions do not establish that the same report or identical content must be submitted twice; Norm B incorporates a separate Article 19 reporting duty and adds a sectoral CSIRT recipient, while Norm A specifies a broader NIS2 reporting sequence and content.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require an entity to respond to a justified request by making information available to the requesting authority or legitimate requester. However, Norm A concerns access to specific domain-name registration data, while Norm B concerns supplying all necessary information and documentation to substantiate conformity of a high-risk AI system, including access to technical documentation.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: The duties concern different substantive information, different regulatory purposes, and different obligated actors: domain-name registries/registration-service providers under Norm A versus importers of high-risk AI systems under Norm B.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms do not impose the same duty because they concern different actor roles and different substantive regulatory events/purposes: domain-name registration-data access requests versus requests for high-risk AI conformity information and technical documentation.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms involve submitting or making a notification to an external body, but they concern different substantive duties: a fundamental-rights-impact-assessment result and template under the AI Act versus an ICT-incident notification under the financial-sector cybersecurity regime.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires a user/deployer of certain high-risk AI systems to notify the market-surveillance authority of the results of a completed fundamental-rights impact assessment and include a completed template. Norm B requires specified financial-sector entities to make an ICT-incident notification (including a voluntary notification) additionally to the designated sectoral CSIRT.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in the underlying action's substantive purpose and triggering event: Norm A concerns reporting an AI fundamental-rights impact assessment before use of certain high-risk AI systems, while Norm B concerns reporting ICT incidents by specified financial entities. The shared notification form and broad authority/addressee category do not make the compliance work the same.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Norm A imposes liability for damage caused by unlawful processing; Norm B imposes multiple incident-reporting duties concerning a significant incident, including warnings, incident reports, interim updates, and final reports.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a substantive civil-liability/allocation-of-loss rule triggered by unlawful processing and resulting damage, whereas Norm B is a procedural cybersecurity incident-reporting regime triggered by knowledge of a significant incident and requiring specified reports to a CSIRT or competent authority.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in core action, triggering event, and legal purpose: liability for damage from unlawful processing versus reporting a significant cybersecurity incident to an authority.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require an entity to promptly inform potentially affected customers/service recipients about protective or mitigating measures in response to a significant cyber threat or ICT-related incident. Norm B additionally requires notification of the serious ICT-related incident itself and measures already taken to mitigate its negative effects; Norm A is framed around communicating measures the recipients can take, with possible notification of the threat itself.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm B covers financial entities notifying clients about serious ICT-related incidents affecting clients’ financial interests, including the incident and mitigation measures, and separately covers significant cyber threats. Norm A covers essential and important entities informing recipients of their services about measures those recipients can take in response to a potentially affecting significant cyber threat, with threat notification only if necessary.
verdict.criterion_fired: Same actor role and broadly overlapping cyber-threat/incident communication duty, but the required information and purpose are not near-identical: A focuses on recipient-facing protective measures (and possibly the threat), whereas B requires incident notification and entity-taken mitigation measures, with a separate threat-related protective-measures limb.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both provisions concern regulatory oversight involving information or representation, but they do not impose the same underlying compliance action: Norm A requires appointing an EU representative, while Norm B empowers the lead overseer to investigate and obtain information/materials.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a substantive designation duty imposed on certain non-EU essential or important entities offering services in the Netherlands; Norm B is an investigative power of the lead overseer concerning critical third-party ICT service providers.
verdict.criterion_fired: Different core action, event/subject matter, and actor role; no duplicated compliance work is established.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern addressing a potential risk-related condition, but Norm A requires implementing preventive/mitigating security measures, whereas Norm B requires the provider to notify the European Commission and substantiate that an AI-model threshold is met.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an ongoing risk-management and incident-prevention duty for network and information systems; Norm B is a specific notification duty triggered by an AI model meeting, or being known likely to meet, the Article 51(1)(a) condition.
verdict.criterion_fired: The underlying action, triggering condition, and regulated actor differ: Norm A requires an essential or important entity to take technical, operational, and organisational security measures, while Norm B requires an AI provider to notify the Commission and provide substantiating information.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms involve making a notification/report, but they require notifications for materially different purposes and events: advance notice of cable-maintenance works versus notification of a serious AI-system incident.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A concerns planned physical works on public land and requires advance notice to the local mayor or authorised official; Norm B concerns a serious incident causally linked, or potentially linked, to an AI system and requires prompt incident reporting within a maximum period.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties concern different triggering-event families and different responsible actor roles; the shared reporting verb and broadly public-authority addressee are insufficient to establish duplicated compliance work.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require a regulated entity to provide information or access to information upon an external request. However, Norm A concerns access to specific domain-name registration data for a legitimate party, while Norm B concerns supplying a corporate-register extract to the Minister and, alternatively, conducting an ownership-control investigation.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: The duties concern different subject matter, purposes, and requesting parties: domain-name registration-data access for a legitimate requester versus national-security/public-interest oversight of controlling ownership for the Minister.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms do not impose the same underlying duty: Norm A is a domain-name data-access obligation triggered by a lawful, duly reasoned request, whereas Norm B is a telecommunications-party obligation triggered by suspected or actual predominant control threatening the public interest and requires either a free register extract or an investigation into the controller's identity and affiliations.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both provisions concern the manufacturer/provider taking a compliance-related organizational or conformity step, but they do not require the same underlying work: A permits appointment of an authorized representative, while B requires selection and, in specified cases, following a high-risk AI conformity-assessment procedure.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an optional written appointment of an authorized representative, expressly excluding certain obligations; Norm B is a substantive conformity-assessment procedure for high-risk AI systems, potentially involving quality-management and technical-documentation assessment by a notified body.
verdict.criterion_fired: The provisions impose different core actions on different regulated roles in different regulatory contexts: appointment of an authorized representative versus conformity assessment of a high-risk AI system.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A requires the controller to conduct a review to assess whether processing is carried out in accordance with the data-protection impact assessment when processing risks change; B requires financial entities to establish and maintain a broad ICT-risk-management and protection framework, including documented patch and update policies.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: A is a conditional review of processing against a DPIA triggered by a change in processing risk; B is a standing set of ICT-security governance, prevention, access, authentication, change-management, network-segmentation, and patch/update measures.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms do not impose the same core action or address the same event family: A concerns reviewing processing against a DPIA after a change in processing risk, while B concerns ongoing ICT-security and risk-management measures for financial entities. The apparent similarity based on risk/security context does not establish duplicated compliance work.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both provisions concern technical documentation in the broader conformity/compliance context, but they do not impose the same action: Norm A permits appointing an authorised representative while expressly excluding the obligation to prepare technical documentation; Norm B requires the provider of a high-risk AI system to prepare and update technical documentation.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a rule about the scope and limits of appointing an authorised representative; Norm B is a substantive documentation duty for high-risk AI systems, including timing, conformity-demonstration purpose, and minimum contents.
verdict.criterion_fired: The provisions do not impose the same verb-level duty, do not concern the same triggering event, and do not clearly bind the same actor role. Norm A concerns a manufacturer's appointment of an authorised representative and excludes delegation of specified technical-documentation obligations; Norm B requires preparation and updating of high-risk-AI technical documentation before placing on the market or putting into service.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require the regulated entity to create or maintain compliance-related information/documentation, but they do not require the same underlying compliance work: Norm A requires supplying entity-identification and contact information to competent authorities, including prompt updates; Norm B requires preparing and updating technical documentation for a high-risk AI system to demonstrate conformity and support conformity assessment.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A concerns registration/listing information about the entity and changes to that information; Norm B concerns substantive technical documentation about a high-risk AI system and its conformity with applicable requirements.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in actor role, subject matter, purpose, and content. Norm A applies to entities covered by the NIS2 listing mechanism and requires information to be provided to competent authorities, with changes reported within two weeks. Norm B applies to providers of high-risk AI systems and requires technical documentation to be prepared before placing the system on the market or putting it into service and kept updated. The shared broad idea of producing information/documentation is insufficient to establish duplicate compliance work.

verdict.evidence_span_b: De technische documentatie van een AI-systeem met een hoog risico wordt opgesteld voordat dit systeem in de handel wordt gebracht of in gebruik wordt gesteld, en wordt geactualiseerd.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both provisions concern appointing/using an EU-based representative or authorised representative for regulatory compliance, but they impose materially different duties: A requires certain non-EU entities offering services in the Netherlands to appoint a representative; B specifies the authorised representative’s AI Act tasks, including checking the provider’s technical documentation and compliance, retaining documentation, supplying information on request, and cooperating with authorities.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an appointment requirement for specified non-EU digital-service entities lacking an EU representative. Norm B governs the functions of an already appointed authorised representative for providers of general-purpose AI models, including documentation retention, information production, and cooperation with authorities.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms do not impose the same underlying action on the same actor role in response to the same event. A requires appointment of a representative; B imposes substantive verification, retention, disclosure, and cooperation duties on an authorised representative for general-purpose AI providers.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both concern communicating information about a serious/significant ICT-related event, but A requires an incident report to cybersecurity authorities, while B requires crisis-communication capability for responsible disclosure to clients, counterparties, and potentially the public.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an actual, time-bound incident notification duty to a CSIRT and competent authority, including specified incident-assessment and cross-border-impact information. Norm B is a preventive ICT-risk-management requirement to maintain crisis-communication plans enabling outward disclosure to clients, counterparties, and possibly the public; it specifies no incident-report deadline or equivalent information package.
verdict.criterion_fired: Same broad ICT-incident event family and same regulated-entity role, but the duties differ in core action, recipients, purpose, timing, and required content; therefore this is related compliance work rather than the same reporting work repeated.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A requires informing service recipients about a significant cyber threat and the measures they can take; B requires the AI provider, after reporting a serious incident, to investigate it and the AI system, including a risk assessment and corrective measures, while cooperating with authorities and observing a restriction on modifying the system during the investigation.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: A is an outward-facing warning/information duty to potentially affected service recipients. B is a post-incident investigation, risk-assessment, remediation, cooperation, and procedural-preservation duty; it does not require the same communication to recipients.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in both the core action and actor role: A requires an essential or important entity to inform service recipients about a significant cyber threat and possible protective measures, whereas B requires an AI provider to investigate a serious incident and undertake risk assessment and corrective measures.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms impose ongoing organisational/compliance obligations on regulated providers, but A requires supplying entity-identification and registration information to a central contact point, whereas B requires maintaining a quality-management system (among other AI-provider duties).
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an information-submission duty for specified essential or important digital-service entities, with the information defined in Article 47(3); Norm B is a substantive quality-management-system obligation for providers of high-risk AI systems.
verdict.criterion_fired: Different underlying action, regulated actor category, and compliance purpose; the apparent similarity is only that both address regulated providers and compliance obligations.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both provisions involve information being communicated or obtained in a regulatory context, but Norm A imposes a controller's duty to inform the supervisory authority (and the data subject) about an exceptional international data transfer, whereas Norm B empowers the lead overseer to summon critical ICT third-party-provider representatives and request oral or written explanations during an investigation.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a substantive notification duty triggered by a specific exceptional personal-data transfer; Norm B is an investigative power concerning explanations about facts or documents, not a duty on the same actor to make a transfer notification.
verdict.criterion_fired: The underlying action, triggering event, and duty-bearing actor differ: Norm A requires the data controller to inform the supervisory authority and data subject about a qualifying transfer, while Norm B authorizes a lead overseer to obtain explanations from representatives of critical ICT third-party providers in an investigation.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De verwerkingsverantwoordelijke informeert de toezichthoudende autoriteit over de doorgifte. De verwerkingsverantwoordelijke informeert de betrokkene

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms involve communicating information about a security-related situation or measure, but they require different communications: A requires an interim update report within an existing incident notification process, on request; B requires the provider to notify the affected subscriber about a contemplated or urgently implemented measure and give the subscriber an opportunity to remedy a network, service, or device integrity/security threat.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an authority/CSIRT-facing interim incident update by an essential or important entity; Norm B is a subscriber-facing warning or notice by a provider concerning a protective measure, including an opportunity for the subscriber to remove the threat.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties do not impose the same compliance work: the actor roles differ, the recipients differ, and the required content and purpose differ. A concerns relevant updates to an incident situation; B concerns notice of a specific measure and, ordinarily, an opportunity for the subscriber to remedy a threat. The shared security-related context is insufficient to establish duplicate burden.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms involve compliance activity connected with an ICT/security incident, but A requires including specified incident characteristics and a responsible officer’s contact details in an early warning, whereas B requires documenting and evaluating the ICT-risk-management framework, continuously improving it, and submitting an evaluation report on request.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an incident-warning content obligation; Norm B is a risk-management-framework documentation, evaluation, improvement, and on-request reporting obligation.
verdict.criterion_fired: Same incident-related context and broadly comparable regulated-entity role, but the required work and purpose differ: A supplies early-warning incident information, while B documents/evaluates and improves the risk-management framework and may submit an evaluation report on request. verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms impose a substantive restriction on conduct: they require the addressee to refrain from, or limit, specified activities. However, the underlying prohibited/restricted conduct is materially different: Norm A requires financial entities to restrict access to ICT assets to legitimate and approved functions, while Norm B prohibits placing on the market, putting into service, or using specified AI systems for biometric categorisation.

verdict.criterion_fired: The norms do not concern the same core action, triggering event, or actor role. Norm A concerns implementing and maintaining access-control policies and controls for ICT assets; Norm B concerns prohibiting specified AI-system conduct. The apparent similarity is not a repeated reporting or compliance obligation.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A requires covered digital-service entities to provide identification and registration information to the central contact point for the ENISA register. B requires high-risk AI-system providers to retain automatically generated system logs under their control for at least six months. These are different underlying compliance actions.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both provisions concern the appointment/mandate and functions of an authorised representative, but A permits appointment while expressly excluding certain manufacturer obligations; B specifies the authorised representative’s duties, including maintaining and supplying technical documentation and cooperating with authorities.

verdict.criterion_fired: The provisions do not impose the same underlying action on the same actor role: A concerns a manufacturer appointing a representative and limits what may be delegated; B concerns an AI-model provider’s representative performing specified regulatory tasks, including a ten-year document-retention duty and responding to the AI Office or authorities.

verdict.criterion_fired: Same incident-related context and actor role, but different core actions and low content overlap: contact details for the incident-reporting officer versus documentation/evaluation and an evaluation report concerning the ICT-risk-management framework.

verdict.criterion_fired: The duties concern different regulated events, different substantive actions, and different actor roles: an exceptional international data transfer by a controller versus exceptional special-category-data processing by a high-risk AI provider.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A requires entities, when selecting supply-chain security measures, to take account of supplier/service-provider vulnerabilities, overall supplier security quality and secure development practices, and coordinated critical-supply-chain risk-assessment results. verdict.criterion_fired: The norms do not impose the same underlying action: A concerns considering supplier and critical-supply-chain risk-assessment results when choosing measures; B concerns implementing and documenting a broad set of ICT-risk-management and preventive security controls. They also address different regulated actor categories and no reporting recipient or deadline is specified.

Norm A is a controller/processor substantiation duty tied to an exceptional international data transfer and registration; Norm B is a set of operational conditions governing AI-sandbox processing, with no equivalent reporting or register duty.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern communicating information about a cyber/ICT-related event, but A requires an interim update report to a CSIRT or competent authority on request, whereas B requires financial entities to inform clients without delay about a serious ICT incident and mitigation measures, or about protective measures in response to a significant cyber threat.

verdict.criterion_fired: The duties do not impose the same core action on the same actor role: A concerns an essential or important entity reporting relevant situation updates to its CSIRT or competent authority on request, while B concerns financial entities notifying clients about an incident, mitigation measures, or protective measures. verdict.criterion_fired: The duties concern different actors, different triggering contexts, different objects of compliance, and different core actions; any superficial similarity as digital-record obligations does not create duplicated compliance work.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern obligations of a manufacturer/provider connected with placing or supplying a regulated product or system on the market, but they do not require the same compliance action. verdict.shared_compliance_action: Norm A permits a manufacturer to appoint an authorised representative in writing, while Norm B determines which Member State has jurisdiction over covered entities and, in certain cases, requires designation of an EU representative. Norm A requires financial entities to establish procedures and processes for monitoring, handling, and following up ICT-related incidents, including registration and root-cause remediation. Norm B requires notified bodies to inform the notifying authority about specified conformity-assessment matters and, on request, provide information about their activities.

verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in core action, triggering subject matter, and actor role: Norm A concerns internal management of ICT-related incidents by financial entities, while Norm B concerns notifying an authority about conformity-assessment matters by notified bodies.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern regulated ICT/AI-system governance, but A concerns the contents of an investigation authorisation and possible coercive fines, whereas B requires retention of automatically generated logs.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A governs an overseer's investigation authorisation and the consequences of failing to provide requested material; Norm B imposes a substantive log-retention duty on high-risk AI-system providers.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms do not impose the same underlying action: A concerns stating possible coercive fines in an investigation mandate, while B requires retaining logs for at least six months. They also concern different triggering situations and duty-bearer roles.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both require an interim report/update concerning an ICT or cybersecurity incident, submitted to a competent authority (and, for Norm A, potentially also to a CSIRT), within an incident-reporting process. Norm B additionally forms part of a broader mandatory sequence of initial, interim/updated, and final reports.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires an interim report on relevant situation updates only when requested by the CSIRT or competent authority, whereas Norm B mandates financial entities to submit a structured interim report after an initial notification when the incident status or handling materially changes, with further updates and a final report under specified conditions.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties do not bind the same actor category: Norm A applies to essential or important entities under the NIS2 framework, while Norm B applies to financial entities under DORA. Although both concern interim incident reporting to a competent authority and overlap in subject matter, the distinct regulated populations and reporting regimes mean the texts do not establish the same compliance duty for the same actor.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A requires the affected party to comply with a suspension; B requires the AI provider, after reporting a serious incident, to promptly investigate it and the AI system, including risk assessment and corrective measures, while cooperating with authorities and giving prior notice before certain system-changing investigations.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: The norms concern fundamentally different measures: compliance with a suspension versus post-incident investigation, risk assessment, corrective action, and procedural cooperation/notice.
verdict.criterion_fired: Different core action, triggering context, and actor role; the apparent similarity does not establish overlapping compliance work.

verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in actor scope, recipient, purpose, and substantive content: A concerns essential and important entities warning potentially affected service recipients, while B concerns financial entities reporting serious ICT-related incidents to a competent authority. verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms impose multiple obligations on covered providers, but they do not impose the same underlying compliance action: Norm A requires supplying specified entity-registration information to the Dutch central contact point for the ENISA register, whereas Norm B requires high-risk AI providers to take corrective measures and provide information required under Article 20, among other AI-compliance duties.

Similarity of provider/addressee terminology does not establish the same compliance work.

verdict.criterion_fired: Same actor role and broadly related cyber/ICT-incident trigger, but the required actions, recipients, purposes, and substantive content differ; this is not the same reporting or information work repeated.

Similarity in the broad idea of using information does not create the same compliance work.
