verdict.shared_compliance_action: Beide normen houden verband met het verstrekken van informatie aan een bevoegde autoriteit, maar norm A betreft identificatie- en registratiegegevens van essentiële/belangrijke entiteiten, terwijl norm B betreft het bijhouden en op verzoek verstrekken van een ICT-contractueel informatieregister door financiële entiteiten.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A ziet op initiële en gewijzigde entiteitsgegevens voor de nationale lijst; norm B ziet op ICT-dienstverleningscontracten, jaarlijkse rapportage en toezichtsinformatie van financiële entiteiten.
verdict.criterion_fired: De actorrol en het voorwerp van de informatieplicht verschillen wezenlijk: norm A betreft entiteiten die voor een cyberbeveiligingslijst relevante identificatiegegevens verstrekken, terwijl norm B financiële entiteiten verplicht een ICT-contractenregister te rapporteren of op verzoek beschikbaar te stellen. De gedeelde autoriteit en het algemene werkwoord 'informatie verstrekken' maken de verplichtingen niet dezelfde.
verdict.evidence_span_a: de in dat lid bedoelde entiteiten dat zij ten minste de volgende informatie aan de bevoegde autoriteiten verstrekken
verdict.evidence_span_b: Financiële entiteiten stellen de bevoegde autoriteit op verzoek het volledige informatieregister of desgevraagd specifieke onderdelen daarvan ter beschikking

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A requires affected entities to report significant incidents through early warnings, incident notifications, interim/progress reports, and final reports to the CSIRT or competent authority. B requires the ICT-risk-management framework to be periodically and incident-triggeredly documented and evaluated, with an evaluation report submitted to the competent authority on request.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: A is an incident-reporting and notification duty concerning the incident itself, its severity, effects, cause, indicators, and mitigation measures. B is an ICT-risk-management governance duty concerning documentation and evaluation of the entity’s risk-management framework and its continuous improvement; any report is an evaluation report, not an incident report.
verdict.criterion_fired: Same significant/serious ICT-incident family and broadly the same regulated-entity role, but different core actions and substantially different content and purpose: incident reporting under A versus documenting/evaluating the ICT-risk-management framework under B. The different authority-facing outputs do not make the duties different by themselves, but the low content overlap prevents a duplicate-burden finding.
verdict.evidence_span_a: onverwijld en in elk geval binnen 24 uur nadat zij kennis hebben gekregen van het significante incident, een vroegtijdige waarschuwing geven
verdict.evidence_span_b: bij ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incidenten gedocumenteerd en geëvalueerd

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms impose an affirmative compliance duty on a regulated entity, but the duties differ: Norm A requires designation of an EU representative, while Norm B requires a notified body to inform its notifying authority about specified conformity-assessment matters.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A concerns appointing an EU representative based on establishment and service-location conditions; Norm B concerns information reporting by notified bodies to their notifying authority about certificates, approvals, changes affecting notification, requests, and activities.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in core action, triggering circumstances, actor role, recipient relationship, and substantive content; the apparent similarity as affirmative obligations imposed on regulated entities is insufficient for duplicate burden.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A requires continuous incorporation of lessons from ICT resilience tests and real-world ICT incidents into ICT-risk assessment and subsequent revision of the ICT-risk-management framework; B prohibits or strictly conditions specified uses of AI systems, including real-time remote biometric identification in public spaces for law enforcement, with authorization, impact-assessment, registration, and deletion safeguards.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: A is an internal ICT-risk-management learning and remediation duty triggered by tests and real-world ICT incidents. B is a substantive prohibition and authorization regime governing particular AI uses, especially real-time remote biometric identification for law enforcement.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms do not impose the same underlying action: A requires continuous internal risk-assessment and framework revision based on lessons from ICT incidents and tests, whereas B prohibits or regulates specified AI-system uses and requires authorization and related safeguards. They also concern different triggering-event families and actor roles.
verdict.evidence_span_a: In het ICT-risicobeoordelingsproces wordt voortdurend naar behoren rekening gehouden met lessen die voortspruiten uit de overeenkomstig de artikelen 26 en 27 uitgevoerde tests op de digitale operationele weerbaarheid en uit ICT-gerelateerde incidenten die zich in het reële leven hebben voorgedaan

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Beide normen leggen een actieve compliancehandeling op aan een gereguleerde actor: A vereist dat een telecommunicatiepartij op verzoek informatie verstrekt of onderzoek doet; B vereist dat een aanbieder een conformiteitsbeoordelingsprocedure kiest en volgt voor een hoog-risico-AI-systeem.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: De normen zien op wezenlijk verschillende onderwerpen en compliance-doelen: A betreft informatieverstrekking/identiteitsonderzoek naar zeggenschap over een telecommunicatiepartij ten behoeve van de minister; B betreft de keuze en uitvoering van een conformiteitsbeoordelingsprocedure voor een hoog-risico-AI-systeem.
verdict.criterion_fired: Verschillende kernhandelingen, verschillende triggering contexten en verschillende actorrollen; de overeenkomst is slechts dat beide een gereguleerde partij tot een actieve compliancehandeling verplichten.

verdict.evidence_span_b: kiest de aanbieder ... een van de volgende conformiteitsbeoordelingsprocedures

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A vereist het bijhouden van een register van verwerkingsactiviteiten met voorgeschreven inhoud; B vereist dat aangemelde instanties de aanmeldende autoriteit informeren over certificaten, wijzigingen in hun aanmelding, ontvangen informatieverzoeken en conformiteitsbeoordelingsactiviteiten.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: De normen betreffen wezenlijk verschillende verplichtingen: een doorlopende interne documentatieplicht over persoonsgegevensverwerking tegenover een informatieplicht aan een aanmeldende autoriteit over conformiteitsbeoordeling en de status/activiteiten van een aangemelde instantie.
verdict.criterion_fired: Verschillende actorrollen en verschillende kernhandelingen: A betreft registerhouden/documenteren door een verwerkingsverantwoordelijke; B betreft melden/informeren van een aanmeldende autoriteit door een aangemelde instantie.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Elke verwerkingsverantwoordelijke en, in voorkomend geval, de vertegenwoordiger van de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke houdt een register van de verwerkingsactiviteiten die onder hun verantwoordelijkheid plaatsvinden.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both require the responsible entity to submit information to a public authority, but A requires incident reporting while B requires notification of the results of a fundamental-rights impact assessment together with a completed template.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A concerns reporting a significant cybersecurity incident, including incident severity, effects, compromise indicators, and possible cross-border consequences, to the CSIRT and competent authority. Norm B concerns notifying the market-surveillance authority of the results of a pre-deployment fundamental-rights impact assessment for a high-risk AI system and submitting a prescribed template.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties concern different triggering events, different responsible actors, and materially different information and regulatory purposes; the shared feature of notifying a public authority is insufficient to establish duplicate compliance work.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit dient onverwijld of, indien dat niet mogelijk is, binnen 72 uur nadat zij kennis heeft gekregen van het significante incident een melding in bij haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit
verdict.evidence_span_b: stelt de gebruiksverantwoordelijke de markttoezichtautoriteit in kennis van de resultaten ervan, en dient hij als onderdeel van de kennisgeving het in lid 5 van dit artikel bedoelde ingevulde sjabloon in

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Beide normen leggen geen identieke rapportage- of informatieverstrekkingsplicht op. Norm A betreft het beschikbaar houden en op verzoek verstrekken van conformiteitsdocumentatie en medewerking aan risicobeperkende maatregelen; norm B betreft voorwaarden voor verwerking in een AI-testomgeving, waaronder wissen van persoonsgegevens, logging, technische bescherming, documentatie en publicatie.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is een gemachtigdenplicht tegenover de bevoegde minister inzake conformiteitscontrole van apparaten/radioapparaten. Norm B is een gegevensverwerkingsregime voor AI-testomgevingen, met verplichtingen rond persoonsgegevens, beveiliging, bewaring en transparantie.
verdict.criterion_fired: De normen hebben niet dezelfde kernhandeling, actorrol of gebeurtenisfamilie. A ziet op conformiteitsdocumentatie en medewerking aan toezicht/maatregelen; B ziet op rechtmatige verdere verwerking van persoonsgegevens in een AI-testomgeving en bijbehorende waarborgen.
verdict.evidence_span_a: het ter beschikking van Onze Minister houden van de EU-conformiteitsverklaring en de technische documentatie gedurende tien jaar nadat het apparaat of het radioapparaat in de handel is gebracht
verdict.evidence_span_b: in het kader van de testomgeving verwerkte persoonsgegevens worden beschermd met passende technische en organisatorische maatregelen en worden gewist nadat de deelname aan de testomgeving is beëindigd of de periode van bewaring van de persoonsgegevens ten einde is gekomen

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Geen gedeelde compliance-actie: norm A verleent de lead overseer onderzoeksbevoegdheden om telefoon- en dataverkeersoverzichten op te vragen; norm B verplicht de aanbieder een conformiteitsbeoordelingsprocedure te volgen voor bepaalde hoog-risico-AI-systemen.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A betreft een toezichts- en onderzoeksbevoegdheid van een autoriteit; norm B betreft de productconformiteitsbeoordeling die een aanbieder moet uitvoeren of laten uitvoeren.
verdict.criterion_fired: De normen verschillen zowel in kernactie als in actorrol en onderwerp: het opvragen van verkeersgegevens voor een onderzoek tegenover het volgen van een conformiteitsbeoordelingsprocedure voor hoog-risico-AI.
verdict.evidence_span_a: e) overzichten van telefoon- en dataverkeer op te vragen.
verdict.evidence_span_b: volgt de aanbieder de conformiteitsbeoordelingsprocedure van bijlage VII

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both require incident-related communications following a significant/serious ICT or cyber event, but A requires a structured regulatory incident-reporting sequence to the CSIRT or competent authority, while B requires prompt client notification about the incident and mitigation/protective measures.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an authority-facing, multi-stage report containing incident assessment, indicators, detailed description, cause/threat type, impacts, and mitigation measures; Norm B is a client-facing notification focused on informing clients of the incident and measures or protections relevant to them.
verdict.criterion_fired: Same incident family and actor role, but different core action, recipients, deadlines, purpose, and required content; the duties are related rather than the same reporting work repeated.
verdict.evidence_span_a: bij het CSIRT of, indien van toepassing, de bevoegde autoriteit ... een incidentmelding indienen met ... een initiële beoordeling van het significante incident, met inbegrip van de ernst en de gevolgen ervan en, indien beschikbaar, de indicatoren voor aantasting
verdict.evidence_span_b: stellen financiële entiteiten ... hun cliënten onverwijld in kennis van het ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incident en van de maatregelen die zijn genomen om de negatieve gevolgen van een dergelijk incident te beperken

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Geen gedeelde concrete compliance-actie: norm A verplicht aanbieders en frequentiegebruikers om op bevel van het militair gezag medewerking te verlenen en opdrachten uit te voeren; norm B regelt onder voorwaarden de verdere verwerking van persoonsgegevens in een AI-testomgeving, met onder meer beveiliging, logging, bewaring, verwijdering en publicatie.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A betreft verplichte medewerking aan militair gezag bij toepassing van de Oorlogswet; norm B betreft voorwaarden en waarborgen voor verwerking van persoonsgegevens bij de ontwikkeling, training en test van AI-systemen in het algemeen belang.
verdict.criterion_fired: De normen hebben noch dezelfde kernhandeling, noch dezelfde trigger of actorrol. Norm A ziet op het uitvoeren van opdrachten van militair gezag; norm B op rechtmatige verdere verwerking van persoonsgegevens in een AI-testomgeving en de daarbij horende waarborgen. Een vergelijkbare overheidscontext maakt dit niet tot dezelfde compliance-verplichting.
verdict.evidence_span_a: verplicht het militair gezag alle medewerking te verlenen, daaronder begrepen het uitvoeren van door dat gezag gegeven opdrachten
verdict.evidence_span_b: mogen rechtmatig voor andere doeleinden verzamelde persoonsgegevens uitsluitend worden verwerkt ten behoeve van het ontwikkelen, trainen en testen van bepaalde AI-systemen in de testomgeving indien aan alle volgende voorwaarden is voldaan

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern an essential or important entity taking action in response to a cyber incident/threat, but Norm A requires incident reporting to an authority (a progress report instead of a final report, followed by a final report), whereas Norm B requires communicating the significant cyber threat and possible protective measures to potentially affected service recipients.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an authority-facing incident-reporting duty concerning the incident's status and specified report aspects, with a deadline tied to incident handling. Norm B is a recipient-facing warning/information duty concerning the threat itself and measures recipients can take, triggered where recipients may be affected by a significant cyber threat.
verdict.criterion_fired: Same incident/threat family and same essential/important-entity actor role, but different core actions, recipients, purposes, and substantive content; therefore related compliance burden rather than repeated identical work.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Indien het incident nog voortduurt op het moment dat het eindverslag had moeten worden ingediend, dient de essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit op dat moment in plaats van een eindverslag een voortgangsverslag in
verdict.evidence_span_b: Indien nodig stellen de entiteiten die ontvangers ook in kennis van de significante cyberdreiging zelf.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Communicate incident-related information and mitigation/protective measures to affected clients/data subjects.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A concerns a personal-data breach and requires the data subject communication to contain a description of the breach's nature plus specified GDPR Article 33(3)(b)-(d) information and measures. Norm B concerns a serious ICT-related incident affecting clients' financial interests, or alternatively a significant cyber threat, and requires prompt notice of the incident and mitigation or protective measures.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern obtaining or making available information/material in connection with an authority’s information-access or investigative function, but A imposes a specific access-disclosure duty on domain-name registries/registrars, while B grants the lead overseer investigative powers to inspect relevant material.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both provisions concern obtaining or making available information/documentation in the context of regulatory oversight, but they do not impose the same underlying duty: Norm A imposes continuing duties on an appointed representative, while Norm B grants investigative powers to the lead overseer.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms involve an actor taking compliance action in connection with an ICT/network-security-related matter, but the actions are materially different: Norm A requires the provider to notify the affected subscriber before, or urgently after, taking a protective service measure; Norm B requires documentation and evaluation of an ICT-risk-management framework and submission of an evaluation report to the competent authority on request.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms involve communicating or documenting information concerning a legally relevant condition or incident for regulatory oversight, but they do not require the same underlying compliance action: GDPR Article 33 requires documenting personal-data breaches, whereas AI Act Article 52 requires a provider to notify the Commission that a general-purpose AI model meets a specified condition and to provide substantiating information.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern post-incident compliance involving investigation, evaluation, or learning from a serious ICT/AI-related incident, but they require different operational actions: Norm A requires periodic and incident-triggered documentation and evaluation of an ICT-risk-management framework, with an evaluation report supplied to the competent authority on request; Norm B requires the AI provider to promptly investigate the serious incident and AI system, conduct a risk assessment and corrective measures, cooperate with authorities, and give prior notice before certain system-altering investigative steps.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require an internal governance or risk-management response based on information about risks or adverse events: A requires continuously incorporating lessons from ICT tests and real-world ICT incidents into ICT-risk assessment and revising the ICT-risk-management framework; B requires a high-risk-AI deployer to update the fundamental-rights-impact-assessment information when relevant elements change or become outdated.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A concerns continuous ICT-risk-management learning and framework revision based especially on ICT incidents and resilience testing. Norm B concerns updating a fundamental-rights impact assessment for a high-risk AI system when assessment elements change or become outdated, in connection with the system’s use and before deployment for the initial assessment.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in actor scope, triggering event, and substantive action: A imposes continuous incorporation of lessons into ICT-risk assessment and revision of the ICT-risk-management framework, whereas B imposes updating a fundamental-rights impact assessment when specified elements change or become outdated. They do not require the same compliance work to be repeated.

verdict.criterion_fired: The norms do not impose the same verb-level action, concern different triggering circumstances, and regulate different actor roles and compliance purposes; any superficial similarity from public-interest or data-related language does not create duplicated compliance work.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both impose information-recording or information-provision duties, but A requires domain-name registration service entities to provide specified entity and service information to a central contact point, whereas B requires processors to maintain an internal register of processing activities and specified GDPR-related details.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an external submission to a central contact point for the ENISA register; Norm B is an internal record-keeping obligation concerning processing activities, with no recipient or deadline specified.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in actor role, triggering context, operational action, recipient, and substantive content: A concerns domain-name registration entities supplying registry information, while B concerns processors maintaining a processing-activities register.
verdict.evidence_span_a: verstrekken entiteiten die domeinnaamregistratiediensten verlenen aan het centrale contactpunt de informatie, bedoeld in het derde lid van dit artikel
verdict.evidence_span_b: De verwerker, en, in voorkomend geval, de vertegenwoordiger van de verwerker houdt een register van alle categorieën van verwerkingsactiviteiten die zij ten behoeve van een verwerkingsverantwoordelijke hebben verricht.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both provisions concern controls on processing or transferring personal data, but Norm A requires informing a supervisory authority about an exceptional international transfer, whereas Norm B imposes conditions and safeguards for processing personal data in an AI regulatory sandbox, including monitoring, isolation, retention/deletion, logging, documentation, and publication.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an authority-notification duty triggered by an exceptional transfer to a third country or international organisation; Norm B is a substantive data-processing compliance regime for AI-system development, training, and testing, with no comparable notification duty.
verdict.criterion_fired: The provisions do not impose the same core action or concern the same triggering event: A requires notifying a supervisory authority of an exceptional international data transfer, while B regulates safeguards and operational conditions for personal-data processing in an AI regulatory sandbox.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De verwerkingsverantwoordelijke informeert de toezichthoudende autoriteit over de doorgifte.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern obligations connected with handling information in a regulated digital-law context, but Norm A requires informing the supervisory authority and the data subject about an exceptional personal-data transfer, whereas Norm B requires high-risk AI providers to retain automatically generated logs for at least six months.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an exceptional international personal-data-transfer notification and documentation duty; Norm B is a prospective record-retention duty for high-risk AI logs.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in core action, triggering event, and actor role: Norm A concerns a controller's exceptional transfer of personal data and notification to the supervisory authority/data subject; Norm B concerns an AI provider's retention of automatically generated logs.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De verwerkingsverantwoordelijke informeert de toezichthoudende autoriteit over de doorgifte. De verwerkingsverantwoordelijke informeert de betrokkene

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms involve informing another party about a legally relevant matter, but they do not impose the same underlying compliance action: Norm A requires a controller to inform a supervisory authority about a non-repetitive international personal-data transfer and separately inform the data subject; Norm B requires a notified body to inform other notified bodies about refused, suspended, withdrawn, or otherwise limited approvals/certificates.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: The triggering events, actors, recipients, and information purposes differ: Norm A concerns an exceptional transfer of personal data to a third country or international organisation, while Norm B concerns decisions concerning quality-management-system approvals and technical-documentation certificates.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties are not meaningfully the same because they concern different event families, different actor roles, and different substantive information; the shared generic notion of informing another party is insufficient.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De verwerkingsverantwoordelijke informeert de toezichthoudende autoriteit over de doorgifte. De verwerkingsverantwoordelijke informeert de betrokkene

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require the actor to prepare/provide information or documentation, but they concern different substantive compliance tasks: A requires specified entity-identification and service-location information to be supplied to the central contact point for the ENISA register; B requires technical documentation for a high-risk AI system to be prepared and kept updated to demonstrate conformity and support assessment by authorities/notified bodies.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an information submission to a central contact point for an ENISA register, whereas Norm B is technical documentation of a high-risk AI system prepared for conformity assessment and made available to authorities or notified bodies.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in actor, subject matter, purpose, and recipient: A concerns designated essential or important digital-service entities supplying registry information; B concerns providers or other responsible operators of high-risk AI systems preparing technical conformity documentation. The shared generic notion of supplying/preparing information is insufficient to establish the same compliance work.
verdict.evidence_span_a: verstrekken de volgende entiteiten aan het centrale contactpunt de informatie, bedoeld in het derde lid van dit artikel, middels het daarvoor opgezette mechanisme
verdict.evidence_span_b: De technische documentatie van een AI-systeem met een hoog risico wordt opgesteld voordat dit systeem in de handel wordt gebracht of in gebruik wordt gesteld, en wordt geactualiseerd.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both provisions concern obtaining or supplying information in an information-access or investigative context, but they do not impose the same verb-level duty: A requires a domain-name registry or registrar to grant access to specified registration data upon a lawful, duly justified request; B empowers the lead overseer to hear persons and collect information during a general investigation.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a substantive access-to-domain-registration-data obligation imposed on registries/registrars, with a 72-hour fallback deadline and disclosure procedures. Norm B is an investigative power of the lead overseer to hear consenting persons and gather information; it is not a duty to provide domain-registration data or to grant access on request.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms differ in actor role, operative action, and event/purpose: A concerns responding to a legitimate party's request for specific domain-registration data, whereas B concerns the lead overseer's own general investigation and hearing of persons.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Geen gedeelde concrete compliance-actie: norm A verplicht het invoeren en onderhouden van technische, operationele en organisatorische risicobeheersmaatregelen; norm B verplicht het indienen van eerste, tussentijdse/geactualiseerde en eindrapportages over ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incidenten bij een bevoegde autoriteit.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is een doorlopende preventieve en mitigerende beveiligingsmaatregelenplicht voor essentiële en belangrijke entiteiten. Norm B is een incidentrapportageplicht voor financiële entiteiten, met voorgeschreven rapportage-inhoud, fasen en bevoegde autoriteit.
verdict.criterion_fired: De normen verschillen op het niveau van de kernhandeling, het relevante gebeurtenistype en de actorcategorie: A ziet op risicobeheer en incidentpreventie/beperking als structurele maatregel, terwijl B ziet op rapportage nadat zich een ernstig ICT-gerelateerd incident voordoet.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Norm A requires covered entities to provide registration and entity-identification information to the Minister, including updates within two weeks of a change. Norm B concerns a manufacturer’s written appointment of an authorised representative and excludes certain obligations from that appointment; it does not impose the same reporting or information-provision duty.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an information-supply and update duty for registration in a national register; Norm B is a rule delimiting the scope of an authorised representative’s appointment, with no recipient or reporting deadline.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms do not impose the same underlying action, concern different subject matter and actor roles, and have no common recipient or compliance output. Norm A concerns information provision by essential/important entities and domain-name registration service entities; Norm B concerns a manufacturer appointing an authorised representative and the obligations that cannot be delegated.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Een essentiële entiteit, belangrijke entiteit en een entiteit die domeinnaamregistratiediensten verleent verstrekt ten behoeve van de registratie in het nationale register, bedoeld in artikel 43, aan Onze Minister de volgende informatie
verdict.evidence_span_b: Een fabrikant kan schriftelijk een gemachtigde aanwijzen.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both concern compliance responses connected with serious ICT/AI incidents, but A requires documenting, evaluating, improving, and submitting an ICT-risk-management framework evaluation report on request; B requires making a notification of a serious incident within a specified period.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A concerns periodic and incident-triggered documentation/evaluation and continuous improvement of an ICT-risk-management framework, with a report supplied on request. Norm B concerns an incident notification after a causal link or reasonable likelihood is established, no later than 15 days after awareness.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ at the verb and substantive-content level, and the actor scope is not shown to be the same: A concerns an entity subject to the simplified ICT-risk-management framework under DORA, while B concerns an AI-system provider or, where applicable, deployer. Similar incident context and authority-facing compliance do not make the underlying work duplicated.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Het in lid 1, tweede alinea, punt a), bedoelde kader voor ICT-risicobeheer wordt overeenkomstig de toezichtinstructies op gezette tijden en bij ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incidenten gedocumenteerd en geëvalueerd.
verdict.evidence_span_b: De in lid 1 bedoelde melding wordt gedaan onmiddellijk nadat de aanbieder een oorzakelijk verband tussen het AI-systeem en het ernstige incident of de redelijke waarschijnlijkheid van een dergelijk verband heeft vastgesteld en in ieder geval uiterlijk 15 dagen nadat de aanbieder of, in voorkomend geval, de gebruiksverantwoordelijke zich bewust wordt van het ernstige incident.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both concern incident-related compliance information, but A requires documenting personal-data breaches for supervisory compliance, whereas B requires submitting a sequence of reports and warnings about significant incidents to a CSIRT or competent authority, with specified incident assessments, impacts, indicators, causes, and mitigation measures.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an internal documentation duty concerning personal-data breaches and enabling supervisory inspection; Norm B is an external, time-bound multi-stage reporting duty concerning significant incidents, including early warning, incident, interim, and final reports.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties do not have the same core action or actor role: A requires the controller to document all personal-data breaches, while B requires affected entities to submit specified reports about significant incidents to a CSIRT or competent authority. The shared incident-related theme and some overlapping factual subject matter do not make the compliance work the same.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De verwerkingsverantwoordelijke documenteert alle inbreuken in verband met persoonsgegevens, met inbegrip van de feiten omtrent de inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens, de gevolgen daarvan en de genomen corrigerende maatregelen.
verdict.evidence_span_b: een incidentmelding indienen met, indien van toepassing, een update van de in punt a) bedoelde informatie, een initiële beoordeling van het significante incident, met inbegrip van de ernst en de gevolgen ervan en, indien beschikbaar, de indicatoren voor aantasting

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require an actor to make a notification/report concerning a specified triggering circumstance to an institutional recipient. However, Norm A concerns an AI provider notifying the European Commission that a general-purpose AI model meets a systemic-risk-related condition, with supporting proof; Norm B concerns specified financial-sector entities reporting ICT incidents (or voluntarily reporting them) to the designated sectoral CSIRT, in addition to the reporting required under the referenced EU provision.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: The duties concern different triggering events, different regulated actors, and materially different report content and purposes: systemic-risk qualification of a general-purpose AI model versus ICT-incident reporting by financial-sector entities.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms do not impose the same compliance duty: they differ in actor role and event family, and the required information serves different purposes. The fact that both use a notification/reporting verb is insufficient to establish duplicate burden.

Die kennisgeving bevat de informatie die nodig is om aan te tonen dat aan de desbetreffende eis is voldaan.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Banken, handelsplatformen, centrale effectenbewaarinstellingen en centrale tegenpartijen doen de melding, bedoeld in artikel 19, eerste lid, eerste paragraaf, van de verordening, en de vrijwillige melding, bedoeld in artikel 19, tweede lid, eerste paragraaf, van de verordening, tevens bij het bij of krachtens artikel 16, eerste lid, van de Cyberbeveiligingswet aangewezen CSIRT voor de sectoren bankwezen en infrastructuur voor de financiële markt.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms involve making information or documentation available to another party, but A requires responding to a justified access request for specific domain-registration data, whereas B requires AI-model providers to prepare, maintain, and make available AI-model information and documentation to integrating AI-system providers, and separately make technical documentation available to authorities on request.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: The duties concern different subject matter, actors, recipients, and purposes: domain-registration data access versus AI-model documentation and downstream-provider information duties.
verdict.criterion_fired: Different actor role and event/duty family, with materially different content and purpose; the superficial commonality of providing information does not create duplicated compliance work.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A requires domain-name registration service providers to provide specified entity and operational information to the central contact point for the ENISA register. B concerns investigators exercising supervisory powers under written authorization and mentions possible coercive fines if third-party ICT-service providers fail to provide requested records, data, procedures, materials, or answers.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a proactive register-information submission by domain-name registration service providers; Norm B is a supervisory-investigation authorization and enforcement provision concerning third-party ICT-service providers' responses to investigators.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms do not impose the same underlying action on the same actor in response to the same event: A requires register information to be supplied to a central contact point, while B governs investigators' powers and possible fines for non-provision of investigative materials or answers.
verdict.evidence_span_a: verstrekken entiteiten die domeinnaamregistratiediensten verlenen aan het centrale contactpunt de informatie, bedoeld in het derde lid van dit artikel, middels het daarvoor opgezette mechanisme

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both provisions concern action following a serious/significant incident involving a regulated service or AI system, but A requires urgent notification to service recipients, whereas B requires the provider to investigate the incident and AI system, including risk assessment and corrective measures, while avoiding certain system-modifying investigations without prior notice to authorities.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an outward-facing notification duty to service recipients; Norm B is an investigation, risk-assessment, corrective-measures, cooperation, and procedural restraint duty imposed on an AI provider after a serious incident. The provisions do not require the same compliance work.
verdict.criterion_fired: Different core action and actor role: A requires an essential or important entity to notify its service recipients of significant incidents without delay; B requires an AI provider to investigate a serious incident and the AI system, assess risks, take corrective measures, cooperate with authorities, and avoid certain modifications without prior notice.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit stelt in voorkomend geval onverwijld de ontvangers van haar diensten in kennis van significante incidenten die een nadelige invloed kunnen hebben op de verlening van die diensten.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Na de melding van een ernstig incident op grond van lid 1 verricht de aanbieder onverwijld het nodige onderzoek in verband met het ernstige incident en het betrokken AI-systeem.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms involve compliance activity connected to an event or circumstance and interaction with a public authority, but A requires advance notification of planned cable-maintenance works, whereas B requires documentation/evaluation and continuous improvement of an ICT-risk-management framework, plus submission of an evaluation report on request.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a prior notice about planned works on public land, addressed to the local mayor or delegate. Norm B concerns ICT-risk-management governance triggered periodically and by serious ICT incidents, with an on-request report to the competent authority.
verdict.criterion_fired: The underlying action, triggering event, actor role, and substantive content differ; the shared presence of an authority-facing obligation is insufficient to establish duplicated compliance work.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms involve supplying information or documentation in response to a reasoned request, but they concern different subject matter, purposes, and legal duties.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires a domain-name registry or registrar to grant a legitimate requesting party access to specific domain-registration data; Norm B requires an authorised representative of a general-purpose AI-model provider to provide the AI Office with all information and documentation needed to demonstrate compliance with the Regulation.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in actor, triggering context, recipient relationship, purpose, and required content; the superficial similarity of responding to a request does not establish duplicated compliance work.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require the regulated entity to prepare/provide information or documentation to support regulatory compliance, but they do not require the same underlying reporting work.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires domain-name registration service providers to supply entity-identification and operational details to the central contact point for the ENISA register. Norm B requires providers of general-purpose AI models to create, maintain, and make available extensive technical, copyright, training-content, and downstream-provider documentation, including possible provision to the AI Office and national competent authorities.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties concern different regulated actors, different regulatory purposes, and materially different information: an ENISA-register submission of entity and service details versus AI-model technical and compliance documentation. Similarity at the generic level of providing information is insufficient for duplicate burden.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both involve an information/assistance-related response in an exceptional or special situation, but the underlying duties are not the same: Norm A requires broad cooperation and execution of military-authority orders, whereas Norm B requires the controller to inform the supervisory authority about a specific international data transfer and to inform the data subject about that transfer and the compelling legitimate interests pursued.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a general cooperation-and-implementation duty owed to military authority during application of the War Act; Norm B is a GDPR transparency/notification duty triggered by an exceptional transfer of personal data to a third country or international organisation.
verdict.criterion_fired: Different event family, actor role, recipient relationship, and substantive action; the superficial similarity of an authority-facing obligation does not establish duplicated compliance work.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms involve a regulated actor taking a compliance-related step connected to a legally relevant situation, but the underlying actions differ: Norm A permits requesting a formal decision from the ACM; Norm B requires documenting and evaluating an ICT-risk-management framework and submitting an evaluation report on request.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A concerns an unresolved agreement about a statutory toleration obligation and a request for an ACM decision. Norm B concerns periodic and serious-incident-triggered documentation and evaluation of an ICT-risk-management framework, with possible submission of an evaluation report to the competent authority.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in core action, triggering event, actor role, recipient relationship, and substantive content; the apparent similarity is not a duplicated reporting or compliance burden.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern organizational responsibility in the context of potentially harmful or risky processing/ICT operations, but Norm A imposes civil liability to compensate damage caused by GDPR-infringing processing, whereas Norm B requires covered entities to establish and maintain ICT-risk controls, including rapid identification and handling of ICT incidents.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a damage-compensation liability rule triggered by unlawful processing and concerns allocation/recovery of compensation; Norm B is a preventive and operational ICT-risk-management obligation requiring systems, monitoring, detection, response, continuity, and related controls.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties do not impose the same underlying action: Norm A concerns liability for and compensation of damage caused by GDPR-infringing processing, while Norm B requires ongoing ICT-risk-management measures. They also differ in triggering event and actor scope: Norm A applies to controllers/processors involved in processing, while Norm B applies to specified small or exempt financial entities.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern actions by entities in the domain of digital/technical regulation, but their operative duties are different: Norm A requires collecting and maintaining accurate, complete domain-registration data; Norm B permits a manufacturer to appoint an authorised representative in writing, while excluding specified obligations from that appointment.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a data-collection and database-maintenance duty imposed on top-level-domain registries and domain-registration service entities. Norm B is an optional delegation/appointment mechanism for manufacturers, with specified technical-documentation and other obligations excluded from the delegation.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms impose different actions on different actor roles and do not concern the same triggering event or compliance work; any superficial similarity in digital-regulatory subject matter is insufficient.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De registers voor topleveldomeinnamen en de entiteiten die domeinnaamregistratiediensten verlenen verzamelen nauwkeurige en volledige domeinnaamregistratiegegevens in een database en houden die gegevens bij.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern cybersecurity-related compliance, but Norm A requires an essential entity to bear the cost of a targeted security audit, whereas Norm B requires financial entities to design network infrastructure capable of immediate disconnection or segmentation to limit contamination.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A concerns payment for an independent targeted security audit imposed in the context of supervisory measures; Norm B concerns implementing a preventive network-infrastructure design measure.
verdict.criterion_fired: The underlying actions, triggering context, and duty-bearing actor roles are materially different: audit-cost payment for an essential entity versus preventive infrastructure design by a financial entity.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De kosten van een dergelijke gerichte door een onafhankelijke instantie uitgevoerde beveiligingsaudit worden betaald door de gecontroleerde entiteit

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern action following a technology/security-related incident, but A requires urgent notification of an affected individual, whereas B requires periodic and incident-triggered documentation and evaluation of an ICT-risk-management framework, with an evaluation report submitted to the competent authority on request.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an individual data-subject breach notification duty; Norm B is an ICT-risk-management governance, documentation, evaluation, improvement, and authority-reporting duty.
verdict.criterion_fired: Same broad ICT/security-incident context and comparable regulated-provider role, but the operative actions, recipients, purposes, and required content differ substantially; this is related compliance work rather than repetition of the same reporting duty.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Geen gedeelde compliance-actie: norm A verplicht bepaalde buiten de EU gevestigde entiteiten een vertegenwoordiger in de EU aan te wijzen; norm B regelt voorwaarden voor verdere verwerking, delen, beveiliging, logging, bewaring en openbaarmaking van persoonsgegevens in een AI-testomgeving.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A betreft de aanwijzing van een EU-vertegenwoordiger door bepaalde aanbieders; norm B betreft gegevensverwerkingsvoorwaarden voor AI-testomgevingen, waaronder dat oorspronkelijk verzamelde gegevens alleen overeenkomstig het gegevensbeschermingsrecht verder mogen worden gedeeld.
verdict.criterion_fired: De normen hebben noch dezelfde kernhandeling, noch dezelfde gebeurtenisfamilie of actorrol. Norm A ziet op vertegenwoordiging; norm B op verwerking en governance van persoonsgegevens in een AI-testomgeving. verdict.criterion_fired: The actor roles, triggering circumstances, core verbs, and required content differ materially. A concerns a telecommunications party conducting an investigation at the Minister’s request; B concerns notified bodies notifying the notifying authority about certification, notification-scope, market-surveillance requests, and conformity-assessment activities.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern compliance-related obligations connected with regulated products/systems, but they do not impose the same underlying action. Norm A requires an authorised representative to retain and, on request, provide conformity information/documentation and cooperate with risk-elimination measures. Norm B requires a high-risk AI provider to perform multiple provider obligations, including corrective measures and supplying information required under Article 20.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an authorised representative's document-retention, information-provision, and cooperation duty toward the Minister; Norm B is a high-risk AI provider's broader product-compliance duty, including corrective measures and Article 20 information.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms do not share the same actor role, triggering event, or core compliance action. Norm A is triggered by a Minister's request or by measures addressing risks in devices/radio equipment; Norm B imposes standing obligations on providers of high-risk AI systems, including corrective measures and Article 20 information. Similarity of regulated-product context is insufficient to establish duplicated compliance work.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms impose a time-related obligation concerning records or information associated with a regulated system or user: Norm A requires number holders to register number users, while Norm B requires high-risk AI providers to retain automatically generated logs. They do not require the same compliance work.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a one-time registration of number users by number holders; Norm B is ongoing retention of automatically generated high-risk-AI logs by AI providers.
verdict.criterion_fired: Different core action, event family, and actor role; the apparent six-month similarity does not create duplicate compliance work.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern communicating information about a cyber/security-related threat or incident, but A requires supplying the contact details of the official responsible for an incident report, while B requires entities to inform potentially affected service recipients about a significant cyber threat and, where relevant, measures they can take.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an incident-reporting-content requirement directed to the reporting process; Norm B is an outward warning/information duty to potentially affected service recipients.
verdict.criterion_fired: Same general cyber-incident/threat context and actor category, but the required information, purpose, and recipient differ: A supplies the responsible reporting official’s contact details as part of an early warning, whereas B warns potentially affected service recipients about the threat and possible response measures.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both involve an authority-facing information obligation concerning serious/significant ICT incidents: Norm A requires incident reporting and updates, while Norm B requires providing an estimate of aggregated annual costs and losses on request.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a structured, time-bound incident-reporting regime requiring warnings, incident assessments, updates, and final reports to the CSIRT or competent authority. Norm B is an on-request provision of an aggregated annual financial-loss estimate to competent authorities; it does not require the incident report itself or the same substantive information.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in both actor scope and core content: Norm A concerns affected entities reporting a significant incident and its technical/severity/impact details, whereas Norm B concerns non-micro financial entities supplying an aggregated annual cost-and-loss estimate on request. The shared ICT-incident context and authority recipient do not make the compliance work the same.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both require an incident-related notification, but A requires reporting a significant incident to cybersecurity authorities, while B requires notifying clients about a serious ICT incident and mitigation measures (and, separately, potentially informing clients about protective measures for a significant cyberthreat).

verdict.criterion_fired: The event family is similar, but the actor roles and compliance duties are not the same: A applies to essential or important entities offering trust services and requires an authority/CSIRT report; B applies to financial entities and requires client notification. The different recipient and substantially different content reinforce that these are not the same duty.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms involve supplying information or documentation to a supervisory authority upon request, but the underlying duties are not the same: Norm A concerns making available an ICT-services contractual information register and related supervisory information; Norm B concerns an authorised representative providing a copy of its mandate to the AI Office, plus separate duties to retain technical documentation and respond to reasoned requests.

verdict.criterion_fired: The norms do not impose the same core duty on the same actor role concerning the same event or subject matter. Any superficial similarity is limited to authority-facing provision of information on request; the requested information, regulatory context, and responsible actors differ.

verdict.criterion_fired: The norms differ in both the underlying action and the regulated subject matter: A authorizes investigative examination and copying by a lead overseer, while B regulates conditions for personal-data processing in an AI test environment. verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms involve regulatory action connected to a regulated entity and a compliance-related circumstance, but Norm A imposes a coercive fine on a critical ICT third-party provider for non-compliance with oversight measures, whereas Norm B requires a general-purpose AI provider to notify the Commission and provide substantiating information when a specified condition is met.

verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in actor role, triggering event, operative action, purpose, and content: Norm A concerns the lead overseer's imposition of a coercive fine to compel compliance, while Norm B concerns an AI provider's notification to the Commission with evidence of compliance.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both provisions concern compliance-related cooperation or information/documentation in an oversight context, but they do not impose the same concrete action: Norm A requires an authorised representative to retain and, on request, provide conformity information/documentation and cooperate with risk-mitigation measures; Norm B concerns an investigation authorisation stating possible coercive fines if investigated third-party ICT-service providers fail to provide registers, data, procedures, other material, or answers.

verdict.criterion_fired: The provisions differ in actor, operative action, and legal context: Norm A governs an authorised representative's conformity-documentation and risk-measure duties, while Norm B governs an investigation authorisation and coercive-fine notice concerning third-party ICT-service providers.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A requires affected entities to report significant incidents to a CSIRT or competent authority through early warning, incident, interim, and final reports, including incident assessments, impacts, causes, indicators, and mitigation measures. verdict.distinguishing_factor: A is an external, time-bound incident-reporting duty to a CSIRT or competent authority; B is an internal ICT-incident management, registration, root-cause, and remediation duty, with no reporting recipient or deadline specified.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms concern the same broad ICT/cyber-incident domain and comparable regulated entities, but they require materially different work: external, staged reporting under A versus internal registration, monitoring, investigation, documentation, and remediation under B. The different recipient does not itself make the duties different; the decisive factor is the low overlap in action and content.

verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in both the underlying action and the regulated event/context: inspection compliance by a critical ICT service provider versus AI-system conformity and corrective action by an AI provider. They therefore do not impose the same compliance work.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern communicating information about a cyber/data-security incident, but GDPR Article 34 requires communicating breach information to affected data subjects, whereas DORA Article 19 requires financial entities to submit incident notifications and reports to a competent authority, including initial, intermediate/updated, and final reports.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: The recipient and compliance purpose differ fundamentally: affected individuals receive an understandable explanation and protective information under GDPR, while a supervisory authority receives structured, ongoing incident reports under DORA, including scope, cross-border effects, status changes, root-cause analysis, and impact figures.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties are not meaningfully the same because they are owed by different actor categories in different roles and serve different recipients and purposes: GDPR Article 34 concerns a controller communicating a personal-data breach to affected data subjects; DORA Article 19 concerns financial entities reporting serious ICT-related incidents to a competent authority.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms impose substantive preventive/operational requirements concerning the use or design of technology, but they do not require the same compliance action: Article 9 requires financial entities to design ICT network connection infrastructure so it can be disconnected or segmented to limit and prevent infection, whereas Article 5 prohibits specified AI practices, including placing on the market, putting into service, or using certain AI systems.
